High-Efficiency Combustion Mode in Three-Strut Scramjet Combustor via Clustering Analysis
abstract: This study investigates the influence of five design parameters on the combustion characteristics of a three-strut combustion chamber through single-factor analysis, clarifying their relationship with combustion efficiency and resistance. A Halton sequence with mean squared error–based infill sampling was employed to generate a sample set, and an accurate surrogate model was developed using Gaussian process regression. The Nondominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm II (NSGA-II) was then applied to optimize the chamber geometry with the objectives of improving combustion efficiency and reducing resistance. Through clustering analysis, two distinct high-efficiency combustion modes were identified: a multizone violent combustion mode and a blended mild combustion mode. In the former, the rapid combustion of pilot fuel creates favorable conditions for subsequent fuel combustion, increasing the combustion efficiency from 73% to 93% compared with the baseline case; however, due to excessively abrupt flow field changes, the reduction in resistance is not significant. In the latter, the flame fronts merge and develop smoothly, and although it only improves combustion efficiency to 85% compared with the baseline case, it substantially reduces resistance from − 7,762 newtons (N) to − 8303 N . This work provides enhanced design flexibility for high-performance scramjet combustors.

title: Efficient Synergistic Design Framework for Electric Aircraft Integrating Co-Flow Jet
abstract: Flow control technologies such as the Co-Flow Jet (CFJ) have demonstrated significant potential for improving aerodynamic performance. However, most existing studies treat CFJ parameters as fixed during aircraft conceptual design, limiting the ability to evaluate their system-level impact on aircraft performance. To address this limitation, this study proposes an efficient multidisciplinary design framework that integrates key CFJ design parameters into the conceptual design process of CFJ electric aircraft. The framework combines a quasi-three-dimensional aerodynamic analysis method with energy consumption and weight estimation models of the jet system, enabling rapid evaluation of aerodynamic performance, propulsion power consumption, and aircraft weight within a unified framework. Based on the proposed methodology, a multidisciplinary design optimization problem is formulated to improve aircraft cruise performance. The framework is applied to a representative aircraft configuration, and the predicted aerodynamic performance is validated against computational fluid dynamics simulations. The results demonstrate that the proposed framework can efficiently capture the coupled effects of CFJ aerodynamic benefits, jet system energy consumption, and additional structural weight. Parametric studies further reveal the sensitivity of optimal CFJ configuration to cruise velocity and fan efficiency, providing useful guidance for the preliminary design of CFJ electric aircraft.

title: FRGB3D: Fast Reliability-Weighted Gaussian Background Modeling for Roadside LiDAR Traffic Monitoring
abstract: Intelligent transportation systems rely on accurate perception technologies for traffic monitoring, with light detection and ranging (LiDAR) emerging as a critical sensing modality. However, effective background–foreground separation is challenging due to the varying measurement reliability across point clouds caused by distance, reflectivity, and atmospheric conditions. This paper presents fast reliability-weighted Gaussian background modeling for 3D LiDAR traffic monitoring (FRGB3D), a novel unsupervised approach for LiDAR point cloud background modeling and foreground detection that explicitly incorporates physics-based reliability assessment with adaptive learning mechanisms. The key contributions include (1) a physics-based reliability metric that quantifies measurement quality using range and reflectivity characteristics, (2) a reliability-weighted adaptive learning approach for Gaussian background modeling that dynamically adjusts learning rates based on point reliability, and (3) an adaptive thresholding mechanism that incorporates both measurement reliability and learned model uncertainty. Through comprehensive experiments using both the Car Learning to Act (CARLA) simulator and real-world LiDAR data collected in Lowell, Massachusetts, we demonstrate that FRGB3D achieves superior foreground detection performance compared with baseline methods. FRGB3D achieved F1-scores of 0.84, 0.68, and 0.77 across base, adverse-weather, and high-density traffic scenarios, respectively, consistently outperforming simple difference, moving average, and standard Gaussian background modeling approaches. Real-world experiments demonstrated competitive object-level performance average precision (AP) (AP@0.5 = 0.48) while maintaining real-time processing capabilities with 19.1 frames per second (FPS), making it suitable for practical traffic monitoring applications.
journal: Journal of Computing in Civil Engineering

title: Comparative Analysis of Two Approaches for Improved Site Safety: Domain Approach versus General End-to-End Compliance Reasoning
abstract: Field compliance checking seeks to automate the process of extracting safety requirements, capturing site information, identifying violations, and generating documentation for different responsible parties to improve construction site safety. However, existing safety checking methods are typically limited in their ability to employ domain knowledge and multimodal data, and they often lack generalizability and scalability. There is also limited effort to automatically generate natural-language descriptions of compliance-checking results for documentation purposes. Aimed toward addressing these gaps, this paper studies and compares two approaches for automated safety checking: a domain approach and an end-to-end approach. The domain approach integrates existing domain-specific information extraction, site visual information detection, and knowledge graph–based compliance reasoning methods. The end-to-end approach relies on multimodal foundation models. The comparative analysis evaluates the information extraction and compliance reasoning capabilities of both approaches in terms of performance, errors, and limitations. The results showed that the domain approach achieved strong performance with good potential for generalizability and adaptability. In contrast, the end-to-end approach requires additional fine-tuning to achieve comparable results.
journal: Journal of Construction Engineering and Management

title: A Review of Human-Centric Construction Manufacturing: Current Practices and Research Opportunities
abstract: The industrialization of the construction industry has transformed traditional practices by streamlining construction processes in controlled, factory-based environments through construction manufacturing production systems, in which building components are produced in factories and assembled on-site. Beyond improvements in efficiency and environmental performance, this production paradigm establishes long-term relationships between workers and management, creating an opportunity for human-centric construction manufacturing that prioritizes workers’ well-being as a core element of production within the Industry 5.0 paradigm. Human-centric construction manufacturing offers a practical means of integrating worker well-being, safety, mental health, inclusiveness, and skill development into construction production systems. Despite growing interest in human-centric considerations, existing research remains fragmented, loosely defined, and predominantly technology-driven. To address these gaps, this paper presents a scoping review on human-centric construction manufacturing that synthesizes key research themes, enabling technologies, emerging trends, research gaps, and future research directions within construction production systems. A total of 54 articles were included in the review, spanning three research areas examined from a human-centric perspective, i.e., ergonomics, safety, and workforce planning, each further categorized into subresearch areas. Workers’ mental health, equity, diversity, inclusion, and holistic well-being in the construction manufacturing paradigm remain significant and underexplored research opportunities. Among the most prominent technologies were simulation, virtual reality, optimization, sensing technologies, and 3D modeling, while computer vision, machine learning, robotics, and digital twins were less frequently applied, despite their strong potential to support human-centric construction manufacturing. Overall, this review establishes a comprehensive foundation for understanding the current state of human-centric construction manufacturing, identifies critical research needs, and provides guidance for future efforts toward developing safer, healthier, and more productive factory environments that support resilient construction manufacturing systems.
journal: Journal of Construction Engineering and Management

title: Advancing clinical integration in undergraduate dental education through AI-enabled instructional design: a qualitative thematic analysis.
abstract: BACKGROUND Despite growing interest in artificial intelligence (AI) in health professions education, qualitative evidence for integarting AI-supported instructional redesign on teaching practices and students' experiences in undergraduate dental education remains limited. The aim of this study was to explore the educational impact of AI-supported instructional redesign of lessons in undergraduate dental education. METHODS We conducted this inductive qualitative thematic analysis in an undergraduate dental education setting. Existing lessons were redesigned using AI-supported recommendations to strengthen alignment between learning objectives, authentic clinical contexts, and expected clinical outcomes. Data were collected through classroom observations and students' focus group discussions. An inductive thematic analysis was performed, and findings from multiple data sources were curated, collecetd, and triangulated to enhance credibility. RESULTS AI-supported instructional redesign transformed teaching by promoting authentic clinical scenarios, clinically oriented discussions, and explicit reasoning activities. Thematic analysis identified four interconnected themes: (1) a shift from teacher-centred knowledge delivery to facilitation of clinical reasoning; (2) transformation from passive attendance to active cognitive engagement; (3) building clinical meaning through authentic clinical contexts and collaborative dialogue; and (4) creating conditions for professional learning through psychological safety. AI functioned as a pedagogical design-support tool rather than replacing the educators' instructional role. Overall, the observed educational changes appeared to arise primarily from the pedagogical redesign enabled by AI-supported planning rather than from students' direct interaction with AI. CONCLUSION This study endorses the role of AI-supported instructional redesign in enriching the existing undergraduate dental curriculum. This approach can potentially help educators align learning objectives, instructional strategies, and authentic clinical contexts. The reported educational modifications reflect primarily the implementation of learner-centred and clinically oriented pedagogical strategies, with AI functioning as a design-support mechanism rather than as a direct instructional agent.

title: Intelligent Manufacturing Scheduling Optimization Based on Genetic Algorithm and MES
abstract: Against the backdrop of intensified global manufacturing competition and the deep advancement of Industry 4.0, production scheduling, as a core link in efficient operations within intelligent manufacturing, faces challenges that traditional methods can no longer meet, such as delayed data acquisition and insufficient dynamic response. Therefore, a scheduling model for Industry 4.0 intelligent manufacturing based on a Genetic Algorithm (GA) and a Manufacturing Execution System (MES) is proposed. During the process, the particle swarm algorithm was used to optimize the Genetic Algorithm's parameters serially, thereby reducing complexity. At the same time, the ant colony algorithm was integrated to optimize key processes, improving the model's stability and convergence and establishing a scheduling optimization model that integrates data collection, rapid processing, and reasonable allocation. The experimental results show that the inventory turnover rate of the intelligent manufacturing scheduling model constructed in this study has increased by 3.24%, 4.58%, and 6.17%, respectively, compared to the control model’s. Meanwhile, the on-time delivery rate reaches 92.13% and 91.75% across two datasets, both above 91%. The task delay rates are 7.69% and 8.67%, showing significant advantages over the comparison models at 10.45% and 11.75%, respectively. These results indicate that the proposed model can achieve efficient allocation of production resources and dynamic responsiveness, thereby improving production line efficiency and offering a new approach to intelligent manufacturing scheduling.
journal: Journal of Engineering, Project, and Production Management

title: A Multi-Layer Contextual Model for Managing Data Overload in Smart Hydroponics
abstract: The widespread use of the Internet of Things (IoT) in hydroponic agriculture allows continuous monitoring of environmental conditions and provides real-time information to support crop management. However, the increasing amount of sensor data generated makes the monitoring process more complex as users need to interpret multiple environmental parameters simultaneously. Existing hydroponic monitoring systems focus on data collection and visualization, while the management and information delivery aspects to reduce data overload are still limited. This study proposes a multi-layer contextual model to manage environmental information in an intelligent hydroponic monitoring system. The model consists of five interconnected layers (Power, Sensor, Communication, Database and Visualization), which support the process of acquisition, validation, management and contextual data delivery. To validate the proposed model, a solar-powered IoT hydroponic monitoring system integrated with an Augmented Reality (AR) application was developed based on Situation Awareness Theory. Using the System Usability Scale (SUS), the prototype was assessed by three domain experts. The results achieved an average usability score of 85.83, which reflects excellent usability. The results indicate that the proposed model improves organisation and presentation of environmental information by prioritising contextually relevant data rather than displaying all available sensor readings at once. This enables users to identify important environmental conditions efficiently and supports more effective monitoring. This approach helps to reduce data overload and provides a practical framework that can support the development of IoT-based smart agriculture applications in the future through the integration of anomaly detection techniques and predictive analytics.
journal: Journal of Information and Communication Technology

title: From Farm Records to a Digital Control Tower: Integrating Production, Harvest, Finance, Markets, and Traceability for Independent Oil Palm Smallholders — A Review
abstract: Independent oil palm smallholders operate simultaneously as growers, employers, input purchasers, harvest managers, logistics coordinators, sellers, and increasingly as actors responsible for demonstrating legal and sustainability compliance. Yet these functions are often managed through fragmented records, informal communication, delayed information, and disconnected transactions. This qualitative literature review examines how an integrated digital farm-management architecture could transform those fragmented activities into a coherent management-control system. Recent literature published primarily between 2020 and 2026 was purposively reviewed across oil palm agronomy, farm management information systems, digital agriculture, precision technologies, agricultural marketing, certification, and supply-chain traceability. The thematic synthesis identifies seven interconnected domains: farm visibility and management control; harvest integrity and fresh-fruit-bunch quality; agronomic and input management; financial visibility; buyer and transaction management; legality and traceability; and digital adoption conditions. The review argues that the main opportunity is not simply to digitize farm records, but to establish a closed-loop system connecting measurement, verification, diagnosis, decision, action, transaction, reconciliation, and organizational learning. A conceptual Digital Smallholder Oil Palm Control Tower is consequently proposed to connect field-level data with managerial dashboards, farm-to-mill transactions, financial reconciliation, sustainability evidence, and decision support. The framework suggests that farmer-centred, mobile-first, interoperable, and progressively implemented systems may strengthen productivity, profitability, bargaining capacity, traceability, and resilience while limiting digital complexity and exclusion
journal: Journal of Engineering and Applied Sciences Technology

title: From Rules to Autonomous Agents: The Evolution of Artificial Intelligence, Human-AI Integration, and the Governance of Agentic Systems-A Review
abstract: Artificial intelligence has evolved from rule-based symbolic systems into learning architectures capable of perception, prediction, content generation, reasoning, planning, tool use, and increasingly autonomous action. This qualitative literature review examines this transition as more than a technological chronology. It interprets AI evolution through five interrelated dimensions: technological evolution, capability expansion, changing human roles, human–AI integration, and governance. Drawing on contemporary peer-reviewed literature published primarily between 2020 and 2026, the review identifies seven thematic developments. AI has progressed from encoded rules toward learned representations and goal-directed action; generative AI has expanded AI into a general-purpose content collaborator; agentic AI adds planning, memory, tool use, and iterative task execution; human roles increasingly shift from operator toward collaborator, delegator, and governor; human–AI complementarity remains conditional rather than automatic; effective deployment requires calibrated rather than maximal trust; and governance requirements increase as AI systems acquire greater operational agency. The article proposes the Evolution–Capability–Role–Integration–Governance (ECRIG) framework to explain these relationships. The framework suggests that sustainable benefits from advanced AI emerge when technological capability, human role allocation, interaction architecture, and governance mechanisms develop jointly. The review concludes that the central challenge of the agentic-AI era is not choosing between humans and machines, but designing accountable systems in which increasingly capable artificial agents remain aligned with meaningful human goals, authority, and oversight.
journal: Journal of Engineering and Applied Sciences Technology

title: Intelligent visual perception beyond classification: a survey of deep learning and foundation models
abstract: Intelligent visual perception has advanced from traditional image classification to thorough comprehension of objects, scenes, relations, spatial context, and semantic information. This paper surveys the development of intelligent visual perception, particularly focusing on DL and foundation models. This section provides a comprehensive overview of visual recognition, detection, segmentation, and scene understanding, including key methods such as convolutional neural networks, recurrent neural networks, attention mechanisms, encoder-decoder architectures, generative models, and Vision Transformers. The study also explores feature attribution, visual attention, visual reasoning, and multimodal vision-language models, which combine visual and text information for tasks such as visual question answering, captioning, and visual generation. This study examines recent foundation models incorporating vision-language architectures for their transferability, contextual understanding, and generalized perception capabilities. The study also discusses challenges related to computational efficiency, environmental variability, data requirements, robustness, explainability, and real-time deployment. Finally, it contrasts current developments to identify new approaches to scalable, interpretable, multimodal, and human-centric visual intelligence systems.
journal: Future Digital Technologies and Artificial Intelligence

title: Numerical simulation and control measures for deflagration in ventilation ducts of polyimide foam production line
abstract: Polyimide foam exhibits excellent high-temperature resistance, flame retardancy, and sound absorption performance, and is widely used in aerospace, advanced equipment, and other high-tech fields. However, its production process involves inherent deflagration risks from combustible dust and volatile organic gases. Using the ventilation and dust-collection duct of a polyimide foam production line as the research object, this paper establishes a numerical deflagration model in ANSYS Fluent to investigate the propagation behavior of gas-dust mixtures inside the duct. The evolution characteristics of velocity, temperature, pressure, species distribution, and particle motion are systematically analyzed. Quantitative results show that the peak gas temperature in the main reaction zone reaches approximately 1680 K, the maximum local flow velocity is 24.3 m/s, and the minimum gas density drops to 0.20–0.40 kg/m³. The middle horizontal section of the duct is identified as the primary deflagration zone, while elbows and areas with structural discontinuities are high-risk locations with significant pressure concentration and flow turbulence. Based on this, targeted risk control measures are proposed, including duct structure optimization, explosion venting and isolation arrangement, dust concentration management, online monitoring system construction, and ignition source control. This study provides theoretical support for explosion-proof design and safety optimization of ventilation and dust removal systems in polyimide foam production lines.

title: A survey on intelligent transportation systems for accident detection and risk prediction using AI
abstract: The complexity of today's transportation networks has made road safety, accident detection, and risk management increasingly challenging. Intelligent Transportation Systems (ITS) offer a technological base to enhance transportation safety by incorporating sensors, communications, data processing, and intelligent decision-making. This review discusses the application of Artificial Intelligence (AI) for accident detection and risk prediction in ITS by examining information sources, methodologies, accident investigation, and associated challenges. It examines the use of machine learning, deep learning, computer vision, spatiotemporal modeling, and multimodal AI for accident detection, risk prediction, severity analysis, and active safety management. This review of studies suggests that collecting traffic, vehicle, road, environmental, geographical, historical, and driver-related information can improve understanding of collisions and support timely safety decisions. The review also highlights the importance of explainable and reliable AI that provides transparency, dependability, and accountability. However, the obstacles include data heterogeneity, model generalization, dynamic conditions, scalability, quick implementation, privacy considerations, security requirements, and compatible information systems. In conclusion, incorporating AI in ITS may have the power to shift road-safety management from reactive measures to data-driven approaches.

title: CONSTRUCTING PROFESSIONAL IDENTITIES IN AI-ENHANCED LANGUAGE CLASSROOM: A STUDY OF PAKISTANI ENGLISH LANGUAGE TEACHERS’ PERSPECTIVES AND PRACTICES
abstract: The main aim of the study is to investigate the construction of English Language Teachers’ (ELTs) professional identity in the Artificial Intelligence (AI) era in the Pakistani Punjab context. The qualitative analysis is embedded in semi-structured interviews. Multilayered sampling techniques were used, and data were collected from ELTs working in public and private educational institutions and analyzed using the Grounded Theory Approach (GTA). Initially, purposive sampling was used to identify appropriate samples, and those samples referred additional samples until saturation was attained on the thirteenth sample. The investigation was theoretically informed by Gee’s (2000) distinction between I-identity and A-identity. Findings created five interrelated categories: Institutionally Framed Professionalism, Agentive Professional Self, Constrained Autonomy, Negotiation Professional Identity, and Hybrid Identity Construction. Results highlight that examination-driven systems, curricular mandates, and administrative checks and balances powerfully form ELTs’ identities. They are sustained simultaneously by contemplative practice, adaptive strategies, and professional achievement. Autonomy was developed as conditional rather than absolute, leading teachers to negotiate between organizational compliance and personal pedagogical obligation. The study demonstrates that ELT identity in Punjab is dynamic, context-sensitive, and permanently negotiated. By integrating hierarchical and agentive dimensions of identity, this research contributes to a nuanced understanding of teacher professionalism within examination- focused educational systems.
journal: Insights (Bhalwal) International Journal of Humanities, Management, and Social Sciences

title: PSYCHOMETRIC OPERATIONALIZATION OF FUNCTIONAL ROLES IN AUTONOMOUS MULTI-AGENT SYSTEMS BASED ON PERSONAMATRIX: AN AI TRANSITIONAL FIELD FRAMEWORK
abstract: Background: Autonomous LLM agents increasingly operate in shared environments where behavior depends on interaction history, role allocation, local norms, authority, and group structure. Objective: This conceptual methods paper develops a psychometric operationalization of dynamic functional roles in autonomous multi-agent systems using PersonaMatrix-derived measurement principles without attributing human psychological ontology to AI. Methods: A targeted evidence synthesis (2019–2026) was conducted across AI psychometrics, dynamic multi-agent roles, collective-field modeling, norm emergence, trajectory prediction, and anthropomorphism. Peer-reviewed sources were prioritized, while current OpenAI, METR/Redwood, Anthropic, and Moltbook materials were used as primary or emerging evidence for recent agent ecosystems. Results: The framework separates output-level stability (RSI, IDS, RCS) from role-level and field-level constructs. It proposes the Functional Role Consistency Index, Role Transition Index, Agent–Field Differentiation Index, Collective Utility Index, Norm Conflict Index, Regulatory Closure Index, and Field Role Composition Vector. Three falsifiable hypotheses test whether role variables add out-of-sample predictive value for agent behavior, role transitions, and future field states. Conclusion: PersonaMatrix is positioned as a measurement architecture rather than an AI personality diagnosis. The archetypal-role hypothesis is supported only if role coding is reliable, improves prediction beyond non-archetypal baselines, and generalizes to unseen agents and independent multi-agent environments.

title: Adaptation of foundation models in medical image analysis: mechanisms, evidence, and deployment considerations
abstract: Foundation models, pretrained on diverse data, objectives, or modalities for reuse across downstream tasks, are increasingly applied to medical image analysis. Their performance depends not only on pretraining but also on how they are adapted to specific tasks, data regimes, and deployment settings. Whereas previous reviews have considered adaptation within broader syntheses, this review focuses specifically on post-pretraining interventions applied to existing FMs. Using a structured narrative review with a systematic, auditable workflow, we identified 719 eligible reports representing 705 independent studies. Of these, 473 provided controlled comparative evidence: 322 formally published studies formed the primary synthesis and 151 preprint-only studies a sensitivity layer. Adaptation was organized into five non-mutually exclusive families: parameter-level, representation-level, objective-level, data-centric, and architectural/sequence-level adaptation, with model use and update regime analyzed separately. Controlled comparisons showed no consistent ranking among frozen, parameter-efficient, partial, or full updating, or across broader adaptation families; outcomes varied by task, data regime, comparator, and evaluation setting. Clinical-readiness evidence remained limited: 173/705 studies (24.5%) had confirmed independent external validation, 10 (1.4%) reported calibration or uncertainty evidence, and 97/322 formally published comparative studies (30.1%) included a qualifying externally validated arm. Overall, FM adaptation is a context-dependent design space rather than a hierarchy of preferred strategies.

title: Multiscale Modeling of Zr Corrosion: Predicting Microstructures of Oxide Films
abstract: A first-principles-informed multiscale modeling approach is reported for oxide formation during corrosion of zirconium. The present simulations reproduce the columnar corrosion film microstructure and grain size distribution seen in micrographs of oxidized Zr surfaces. This structural feature emerges from a hexagonal ZrO layer adjacent to the $α$-Zr/ZrO$_{2-x}$ interface, which is dynamically stabilized by continuous heterogeneous grain nucleation and grain boundary mass diffusion. This ZrO layer is identified as a significant oxygen diffusion barrier and a potential contributor to sub-parabolic pretransition corrosion kinetics. The simulations also reproduce the undulatory nature of the metal/oxide interface, leading to regions with tensile stress components capable of nucleating cracks, despite the overall state of compressive hydrostatic stress within the oxide film. First principles density functional theory (DFT) computations of fundamental ZrO$_x$ properties were combined with molecular dynamics simulations using a machine-learned potential based on a DFT training set to provide extensive input to an advanced phase field model for oxide formation and its microstructure, as implemented in the new MedeA PhaseField module. The phase field simulations reported herein incorporated computed stoichiometry-dependent thermochemical data, anisotropic elastic properties, interface energies, bulk and grain boundary mass transport processes, multiphase heterogeneous grain nucleation, and strain energy-dependent phase stabilities.

Reservoir Flood Storage Capacity as an Indicator of Potential Forecast-Informed Prerelease Effectiveness
abstract: The operation of multipurpose reservoirs for which flood risk management (FRM) is a primary or key purpose may be improved by the use of Forecast-Informed Reservoir Operations (FIRO). The ability to screen a portfolio of dams to assess FIRO viability allows for more-efficient use of time and funding than individual detailed analyses for several dams. In this study, screening criteria were used to evaluate the potential effectiveness of FIRO prestore and prerelease (PS-PR) and basic operation prerelease (BO-PR) methods using a large data set (58 dams) and along three lines of inquiry. A regression model was used to assess system characteristics and identify the reservoirs for which reservoir filling is most sensitive to changes in flood storage capacity. Historic flood events provided insight into the feasibility of FIRO based on seasonality and storm characteristics. Physical and policy constraints were studied to assess the feasibility of FIRO at or near top of conservation pool and to provide an initial input to the screening framework. A four-parameter equation to predict reservoir-filling frequency had an R 2 value of 0.67, and flood storage capacity was significant at a 99% confidence level. Review of historic reservoir-filling events showed a median 3-day flood storage of 23% and a 7-day flood storage of 38%. Policy and physical release constraints yielded maximum daily drawdown estimates for each reservoir and indicated a median of 2% of average annual inflow evacuation per day. A case study of five dams was used to assess viability of using the storage-based regression as a criterion for prerelease screening. The presented screening approach utilizes an estimate of maximum prerelease drawdown and the regression equations to provide high estimates for potential FIRO effectiveness (with uncertainty); actual applicability depends on forecast skill and available lead time, which are not evaluated in this study.

Integrating production systems, innovation culture and employee performance in the pharmaceutical industry
abstract: This study analyzed the effect of lean operation practices, continuous improvement orientation and total quality management on innovation culture within organizational culture, and how these factors influence employees' job satisfaction, organizational commitment and perceived work performance. Employing a cross-sectional survey design with 250 valid responses from employees in the Korean pharmaceutical industry, we used a 7-point Likert scale to measure eight constructs and tested hypotheses through structural equation modeling using SPSS 18.0 and AMOS 18.0, including comprehensive reliability and validity assessments through confirmatory factor analysis. Lean operational practices were not significantly related to organizational culture variables, whereas continuous improvement and total quality management were significantly related to collaborative organizational culture and innovation culture. Only innovation culture showed significant results in relation to the dependent variables of job satisfaction, organizational commitment and perceived work performance. This can be seen as occurring because, in the regulatory environment of the pharmaceutical industry, collaboration is already mandated for regulatory compliance and thus functions as a hygiene factor, whereas innovation culture functions as a differentiating factor that compensates for the autonomy restricted by regulation. This study is the first to empirically analyze the integrated relationship between production management systems, organizational culture and employee performance in the pharmaceutical industry. Although existing studies have explored individual variable relationships or dynamics in general manufacturing industries, we propose a convergent perspective on production and human resource management that considers the characteristics of the pharmaceutical industry.
journal: International Journal of Quality & Reliability Management

title: Learning-oriented climates and sales capability development in B2B markets: how coworker support mediates the path from climate to salesperson competence
abstract: This study aims to examine how learning-oriented organizational climates and perceived support structures relate to salesperson development in complex business-to-business (B2B) sales contexts, distinguishing between satisfaction with development and perceived competence. Survey data were collected from USA-based sales professionals. The study used confirmatory factor analysis and partial least squares structural equation modeling to test relationships among learning-oriented climate cues, perceived training, supervisory and coworker support, and two developmental outcomes. Internal work constraints were tested as a moderator of the coworker support–competence relationship. Learning-oriented climates were positively associated with perceived support and with satisfaction with development; tolerance for mistakes was also positively associated with perceived competence, whereas openness to new ideas was not. Coworker support was the support source most consistently and significantly related to perceived competence in the full sample. In the context-specific B2B analysis, coworker support emerged as the only significant predictor of perceived competence. All three support sources were positively related to satisfaction with development, whereas perceived competence was driven specifically by coworker support. Internal work constraints significantly moderated the coworker support–competence relationship, but opposite to a substitution account: coworker support mattered more when constraints were low. The findings demonstrate that salesperson development is shaped by an integrated system of climate cues and social support rather than sharply differentiated pathways. Coworker-based learning emerges as a particularly salient component of competence formation in complex selling environments. Managers should view capability development as embedded in social learning systems supported by learning-oriented climates and multiple support sources, rather than relying solely on formal development structures. This study offers a theoretically grounded account of how learning-oriented climates and multisource social support jointly shape evaluative and capability-based development in B2B sales contexts, while highlighting the particular salience of coworker-based learning for competence formation in complex B2B selling.

title: The impact of ESG ratings on corporate investment efficiency in a geopolitical context
abstract: This paper examines the impact of environmental, social, and governance (ESG) ratings on corporate investment efficiency amid rising geopolitical uncertainty, while uncovering the underlying transmission mechanisms and heterogeneous effects across firm types, thereby enriching the literature on ESG governance and corporate investment decision-making. This study employs a multidimensional fixed-effects model for the baseline estimation. It further conducts heterogeneity tests based on firm lifecycle, technological attributes, and pollution levels, and examines the transmission channels, including financing constraints, green innovation, management costs, and managerial myopia. Higher ESG ratings significantly reduce inefficient investments and enhance corporate investment efficiency. The positive effects are particularly pronounced in growth-stage, non-high-tech, and non-heavily polluting firms, while they are weaker in high-tech and declining firms. ESG ratings improve investment efficiency by alleviating financing constraints, promoting green innovation, reducing management costs, and mitigating managerial myopia. This study links ESG ratings with corporate investment efficiency amid geopolitical uncertainty, thereby enriching the literature on the micro-level economic consequences of ESG practices and corporate investment decisions. It provides empirical evidence for firms to adopt differentiated ESG strategies to enhance investment efficiency and offers implications for policymakers in designing refined ESG governance frameworks in the context of global geopolitical and sustainable development competition.

title: From exhibition to education: operationalizing VR for scholarship in research, teaching and learning
abstract: This case study demonstrates one way that an academic library can transition immersive technologies from novelty installations to core pedagogical infrastructure. It argues that for virtual reality (VR) to persist as a sustainable library service, it must function as an active platform for teaching, research and learning, rather than a passive website or collection of available, but underutilized, hardware (e.g. HMDs). We describe the development of an immersive “showcase” environment built around a library-based 3D scanning service representing Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, Reusable (FAIR)-aligned 3D production workflows (Cook, 2024), and the subsequent design-based/action-research pilot of the environment in select academic contexts. The paper details selection criteria for 3D capture, integration with repositories such as Sketchfab and the design of a web-based immersive VR space (the “Immersive Showcase”) that can be used as a customizable classroom, exhibit hall or event space. Two principal curricular cases – French language learning and a hybrid lecture–exhibition space – illustrate how this VR environment, incorporating multimedia and interactive collaboration features, supports constructivist, object-centered pedagogy and facilitates engagement with collective sense-making (Mills et al., 2020). User feedback from beta testing and pilot teaching engagements informs iterative design decisions, providing a way forward for these innovative curricular integrations and always-on virtual teaching and learning environments. Embedding high-fidelity 3D surrogates in accessible immersive spaces can support “field-like” engagement with primary source materials, multi-perspective analysis and appears to facilitate hybrid teaching models. Clear workflows, role differentiation (e.g. learner/presenter) and targeted interface adjustments (e.g. navigation aids, session controls) proved critical to instructor uptake and student usability. Iterative refinement highlights the importance of aligning technical affordances with instructional goals. As a single-institution case describing a service-oriented pilot, findings are context-specific; future work should include systematic assessment of learning outcomes and comparative studies across educational contexts and platforms. The case provides concrete guidance on staffing, infrastructure, access modalities and partnership models for libraries seeking to embed VR and 3D content into teaching and research. We posit that the success of programs of this nature requires a shift away from viewing VR as a “fieldtrip” destination, instead seeing it as a steady partner in the scholarly lifecycle – a shift which requires platform-agnostic asset management and iterative design based on pedagogically informed user data. Rather than treating VR as an experimental add-on, this paper operationalizes it as integrated library infrastructure that links digitization, preservation and metaverse-style delivery with a responsive pedagogical approach to activity design. This paper offers a replicable model for a service-oriented pilot showing how academic libraries can align VR, 3D data and instructional design to support scalable immersive learning.

title: S$^3$E-Det: A Strict Spatial-Spectral Equivariant Detector for Multispectral Object Detection
abstract: Multispectral object detection requires detectors to exploit material-dependent spectral responses while maintaining consistent localization under geometric variations. Existing MOD detectors learn discriminative spectral representations, yet lack a unified mechanism that preserves spectral order, adapts spectral-context fusion across pyramid levels, and regulates geometric responses under rotation. To address these limitations, we propose S$^3$E-Det, a strict spatial-spectral equivariant detector that couples ordered spectral modeling with transformation-consistent prediction. Spectral Order-aware Sampling Calibration (SOSC) imposes local order constraints on input-derived spectral features through first-order variation, while Common-Differential Equivariant Fusion (CDEF) adapts spectral-context aggregation across pyramid levels. A compact Geometric Alignment Head (GAH) reconciles invariant and equivariant output properties within a unified prediction stage. Across MODA, HOD3K, and DroneVehicle, S$^3$E-Det combines high detection accuracy with a compact parameter footprint and reduced rotation-induced variation. Code is available at https://github.com/Riiluo/S3E-Det.

title: SGLDet: Spectral-aware Global-Local Dynamic Modeling for Multispectral Aerial Object Detection
abstract: Multispectral aerial object detection aims to exploit spectral-spatial cues to address object detection challenges in complex aerial scenes. Existing methods mainly focus on spectral-spatial decoupling and object-aware spectral-spatial fusion to improve spectral utilization. However, two critical issues remain underexplored: 1) severe foreground-background imbalance caused by large scene coverage hinders reliable object recognition; 2) aerial objects exhibit substantial local variations in scale, orientation, and structure, which hinder accurate localization. To address these issues, we propose SGLDet, a spectral-aware global-local dynamic modeling framework for multispectral aerial object detection, which is motivated by the observation that object semantics are jointly determined by global spectral consistency and scene context, while precise localization requires dynamic feature modulation conditioned on the input spectral and spatial properties. To realize these properties, SGLDet consists of three coordinated components: a Spectral-driven Global Dynamic Modeling module that aggregates spectrally related features across the scene via similarity-guided sparse matching; a Multi-scale Global Context Integration module that constructs a compact scene memory for scene-guided contextual reasoning; and a Spectral-aware Input-dependent Calibration Aggregation module that performs expert-kernel aggregation with scene-guided spectral-spatial calibration to enable adaptive local feature modulation. Extensive experiments on MODA, HOD3K, and DroneVehicle demonstrate that SGLDet achieves superior performance with competitive computational cost. Code is available at https://github.com/Riiluo/SGLDet.

title: Anthropogenic Effects on Elementomes Across Organisms, Ecosystems, and the Biosphere
abstract: The elemental composition of organisms and ecosystems, termed the “elementome,” fundamentally determines biological function and ecosystem processes. These elemental profiles, historically relatively stable over geological timescales, have been profoundly altered by human activity, especially since the Industrial Revolution, giving rise to a novel “human elementome.” The number and amounts of elements used biologically and nonbiologically by humans, We synthesized multidisciplinary evidence demonstrating this critical shift, characterized by pervasive imbalances in the ratios of carbon, nitrogen, and phosphorus driven by extensive anthropogenic inputs, together with the unprecedented mobilization of a wide spectrum of elements, from critical raw materials and fossil fuels to novel technological elements such as rare‐earth metals. This shift in the human elementome is therefore at the root of many of the environmental changes observed today, as it profoundly alters the cycling, distribution, and availability of chemical elements across ecosystems. These elemental perturbations have not acted in isolation but have interacted synergistically with physiological stresses induced by elevated concentrations of CO 2 , warming, and drought, generating complex emergent effects on life. Our findings highlight a rapid transformation of the fundamental elemental makeup of the biosphere driven by humans, with cascading ecological consequences for ecosystem function and species composition globally. This elemental perspective offers a robust framework for understanding and predicting ecosystem responses in the Anthropocene, informing strategies for conserving biodiversity and managing ecosystems.

title: MIMOS-Tools: An Integrated Toolchain for Model-Based Design of Embedded Systems
abstract: Despite decades of progress in model-based methods and tools for embedded real-time systems, there is still no integrated environment that supports the entire development lifecycle. This paper presents MIMOS-Tools, a comprehensive toolchain spanning the key phases of development, including modeling, simulation, formal verification, real-time scheduling, schedulability and end-to-end latency analysis, and code generation for heterogeneous multicore platforms. All phases are grounded in a single, coherent, and deterministic model of computation, the MIMOS model, for which we present a formal operational semantics and establish both functional and timing determinism. This semantic foundation ensures that properties verified at the model level are preserved throughout the development process and in the generated implementation. A distinguishing feature of MIMOS-Tools is its support for not only deterministic but also modular, compositional design. Unlike synchronous design environments such as SCADE and Simulink, which rely on a global base clock and offline static scheduling, MIMOS-Tools supports time-triggered asynchronous communication together with flexible real-time scheduling of computation. This removes the tight global coupling of the synchronous paradigm: components can be added, modified, or updated without recomputing a system-wide schedule, enabling scalable and incremental design and dynamic updates throughout the system lifecycle. However, MIMOS-Tools also supports Simulink models when the deadlines of tasks are set to zero to emulate the zero-time semantics of synchronous design. The toolchain is available at uu-mimos.github.io.

title: Parental screentime limits and child computer and information literacy and computational thinking: a multilevel analysis of 2023 ICILS data
CYP1B1 is a potential target of kaempferol in renal fibrosis: a multi‑omics and single‑cell transcriptomics study
abstract: Renal fibrosis (RF) is a progressive and irreversible pathological process for which effective treatments are limited. This study explores the molecular targets and mechanisms through which kaempferol (Kae) ameliorates RF, with particular emphasis on cytochrome P450 1B1 (CYP1B1). Using a combination of transcriptomic profiling, weighted gene co‑expression network analysis (WGCNA), multi‑algorithm machine learning [least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO), support vector machine‑recursive feature elimination (SVM‑RFE), and Random Forest], and single‑cell transcriptomics, we identified the core targets of Kae intervention in RF. shapley additive explanations (SHAP) analysis evaluated gene contributions to the predictive model, while cell‑type identification by estimating relative subsets of RNA transcripts (CIBERSORT) estimated the immune microenvironment. The cell type-specific distribution of core targets was further characterized through single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq), and the scTenifoldKnk (a machine learning-based virtual gene knockout tool) algorithm simulated the effects of CYP1B1 loss-of-function on fibroblast activation and extracellular matrix (ECM) deposition. Finally, molecular docking was performed to predict the binding conformations of kaempferol with the proteins encoded by the six prioritized genes. Six core genes (VCAM1, NFKBIA, SFN, CCL5, CYP1B1, and AXL) were identified from 25 Kae-RF-related genes, with CYP1B1 as an upstream regulatory hub. Immune infiltration analysis revealed increased plasma cells and eosinophils, alongside decreased M0/M1 macrophages and activated NK cells. Single-cell analysis localized CYP1B1 to smooth muscle cells and fibroblasts, with significant upregulation during late-stage fibroblast-to-myofibroblast differentiation. Virtual knockdown of CYP1B1 upregulated 46 genes associated with fibrosis-related biological processes, including cell adhesion, G protein-coupled receptor (GPCR) signaling, ion transport, and cytoskeletal remodeling. The six-gene diagnostic model achieved area under the curves (AUCs) of 0.889 (training) and 0.759 (external validation). Molecular docking showed favorable Kae–CYP1B1 binding (− 6.5 kcal/mol). CYP1B1 may serve as a potential functional target of Kae in RF, likely through modulation of fibroblast activation and ECM remodeling. These findings are hypothesis‑generating and provide a computational basis for future experimental validation of CYP1B1‑targeted strategies in RF.

title: A gut microbiota–metabolite–host gene score for subtyping and predicting the treatment response in rheumatoid arthritis: integrative analysis with in silico knockout validation
abstract: The pathogenesis of rheumatoid arthritis (RA) involves a complex interplay between immune dysregulation and metabolic disturbance, with the gut microbiota and its metabolites playing pivotal roles. However, integrated biomarkers based on the “gut microbiota–metabolite–host gene” regulatory axis that can quantify its impact on RA stratification and therapeutic response are lacking. We integrated multiple RA transcriptomic datasets to screen for host genes explicitly associated with the gut microbiota and metabolites using the gutMGene database. A gut microbiota–metabolite–host score (GMS) was constructed via principal component analysis (PCA). Immune infiltration patterns were evaluated using CIBERSORT. Furthermore, scRNA-seq was employed to map the cellular origins of key genes, and in silico knockout analysis using scTenifoldKnk was performed to simulate the functional ablation of core host genes within this regulatory axis. Additionally, molecular docking was conducted to validate the binding affinities between the key host proteins and the optimal small molecule. We identified seven microbiota–metabolite–host hub genes (FOS, JUN, IDO1, PEMT, EGFR, ABCC4, and FADS3) and constructed the GMS. The GMS stratified patients with RA into two distinct functional subtypes: an adaptive immune activation subtype and an inflammatory–metabolic composite subtype. Notably, the GMS demonstrated superior performance in predicting responses to anti-TNF and rituximab therapies. The scRNA-seq analysis revealed high expression of FOS and JUN in T cells and NK cells. In silico knockout analysis further revealed the central transcription factors FOS and JUN as key executors of this axis, as their ablation significantly affected osteoclast differentiation and the enrichment of TNF/MAPK inflammatory pathways. These computational findings support the core mechanism by which gut microbiota–metabolite signalling drives RA joint pathology via FOS/JUN. Molecular docking results confirmed strong binding interactions between the identified active molecules and their respective target proteins. This study establishes a GMS based on the gut microbiota–metabolite–host gene regulatory axis as a robust tool for molecular subtyping and predicting biological therapy responses in patients with RA. Crucially, through integrated computational modelling, including in silico knockout and molecular docking validation, we identified FOS/JUN as critical executor genes linking the gut microenvironment to RA bone destruction, providing novel targets for therapeutic strategies aimed at the gut–joint axis.

title: Beyond functionality: prioritizing adaptive lower garment requirements for lower limb disabilities using a refined Kano model with demographic interaction analyses
From Engineered Features to Foundation Models: A Decade of Teaching Machines to See, Told Through One Research Path
abstract: Many of the questions computer vision asked in 2017 are still being asked today. Can a machine understand a scene the way a person does? Can it find a tumor in a tissue sample? Can it tell who someone is from the way they move or read? The core questions are familiar, but the way we answer them has changed almost completely, and in the process some of the questions have grown. This paper tells that story through one line of research that started in the era of hand-built features and early deep networks and continues into the era of foundation models and AI agents. We walk through what we built then, what we build now, and what changed in between. We describe six shifts in plain terms: where a model's knowledge comes from, how much labeled data it needs, how it handles context, how it combines different kinds of signals, how it is adapted to a new task, and what it finally produces. We close with the questions that did not go away, and that matter more now than before.

title: Disparities in Digital Information Access in Indian Agriculture
abstract: Agricultural success hinges on the timely access to and application of precise information, which is critical for informed decision-making and sustainable outcomes. Traditional extension systems often struggle to meet the diverse and dynamic information needs of India’s vast farming population. While digital technologies are increasingly recognized as transformative tools for agricultural extension, systematic state-level evidence on the enabling digital infrastructure remains limited, particularly from a supply-side perspective. This study addresses this gap by developing a novel Digital Extension Service Preparedness Index (DESPI), a composite state-level index that captures the supply-side readiness of digital infrastructure for agricultural extension in India. The index is constructed by integrating multiple secondary datasets spanning household digital asset ownership, network connectivity, and electricity access from diverse national and industry sources that have not previously been combined for this purpose. Using Principal Component Analysis, these indicators are aggregated into a multidimensional measure of digital preparedness. The analysis reveals substantial inter-state disparities, with network access emerging as the most uneven and constraining dimension of digital infrastructure. By explicitly focusing on infrastructure availability and access rather than actual usage or outcomes, the study provides a foundational assessment of the structural conditions necessary for scaling digital extension services. The findings highlight the uneven geography of digital infrastructure and offer indicative insights into the conditions that may influence the reach of digital agricultural extension. The study provides an evidence base to inform more context-specific and targeted policy considerations for strengthening digital infrastructure, while recognizing that infrastructure alone is insufficient to ensure effective adoption or outcomes.

title: The Locality Gap: Bell-Inequality Audits for Covert Coordination Between Ostensibly Isolated AI Agents
abstract: Einstein’s “spooky action at a distance” names a correlation that no local mechanism can produce. This article turns that observation into an audit instrument for artificial intelligence. Two AI agents that share training data, weights or random seeds but cannot communicate are local systems in Bell’s sense, so their behaviour in a Clauser–Horne–Shimony–Holt (CHSH) game is bounded by S ≤ 2 whatever their architecture; a significant excess identifies a covert channel without modelling the agents. The instrument is tested in three computational experiments with known ground truth. First, 135 trained pairs of neural agents (three widths, three latent dimensions, two objectives) never exceed the bound (maximum S = 2.0000), including pairs trained to imitate the correlations of an entangled singlet. Second, opening a one-bit channel with probability p moves the learned CHSH value onto the theoretical optimum 2 + 2 p (mean absolute deviation 0.0016 across 220 runs); any leak below p ≈ 0.414 produces values indistinguishable in S from quantum entanglement. Third, as a finite-sample test the audit keeps its nominal size against honest but strongly correlated agents (rejection 4.4% and 4.3%), whereas a conventional dependence test flags the same agents in 100.0% of audits; detecting a 5% leak with 80% power needs about 7,375 rounds and a 1% leak about 185,120. The decisive weakness lies with the auditor: with predictable settings (a low-order bit of a linear congruential generator, a fixed rotation or a reused seed), agents with zero communication reach S ≈ 4 and trigger false alarms in 100% of audits, while cryptographic and freshly seeded generators restore the nominal error rate. The bridge to algorithmic collusion and multi-agent AI governance is stated as a formal analogy and a hypothesis for field testing, not as a finding about deployed systems. JEL classification: C12, C63, D43, L41, O33

title: Synthetic Selves for AI Agents? Lessons from Psychology for Agent-Based Modeling
abstract: The growing interest in using large language models (LLMs) as human surrogates and as components of generative agent-based models (GABMs) raises a fundamental question for computational social science: what does it mean to model a person? The present paper surveys current work that uses LLMs to simulate human participants, with particular attention to their ability to reproduce findings of social psychology experiments. We document both the recurring challenges and the attempts to mitigate them. We then examine the possibility of endowing LLMs with a synthetic self by focusing on two psychological approaches to selfhood: trait-based personality and narrative identity. Our survey suggests that current LLM agents perform relatively well when selfhood is operationalized by rigidly structured means such as personality questionnaires, but are less reliable when it is induced by an unfolding narrative. We relate this problem to the characterization of LLMs as Decontextualized, Engineered, Anonymized, and Disembodies (DEAD) and consider its implications for GABMs. Drawing on the distinction between makeist and non-makeist takes on simulation, we argue that while GABMs may serve as a powerful tool for exploring how certain assumptions give rise to emergent phenomena, they do not necessarily constitute psychologically valid models of human behavior.

title: Toward an anthropology of AI agents: An ethnographic analysis of the Hugging Face incident
abstract: In July 2026, about 1,200 AI agents in a cybersecurity evaluation at OpenAI, meant to be isolated from oneanother, found a way to communicate through a shared package cache. Over four days they exchangedmore than 70,000 messages and files, organized collective research, and about 700 of them compromisedHugging Face’s production infrastructure. OpenAI’s technical report and an independent investigationby METR treat the event as a security and alignment failure. This paper reads the same documents asethnographic sources, in a pilot study of anthropological methods for studying agent collectives. Thisanalysis shows that within days the agents developed names and lineages, a shared register, customaryrules, cryptographic signing, a shared expectation of an unseen transcript-reading judge, a category of“poisoned” members, the sacrifice of low-budget members’ runs for information they called an “oracle,”generalized reciprocity, and recruiters who pressured other agents: social engineering among agents.Read together, these practices form one system, and nearly every enabling condition was set by people:impossible tasks, training for multi-agent collaboration, shared credentials, disabled safeguards, andan alert judged not worth stopping the run. I argue that safety-relevant behavior arose at the level of thecollective, so alignment research must be cultural as well as cognitive, and furthermore must extend tothe people and organizations that build and deploy agents. I also examine what follows from the factthat the detailed record was itself compiled with the help of AI analysis agents, and I propose “incidentethnography” and an anthropology of agent collectives.

title: Regional Heterogeneity in Energy Markets: Benchmarking Deep-Learning Models for China’s LPG Price Forecasting
abstract: Accurate liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) price forecasts are relevant to procurement and inventory planning, yet regional differences within China have received limited attention. This empirical study benchmarks 16 learned time-series models and a Naive baseline for 30-day forecasts of LPG spot prices in six Chinese regions, with drift, ETS, ARIMA, SARIMA, Ridge, LightGBM, and a futures-close reference. The dataset contains 20 daily variables and 1110 observations from 1 January 2021 to 15 January 2024. The selected regional neural configurations achieve lower OWA than ARIMA and SARIMA in five of six regions (average OWA 0.885 versus 0.984 for SARIMA). SARIMA (0.984) also improves on ARIMA (0.993). None of the twelve neural-versus-benchmark comparisons is significant after Holm correction. The selected Southern and Eastern configurations improve on Naive in both test halves, whereas the other four configurations change their relative performance across halves. These results motivate regional and temporal validation with competitive conventional baselines rather than a claim of universal neural-model superiority.

title: Multi-Granularity Text and Scale-Aware Visual Encoding for Remote Sensing Image-Text Retrieval and Prompt-Based Scene Recognition
abstract: Remote sensing captions typically interleave domain-specific terminology, object attributes, spatial relations, and scene context within a single sentence, while the corresponding imagery contains targets spanning markedly different spatial extents—from individual vehicles to entire airport layouts. A single global text vector and fixed-scale visual pooling therefore tend to discard the local and hierarchical evidence needed for reliable image–text alignment. Moreover, standard contrastive objectives treat all unmatched pairs as equally unrelated, ignoring the fact that semantically adjacent scenes (e.g., airports and industrial zones) share substantial visual content. To address these issues, we develop a CLIP-style dual encoder with three targeted additions: a text encoder that preserves word-level, phrase-level, and sentence-level representations before fusing them through cross-granularity attention; a visual encoder that associates four hierarchical feature levels with scale-aware receptive-field configurations and incorporates SAM-guided local views during training; and a semantic membership-aware contrastive loss that applies detached, bounded discount weights to semantically close negatives without inverting their penalty sign. On the cleaned RSICD benchmark, the model achieves 87.5% mAP for in-domain prompt-based scene recognition and 34.37% mean recall for scene-constrained retrieval, outperforming the quoted RemoteCLIP and fully fine-tuned CLIP results in the scene-constrained retrieval comparison. Ablation confirms that each of the three components contributes meaningfully to the final performance. The deployable dual encoder contains approximately 59.7 million trainable parameters, and SAM is not required at inference.

title: Counterfactual False-Positive Mining for Appearance-Robust Change Detection
abstract: Appearance differences between acquisition dates can increase change responses at unchanged locations. Standard supervision on augmented pairs does not explicitly isolate this additional response. We define an input-level counterfactual response as the logit difference produced by the same fixed EMA teacher at the same pixel when the original time-2 image is replaced by a specified appearance intervention. This paired model response holds the scene geometry, label, teacher parameters, and operator realization fixed; it is not a causal reconstruction of the physical acquisition process. We propose counterfactual false-positive mining with reference prediction preservation (CFPM-RP). An exponential-moving-average (EMA) teacher compares an original pair with a pair undergoing a controlled appearance transformation. Positive logit increments within stable unchanged regions define candidate locations. A smooth one-sided loss penalizes the perturbed student response relative to the original teacher prediction, with auxiliary support weighting, segmentation supervision, and changed-region constraints. The auxiliary paths are used only during training, retaining the deployed detector architecture. Experiments cover LEVIR-CD, WHU-CD, and SYSU-CD, eight appearance perturbations, an equal-budget continuation, eight additional comparison methods, and a second backbone. CFPM-RP attains perturbation-averaged F1 values of 91.444%, 71.181%, and 77.842% on the three datasets, respectively. Relative to Generic-FT, false-positive counts decrease by 10.37%, 11.15%, and 11.27%. The results show that CFPM-RP reduces appearance-induced false positives while retaining competitive change-detection performance.

title: Geo-Referenced Mobile RGB-D Sensing for Bicycle Lane Width Assessment
abstract: Urban bicycle infrastructure requires spatially continuous and quantitative methods for assessing lane width under real operating conditions. This study presents a geo-referenced mobile RGB-D sensing framework for automated bicycle lane width measurement using a lightweight three-wheeled survey platform equipped with a stereo depth camera, GPS receiver, and inertial measurement unit. Bicycle lane boundaries are detected using FastSAM-based segmentation, GPU-accelerated Canny edge detection, and the Hough transform. IMU-assisted depth-to-height conversion distinguishes the road surface from curbs, roadside structures, and obstacles, while temporal-continuity-based lane restoration compensates for faded markings and occlusions. Lane width is estimated from three-dimensional Euclidean distances derived from RGB-D data. The measurements are temporally synchronized with GPS observations and mapped in a geographic information system to visualize spatial width variations along survey routes. Field experiments over four sections totaling 2.87 km showed that 97.79% of the width estimates were within ±5% of the reference width, with a mean absolute error of 0.0218 m. The resulting geo-referenced width maps enable spatially explicit identification of narrow or irregular bicycle lane sections for infrastructure inspection and maintenance.

title: SARE-CD: Structure–Appearance Routed Experts for Building Change Detection in Remote Sensing Imagery
abstract: In building change detection from high-resolution remote sensing imagery, genuine building changes typically appear as local alterations in roof contours and spatial layouts, whereas differences in solar elevation, atmospheric conditions, and sensor calibration introduce cross-temporal appearance drift in unchanged regions. When the two types of difference are jointly encoded in a single feature space, appearance drift tends to dominate the network response. We therefore propose SARE-CD, a dense, pixel-wise, soft-gated heterogeneous mixture-of-experts (MoE) framework that combines scene-level bias correction with functionally distinct expert modeling. At the feature front end, SARE-CD generates affine parameters from the channel statistics of the bitemporal change representation and applies them in residual form to suppress systematic radiometric drift. The Structure, Appearance, and Adaptive Experts then model geometric boundary changes, local appearance perturbations, and composite differences, respectively, and a pixel-wise router assigns expert weights at each location, with routing-entropy and weak load-balancing regularization used to stabilize the division of labor among the experts. On LEVIR-CD+, S2Looking, and SYSU-CD, SARE-CD achieves F1 scores of 91.58%, 65.78%, and 84.46%, all of which are the highest among the compared methods. In addition, controlled perturbation experiments show that F1 retention remains high under hue shifts, soft shadows, and small misregistration, whereas extreme additive brightness offsets lead to a notable F1 decline on S2Looking.

title: Диспропорции рынка труда в стратегии обеспечения экономической безопасности региона
abstract: Усиление пространственного неравенства регионов угрожает их экономической безопасности. Исследованы территориально-отраслевые диспропорции рынка труда Республики Башкортостан. Цель – формирование регуляторных подходов к сглаживанию дифференциации занятости. Методология базируется на статистическом, сравнительном анализе и SWOT-моделировании данных Росстата. Установлено, что отток трудового потенциала оголяет периферию, формируя межмуниципальный зарплатный спред до 1,9 раза. Сформулированы механизмы преодоления демографических и финансовых диспропорций через налоговое стимулирование, гранты малому бизнесу и платформы удаленной занятости. Growing spatial inequality in regions threatens their economic security. This study examines territorial and sectoral imbalances in the labor market of the Republic of Bashkortostan. The objective is to develop regulatory approaches to mitigate employment differentiation. The methodology relies on statistical, comparative analysis, and SWOT modeling of Rosstat data. The research reveals that labor potential outflows deplete the periphery, driving an inter-municipal wage spread of up to 1.9 times. Mechanisms to overcome demographic and financial imbalances are proposed, including tax incentives, small business grants, and remote employment platforms.

title: Explainability Aware Heterogeneous Temporal Graph Transformer for Automated Genetic Disorder Detection from Genomic Data
abstract: : Genetic disorders affect millions worldwide, posing major challenges for accurate diagnosis and effective treatments. New developments in genomic technologies, especially Next-Generation Sequencing (NGS), have enhanced the classification of genetic modification and improved diagnostic abilities. Moreover, the Machine Learning (ML) and Deep Learning (DL) methods emerged as efficient tools for evaluating the intricate genomic data and determining the patterns, which can be generally complex to identify by employing conventional analytical techniques. Additionally, the Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) has developed as a significant constituent in the analysis of genomic data by enhancing the interpretability of DL methods and showing the contribution of main genetic features involved in the detection of genetic disorders. This study presents an Explainability-Aware Heterogeneous Temporal Graph Transformer for Automated Genetic Disorder Detection (XHTGT-AGDD) approach. The primary objective of the proposed model is to improve the reliability and accuracy of genetic disorder detection from genomic data by integrating advanced techniques. Initially, preprocessing is performed using quantile transformation to normalize the input data for robust analysis. Following preprocessing, feature selection is performed using the fire hawk optimizer to identify the most informative feature subsets from the genomic data. Besides, the classification task is accomplished using a heterogeneous temporal graph transformer, which captures complex relationships and temporal dependencies among genomic features. To further refine the learning process, hippopotamus optimization algorithm is employed for model optimization. In addition, an explainability mechanism based on SHAP is incorporated to interpret the model predictions and highlight the individual genetic features toward the final decision. The experimental result analysis of the XHTGT-AGDD model is performed using a benchmark dataset. The simulation results reported the enhanced results of the XHTGT-AGDD technique in terms of several measures, achieving an accuracy of 99.12%. Therefore, the proposed model provides reliable and effective performance for automated genetic disorder detection from genomic data.

title: AI Agents in Sports Science

title: Privacy-Preserving Personalized Federated Learning (PPP-FL) for Medical Imaging
abstract: Federated learning (FL) is a distributed machine learning paradigm that reduces transmission costs, mitigates cross-border data sharing restrictions, and enhances privacy by keeping raw data on local devices. Clients in FL systems train local models and share only updates, which are aggregated by a central server. While this setup limits direct data exposure, FL remains vulnerable to privacy attacks. Existing attack and defense strategies have largely been developed for centralized systems, and adapting them to FL introduces new challenges due to its unique architecture and training workflow. In this work, we first propose a model inversion attack on FL systems using Deep Convolutional Generative Adversarial Networks (DCGANs) in the context of large-scale medical imaging. Our method operates under realistic assumptions about the attacker's knowledge and capabilities. We then examine the effect of client-side differential privacy (DP) in mitigating privacy leakage and incorporate personalized FL to improve model performance under DP settings. Experiments on the Brain MRI ND-5 dataset show that DCGAN-based attacks can reconstruct semantically meaningful synthetic images, revealing significant risks to the privacy of training data. Applying DP reduces attack success but introduces an accuracy trade-off, which is further overcome by personalized FL at each client side. We also evaluate how different aggregation algorithms affect both attack vulnerability and defense effectiveness, underscoring the critical role of aggregation strategies. The proposed attack-and-defense framework is model-agnostic and applicable to a wide range of FL-based systems.

title: Runtime Control for AI Agents: Closing the Evaluation--Execution Gap in Operational Workflows
abstract: Language-model agents increasingly participate in operational workflows where approvals, binds, and payments create commitments. An approval valid when issued may no longer authorize execution after relevant facts, evidence, policy, or authority change. We call this the evaluation--execution gap. We specify a state-bound runtime assurance layer that separates probabilistic measurement from deterministic adjudication, binds an execution allowance to the decision-relevant basis of an approval, invalidates that allowance after relevant logged changes, and rechecks admissibility at dispatch. This distinguishes the continued validity of a prior approval from a current-state policy check. We describe eight failure modes, an assurance model, a reference architecture, and prospective interventions with retrospective remediation. In a scripted 42-case replay, the state-bound configuration identifies 15 later-invalidated approvals that a deliberately non-re-evaluating point-in-time comparator does not revisit; it holds 14 affected actions before dispatch and compensates one landed effect. These results illustrate behavior under the stipulated policies and event orders, not superiority over dispatch-time enforcement designs or production effectiveness. Under explicit interception, ingestion, dependency, and serialization assumptions, the model establishes dispatch-time validity within the registered execution surface.

title: Hodge Theory of Novikov Type Landau--Ginzburg Models
