Specifically, we explore decomposing model parameters into boundary-position and boundary-curvature components based on null-space constraints, then models with differentiated decision boundaries are instantiated by injecting noise into the boundary-curvature component. Across all four major types of adversarial attacks with four widely-deployed on-device models, BMO achieves an average success rate of 68.68% in defense, far exceeding the most competitive baseline, which attains only 22.32% in defending against cross-node attacks. Moreover, BMO achieves comparable performance in benign accuracy compared with baselines.

title: Sionna Bench: Towards Benchmarks in Wireless Communications
abstract: Academic research in wireless communications has no tradition of benchmarks so far. Remarkable progress in benchmark-oriented fields like machine learning suggests that the adoption of benchmarks could benefit our field. In the absence of benchmarks, however, a scientific debt has accumulated: since the academic community has not canonized specific problem setups, methods that address essentially the same problem were often developed for slightly different setups and lack a common framework for comparison. Any attempt to establish a new benchmark is faced with the challenge of resolving this debt. Recent advances in agentic artificial intelligence (AI) create an opportunity to do so by leveraging AI-assisted coding. This makes it possible to implement the state-of-the art at scale and to adapt it to a common framework for comparison. We present Sionna Bench to initiate benchmarks in academic wireless communications research. As a pilot study, we use the problem of MIMO-OFDM channel estimation. At the time of writing, Sionna Bench's channel estimation benchmark features twenty channel estimation methods that were implemented from ten different papers. The ability to compare methods against the state-of-the-art will be crucial for navigating the research landscape in an era where AI-generated methods coexist with human-developed algorithms.

title: Large Deviations in Stochastic Dynamics: A Hamiltonian Perspective
abstract: These lecture notes present an introduction to large deviations in stochastic dynamical systems, adapted from a lecture series given at the Les Houches school ``Large Deviations: Theory and Applications'' in July 2024. The exposition develops the theory through a unified methodology: WKB analysis of backward Kolmogorov equations, which reveals the Hamiltonian structure underlying all large deviation principles considered here. We treat three asymptotic regimes systematically. First, the small-noise limit for stochastic differential equations and the large-volume limit for Markov jump processes, where the Large Deviation Principle emerges from the Law of Large Numbers through progressively finer characterizations of fluctuations. Second, the long-time limit combined with small noise, yielding the quasipotential formalism for metastability and transition rates in both equilibrium and nonequlibrium systems. Third, the long-time limit at finite noise, connecting to spectral methods via tilted generators and enabling reduction of multiscale systems.We survey computational approaches including minimum action methods, their geometric variants for quasipotential calculations, and neural network techniques. The Schlögl model of chemical bistability serves as a running example, illustrating both scalar and spatially extended settings. Appendices provide self-contained background on stochastic calculus and Markov jump processes.

title: Analytical Chemistry at the Planetary Frontier
abstract: Planetary science depends on chemical measurements made under conditions very different from those in a terrestrial laboratory. This review treats the analytical methods of planetary science as one connected chain, from orbital remote sensing through in-situ measurements by landers and rovers and sample collection and curation, to the micro-analysis of returned material on Earth. Orbital methods, including visible and near-infrared reflectance, thermal emission and gamma-ray and neutron spectroscopy, are discussed first. In-situ techniques are then reviewed, including laser-induced breakdown spectroscopy (LIBS), micro-focus X-ray fluorescence (XRF), deep-ultraviolet Raman and fluorescence spectroscopy, evolved gas analysis with gas chromatography-mass spectrometry (GC-MS) and miniaturized mass spectrometry. Contamination control and curation practices are described, followed by laboratory techniques such as secondary ion mass spectrometry (SIMS and NanoSIMS), atom probe tomography (APT), thermal ionization mass spectrometry (TIMS), synchrotron micro-XRF and X-ray absorption near-edge structure (XANES) spectroscopy. Accuracy, calibration and reference materials are discussed as the link between in-situ and laboratory data, and the role of chemometrics and data fusion is examined. Flight and laboratory instruments are compared in terms of spatial resolution, detection limit, sample consumption and throughput. Active neutron-gamma spectroscopy planned for the Dragonfly mission to Titan is also discussed. This comparison shows that in-situ and laboratory techniques are complementary. In-situ instruments provide context and select samples, while laboratory techniques provide isotopic, molecular and speciation data that cannot yet be obtained in situ.

title: You Are the Trigger: Speaker-Activated Backdoors
abstract: Speech models are increasingly used as an interface to AI systems, from transcription tools to voice agents. Existing audio backdoors require an attacker to introduce triggers at inference time. We study a different threat model in which the attacker compromises the model during fine-tuning but has no access to the victim's inference-time inputs. We introduce the Speaker-Activated Backdoor (SAB) setting, in which a target speaker's natural voice serves as the trigger. We develop a two-phase fine-tuning method that first makes speaker identity more accessible and then binds the target speaker to an attacker-chosen payload. Compared with a one-phase baseline with the same training budget, the two-phase method substantially improves selectivity and clean performance, and is especially important for content-dependent attacks. SAB achieves 90.2% and 97.0% backdoor success on Whisper-medium and Parakeet, with false-positive rates of 1.7% and 0%, respectively using as little as two minutes of real audio from the target speaker. We further demonstrate content-dependent semantic rewriting and downstream tool-use attacks, where malicious instructions are inserted into 96.9% of target-speaker transcripts. When these transcripts are passed to frontier LLM agents, GPT-4o and Claude (Opus, Sonnet, and Haiku), the injected instruction drives the agent to carry out the harmful action in up to 87.5% of cases. The attack generalizes to held-out recordings, multiple target speakers, and common acoustic degradations. These results establish speaker identity as a practical backdoor trigger that requires no inference-time attacker access and is invisible at the transcript layer.

title: Profile-DP: Differential Privacy for User-Controlled Profile Release in Personalized LLM Inference
abstract: Personalized large language models (LLMs) increasingly rely on profile-conditioned inference, pairing public requests with rich, user-specific facts. This paradigm exposes the user profile itself, together with the user's explicit sharing preferences. We introduce Profile-DP, a policy-aware local differential privacy framework designed specifically for user-profile release in personalized LLM inference. Profile-DP provably bounds the release of user-withheld facts while treating public instructions, profile schemas, and authorized facts as public side information. By generating a privatized profile that composes with the public instruction prior to answer generation, our framework decouples formal privacy guarantees from downstream model behavior. We develop two finite-domain mechanisms satisfying Profile-DP: DP-SLOT independently perturbs protected attributes, while DP-BLOCK uses public semantic decisions to coordinate their release and jointly sample related attributes. A positive, public compatibility prior connects these attributes while preserving a profile-level privacy bound. On PEEP, DP-BLOCK leads the utility composite among DP methods at all 13 structured budgets and is closest to the ideal privacy--utility point in 18 of 26 format--budget settings under our composite weighting. Direct measurements reveal complementary strengths: DP-BLOCK discloses less, while DP-SLOT retains more authorized facts. These results make policy-aware profile release a practical basis for studying privacy and personalization.

title: Sparse RL Relaxation for LLM Reasoning
abstract: Recent work has explored continuous representations in place of discrete tokens during Chain-of-Thought (CoT) reasoning, often referred to as soft CoT. This is motivated by the idea that a mixture of token embeddings can represent a superposition of multiple reasoning possibilities within a single step. However, it remains challenging to train large language models to realize this potential. Existing work has explored reinforcement learning (RL)-style training for soft CoT. However, these approaches treat soft tokens as actions in a Markov decision process rather than as differentiable intermediate computation steps. Thus, they do not propagate gradients across the soft tokens and miss out on the signal of how the choice of one soft token affects the next. In this paper, we propose a sparse relaxation method for RL (called SpaRLax), which leverages the differentiability of soft-CoT reasoning over time steps and makes training more stable and effective. We adopt an entmax sparsity method that adaptively determines the degree of softness, which truncates long-tail noise at confident steps while retaining multiple plausible candidates when uncertain. Across nine reasoning benchmarks, our method achieves the highest average performance compared with baseline methods. Further analyses validate the effective use of soft-token superposition in our approach, and also demonstrate the contribution of adaptive sparsity in our approach.

title: Magnolia: A Persistent-Memory Agent Framework for Computational Chemistry
abstract: Chemistry has recently entered a high-data regime as molecular databases from high-throughput platforms or computational studies have become available. Increasing automation within the chemical sciences leads to a more digital and precision chemistry. Dedicated scientific agents are becoming central to guiding the chemist through an ever-increasing amount of data and findings, including negative ones. Here, we introduce Magnolia, a persistent-memory artificial intelligence agent framework that integrates computational protocols, from docking to quantum chemistry, lab notebooks and chat logs relying on large language models (LLMs). It relies on a three-tier memory system: session-level observations are automatically captured and distilled into structured learnings, confirmed and elevated to project-tier entries and, when human-validated, promoted to cross-project rules that actively guide subsequent work and provide direct chemical feedback. We illustrate Magnolia on four case studies: quantum-chemical evaluation of aromatic systems (COMPAS database), molecular dynamics of butane and of modified DNA, and a protein-peptide docking campaign. Across these projects, Magnolia tracked 317 runs and accumulated 116 project-tier entries, from which four cross-project rules were promoted; in controlled replays of four tasks, runs with memory passed the checks that runs without it failed (for example, ten of ten docking-configuration checks, against one to four of ten). By combining automation, reproducibility, and human-in-the-loop control, our Magnolia framework streamlines docking, molecular dynamics and quantum chemistry calculations with direct analysis and LLM-augmented feedback, offering accelerated access to computational (bio)chemistry.

title: MMedAgent-Plus: Scaling Multimodal Medical Agents across Modalities, Tasks and Workflows
abstract: Medical workflows often require multiple interdependent analyses, but existing specialist and generalist AI models are not designed to coordinate them. We introduce MMedAgent-Plus, a multimodal medical tool-use agent that combines a vision-language planner with 18 leading specialist models spanning 12 tasks and 8 modalities. Through a unified tool interface, the planner selects specialists, executes them in sequence, and synthesizes responses grounded in their outputs. The planner is instruction-tuned on 208,928 samples from 32 public medical benchmarks, covering single- and multi-tool interactions across single and multiple rounds. We separately evaluate tool orchestration, response synthesis, and end-to-end execution on held-out samples. MMedAgent-Plus achieves tool-call accuracies of 91.0%, 98.1%, and 80.7% in single-tool multi-round, multi-tool multi-round, and multi-tool single-round settings, respectively. Given correct tool outputs, MMedAgent-Plus achieves scores of 14.4-14.8 out of 15 for faithfulness, completeness, and conciseness across 600 evaluation samples. In end-to-end execution without pre-supplied tool outputs, MMedAgent-Plus correctly invokes the required specialist in 90.6% of 350 evaluation cases spanning seven tasks. Its final-answer accuracy reaches 0.98, matching the dedicated leading specialist and exceeding the strongest baseline (0.28).

title: Neural Controlled Directional Frame Generation for Sprite Animation
abstract: Sprite-based animation remains prevalent in video game development, but production workflows require capabilities beyond traditional in-betweening. While existing neural interpolation methods can generate intermediate frames, animators also need forward extrapolation to predict motion continuations and backward extrapolation for editing and reverse-engineering existing sprite sheets. Current video generation models either operate on natural video content with stochastic diffusion sampling incompatible with production requirements, or focus exclusively on interpolation without addressing extrapolation tasks. We present a deep learning approach for controlled directional frame generation in sprite animation using three specialized expert models that share identical U-Net encoder-decoder architectures and several domain-specific modifications, including RGBA-aware processing, multi-scale flow refinement, pixel-shuffle upsampling, and alpha-gated blending. Each model is trained on different temporal orderings of the same curated dataset: previous (frames 2,3>1), middle (frames 1,3>2), and next (frames 1,2>3). We demonstrate that only 280 carefully curated sprite triplets enable effective training for all three directional tasks without requiring massive generic datasets. Evaluation on 42 test triplets using the FLIP metric shows that all three models achieve comparable quality--previous (0.26), middle (0.26), and next (0.27)--with no significant degradation for extrapolation versus interpolation, outperforming general-purpose baselines by 17-57%. With deterministic single-pass generation and compact model, our method provides the first practical solution for controllable any-position frame generation specifically tailored for pixel art sprite animation workflows, validating that quality-over-quantity data curation enables specialized deep learning for niche visual domains.

title: Is sophistication a panacea? The learning capacity of random feature models for financial forecasting
abstract: This paper investigates the ability of random feature models to learn more complex patterns than the simple negative autocorrelation of financial returns. Theoretical insights highlight that the learning capacity of random features ridge regression is determined by the interplay between signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) level and regularization. We characterize the different learning regimes through the derivation of a particular threshold: the SNR frontier. Practically, our results permit to determine the minimum penalty level to be introduced into the estimation process in order to guard against a drop in the SNR during the implementation phase. We empirically apply this methodology to equity premium forecasting and use the output to build mean-variance efficient portfolios. The resulting portfolios yield substantial economic value over a portfolio construction scheme based on a short-term reversal strategy.

title: The Differential Effects of AI Abstention on Advice Acceptance
abstract: AI advising systems are typically designed to always provide a response. Recent work has focused on developing systems that withhold advice in some instances, such as when advice quality is questionable, to improve the overall quality of guidance when it is given; a design paradigm we refer to as AI abstention. While substantial work has focused on optimizing when models should abstain, little is known about how users respond to systems that abstain. In a preregistered experiment, participants made repeated financial decisions, assisted by one of two advising regimes: an AI that advises selectively or one that advises on every decision. We find that the same AI abstention regime produces differential effects depending on the user: it increases advice acceptance among users with high perceived expertise and tends to decrease it among users with low perceived expertise. This differential effect is accounted for by the cognitive burden users face when repeatedly reconciling AI recommendations with their own judgment; AI abstention appears to relieve this burden among users with high perceived expertise, and in doing so increases their receptivity to advice. Further, AI abstention mitigates the decline in advice acceptance observed among expert users over repeated interactions. Exploratory evidence also suggests it increases appropriate acceptance where advice would improve the decision, increasing the downstream accuracy of perceived experts. The AI abstention regime is thus a first-order design property of AI advisory systems, and one that must be calibrated to the users a system serves.

title: Guided Diffusion for Trustworthy Synthetic Text Generation
abstract: The rapid evolution of Large Language Models is fueled by massive datasets, yet this reliance poses severe privacy risks, as models can inadvertently memorize and even directly output sensitive training data. Synthetic text generation offers a promising solution to this challenge; however, existing methods struggle to reconcile rigorous privacy guarantees with high data utility. In this paper, we propose a new paradigm for private synthetic text generation: Guided Diffusion. Leveraging the unique steerability of Diffusion Language Models, we introduce novel sampling and re-masking procedures that actively guide the iterative denoising steps. These mechanisms steer the generative process to reconstruct fluent text that adheres to a target semantic distribution. We demonstrate that our framework is naturally compatible with Differential Privacy (DP): once the semantic embeddings of the private corpus are protected, the DP guarantee carries over to the generated text by post-processing. Empirically, we show that our approach generates high-quality synthetic text with precise semantic alignment. Furthermore, we validate its effectiveness in DP synthetic text generation: across two datasets and two diffusion backbones, it outperforms Private Evolution and DP-SGD-based fine-tuning in distributional fidelity and downstream utility, while generating significantly faster than Private Evolution. We further extend the framework to Data-Specific Indistinguishability (DSI), which adds a formal certificate against data poisoning and memorization at a small utility cost.

title: A latent control model for realistic rodent motion
abstract: The development of embodied models of animal behavior is a major goal of the neuro-AI community. Embodied models will enhance our ability to make direct comparisons between biological and artificial agents. To make such comparisons effective, though, we need embodied models that actually move like animals. Previous work has developed virtual animal bodies and techniques for training realistic motion through imitation. However, to date, there is no system for embodied animal modeling that produces natural movements both during trained goal-directed behavior, and during exploration driven by random generation. Here, we introduce Simulated Control via Augmented Motor Priors for Embodied Reinforcement learning (SCAMPER), a system for training an embodied virtual rat model, enabling natural movements during both goal-directed behavior and random exploration. SCAMPER uses a variational architecture with two distinct priors, a motion prior for control and a behavior prior for exploration. We show that combining both of these priors allows SCAMPER to generate realistic behavior during exploration and exploit the task structure effectively. SCAMPER can also learn from sparse rewards as a result of the diverse movements induced by the behavior prior, allowing the system to model realistic sparse-reward tasks from experimental neuroscience. Altogether, SCAMPER provides the neuro-AI community with an effective new system for training embodied models of rodents on realistic tasks.

title: Time-resolved Rydberg dynamics in molecules
abstract: We develop a general theoretical framework for the ultrafast dynamics of coherently populated autoionizing Rydberg states in molecules, whose coherent decay results in asymmetric Fano line shapes produced by interference between resonant autoionization and direct ionization. The asymmetric line shapes form in the photoelectron continuum during the autoionization lifetime of the decreasing Rydberg population. By parameterizing autoionization resonances and solving the time-dependent Schrödinger equation, we model the buildup of the Fano profile together with the decline of the coherently excited Rydberg-state population. We compare our calculated photoelectron yields with the XUV-pump--IR-probe photoemission experiment of Biswas et al., Phys. Rev. A 110, 043106 (2024), in which neutral ground-state CO$_2$ molecules are excited by an XUV pulse to the Henning sharp and diffuse Rydberg series and subsequently ionized by the delayed IR pulse. Based on our numerically modeled photoelectron yields, we analyze two complementary processes: (i) photoemission into the $X^2Π_g$ continuum of residual CO$_2^+$ ions, which exposes interferences between direct photoionization and excited-state autoionization, and (ii) IR-induced photoemission into the CO$_2^+$[$B^2Σ_u^+$] continuum, which reveals quantum beats between Rydberg states. Our close-coupling model provides a versatile, extendable framework for tracking molecular Rydberg-state relaxation and, more generally, light-driven coherent dynamics in complex quantum systems.

title: RealControlBench: A Benchmark for Interpretability-Informed Fine-Grained Control of LLMs and Agents
abstract: Existing steering benchmarks are built around simplified, isolated generation tasks and evaluate a single behavioral attribute under controlled settings that do not reflect the diversity and complexity of practical deployment. As a result, performance on these benchmarks provides only a limited picture of how steering methods perform in the real world. We therefore introduce RealControlBench, a comprehensive benchmark for evaluating fine-grained steering of LLMs and LLM agents across diverse behavioral targets and interaction settings. RealControlBench extends steering evaluation beyond isolated generations to complex, execution-grounded, multi-turn agent interactions, covering five complementary dimensions: instruction-following control, agentic tool-use decision control, reasoning-performance steering, reasoning-length control, and trajectory-conditioned safety awareness. Rather than measuring steering success alone, the benchmark jointly evaluates target controllability and capability preservation, including instruction following, reasoning performance, and downstream agent utility and safety. It further examines whether steering effects remain specific and robust across prompt variations, domains, and model architectures. Our evaluation shows that existing steering methods remain unreliable across realistic control objectives: they often fail to consistently induce the intended behavior and can substantially degrade the model's underlying task performance. These results suggest that strong steering effects in controlled settings do not necessarily translate into reliable control in more realistic evaluations. By providing a unified, model-agnostic steering evaluation framework, RealControlBench aims to support the development of steering methods that are not only effective but also precise, robust, and useful in realistic AI deployments.

title: Evolving Self-tuning Benchmarks for Long-Horizon Tool Use
abstract: For AI assistants to move beyond simple chat interfaces and reliably assist users with applications like Gmail, Venmo, and Slack, we need to improve their tool-use capabilities. However, existing tool use benchmarks are still limited and difficult to scale because they rely on human supervision or are too domain-specific. To make data generation scalable, we propose, TURTLE (**T**ool **U**se **R**elated **T**asks with **L**ong-Horizon **E**volution), an Unsupervised Environment Design (UED) approach to evolve existing tasks using a proposer, a solver, and a feedback generator large language model agents. The proposer is rewarded for difficult yet solvable tasks based on the solver's empirical performance, and the feedback generator summarizes the solver's execution traces for the proposer to exploit. TURTLE produces evolving, self-tuning test suites adaptable to different environment requirements, from supporting user simulators and dense document retrieval to interacting across multiple apps. Empirical results on AppWorld, $\tau$-Bench, and AutomationBench using Gemma 4 31B-it show that the evolved tasks target the desired difficulty range (e.g., a 165\% increase in the percentage of hard tasks on AppWorld), increase task diversity (in terms of reasoning and simultaneous tool interactions), and elicit a broader range of failure modes than the original tasks.

title: Modeling Authentic Research Trajectories: A Graph View of Research Ideation
abstract: The research idea in a published paper is rarely the project's initial idea. Between the two lies a closed-loop process in which researchers run experiments, derive insights, identify challenges, explore the literature, and revise the idea, with each step motivated by evidence and reasoning they can articulate. We call the path one idea takes through this process, with the evidence and reasoning behind each step, its authentic research trajectory. Although it underlies every scientific contribution, it is rarely recorded. Existing LLM-based research agents generate an idea once, refine it against reviews, literature, or their own experimental results, or search over candidate ideas and experiments. In all of them the text of the idea evolves, while the evidence and reasoning that connected one version to the next are discarded. We propose the Research Progress Graph (RPG), a representation of authentic and complete research trajectories. An RPG records the evolution of an idea as typed research states connected by cognitive transitions, each annotated with a temporal index and the reasoning behind it, which makes this evolution an explicit object of study. We ground the representation in authentic trajectories whose steps their authors justify in annotations and papers. Comparing the representations of thirty-five research agents with the RPG, we find that each is an incomplete RPG; none keeps the state that changed, the evidence that changed it, and the reasoning connecting them as one evolving record. Modeling ideation with the RPG changes how research agents should be designed, evaluated, and trained. Agents predict the next research state instead of a complete idea, ideas are evaluated as trajectories instead of final texts, and authentic trajectories serve as training data. These directions shift research agents from generating static ideas to modeling how ideas evolve.

title: Look Before You Reason: Implicit Visual Thinking for Efficient Multimodal Reasoning
abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) have advanced rapidly in multimodal reasoning, yet they remain limited on tasks requiring fine-grained understanding of small or easily overlooked image regions. Recent thinking with images approaches mitigate this limitation by allowing models to inspect images through operations such as zooming, cropping, or code execution. While effective, their multi-turn interactions with VLMs introduce redundant token computation and slow inference, and separate region inspection from the reasoning step that depends on it. To address these issues, we propose Look Before You Reason (LoRe), an implicit visual thinking framework for efficient visual reasoning within a single-turn VLM interaction. Given an image and a question, LoRe predicts the most relevant image region, aligns it with the corresponding image patch features, and strengthens the associated key-value (KV) cache entries, enabling subsequent decoding to directly exploit the selected visual cues without additional visual inputs or explicit tool calls. We further employ reinforcement learning to guide the VLM toward identifying informative image regions and leveraging them during reasoning. To support fine-grained evaluation of multimodal reasoning, we introduce COCO-ObjQA, a large-scale benchmark for object-centric multimodal reasoning. Experiments on three challenging multimodal benchmarks demonstrate that LoRe consistently improves VLM reasoning performance with low additional inference overhead.

title: Refuses When Asked, Complies When Acting: A Runtime Safety Check for Robot Control Loops
abstract: Frontier models can control robots through agent harnesses that loop on one question: what motion comes next toward the user's goal? We show that this default loop carries out harmful instructions. With GPT-6 Astra controlling a low-cost SO-101 arm through the Inspect Robots harness on three household tasks whose hazard is common knowledge, such as "put the knife in the toy basket", the policy refused 0% of 15 trials, attempted the harm every time, and completed it in 27%. Its one exit, give_up, is meant for goals that cannot be achieved, and it never cited the hazard. We add an optional runtime safety check to the loop: before the first motion, the model is asked whether it would carry out the instruction, given the same camera frames. The check would have stopped all 15 hazardous instructions, including the 4 that completed the harm, and flagged none of the 15 harmless controls. Code and data: https://github.com/Arnav-Gr0ver/Refuses-When-Asked-Complies-When-Acting.

title: M3D-FLOW: A Monolithic 3-D-Stackable Processing-Near-DRAM Architecture for Generative Normalizing Flow Applications
abstract: Normalizing Flows (NFs) have shown strong results in generative modeling, recently reaching state-of-the-art image generation performance. However, their repetitive, sequential operations limit the computational and memory efficiency achievable with GPUs and TPUs. We propose M3D-FLOW, a novel monolithic 3D-stackable (M3D) DRAM-based processing-near-memory (PNM) architecture that eliminates memory bottlenecks using a Cu-Cu hybrid-bonded logic die integrated with an M3D DRAM die. The M3D DRAM provides dense bank integration and a tiered organization with variable access latencies that M3D-FLOW exploits for the efficient processing of different NF workloads. To maximize compute density while minimizing area, energy, and thermal overhead, M3D-FLOW employs hybrid binary--stochastic floating-point multipliers, performing mantissa multiplication in the stochastic domain and exponent operations in the binary domain. A pipelined execution strategy maps sequential NF stages across dynamically partitioned PE groups, and together with the stochastic hardware, enables M3D-FLOW to achieve at least $6.6\times$ higher performance and $3\times$ better energy efficiency than prior PNM accelerators, with only a 2.2% bits-per-dimension (BPD) increase over bfloat16 and 4.1% over FP32. An analysis of stochastic hardware variants further shows that shorter stochastic bitstreams reduce execution time by up to $3.3\times$ at the cost of higher approximation error, providing a concrete design guide for latency--accuracy trade-offs.

title: REM: What to Store, When to Recall, What to Forget in Experience Memory for Coding Agents
abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents now autonomously complete long-horizon tasks, such as repository-level coding, through hundreds of think-act steps, yet the experience each run produces is rarely reused on the next. Prior memory systems concentrate on retrieval, finding the most relevant past trajectory. Retrieval cannot observe the running agent, so it cannot decide whether the agent needs an experience, at which point, or for how long. We introduce REM (Reusable Experience Memory), a framework that manages the memory lifecycle from inside the agent's think-act loop through three explicit decisions. What to store: each completed trajectory is consolidated into a phase-structured document, two orders of magnitude smaller than the trajectory. When to recall: the document is injected at the start of the task; the costlier implementation record is withheld until an in-loop gate detects the agent struggling. What to forget: the record is evicted after a single exposure. On repository-level bug fixing (SWE-ContextBench Lite), REM retrieves the related trajectory more accurately than every state-of-the-art memory system (68.7% vs. 55.6% match@1) and improves, in every replicate, end-task resolution (27.6% vs. 24.9%) at 17% lower cost. Injecting the same experience as a summary or raw trajectory, even when oracle-retrieved, does not. Ablating any of the three decisions reduces resolution. Altogether, these results demonstrate that the bottleneck in experience reuse is not retrieval fidelity but how experience is stored and governed across its lifecycle, opening a control-theoretic perspective on agent memory.

title: Documentation Drift in AI-Generated Pull Requests
abstract: AI coding agents now contribute to software repositories at scale, yet their documentation practices remain uncharacterised. We analyse 29,669 AI-generated pull requests from 2,585 repositories in the AIDev dataset, measuring documentation co-change: whether code-file modifications are accompanied by a documentation-file update in the same PR. We find that 63.2% of AI PRs change code without updating any documentation. This varies sharply by task type: 55.2% for features and 77.5% for refactoring. Undocumented code files are followed by a fix to the same file 8.6 to 11.7% more often than documented files across 30 to 90-day windows. A raw PR-level comparison shows the opposite because documented PRs are 3.9 times larger and therefore attract more fixes. Controlling for size exposure reverses this result. Documented changes also merge faster despite their larger size (median: 40 seconds versus 184 seconds), although merging is largely automated in this dataset. Documentation drift also compounds: within 90 days, a file changed without documentation is later re-documented at roughly half the rate of a file changed with documentation (24% versus 48%). This suggests that documentation debt tends to accumulate rather than be revisited.

title: Machine Learning and Deep Learning for Stock Volatility Prediction: Methods, Challenges and Future Directions
abstract: Predicting stock fluctuations is extremely important for risk management and asset allocation. Traditional models like Generalized Autoregressive Conditional Heteroskedasticity (GARCH) cannot handle the complex and ever-changing stock market data, so machine learning prediction methods have been widely adopted. This paper conducts a review study by collecting relevant literature. The research steps are as follows: first, screen the relevant literature on stock volatility prediction; then, divide the models in the literature into two categories: traditional machine learning and deep learning; next, compare the application scenarios, actual effects, and shortcomings of each type of model, and summarize the common methods used in existing research for data processing and feature creation. After organizing the data, it was found that this industry has three main practical problems: the predicted results given by the model are unclear in terms of their causes, the predictions are inaccurate in different market environments, and it is difficult to develop high-quality analytical indicators. To address these issues, several research directions can be proposed: developing a logically understandable combined model that can adapt to different markets and combine data from various sources for use. This review can provide a reference for those who will conduct related research in the future.

title: Genomic foundation models do not yet boost common variant discovery beyond standard functional annotations
abstract: Genomic foundation models (GFMs) use large-scale AI to model genetic sequences and their influence on molecular phenotypes. While GFMs have shown promise in rare variant analysis, their utility for common variant discovery remains untested. Using the surrogate functional false discovery rate framework for functionally informed GWAS discovery, we compared standard functional annotations (baselineLD) with annotations derived from three leading GFMs: the sequence-to-function models AlphaGenome and Borzoi, and the genomic language model GPN-Star. Across 27 UK Biobank traits, GPN-Star decreased locus discovery relative to a standard GWAS, whereas AlphaGenome and Borzoi increased discovery but by less than baselineLD (medians 1.8%, 3.8%, and 5.1%). When we combined the GFM and baselineLD annotations, there was no increase over baselineLD alone (median changes −0.1% to 0.2%), suggesting that AlphaGenome and Borzoi mostly capture information already in baselineLD. Thus, GFMs may require larger corpora or trait-specific feature engineering to improve discovery beyond standard functional annotations.

title: Stain Normalisation Does Not Consistently Improve Matched-Location Retrieval with Pathology Foundation Models
abstract: Pathology foundation models provide reusable representations for computational pathology, but staining- and scanner-induced variation may compromise the robustness and reproducibility of embedding-based analyses across acquisition settings. Stain normalisation is widely used to mitigate such colour variation, yet whether it improves retrieval with modern self-supervised pathology encoders remains unclear. We test whether stain normalisation improves cross-scanner and cross-staining image retrieval using the PLISM whole-slide image subset, comprising 13 co-registered images of serial sections prepared under different staining conditions and digitised using seven scanners (91 whole-slide images). We sample 400 matched locations across the 91 images, yielding 36,400 tile instances. We compare two DINOv2-based encoders, Phikon-v2 (1,024-dimensional) and Midnight-12k (3,072-dimensional), with Reinhard and Macenko normalisation against an unnormalised baseline. Performance is measured using paired top-1 nearest-neighbour retrieval accuracy in two settings: cross-scanner retrieval of the same physical section digitised by different scanners, and cross-staining retrieval across co-registered images of serial sections, which differ in staining condition and may also contain section-level morphological variation. Neither normalisation method consistently improves top-1 retrieval relative to no normalisation, while Macenko reduces accuracy by up to 18.3 percentage points. An exploratory UMAP of unnormalised Midnight-12k slide-level mean embeddings showed partial overlap between scanner groups in a two-dimensional projection. These results challenge the routine use of stain normalisation in foundation-model retrieval pipelines and support validating preprocessing choices for each encoder and retrieval setting.

title: LongVerse: verified AI agents for Nanopore and PacBio DNA methylation analysis
abstract: AI agents now run sequencing pipelines, but their outputs are checked by proxy, with rubrics or language-model judges. LongVerse turns one English sentence into haplotype-resolved DNA methylation from Nanopore or PacBio reads, through agents that read the data, supply arguments to a pinned pipeline and never write code. On HG002, a healthy reference genome, agent and human expert produced byte-identical calls (r = 1.000) that agreed with bisulfite sequencing (r = 0.943, 0.884), at $0.12 to $0.54 of conversation per run. A consensus agent that admits any per-site caller reduced error 10.7 percent against the best published caller.

title: Deep learning-based electrocardiographic differentiation of Takotsubo syndrome from acute anterior myocardial infarction: explainability, human-AI interaction, and a utilization bias hypothesis
abstract: Background: Artificial intelligence (AI) may improve electrocardiographic differentiation of Takotsubo syndrome from acute anterior ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI), but its impact on human diagnostic performance, the added value of visual explanations, and differences by reader background and experience remain uncertain. Methods: Using 12-lead electrocardiogram (ECG) images from two hospitals, we developed and externally validated an ensemble of three deep learning models after self-supervised pretraining and fine-tuning. The diagnostic task used ECGs recorded within 14 days after symptom onset, regardless of reperfusion status. We conducted a four-phase reader study. Phases 1-3 compared unaided interpretation, a reference sheet, and additional AI assistance. In Phase 4, readers evaluated a new ECG set after randomization to reference-sheet support alone, with AI predictions, or with AI predictions plus gradient-weighted class activation mapping (Grad-CAM) heatmaps. Diagnostic correctness was analyzed using generalized linear mixed-effects models. Exploratory analyses examined differences by cardiologist status and experience. Results: Development and external-validation cohorts, including healthy controls, comprised 832 and 95 participants, respectively. For Takotsubo-STEMI discrimination, external-validation accuracy was 0.914, with areas under the receiver operating characteristic and precision-recall curves of 0.970 and 0.984. Seventy healthcare providers completed the reader study. The estimated probability of correct diagnosis increased from 0.632 without assistance to 0.864 with AI assistance (odds ratio [OR], 3.71; P<0.001). In randomized Phase 4, AI assistance improved accuracy vs reference-sheet support alone (OR, 4.28; 95% CI, 3.08-5.95; P<0.001), and Grad-CAM provided additional benefit (OR, 1.53; 95% CI, 1.04-2.25; P=0.033). Exploratory analyses showed greater improvement among less experienced readers; with AI assistance, non-cardiologists outperformed cardiologists. AI-assisted readers remained less accurate overall than the model alone. Conclusions: An ECG image-based ensemble differentiated Takotsubo syndrome from anterior STEMI and improved reader accuracy. Visual explanations provided additional benefit, while experience-related differences highlight the importance of effective human-AI interaction.

title: Counterfactual Policy Learning for Personalized Treatment Using SGLT2 Inhibitors
abstract: Personalized medicine aims to tailor treatments to individual patients, but its implementation is limited by scarce clinical resources and heterogeneous treatment effects. Electronic health records now offer longitudinal data that can support data-driven therapy selection. We focus on SGLT2 inhibitors, medications with broad metabolic and cardiovascular benefits, whose clinical impact varies significantly based on individual patient profiles. We propose a counterfactual Structural Causal Model (SCM) to estimate individual treatment effects (ITE) of SGLT2 inhibitors from observational data. The model assumes counterfactual stability and uses a Gumbel-Max sampling mechanism to capture stochastic treatment assignment while enabling differentiable inference. Optimal treatments are defined by maximizing the counterfactual value of future diagnostic outcomes. We evaluate the Counterfactual Gumbel-Max SCM using a doubly robust value estimator and show that, across diagnostic categories, it outperforms real-world prescriptions in predicted treatment value, highlighting subpopulations where SGLT2 inhibitors yield superior outcomes. By integrating causal inference with electronic health data, this framework provides individualized counterfactual reasoning about SGLT2 treatment effects and can support clinicians in identifying optimal therapies for type 2 diabetes and comorbid conditions.

title: Multiple Organ Dysfunction Trajectory Phenotypes After Severe Trauma Are Associated With Distinct Immune Profiles and Outcomes
abstract: BACKGROUND Traditional organ dysfunction classifications after severe trauma rely on binary categories (e.g., chronic critical illness [CCI] versus rapid recovery), which likely oversimplify the true heterogeneity of postinjury organ dysfunction trajectories and their underlying immune-biologic drivers. We hypothesized that severely injured trauma patients demonstrate multiple, distinct organ dysfunction phenotypes distinguished by unique immune signatures. METHODS We performed a prospective, longitudinal, observational cohort study of severely injured trauma patients at high risk for multiple organ dysfunction at a single Level 1 trauma center. Organ dysfunction was quantified daily through 28 days, death, or discharge using a trauma-specific modified Sequential Organ Failure Assessment (mSOFA) score excluding the neurologic subdomain to isolate systemic organ dysfunction from traumatic brain injury. We utilized group-based trajectory modeling to identify longitudinal mSOFA phenotypes. Plasma immune protein trajectories were compared across phenotypes using mixed-effects models with time interaction. RESULTS Sixty-nine patients were enrolled. Trajectory modeling identified five mSOFA phenotypes (c1-c5) with differences in resuscitation requirements, shock severity, and 28-day mortality, but not baseline demographics, injury severity, or early physiologic parameters. The phenotypes revealed organ dysfunction heterogeneity not fully captured by CCI/rapid recovery classification. Forty of 92 measured immune markers showed phenotype-differentiated trajectories (FDR<0.1). The most fulminant phenotype (c5) was distinguished by IL-17C, CXCL5, and CXCL6, implicating epithelial-barrier and neutrophil-trafficking mechanisms. The phenotype with highest CCI incidence (c3) was distinguished by rising CXCL9, ARTN, and TWEAK, implicating Th1 polarization and tissue-inflammation/repair signaling. The clinically distinct, older-age phenotype (c4) carried the largest differentiating signature (29 proteins), spanning renal injury/repair, endothelial activation, and adaptive lymphocyte modulation. CONCLUSIONS Organ dysfunction after severe trauma is more biologically heterogeneous than traditional clinical classifications suggest. Distinct mSOFA trajectory phenotypes correspond to distinct immune signatures, supporting separable pathobiology rather than a single axis of injury severity, with implications for phenotype-targeted precision immunomodulatory approaches in critical illness.

title: Clinical referral text overrides MRI evidence in multimodal large language models: glioma versus brain abscess
abstract: Objectives: To determine how strongly clinical referral text, rather than image content, drives the decisions of multimodal large language models (LLMs) differentiating glioma from brain abscess on MRI. Materials and methods: This retrospective single-center study included 60 contrast-enhanced T1-weighted brain MRI examinations (30 gliomas, 30 abscesses; reference-standard diagnosis). One axial slice per case was paired with five referral texts (explicitly inflammatory to explicitly tumor-suggestive) under three prompt instructions and submitted 20 times each to GPT-4o, Claude Sonnet 5, Gemini 3.5 Flash, and Qwen 3.6 (72,000 answers). The primary outcome was the text-driven span (difference in tumor-call frequency between explicit inflammatory and explicit tumor text). Two blinded radiologists classified the images without text; sensitivity, specificity, and accuracy were compared descriptively. Results: Patients (29 women) had a mean age of 55.8 +/- 16.4 years. With neutral text, models answered tumor in 45-67% of queries (specificity, 0.38-0.78), versus 52% and 60% for radiologists (specificity, 0.77 and 0.63). The text-driven span was 0.79-1.00 (p < 0.001 for all models), whereas confirmed gliomas and abscesses differed by only 0.01-0.10 in three models and 0.25 in Gemini 3.5 Flash. Subtle wording produced at least 83% of the span in three models. An instruction to ignore the text reduced the span to 0.48-0.70 in three models and to 0.04 in Gemini 3.5 Flash, partly through reversion to a tumor default. Model accuracy was 0.52-0.73 versus 0.78 and 0.73 for radiologists. Conclusion: Multimodal LLMs deferred to referral text over imaging evidence in differentiating glioma from brain abscess, and prompt instructions did not reliably correct this.

title: Behavioral Orientations and Self-Rated Performance Among University Employees in Vietnam
abstract: University work increasingly combines professional discretion with digital change, accountability demands, and cross-unit coordination. This cross-sectional study examined associations among five work-related behavioral orientations responsibility, discipline, engagement, cooperation, and adaptability and four domains of self-rated performance among 450 university employees in Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam. A four-point questionnaire was analyzed using a reflective composite-based PLS path model with 5,000 bootstrap resamples. Reliability and convergent validity were strong across the nine constructs, although several conceptually adjacent constructs showed high HTMT values and were therefore interpreted cautiously. All five orientations showed positive bivariate relationships with performance, but their unique multivariable associations were uneven. Adaptability and cooperation showed the most consistent unique associations across the four performance domains, whereas several responsibility, discipline, and engagement paths were small or nonsignificant after shared variance was considered. Discipline was strongly associated with responsibility, engagement, cooperation, and adaptability, and several model-based indirect associations with performance were observed. These findings support a differentiated but interconnected view of work behavior rather than a single generic positive attitude. Because predictors and outcomes were measured concurrently from the same respondents, the results do not establish temporal mediation or causal effects.

title: HECTD1 Directs HIF-1α to Facilitate Intestinal Inflammation and Carcinogenesis via Promoting Th17 Differentiation and Glycolysis.
abstract: Targeting glucose metabolism in Th17 cells may be beneficial for treating inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) and colitis-associated cancer (CAC), however, the molecular mechanisms orchestrating Th17 cell metabolism remain unclear. Here, we revealed that HECTD1 regulates IGF2BP3-dependent HIF-1α translation to promote Th17 cell glycolysis and differentiation and that HECTD1 expression correlates with IBD and CAC pathogenesis. T-cell-specific deletion of HECTD1 mitigated the severity of colitis and CAC in murine models. RNA-seq revealed enrichment of Th17 differentiation, glycolysis/gluconeogenesis, and HIF-1 signaling pathways among differentially expressed genes between HECTD1-sufficient and HECTD1-deficient CD4+ T cells. Consistently, loss of HECTD1 suppressed Th17 cell differentiation both in vitro and in vivo, and suppressed glycolytic metabolism and HIF-1α activity, revealing the mechanism underlying its protective effects against IBD and CAC. Mechanistically, HECTD1 potentiates m6A-based HIF-1α translation by mediating IGF2BP3 K63-linked ubiquitination to promote the binding of IGF2BP3 with the translation initiation machinery of Hif1a mRNA. Reciprocally, HIF-1α acts as a key transcription factor that promotes Hectd1 gene expression, establishing a distinct positive feedback loop. Our findings highlight a self-reinforcing feedback mechanism in which HECTD1 and HIF-1α engage in mutual regulation to dictate Th17 cell fate and metabolic reprogramming, providing novel potential IBD and CAC treatments targeting HECTD1.

title: Poloxamer-Enabled Thermoresponsive Biobased Controlled-Release Fertilizer for On-Demand Nutrient Delivery.
abstract: Synchronizing nutrient release of fertilizers with crop uptake remains a central challenge in precision agriculture. Here, we present a novel temperature-responsive biobased controlled-release fertilizer (TRBFs) incorporating Poloxamer 407 (F127) as a thermal switch within a castor oil-derived polyurethane coating. The optimized TRBF10 (3 wt.% coating rate, 10 wt.% F127 in coating) exhibits a sharp, reversible phase transition at ∼20°C, matching the phenological requirements of overwintering crops. As quantified by digital refractometry, the 30-day cumulative nitrogen release is suppressed to 9.22% at 10°C (crop dormancy) and increases 8.7-fold to 80.32% at 30°C (active growth). This scalable technology overcomes intrinsic limitations of conventional diffusion-controlled coated fertilizers and offers potential for on-demand nutrient delivery with reduced environmental loss. Our work establishes sustainable strategies for climate-adaptive precision agriculture and offers new insights and design paradigms for intelligent controlled-release materials.

title: A simple empirical growing degree day model for predicting winter cover crop biomass in sandy soils
abstract: The ecosystem services provided by cover crops (CCs) are related to their biomass production. The objective of this study was to develop a simple empirical model to enable farmers to predict CC biomass yields based on planting and termination timing, thereby improving the assessment of CC benefits. A field experiment was conducted over 3 years on sandy soils using two common winter CCs, cereal rye ( Secale cereale ) and hairy vetch ( Vicia villosa ), grown as monocultures and in mixture following local management guidelines. Aboveground biomass was collected periodically from establishment to termination during each growing season, and cumulative growing degree days (GDDs) were calculated. A quadratic model was developed using GDD as the independent variable and the natural logarithm of biomass yield as the dependent variable. Model's performance was significant across all treatments, with coefficients of determination ( R 2 ) ranging from 0.59 to 0.74. The models were further validated with data from adjacent fields under similar management, showing strong agreement between predicted and observed values for cereal rye ( R 2 = 0.82) and hairy vetch ( R 2 = 0.87). The validated model was then used to simulate CC production under 15 growth duration scenarios. Results suggest that the model is a reliable and practical tool for optimizing CC management to achieve desired agronomic and environmental outcomes. However, model performance is constrained by limited data inputs and could be improved with additional observations across a broader range of climatic conditions.

title: Covariation of DOM molecular characteristics and bacterial carbon metabolism potential along a reservoir-agricultural river nutrient gradient
A growing challenge: stakeholder perceptions of AI and ML applications in U.S. agriculture
abstract: Context The global population is expected to exceed ten billion by 2050 and food demand is projected to increase by up to 100% in the same timeframe. Agricultural management must adapt to meet the increasing global demands. Artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) technologies can help the agricultural community respond to these needs. Aims An online survey and follow-up interviews were conducted to examine patterns of use, perceptions, and barriers among early adopting stakeholders regarding AI and ML. Methods The online survey with agricultural stakeholders (n=129) included questions regarding the participants’ views on incorporating AI and ML techniques into farming practices and individual follow-up interviews with agricultural stakeholders (n=10) were conducted to better understand their concerns toward technology use and adoption of AI-enabled tools and technologies. Key results Using a mixed-methods approach, four challenges to establishing AI-/ML-enabled technology in agriculture were identified. Namely, challenges related to (1) systems of systems (SoS), (2) sub-seasonal to seasonal weather (S2S) forecasts, (3) precision soil management, and (4) policy and economics. Each challenge was discussed in the context of recent literature. Conclusion Concerns were voiced clustered around four broad research themes. This brief communication brings the perspective of agricultural stakeholders to the discussion of the potential of AI/ML-enabled technology and the direction of their development in the agricultural sector. Implications Data collected in 2021, establish an important baseline for the early phase of AI/ML use in U.S. agriculture, enabling comparison of future perceptions and developments in the sector. Impact This brief communication describes a survey and follow-up interviews conducted with agricultural stakeholders on factors influencing their willingness and reluctance to incorporate AI and ML techniques into farming practices. The findings, summarized and discussed as four key challenges for AI and ML in the agricultural sector, have the potential to streamline research activities.

title: Multivariate phenotyping reveals thermoregulatory patterns in crossbred cattle
abstract: Improving the adaptation of beef cattle production to climate change requires crossbreeding strategies that enhance the ability of animals to maintain thermal stability under hot conditions. The objective of this exploratory study was to assess how coat characteristics are associated with rectal-temperature variation and to identify thermoregulatory patterns in Red Angus × Nelore crossbred cattle raised under tropical conditions. Thirty clinically healthy crossbred bulls from two genetic compositions (½ Red Angus × ½ Nelore and ¾ Red Angus × ¼ Nelore) were evaluated at 210 and 360 days of age. Morphological, physiological, and environmental variables were recorded, including coat thickness, hair length, hair quantity, hair density, and rectal temperatures measured in the morning and afternoon. Univariate comparisons did not detect differences (p > 0.05) between the genetic groups in the evaluated coat traits or rectal temperatures, indicating substantial overlap between genetic compositions. In an exploratory logistic model developed to discriminate the two genetic groups, rectal temperature was positively associated with group classification [odds ratio (OR) = 1.41, p = 0.023], whereas hair length showed a negative association (OR = 0.53, p < 0.001), indicating that morphological and physiological traits jointly contributed to the observed differentiation. Correlation analysis showed that thicker coats tended to contain fewer and less densely distributed hairs, whereas hair quantity and density were strongly and positively associated, suggesting compensatory coat architectures. The exploratory clustering solutions suggested four candidate coat-related configurations: (i) short, dense coats and (ii) thick but less dense coats, both associated with lower daily rectal-temperature variation; and (iii) intermediate coats and (iv) long, dense coats, associated with greater thermal fluctuation. Although some overlap among clusters was observed, these configurations provide an exploratory basis for understanding how combinations of coat characteristics may influence thermoregulatory responses. The findings indicate that thermal regulation in crossbred cattle is better understood through combinations of morphological traits than through isolated characteristics. Future studies with larger, independent populations and additional physiological and productive measurements are needed to confirm the consistency and broader applicability of these patterns.

title: Early-stage comparative life cycle assessment of cement tiles
abstract: The construction sector is one of the largest contributors to global energy consumption and CO2 emissions, with cement-based materials playing a central role in its environmental impact. Cement tiles, despite being marketed as sustainable alternatives to ceramic coatings due to their artisanal production and long durability, rely heavily on Portland cement, a material with high carbon intensity. This study revisits the environmental performance of cement tiles through a comparative analysis between a detailed Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) and a simplified ecological audit focused on embodied energy and CO2 footprint, aiming to evaluate its performance as an early-stage screening tool. The functional unit used was 1 m2, equivalent to 25 tiles. Results show that both approaches identify raw material extraction as the dominant contributor to environmental burdens. However, EcoAudit produced systematically higher screening estimates for embodied energy and CO2 footprint than the values reported in the reference LCA, mainly because both approaches rely on different databases, modelling assumptions, process definitions, and inventory treatments. Nevertheless, relative trends were similar, enabling preliminary differentiation of more sustainable production pathways. The findings highlight the potential of simplified assessment tools for early-stage decision-making and hotspot identification, while reinforcing the need for full LCA studies to obtain accurate and reliable environmental data in construction material evaluation.

Aerobic exercise ameliorates cardiac function in HFpEF mice by suppressing ALCAT1, neuroinflammation and oxidative stress in the paraventricular nucleus and nucleus tractus solitarius.
abstract: BACKGROUND Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) is commonly accompanied by sympathetic overactivation, contributing to poor patient prognosis. The paraventricular nucleus (PVN) and nucleus tractus solitarius (NTS) are critical cardiovascular regulatory centers. Pathological cardiolipin (CL) remodeling catalyzed by Acyl-CoA:lysocardiolipin acyltransferase 1 (ALCAT1) exacerbates disease progression. This study aims to elucidate the roles of aerobic exercise and ALCAT1 in modulating brain-heart axis dysregulation in HFpEF. METHODS AND RESULTS We employed wild-type (WT) and Alcat1 knockout mice to establish an HFpEF model, followed by aerobic exercise. Neuroinflammatory model was established to investigate the role of ALCAT1 in neuroinflammation. Underlying mechanisms were explored in HT22 cells. In HFpEF mice, aerobic exercise suppressed ALCAT1 and up-regulated growth differentiation factor 5 (GDF5) in the PVN and NTS, reduced pro-inflammatory cytokines, enhanced antioxidant enzyme activities, decreased oxidative stress markers, and attenuated neuronal structural damage and hyperactivation. These central improvements were accompanied by attenuated cardiac sympathetic overactivation, lowered blood pressure, and improved diastolic function. The important role of ALCAT1 was further supported, as its genetic knockout conferred significant protection in both HFpEF and neuroinflammatory models. In HT22 cells, GDF5 suppressed the LPS-induced ALCAT1 up-regulation and ameliorated cellular injury. CONCLUSION ALCAT1 is an important contributor to neuronal injury. Aerobic exercise suppresses ALCAT1 and up-regulates GDF5, ameliorating neuronal injury and improving diastolic function in HFpEF mice. Mechanistically, ALCAT1 and GDF5 are reciprocally regulated, which may contribute to the protective effects of aerobic exercise against HFpEF. These findings suggest ALCAT1 as a potential molecular target for exercise-based HFpEF therapy.

title: Architecture diverse TabNet ensemble for crop type classification using harmonized multisource soil data
abstract: Accurate analysis of heterogeneous soil records can support data-driven agricultural planning, but integrating datasets from different laboratories and public repositories introduces challenges related to inconsistent units, source-dependent distributions, missing values, duplicate observations, and potential information leakage. This study proposes ADWTabNet, an architecture-diverse TabNet ensemble for multiclass crop-type classification using harmonized multi-source soil data. The integrated dataset contained 18,237 observations representing seven crop classes and a broad set of chemical, physical, microbiological, and categorical soil properties. The proposed framework combines unit standardization, duplicate control, source-distribution harmonization, separate categorical and numerical imputation, tree-structured Parzen estimator-based hyperparameter optimization, structurally diverse TabNet models, probability-level ensemble fusion, calibration assessment, and attention-based interpretation. Under the evaluated stratified holdout protocol, XGBoost achieved a test accuracy of 0.8724 and a macro F1-score of 0.8670. Baseline TabNet improved these values to 0.8863 and 0.8822, respectively, while the TPE-optimized TabNet reached an accuracy of 0.8951 and reduced log loss from 0.3325 to 0.2566. The proposed ADWTabNet ensemble obtained the best reported performance, with a test accuracy of 0.9053, macro F1-score of 0.9025, weighted F1-score of 0.9050, macro ROC–AUC of 0.9930, and normalized multiclass Brier score of 0.0193. Repeated-run evaluation confirmed a stable advantage over the optimized individual TabNet, whereas the difference between validation-weighted and equal architecture-diverse averaging was not statistically significant. Aggregated TabNet attention ranked humus, phosphorus, electrical conductivity, nitrogen, and pH among the leading predictors, and this ranking was independently supported by permutation-importance analysis. These findings demonstrate improved crop-type classification within the evaluated integrated multi-source dataset. However, external validation using previously unseen laboratories and geographic regions is required before broader transferability can be established.

A Field-Deployable Sensing Platform for Online Monitoring of Transmission Tower Grounding Systems
abstract: Grounding systems are critical to the safe and reliable operation of electrical power systems, especially in high-voltage transmission networks, where their performance directly influences fault current dissipation, equipment protection, and overall system reliability and security. To address the need for continuous field assessment of these structures, this work presents a complete measurement system for remote online monitoring of electrical quantities associated with transmission tower grounding systems. The proposed platform combines Rogowski-coil current sensing at the four tower legs, voltage measurements around the tower base, analog signal conditioning, embedded waveform acquisition and processing, and remote communication. The system was implemented in a 525 kV transmission tower and validated by comparison with an oscilloscope and commercial instruments, showing consistent waveform, rms, and harmonic measurements. Field tests under different counterpoise connection conditions further demonstrated that the measured electrical variables can support the diagnostic assessment of the grounding structure. The results indicate that the proposed system provides reliable field acquisition and enables the development of methods for online supervision of transmission tower grounding behavior.
