title: Attitude Estimation of Falcon 9 Rocket Body Based on Photometric Characteristics
abstract: The proliferation of space debris, driven by increasingly frequent space activities, poses a severe risk to operational satellites and future missions. Consequently, the surveillance and characterization of space objects have become critical. Current methods for attitude estimation of space objects often rely on target-specific models, such as those with a closed set of facets, and typically employ nonlinear filtering or machine learning techniques. However, these approaches often lack general applicability. This study proposes a more general approach to attitude estimation based on photometric light curves. We define a loss function that quantifies the discrepancy between the measured light curve and a theoretical model parameterized by the attitude parameters. By leveraging automatic differentiation to compute the gradients of this function, we use a gradient descent algorithm to achieve rapid and accurate attitude estimation. The proposed method provides a versatile and efficient framework for attitude estimation, overcoming the target-specificity limitations of existing techniques, with the parameters estimation time reduced to 15 seconds and the mean square error lowered to three decimal places. Validation on the third-party database demonstrates that the method exhibits strong generalization capability.

title: Variable-resolution maps (VRMs) in CCTBX and Phenix: accounting for local resolution in cryoEM.
abstract: Calculation of density maps from atomic models is essential for structural studies using crystallography and electron cryo-microscopy (cryoEM). These maps serve various purposes, including atomic model building, refinement, visualization and validation. However, accurately comparing model-calculated maps to experimental data poses challenges, particularly because the resolution of cryoEM experimental maps varies across the map. Traditional crystallography methods generate finite-resolution maps with uniform resolution throughout the unit cell volume, while most modern software in cryoEM employs Gaussian-like functions to generate these maps, which does not adequately account for atomic model parameters and resolution. Recent work by Urzhumtsev & Lunin [IUCrJ (2022), 9, 728-734] introduces a novel method for computing atomic model maps that incorporate local resolution and can be expressed as analytically differentiable functions of atomic parameters. This approach enhances the accuracy of maps simulated from atomic models, allowing them to better reproduce features of the experimental maps. In this paper, we detail the implementation of this method in CCTBX and Phenix.

title: CryoQSeg: robust particle segmentation for cryo-EM with Qwen-Image-Edit.
abstract: Accurate particle picking remains a critical step in cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM) single-particle analysis, and the field has witnessed the development of a broad spectrum of approaches - from classical template-based methods to modern deep learning frameworks - to address this task. Here we present CryoQSeg, a particle segmentation and picking framework that represents a paradigm shift toward leveraging a state-of-the-art visual large model. Built upon Qwen-Image-Edit-2511 as its core backbone, CryoQSeg is fine-tuned through supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning on the public CryoPPP benchmark dataset, enabling the generation of high-fidelity, pixel-level particle masks directly from raw micrographs. To translate these masks into precise particle coordinates, we further integrate a hybrid post-processing pipeline that couples Hough circle detection with the segment anything model, forming a seamless end-to-end workflow from raw image input to accurate localization. We evaluate CryoQSeg on five representative benchmark datasets, demonstrating competitive performance across a range of protein types and imaging conditions in comparison to mainstream methods including Topaz and CryoSegNet. Furthermore, we validate the framework on the heterogeneous Crt-SPARTA-gRNA-tDNA complex, where it successfully resolves three distinct oligomeric states - monomer, dimer and tetramer - at high resolutions, despite using a fraction of the micrographs employed in the original study. By bridging modern visual large models with classical and foundation-model-based post-processing strategies, CryoQSeg demonstrates the potential of this emerging paradigm to deliver a robust and automated solution for cryo-EM particle picking, thereby contributing to a solid foundation for high-resolution three-dimensional structural determination of biological macromolecules.

title: Spectral-Aware Proposal Enhancement for Diffusion-Based Multispectral UAV Multi-Object Tracking
abstract: Multispectral UAV multi-object tracking (MOT) with oriented bounding boxes remains challenging due to small targets, cluttered backgrounds, and unstable inter-frame associations. Although diffusion-based MOT provides an effective iterative proposal refinement paradigm, existing diffusion-based trackers lack dedicated designs for exploiting multispectral cues in proposal initialization and confidence calibration, limiting tracking robustness in complex UAV scenarios. This letter proposes DSATrack, a diffusion-guided spectral-aware tracking framework for multispectral UAV MOT. Specifically, a lightweight spectral encoder injects multispectral information into the RPN branch through feature fusion, enabling the RPN head to generate high-quality object-aware proposals. These proposals are then injected into the initial proposal set to provide reliable spatial priors for diffusion refinement. Furthermore, a spectral-saliency confidence modulation strategy recalibrates refined tracking confidence according to local multispectral saliency contrast before score thresholding, enhancing spectrally reliable candidates while suppressing unreliable ones. Without modifying the original diffusion refinement head, DSATrack improves both proposal quality and post-refinement candidate selection. Experiments on the MMOT benchmark demonstrate that DSATrack outperforms the adapted DiffusionTrack baseline by 4.6 HOTA, 9.0 MOTA, and 7.7 IDF1 points, showing its effectiveness for multispectral UAV MOT.

title: From Human Speakers to Algorithmic Interfaces: Rethinking Ethos in AI-Mediated Communication
abstract: Generative Artificial Intelligence (GAI) systems increasingly function as communicative agents, raising questions about how credibility is constructed in them. Drawing on Aristotle's concept of ethos, this study examines how credibility is performed through interface‑level cues in large language model (LLM) chatbots: ChatGPT and Copilot. Using a rhetorical interface analysis, the study identifies recurring design patterns such as disclaimer banners and interaction affordances that signal practical competence, ethical restraint, and goodwill. The findings contribute a rhetorical framework for analyzing AI‑mediated credibility as interface‑enacted ethos and highlight the growing importance of communication design in automated persuasive systems.
journal: Proceedings of the 44th ACM International Conference on Design of Communication

title: SwitchSplat: Learning Discrete Object States from Casually Captured Scenes
abstract: 3D Gaussian Splatting has made high-fidelity 3D reconstruction fast and accessible, yet existing representations assume a static world. This assumption breaks down in casual captures, where a user naturally interacts with the environment -- opening doors, toggling switches, or moving objects -- introducing discrete state changes that no current framework can model. Time-conditioned dynamic methods such as 4DGS conflate when a state was observed with what state the scene is in, limiting them to replaying seen sequences rather than composing arbitrary object configurations. We present SwitchSplat, the first 3DGS representation to address this gap via a base+slot decomposition: a shared static base captures the invariant scene, while each slot independently holds the two binary states (on/off) of one interactable object. Because the assignment of Gaussians to slots is fully differentiable, the model discovers the geometry of each state directly from video, without manual annotation. At inference, the user can freely combine slot states and render the resulting scene from any viewpoint. We validate SwitchSplat on a new casual-capture dataset and show that it outperforms static and dynamic baselines in novel-view synthesis quality, while uniquely supporting rendering of state combinations never seen during capture. Project page: https://switchsplat.github.io

title: Quantitative assessment of foot microcirculation by CT perfusion differentiates chronic limb-threatening ischemia from claudication in peripheral artery disease.
abstract: INTRODUCTION Computed tomography perfusion (CTP) is validated to assess foot microcirculatory perfusion in peripheral artery disease (PAD). This study aimed to investigate differences in foot microcirculation on CTP between patients with claudication (Cla) and chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI) and to develop diagnostic models for CLTI. METHODS This single-center prospective study enrolled hospitalized patients with PAD at Huadong Hospital, China (October 2022 to January 2024). Participants underwent preoperative foot CTP and were stratified into Cla (Rutherford category 3) and CLTI (Rutherford categories 4-6) groups. Baseline characteristics and perfusion parameters were recorded. Multivariable logistic regression and receiver operating characteristic curve analysis were performed. RESULTS A total of 57 patients with PAD were included (34 Cla, 23 CLTI). Resting ankle-brachial index and Global Limb Anatomic Staging System scores did not differ significantly between groups. Diabetes mellitus (DM) prevalence was higher in the CLTI group (95.7% vs 52.9%; p = 0.002). Multivariable logistic regression identified hemoglobin (Hb) level (OR, 0.91; 95% CI, 0.822-0.986; p = 0.024), time to peak (TTP) (OR, 1.135; 95% CI, 1.045-1.250; p = 0.003), and blood flow (BF) (OR, 0.668; 95% CI, 0.499-0.894; p = 0.007) as independent predictors for CLTI. Four diagnostic models were constructed: model A (BF + DM, area under the curve [AUC] 0.864), model B (BF + Hb, AUC 0.890), model C (TTP + DM, AUC 0.895), and model D (TTP + Hb, AUC 0.874). CONCLUSION Foot microcirculation differed significantly between patients with Cla and CLTI on CTP. Hb, TTP, and BF were independent predictors for CLTI. All models demonstrated good diagnostic performance, with model C yielding the highest AUC. CLINICALTRIALS gov Identifier:NCT05575778.

title: From Promise to Practice in Digital Sustainability for Agro-Food Systems: A Systematic Review
abstract: Digital technologies are widely promoted as solutions for sustainable agro-food systems, yet their transition from promise to practice remains uneven and poorly understood. Persistent governance, economic, and managerial barriers continue to constrain the realisation of digital sustainability, and these barriers have not been systematically synthesised. This systematic review synthesises evidence from 16 peer-reviewed studies published between 2016 and 2026, identified through a structured search of the Scopus database. Studies were included if they examined digital innovations, economic instruments, or managerial governance in agricultural or livestock systems and reported outcomes related to sustainability, resource efficiency, or adoption. A narrative synthesis approach was used to integrate findings across three interconnected pillars: economic instruments, technological innovations, and governance factors. The review finds that digital technologies such as artificial intelligence, remote sensing, the Internet of Things, and blockchain can improve productivity, resource efficiency, and predictive accuracy. However, sustainability gains depend on supportive institutional frameworks, financial mechanisms, and governance capacity. Environmental taxes and supply chain finance innovations promote low-carbon transitions, but their effectiveness hinges on digital governance infrastructure and farmer trust. Economies of scale mediate the relationship between smart farming technologies and carbon efficiency, while government regulation positively moderates this pathway. Persistent barriers include data ownership disputes, privacy concerns, weak institutional capacity, and uneven digital infrastructure. Evidence is concentrated in Asia and Europe and relies heavily on simulation-based studies, limiting generalisability. Moving from promise to practice requires integrated governance, economic incentives, and institutional capacity building. Policymakers should prioritise trust-reinforcing data governance, progressive financing schemes, and rural digital infrastructure to enable inclusive and resilient agro-food systems.

title: Trustworthy Phishing URL Detection Using Machine Learning: Performance Analysis and Future Directions
abstract: Over the years, Uniform Resource Locator (URL) Phishing has been a threat to online security because their scams exploit trust in a misleading URL to trick unsuspecting users into disclosing their username or passwords and other personal information. Not only that, but it is also crucial to identify these malicious URLs and ensure online platforms and users are protected. The ISCXURL2016 data was utilized for the purpose of analyzing the performance of different Machine Learning (ML) models in differentiating phishing and legitimate URLs in this paper. A wide range of classifiers were explored including the classic classifiers as well as more advanced ensemble classifiers. The results of the experiments indicate that ensemble-based boosting models can be more beneficial for URL phishing detection. HistGradientBoost achieved the highest accuracy of 98.47%, followed closely by LightGBM and XGBoost that both outperformed the accuracy of 98%. The other classifiers, RandomForest and ExtraTrees, also performed well with accuracy above 97% and traditional classifiers such as Quadratic Discriminant Analysis (QDA) showed the poorest performance with an accuracy of 67.75%. The results show that the boosting-based ensembles provide a suitable negation of the complex and non-linear structure of phishing URLs. Along with empirical evaluation, it offers a Properties & Positioning viewpoint as well as the importance of the ML-based phishing detection in the broader context of cybersecurity issues. Moreover, it discusses the future directions, with Federated Learning (FL) in the context of decentralized and privacy-preserving collaboration and Large Language Models (LLM) in the context of semantic reasoning and flexibility. These insights together will provide the building blocks for more intelligent, adaptive and trustworthy phishing organizations.
journal: International Journal of Advances in Soft Computing and its Applications

title: Modeling and simulation methods used in the maritime industry: evolution, applications and future perspectives
abstract: Modeling and simulation (M&S) techniques have evolved from optional engineering tools to indispensable pillars of modern maritime practice. This article presents a comprehensive systematic review of the most important modeling and simulation methodologies applied to maritime industry processes, including workflows for ship design, shipyard fabrication and construction, port and terminal operations, vessel traffic management, maintenance scheduling, supply chain logistics, and risk management procedures. The study demonstrates that M&S techniques enable safer, more efficient, and more environmentally sustainable operations, validated by scientific standards. The COVID-19 pandemic served as a critical catalyst, consolidating the strategic value of M&S as a central component of maritime resilience and innovation. This research traces the evolution of M&S adoption from 2010 to 2025, identifying four dominant research directions: maritime simulators, computational fluid dynamics (CFD)/finite element analysis (FEA), digital twins, and artificial intelligence-based methods. The analysis reveals that while traditional approaches dominated the 2010-2020 period, emerging technologies—particularly digital twins and AI-based methods—have accelerated exponentially since 2020, reflecting the maritime industry's accelerated digitalization. Forward projections through 2035 indicate that AI-based methodologies will experience the highest growth rate at approximately 329%, followed by digital twins at 147%, underscoring the fundamental transformation of maritime research and practice. The integration of these advanced modeling approaches offers optimal equilibrium between physical precision and computational efficiency for addressing complex maritime challenges.

title: AgriEase: One Click Solution for Farmers
abstract: Farmers often face difficulties in finding and purchasing essential farming equipment and agricultural products such as seeds, fertilizers, tractors, pesticides, and tractor accessories. They may have to visit multiple shops to compare prices, check product availability, and find suitable equipment. This process takes time, increases transportation costs, and makes it difficult for farmers to find affordable and quality products. The proposed project aims to develop an online platform that helps farmers easily search, compare, and purchase agricultural products and equipment in one place. It will provide product details, prices, availability, and easy access to Essen The methodology of the AgriEase project involves designing and developing a user-friendly web-based platform that provides farmers with easy access to agricultural products and useful farming information. The project follows a systematic approach, including requirement analysis, system design, website development, database management, and testing. AgriEase aims to provide a convenient digital platform that connects farmers with essential agricultural products and information, helping reduce the effort required to access farming resources
journal: International Journal for Research in Applied Science and Engineering Technology

title: Spherical Physics-informed Neural Operator with Multi-scale Coupling for Meteorological Downscaling
abstract: Meteorological downscaling is crucial for high-resolution regional climate forecasting and disaster early warning. While neural operators have emerged as a promising paradigm for modeling complex spatiotemporal mappings, existing frameworks often struggle with spherical manifold geometric distortions, inherent atmospheric multi-scale coupling mismatches, and lack of explicit atmospheric laws. We propose the Spherical Physics-informed Neural Operator, which utilizes a Spherical Laplacian Decomposition to partition atmospheric fields into hierarchical frequency components, maintaining exact point-wise correspondence across scales. To evaluate these representations at arbitrary locations, we introduce a localized spherical integral operator that approximates continuous kernel transforms via geometry-aware attention. Dynamical consistency is further enforced by embedding differentiable constraints into the learning process. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our framework attains superior accuracy and zero-shot generalization across various meteorological variables and unseen queries, representing a robust and interpretable solution for global-to-regional meteorological downscaling.

title: SEEN ONLINE, VERIFIED OFFLINE: PEER VALIDATION AND THE ADOPTION OF NEW-MEDIA-COMMUNICATED FARM PRACTICES IN KANPUR NAGAR
abstract: New media have made agricultural advice easily available to farmers; however, farmers may not act on what they see on a screen without first checking it. Based on the two-step and multistep flow models and the Diffusion of Innovations theory, the present study examined whether farmers consult another person before adopting practices seen on new media, whether the perceived compatibility of the information is associated with how often they adopt it, and whether peer sharing mediates the link between new-media exposure and adoption. A survey of 260 farmers using new media for agricultural information was conducted in ten villages of Chaubeypur and Kalyanpur blocks of Kanpur Nagar district, Uttar Pradesh. The data were analysed with a binomial test, chi-square tests, ordered logistic regression and a bootstrapped mediation model. Only 1.9% of the farmers adopted practices immediately, while 89.2% consulted another person first, mostly a progressive farmer (58.1%). Each one-point rise in perceived compatibility was associated with 2.35 times the odds of more frequent adoption. Peer sharing accounted for 41% of the association between new-media exposure and adoption (indirect effect = 0.114, 95% CI [0.044, 0.194]). Farmers aged 35–55 depended more on neighbours and relatives and adopted less often than younger farmers. The study concludes that new media start the adoption process, but the decision to adopt is taken through interpersonal validation; hence, digital extension should equip local opinion leaders and not only individual viewers.

title: EVOLVING TOOLS IN CONSTRUCTED WETLAND RESEARCH: FROM RADIOISOTOPE TRACERS TO PREDICTIVE HYDROLOGICAL MODELS
abstract: Constructed wetlands (CWs) have become a key nature-based technology for sustainable wastewater treatment and ecological restoration, yet their performance remains highly dependent on complex interactions among hydrodynamics, biogeochemistry, vegetation, and operational conditions. This paper traces the evolution of research and troubleshooting tools used in CW studies, starting from early radiotracer applications and progressing towards contemporary data rich, model driven frameworks. The paper then presents the recent advances including remote sensing and UAV based monitoring, sensor networks, computational fluid dynamics (CFD), process based hydrological and reactive transport models, integrated systems, and the renewed but regulated use of radioisotope and dye tracers. In parallel, the role of dedicated simulation software in CW design and optimization is analyzed through six main platforms: BIO_PORE, HYDRUS Wetland Module, Wetland Water Quality Model (WWQM), WEST, AQUASIM, and SWAT. A comparative assessment highlights how each tool targets specific spatial scales and processes, from pore scale clogging dynamics to watershed level pollutant loading. The results demonstrate that no single technique or software package can capture the full multi scale complexity of CWs; instead, maximum benefit is achieved by combining complementary tools into integrated monitoring–modelling frameworks. The paper concludes by emphasising the need for multi model, multi-source strategies and outlines future directions involving AI, digital twins, and tighter coupling between field diagnostics and predictive simulation to support more resilient, efficient, and sustainable CW systems.
journal: World Journal of Advanced Research and Reviews

title: Quantitative, longitudinal measurements of response to immunotherapy for glioblastoma using multiparametric MRI in a long-term survivor treated with autologous tumor lysate–loaded dendritic cell vaccine: an illustrative case
abstract: BACKGROUND Neurosurgeons are in the forefront of developing clinical trials that harness the immune system to combat glioblastoma. Autologous tumor lysate-loaded dendritic cell vaccine (DCVax-L) is a novel immunotherapy for glioblastoma. An unmet need is to develop a sensitive, specific, feasible, clinically relevant, neuroimaging biomarker that accurately reflects response to immunotherapy. OBSERVATIONS This illustrative case involves a 63-year-old female who survived for 64 months following near-total resection of a glioblastoma and enrollment in a clinical trial (NCT00045968) using DCVax-L. A multivariate logistic regression model was used to assess treatment response longitudinally at 11 time points measuring predictive probability (PP) of tumor progression based on diffusion tensor imaging- and perfusion-weighted imaging-derived parameters within the contrast-enhancing region. Lesions were considered true progression (TP) if the PP was ≥ 50% and pseudoprogression (PsP; predominant treatment effects) if the PP was < 50 %. These findings were subsequently validated by histopathological analysis during resection for tumor recurrence. LESSONS These findings support the use of multiparametric MRI to monitor the effects of immunotherapy in patients with glioblastoma. Such multiparametric prediction models using noninvasive, advanced neuroimaging may be helpful to differentiate TP from PsP in longitudinal assessment of treatment response. https://thejns.org/doi/10.3171/CASE26655.

title: Landslide Instance Segmentation from Remote Sensing Imagery Using a SwinV2–FPN Mask R-CNN with Spatially Adaptive Feature Modulation
abstract: Landslide inventory mapping supports emergency response and hazard assessment in mountainous regions. Accurate identification and delineation of individual landslides remain challenging because of scale variation, irregular morphology, and interference from visually similar backgrounds in complex mountainous terrain. To address these challenges, we modified Mask R-CNN’s feature pathway and mask supervision. ResNet50 was replaced with SwinV2-Tiny for hierarchical feature extraction, while the feature pyramid network (FPN) was retained for multi-scale fusion. Spatially adaptive feature modulation (SAFM) was applied after the FPN to adjust spatial responses using local features and broader context. Binary cross-entropy (BCE) and Dice losses were combined to supervise pixel-wise foreground–background discrimination and instance-mask overlap. A curated dataset combining imagery from Bijie, the Diverse Mountainous Landslide Dataset (DMLD), and ScienceDB was used for training, validation, and internal testing. All configurations were evaluated using the Common Objects in Context (COCO) instance-mask protocol. Across three training seeds, SwinV2–FPN–SAFM Mask R-CNN achieved an internal test average precision (AP0.50:0.95) of 0.6158±0.0082 (mean ± sample standard deviation). Its mean mask AP0.50:0.95 exceeded those of ResNet50–FPN Mask R-CNN and Mask2Former–Swin-T by 6.21 and 3.51 percentage points, respectively. It achieved the highest mean mask AP0.50:0.95 among the ten evaluated configurations. The ablations indicated small positive increments in mean mask AP0.50:0.95 with SAFM and BCE–Dice, and their incremental benefits remained uncertain. The higher mean mask AP0.50:0.95 indicates improved overall performance in identifying landslide instances and delineating their extent on the internal test set. The resulting instance masks may assist inventory compilation and post-disaster mapping in complex mountainous terrain.

title: ChangeMoE: A Mixture-of-Experts-Based Mamba Network for Building Change Detection from High-Resolution Remote Sensing Imagery
abstract: Mamba has recently become a popular visual representation architecture for building change detection (BCD) in the remote sensing field. Although it effectively models global spatial dependencies, it still struggles to capture fine-grained local structures, thereby limiting its representation capability. To overcome this limitation, we propose ChangeMoE, a mixture-of-experts-based Mamba network for BCD from high-resolution remote sensing imagery. The main contributions and innovations are as follows: (1) A scan-specific mixture-of-experts (ScanMoE) module is proposed, which leverages a scan gating network to enhance global feature representations using eight selective scan mechanisms defined as scan-specific experts. We further quantify their contributions to improve the interpretability of global representation learning. (2) A global-and-local mixture-of-experts (GLMoE) module is proposed. We design the local and global expert networks to capture local details and global dependencies. A gating network is used to reveal their relative importance and adaptively fuse their complementary features. Experimental results on the LEVIR-CD and WHU-CD benchmarks validate the superiority of ChangeMoE over existing state-of-the-art networks. ChangeMoE achieves F1-scores of 92.55% and 94.11%, with IoU values of 86.13% and 88.88%, respectively. Compared with ChangeMamba as the baseline, the proposed ChangeMoE achieves improvements of 1.96% in F1-score and 3.33% in IoU on the LEVIR-CD dataset. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed ChangeMoE and provide an interpretable expert-fusion paradigm for understanding feature representation learning in BCD.

title: Flood Hazard and Vulnerability Assessment of Chitrakoot District, Uttar Pradesh: An Integrated Geographical, GIS and Remote Sensing Approach
abstract: Flood is one of the most important hydro-meteorological hazards affecting human settlements, agriculture, infrastructure and regional economies. Chitrakoot district of Uttar Pradesh presents a distinctive case of hydro-climatic vulnerability because it belongs to the drought-prone Bundelkhand region but simultaneously experiences recurrent riverine and flash-flood conditions during intense monsoon rainfall. The present study assesses the spatial characteristics and determinants of flood hazard and vulnerability in Chitrakoot district using an integrated geographical, GIS and remote sensing approach. The analysis incorporates the Digital Elevation Model (DEM), drainage network, physiography, river proximity, historical flood information, satellite-based flood observations and socio-economic exposure. The district's DEM indicates a marked elevation gradient, approximately from 66 m to 451 m, with relatively higher terrain in the southern part and lower terrain towards the northern Yamuna valley. This topographic configuration facilitates rapid surface runoff from elevated southern terrain towards comparatively low-lying riverine areas. The drainage system is dominated by the Yamuna and Mandakini/Paisuni systems along with Baghain, Gunta, Bardaha and smaller tributaries. The Uttar Pradesh Flood Hazard Atlas identifies 5,114 ha of flood-hazard area in Chitrakoot for 1998–2020, of which 4,129 ha (81%) falls in the very-low hazard category and 985 ha (19%) in the low-hazard category. However, the historical classification does not fully represent the potential consequences of extreme rainfall events. The August 2026 flood provides compelling evidence: the Mandakini at Chitrakoot reached a reported new high flood level of 145.60 m on 29 August 2026, approximately 2.95 m above the previous reported high level, while the water level rose by about 7.5 m within six hours. The study concludes that flood risk in Chitrakoot is spatially concentrated around river corridors, low-elevation areas, floodplains, agricultural land, settlements and tourism infrastructure. A shift from conventional relief-oriented flood management towards integrated floodplain regulation, watershed management, GIS-based risk zonation, real-time monitoring and community-based preparedness is therefore essential.

title: Traditional Resource Utilization and Changing Livelihood Patterns Among the Saura Tribe: A Geographical Study of Rayagada District, Odisha
abstract: This geographical study investigates the dynamics of traditional resource utilization and changing livelihood patterns among the Saura tribe in Rayagada district, Odisha. Long recognized for their indigenous soil-water conservation techniques, terraced paddy cultivation (Jhong), and shifting cultivation (Podu), the Saura tribe represents a distinct socio-ecological system deeply integrated into the Eastern Ghats hill ecosystem. Utilizing a mixed-method research design combining multi-stage stratified random sampling (N = 360 households across four tribal development blocks), GIS spatial profiling, field observations, focus group discussions, and econometric modeling, this study examines the trajectory of tribal resource governance from traditional subsistence to market-driven, wage-dependent economies. Empirical findings indicate a significant contraction in forest-based and shifting cultivation livelihoods-decreasing by 34.2% over two decades-alongside a corresponding rise in seasonal distress migration (28.5%), monoculture cashew cash-cropping (22.1 %), and government safety-net dependency under MGNREGA and OTELP.

title: Digital Disruption in Insurance and Skills Development: Advancing the INSETA Mandate: A Conceptual Review of Technology-Driven Workforce Transformation in the Global and African Insurance Sector
abstract: Purpose: This conceptual review examines the forces driving digital disruption in the global and African insurance sectors and evaluates their implications for employment, professional competencies, and talent management, with particular attention to the role of skills-development institutions such as South Africa’s Insurance Sector Education and Training Authority (INSETA). Methodology: Drawing on Human Capital Theory and Dynamic Capabilities Theory, the study synthesizes peer-reviewed literature, industry reports, and institutional publications published predominantly between 2024 and 2026. A qualitative thematic synthesis of secondary sources was employed to identify patterns relating to technological transformation, skills shortages, evolving occupational roles, emerging risks, and institutional responses. Findings: The findings reveal that digital technologies are reshaping insurance operations and creating hybrid professional roles, yet persistent skills gaps, particularly in data analytics, artificial intelligence literacy, cybersecurity, and digital governance, constrain transformation. Regional evidence from Kenya and South Africa indicates that technological investment without corresponding human-capital development yields limited progress. Unique Contribution to Theory, Practice and Policy: The study proposes an integrated talent-intelligence framework that links technological forecasting, competency development, institutional collaboration, and continuous learning. It offers practical guidance for insurers and training providers, and informs policy on aligning education and regulation with digital insurance transformation

title: An Explainable Uncertainty-Weighted Multi-Task Learning Framework for Joint Crop Recommendation and NPK Prediction with Probabilistic Crop Conditioning
abstract: Crop selection and fertilizer planning are of generally based on farmer experience, even though suitable crops and nutrient needs depend on soil and environmental conditions that vary between fields. In many existing systems, crop recommendation and nutrient prediction are handled by separate models, and few explain how reliable a given prediction is. This study proposes a multi-task learning model that predicts the recommended crop and the nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium (NPK) requirement from seven pre crop inputs: soil type, season, soil pH, temperature, water requirement, relative humidity, and water source. A shared network feeds a crop classification head and an NPK regression head. The NPK head receives the full predicted crop probability vector instead of the true crop label, and the two task losses are balanced using learned uncertainty parameters. Monte Carlo Dropout estimates the uncertainty of each prediction, and SHAP shows which inputs drove it. On a dataset of 57,000 observations covering 57 crops, the model reached an accuracy of 0.9496 and a macro F1-score of 0.9463 for crop classification, below Random Forest (0.9627) and XGBoost (0.9618). The mean NPK R² was 0.8537, compared with 0.8518 for XGBoost and 0.8501 for a standalone DNN. The calibration error was 0.0072, and results were stable across five random seeds. SHAP showed that soil type, season, and relative humidity contributed most to both tasks. The trained model was built into a recommendation system that returns a crop, NPK values with uncertainty intervals, and an explanation.
