title: Generative artificial intelligence conversational agents in mental health care: clinical evidence, psychosocial risks and governance. A narrative review
abstract: Introduction: conversational agents based on generative artificial intelligence (AI) are increasingly used for emotional support, largely outside clinical frameworks. Objective: to synthesise the available evidence on the clinical efficacy, the clinical and psychosocial risks, and the governance of generative AI conversational agents in mental health, and to identify implications for clinical practice and health policy. Methods: narrative review based on a non-systematic search of randomised trials, systematic reviews, observational and experimental studies, technical evaluations and regulatory documents, with a qualitative synthesis organised in four areas. Development: in a national survey, 13.1% of US youths aged 12 to 21 reported using generative AI for mental health advice. A meta-analysis of AI-based conversational agents showed reductions in depressive symptoms and distress, and the first randomised trial of a purpose-built generative agent reported greater symptom reduction than a waitlist over four weeks, whereas a pilot trial in Argentina found no significant between-group differences. Documented risks include stigma and inappropriate responses, inconsistent handling of intermediate-risk suicide-related queries, sycophancy, reinforcement of delusional thinking and emotional dependence. Regulation is fragmented: at its November 2025 advisory meeting the US Food and Drug Administration noted that no authorised AI-enabled device used generative AI for mental health conditions, US states have adopted divergent laws, and the European Union AI Act imposes transparency obligations. Conclusions: evidence of benefit comes mainly from purpose-built agents tested in short trials, whereas real-world use relies on general-purpose and companion chatbots. These tools should be considered a complement to, not a substitute for, clinical care, with risk-based regulation, independent auditing, age-appropriate safeguards and trials in Spanish- and Portuguese-speaking populations.

title: Modernizing Pakistan's trade ecosystem: The role of artificial intelligence in digital customs and trade facilitation
abstract: As AI technology evolves, it has opened up new prospects for enhancing customs management and promoting international commerce. Continuous digitalization efforts such as Web-Based One Customs (WeBOC), Pakistan Single Window (PSW), Faceless Customs Assessment (FCA), and Central Appraising Unit (CAU) serve as a starting point for the technological modernization in Pakistan. The present study focuses on how AI can transform the trade landscape in Pakistan, especially in terms of efficiency in digital customs management, trade facilitation, and transparency and compliance. The research method used is a quantitative method with cross sectional survey by the respondents of customs officers, importers, exporters, clearing agents and other trade parties. Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modelling (PLS-SEM) is used to evaluate the proposed relationships using SmartPLS 4. The results revealed that the adoption of AI is statistically significant and positively related to customs operational efficiency, trade facilitation, and transparency and compliance based on simulated data of 250 respondents. The most prominent association with the use of AI is that of customs operational efficiency, followed by trade facilitation and transparency and compliance. The research emphasizes the role of AI-driven solutions in streamlining customs operations, minimizing paperwork, and enhancing regulatory oversight. It also highlights the need for a robust digital infrastructure, institutional capabilities, data quality, and human oversight in the responsible integration of AI. The study offers a template for how AI can be leveraged for a more streamlined, transparent, and competitive trade environment in Pakistan.

title: Prognosis after a new episode of musculoskeletal pain in children and young people, 2005-21: population-based study
abstract: Objective: to estimate reconsultation risk and trajectories after a new episode of musculoskeletal pain in children and young people (CYP), and to determine routinely recorded prognostic factors associated with reconsultation. Design: Population based retrospective cohort study. Setting: Clinical Practice Research Datalink (CPRD) Aurum, 2005-2021. Participants: CYP aged 8-18 years consulting primary care for a new musculoskeletal pain episode (no musculoskeletal consultation in prior 12-months). Main Outcome Measures: Musculoskeletal pain reconsultation within 12-months, and 3-year musculoskeletal reconsultation trajectories derived using latent class growth analysis. Prognostic factors selected from a literature search and two-year symptom histories (sample prevalence >1%) were examined using regression models (conditional logistic; multinomial). Results: Among 313,830 CYP with >12 months' follow-up, 32% reconsulted for musculoskeletal pain within 12 months. Among 240,384 CYP with >3 years' follow-up, three trajectories were observed: single episode (62%), early reconsultation (18%), and persistent reconsultation (20%). Older age; female gender; hip, knee, multisite and back pain on index; previous headache; previous abdominal pain; and analgesic prescribing were associated with higher reconsultation risk. Asian or Black ethnicity, and residing in more deprived areas, were associated with lower recorded reconsultation. Conclusion: Most CYP had no further recorded consultation, but 38% followed early or persistent reconsultation trajectories. Routinely recorded prognostic factors, particularly index pain side and prior pain/symptom history, may differentiate groups who could benefit from proactive follow-up. Lower recorded reconsultation among Asian and Black individuals, and living in more deprived areas, should not imply lower need and warrants equity-sensitive monitoring of access, health-seeking, and coding.

title: A Framework for Clustering and Zero-Shot Labeling of Ecological Images Using Foundation Models
abstract: The increasing automation of biodiversity monitoring is generating large volumes of ecological images requiring taxonomic identification, creating a substantial annotation bottleneck. Assigning species-level labels requires considerable time and expert knowledge, limiting scalability. We propose a framework for unsupervised clustering and zero-shot labeling of ecological images using foundation models. The framework extracts image embeddings from pretrained models and groups images into taxonomic clusters without task-specific training. Species labels are assigned through zero-shot text matching between image embeddings and prompted information representing taxa expected in the dataset. We investigate dimensionality reduction and six clustering algorithms for organizing fine-grained imagery. An uncertainty score combines clustering and labeling information to triage images into three confidence tiers, allowing experts to focus on uncertain or potentially incorrect assignments. The framework is evaluated on four bird and moth datasets, including two annotated camera-trap collections. The camera-trap datasets, per-image species-level accuracy reached 84% on DK-Moth and 83% on HUGO-Bench Aves. An interactive report presents clusters and zero-shot labels by confidence tier and prioritizes cases requiring expert review. The framework provides a training-free approach for organizing and labeling ecological image collections, reducing manual annotation while retaining expert oversight and demonstrating the potential of foundation models for scalable, semi-automated annotation.

title: Asymmetric Okun Models and Unemployment Forecast Risk
abstract: This study evaluates whether asymmetric output growth improves one-quarter-ahead unemployment forecasts and whether any gains persist during major economic disruptions. Quarterly United States data spanning 1948–2024 were analyzed using autoregressive, linear Okun, and asymmetric Okun specifications. Predictive performance was assessed through 160 recursive pseudo-out-of-sample forecasts for 1985–2024, using root mean squared error and mean absolute error, alongside pandemic-related sensitivity analyses. All forecasts used revised historical data, not real-time information sets. Before 2020, the asymmetric model achieved an RMSE of 0.1779 percentage points, outperforming the linear model (0.1886) and autoregressive benchmark (0.1897). Across the full evaluation period, however, asymmetric RMSE increased to 1.1769, exceeding the linear model’s 1.0502. Excluding 2020–2021 forecast targets restored its advantage over the linear model but yielded virtually identical accuracy to the autoregressive benchmark. Retrospectively omitting pandemic observations from estimation improved post-2021 performance, indicating substantial sensitivity to extreme shocks. The results show that statistically detectable output–unemployment asymmetry does not ensure robust predictive improvement. Forecasting applications should retain parsimonious benchmarks and evaluate model stability across contrasting macroeconomic regimes.
journal: International Journal of Economic and Business Research

title: Comparative Evaluation of Machine Learning and Deep Learning Models for Weather Prediction in Nigeria Using Spatial Analysis
abstract: Accurate prediction of meteorological variables is essential for agricultural planning, disaster risk reduction, water resource management, and climate adaptation in Nigeria, where substantial climatic variability exists across diverse ecological zones. This study presents a comparative evaluation of machine learning, deep learning, and spatial analysis techniques for predicting key meteorological variables, namely rainfall, temperature, and relative humidity, using a nationwide daily dataset comprising 270,285 observations collected across the 36 states of Nigeria between 2005 and 2024. Following comprehensive data pre-processing, spatial feature engineering was performed by incorporating geographic coordinates and spatial lag variables. Global Moran's I statistics confirmed significant positive spatial autocorrelation for rainfall, temperature, and humidity, providing empirical justification for integrating spatial information into the predictive models. Five regression models: Random Forest, Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (Bi-LSTM), and Transformer were developed and evaluated using a chronological train-test split. Model performance was assessed using Mean Absolute Error (MAE), Root Mean Square Error (RMSE), the coefficient of determination (R²), confidence intervals, and statistical comparison of prediction errors using the Diebold-Mariano test. An ablation study was further conducted to quantify the contribution of spatial features. Results demonstrated that the Transformer model achieved the best predictive performance (MAE = 1.87 mm, RMSE = 3.98 mm, R² = 0.78), representing approximately a 19% improvement in RMSE over the best-performing machine learning model (XGBoost). The ablation study showed that incorporating spatial features reduced RMSE by between 3.8% and 8.4% across all models, with the Transformer exhibiting the greatest improvement. The findings demonstrate that combining deep learning with spatial analysis substantially enhances weather prediction across Nigeria and provides a robust framework for supporting climate resilience, agricultural decision-making, and operational weather forecasting.
journal: International Journal of Modeling and Applied Science Research

title: Application of the SCS–CN Method Integrated with GIS and Remote Sensing for Watershed Runoff Estimation: A Review
abstract: Accurate estimation of runoff is crucial for watershed planning, soil and water conservation, flood mitigation, and the management of ungauged watersheds. The Soil Conservation Service Curve Number (SCS-CN) method has been extensively used because of its minimal input requirements and its ability to model the spatial influence of land use, soil properties, and hydrologic soil groups. This review compiles applications of the GIS-based SCS-CN method reported for watersheds in semi-arid and monsoon-affected countries such as India, Saudi Arabia, Afghanistan, China, Iraq, and Ethiopia. The reviewed literature employed rainfall data, land-use/land-cover data, soil maps, hydrologic soil groups, digital elevation models, and watershed morphometry to calculate curve numbers and direct runoff. The reported CN values varied substantially, from about 40 under dry conditions to more than 90 under urban, rocky, agricultural, or poorly infiltrating conditions. Runoff estimates ranged from relatively low values in arid catchments to more than 1,300 mm per year in high-rainfall watersheds. Several studies reported high R2 correlations between observed and estimated runoff, typically ranging from 0.73 to 0.98. Important limitations identified in the review include the sensitivity of results to the choice of curve number, antecedent moisture condition, initial abstraction assumption, land-use classification, soil-group assignment, rainfall representation, and the lack of observed discharge data. The overall design of the SCS-CN method and its integration with RS and GIS offer a practical approach to assessing spatial runoff and prioritising watersheds, but the method requires local calibration, uncertainty analysis, and validation against observed rainfall–runoff data.
journal: International Journal of Environment and Climate Change

title: Precision Plant Breeding: Integrating Genome Editing with Artificial Intelligence- A Review
abstract: Precision plant breeding seeks to link biological target discovery with the development and evaluation of useful alleles in crop improvement. Genome-editing platforms, including CRISPR–Cas nucleases, base editors, prime editors, multiplex editing and cis-regulatory editing, enable targeted genomic alterations; however, their successful use depends on appropriate target choice, editing performance and phenotypic validation. Artificial intelligence (AI) offers complementary approaches for integrating pangenomic, multi-omics, phenotypic and environmental data to prioritise genes and regulatory sequences, predict guide-RNA activity and off-target effects, and support selection across genetic backgrounds and environments. This review examines the potential of combining these methods within a design–build–test–learn framework that connects edit design with molecular verification, high-throughput phenotyping, genomic prediction and conventional breeding operations. Examples discussed include susceptibility-gene and promoter editing for disease resistance, regulatory interventions associated with stress responses, nutritional modification and the emerging application of AI-designed nucleases in rice. Although these advances demonstrate technical feasibility, widespread implementation remains constrained by plant-specific data scarcity, differences among genotypes and environments, transformation and regeneration bottlenecks, complex trait architecture, unintended editing outcomes and regulatory diversity. The review emphasises prospective model validation, causal interpretation, pangenome-aware design, rigorous molecular characterisation and replicated field evaluation. It concludes that AI-guided genome editing can support crop improvement when used alongside quantitative genetics, breeder-defined objectives and responsible governance, rather than as a substitute for empirical breeding evidence.
journal: Journal of Advances in Biology & Biotechnology

title: Atlas-Guided CD55-Enriched Neutrophil Extracellular Vesicles for Complement-Macrophage Modulation in Diabetic Wounds.
abstract: Diabetic wounds are characterized by persistent inflammation and impaired immune resolution, yet the therapeutic translation of single‐cell atlases into rational immunomodulatory strategies remains limited. Here, integration of diabetic‐wound single‐cell transcriptomic datasets identifies a neutrophil subpopulation enriched in cluster of differentiation 55 (CD55) with complement‐regulatory and reparative features. Guided by this atlas‐derived signature, activated neutrophil‐derived extracellular vesicles (aNEVs) enriched in CD55 are generated under high‐glucose and lipopolysaccharide stimulation and incorporated into a microbial transglutaminase‐crosslinked gelatin hydrogel for localized delivery and protease‐sensitive matrix remodeling. The resulting gelatin/aNEV composite hydrogel (Gel/aNEV) attenuates complement‐associated inflammatory signaling, C3a production, oxidative stress, and pro‐inflammatory cytokine expression, while promoting reparative macrophage reprogramming and endothelial migration. In diabetic wounds, a single application of Gel/aNEV accelerates wound closure and enhances angiogenesis, collagen remodeling, and tissue regeneration. Integrated transcriptomic–proteomic analyses further reveal coordinated changes in complement, inflammatory, redox, extracellular‐matrix, and regenerative programs, supporting a multicomponent therapeutic model. Collectively, this study establishes an atlas‐to‐therapy framework that uses disease‐associated neutrophil states to guide extracellular‐vesicle engineering, integrating complement regulation, immune reprogramming, and biomaterial‐assisted delivery for diabetic wound repair.

title: Gut Microbiota-Derived Indole-3-Acetaldehyde Contributes to the Disease-Alleviating Effects of Kurarinone in Experimental Autoimmune Encephalomyelitis.
abstract: Multiple sclerosis (MS) is a central nervous system autoimmune disease primarily driven by Th1 and Th17 cells, whose onset and progression are closely associated with gut microbiota. Kurarinone (KU), an active component from Radix Sophora Flavescens, exhibits anti‐inflammatory, immunoregulatory and gut microbiota‐modulating properties. However, whether KU alleviates MS severity via a gut microbiota‐mediated mechanism remains unclear. Here, we demonstrate that KU ameliorates experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis (EAE)‐an animal model of MS‐by modulating the gut microbiota, particularly via enriching Akkermansia muciniphila, and A. muciniphila is essential for the protective effects of KU in EAE. Furthermore, KU elevates levels of the tryptophan metabolite indole‐3‐acetaldehyde (IAAld). IAAld levels are positively correlated with the relative abundance of A. muciniphila and negatively correlated with EAE severity. In vitro, A. muciniphila alone is sufficient to facilitate tryptophan metabolism to produce IAAld. IAAld treatment ameliorates EAE and reduces the frequencies of pathogenic Th1 and Th17 cells in mice. Mechanistically, IAAld activates the aryl hydrocarbon receptor (AhR) and suppresses JAK/STAT signaling, thereby dampening Th1 and Th17 differentiation; these effects are abolished following AhR blockade. Collectively, this study identifies a novel mechanism by which KU mitigates EAE via the gut metabolite IAAld‐AhR‐immune axis and unveils potential therapeutic targets for MS.

title: Modeling diseased xylem networks.
abstract: Vascular wilt pathogens induce xylem blockages that disrupt plant water transport, posing critical threats to agricultural productivity and food security. Key processes including xylem transport, vessel blockage, and pathogen spread within the xylem remain poorly understood, largely due to our limited ability to internally monitor infected tissues. This review explores how complementary mathematical modeling alongside laboratory studies can elucidate features governing these critical processes. I first provide a brief history of xylem imaging and quantification, highlighting technological advances, and persistent limitations. I then review modeling approaches to describe xylem water transport and pathogen dynamics, emphasizing that different pathogens require fundamentally different modeling frameworks. Existing xylem flow models may provide suitable hydraulic conductivity estimates for healthy stems under idealized conditions; however, they lack explicit representation of pit membranes and lumen-occluding structures, limiting their applicability to diseased stems where these features are actively modified during infection. Previously described biofilm models can replicate bacterial colony growth in controlled experimental settings but are often too complex for integration with flow simulations and rely on parameters that are difficult to quantify experimentally. Finally, I highlight directions and challenges for modeling occlusion and spread at the local scale and discuss how these models might be scaled to network-level architecture. While these types of models remain computationally challenging, advances in multiscale imaging technologies and scaling approaches promise significant progress in the coming decades. Insights from such models stand to advance both our understanding of disease progression and the development of resilient crops for an uncertain climate future.

title: AR: An Artificial Intelligence‐Driven Fluorescent Reporter System for Gene Editing Evaluation
abstract: Accurate and scalable evaluation of gene‐editing efficiency is crucial for the development of novel editing tools. However, conventional methods are laborious, costly, and low‐throughput. Here, we developed an artificial intelligence (AI)‐driven fluorescent reporter (AR) platform, an integrated system that automates and streamlines the entire evaluation workflow. The AR platform combines an enhanced fluorescent reporter with an AI‐driven analytical pipeline. The dual‐fluorescence reporter system, in which mCherry carrying a PEST domain is paired with GFP, supports Cas variants with diverse PAM requirements and quantifies editing efficiency as the proportion of GFP‐only cells. The platform's AI module, EasyReporter, integrates a deep learning model for automated cell segmentation and quantification with a large language model (LLM)‐based agent for intelligent data interpretation and comprehensive report generation. Editing efficiencies measured by AR correlated with those measured by flow cytometry (Spearman ρ = 0.77) and amplicon sequencing (Spearman ρ = 0.83). The AR platform provides a high‐throughput and automated workflow that accelerates gene‐editing research. In the future, it will be particularly effective for quantifying the efficiency of large‐fragment gene editing, offering a new framework for AI‐empowered biological laboratories.

title: Allogeneic Human Bone Marrow-Derived Mesenchymal Stem Cells Accelerate Diabetic Wound Healing via Inflammation Suppression and Angiogenesis Promotion: A Preclinical Study.
abstract: Mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs) have been shown to enhance tissue regeneration and wound healing. This preclinical study investigated the therapeutic potential of human bone marrow-derived mesenchymal stem cells (hBM-MSCs) for accelerating diabetic wound healing. Isolated hBM-MSCs were characterized for surface marker expression and differentiation potential. Their migration-promoting effects were evaluated in vitro. For the in vivo study, a dorsal skin defect model was created in streptozotocin (STZ)-induced diabetic rats. Rats received periwound subcutaneous injections of low- or high-dose hBM-MSCs on Days 4 and 7, or freezing fluid as a vehicle control. Wound healing progression was assessed clinically, and tissue biopsies were analyzed using immunohistochemistry to evaluate inflammatory cell infiltration, cellular proliferation, and angiogenesis. hBM-MSCs exhibited the expected surface marker profile and multilineage differentiation potential. In vitro, hBM-MSCs significantly enhanced the migration of human umbilical vein endothelial cells and human foreskin fibroblasts. In vivo, wounds treated with hBM-MSCs showed significantly accelerated healing compared to vehicle-treated controls (p < 0.05). Immunohistochemical analysis revealed reduced inflammatory cell infiltration and increased expression of Ki-67, epidermal growth factor (EGF), vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF), and prolyl 4-hydroxylase (P4H) in hBM-MSC-treated wounds. Allogeneic hBM-MSCs significantly promote diabetic wound healing by suppressing inflammation, enhancing cellular proliferation and differentiation, and stimulating angiogenesis. These findings highlight the therapeutic potential of allogeneic hBM-MSCs for treating diabetic wounds, particularly in patients unsuitable for autologous cell therapy.

title: Harnessing Artificial Intelligence to Predict Dental Crowding in Modern Orthodontic Practice: A Comprehensive Review.
abstract: Dental crowding is fundamental to orthodontic diagnosis and treatment planning, yet what constitutes “crowding” remains surprisingly heterogeneous. Space analysis quantifies tooth size–arch length discrepancy, irregularity indices characterize alignment displacement, and clinician‐assigned severity reflects broader diagnostic interpretation. This narrative review examines the evolution of crowding assessment from conventional space analysis and digital measurement to two‐dimensional artificial intelligence (AI), three‐dimensional point‐cloud learning, and clinician‐aware agentic AI. Digitalization improves efficiency and reproducibility but does not resolve fundamental dependencies on how crowding is defined, anatomically represented, and established as a reference standard. Two‐dimensional models enable prediction from readily available images but are constrained by projection and scale, whereas three‐dimensional approaches directly learn from dental surface representations and can capture local geometric relationships. In a companion study of 495 arches from 284 patients, PointNet++ achieved an R 2 of 0.718 and a mean absolute error (MAE) of 1.54 mm for prediction of crowding. In a separate retrospective demonstration, a bounded Gemini‐based Agent incorporating matched record‐derived verbal information reduced MAE from 1.951 to 1.437 mm, whereas mismatched information degraded performance. These findings also illustrate that the target construct—the specific clinical feature of crowding that a model is trained to predict—may differ across assessment methods. Together, these findings highlight a fundamental challenge: improving prediction does not resolve ambiguity in the target construct. Future crowding AI should therefore align the target construct, reference standard, and input representation; preserve provenance and uncertainty; integrate complementary clinical information transparently; and route uncertain cases for expert review.

title: A Global Checklist of Disease‐Causing Organisms of Camellia sinensis (Theaceae, Tea Plant)
abstract: Tea is one of the most widely consumed non‐alcoholic beverages. The tea industry plays a significant role in supporting the economies of producing countries and provides livelihoods for millions of people, especially in rural areas. Diseases affecting the tea plant ( Camellia sinensis (L.) Kuntze) are a critical concern, as they reduce crop yield and quality. Information on disease‐causing organisms in tea is scattered across the literature, making it difficult for farmers, researchers, and policymakers to comprehensively assess the full spectrum of pathogens, understand their epidemiology, and to develop integrated disease management strategies. The aim of the present checklist is to provide a comprehensive summary of phytopathogens reported to affect tea, including fungi, bacteria, viruses, algae, and other groups, based on information compiled from research and review articles, books and book chapters, monographs, first disease reports, web resources, and previously published checklists. Here, we report the taxonomic diversity and associated diseases of tea phytopathogens, documenting 188 species affecting foliar, stem, and root tissues. The fungi and fungus‐like pathogens (173 species) belong mainly to Ascomycota (142 species), followed by Basidiomycota (29 species) and Oomycota (2 species), and are represented by 49 families. Additional pathogens include 10 bacterial species, 3 viral and 2 algal pathogens. Most pathogens are associated with foliar tissues, with majority of reports originating from mainland China. Outdated nomenclature used in earlier publications was critically reviewed, and updated taxonomic classifications are provided. However, the taxonomy of several pathogens for which molecular data are lacking requires further re‐evaluation particularly through molecular studies of samples collected from other tea‐growing regions. This checklist provides a global overview of tea phytopathogens and serves as a valuable resource for disease management and future taxonomic and molecular research.

title: A composite, host‐participatory haustorium links host compatibility to defence bifurcation in Alectra vogelii (Orobanchaceae)
abstract: Parasitic weeds of the family Orobanchaceae are among the most damaging constraints on food production in the tropics, draining water and nutrients from their hosts and threatening the livelihoods of millions of smallholder farmers. Yellow witchweed ( Alectra vogelii ) can destroy entire legume harvests across sub‐Saharan Africa, where these crops are a primary source of dietary protein and household income. By revealing how a compatible host enables this parasite to develop, our work pinpoints the developmental and metabolic steps that turn an attachment into a damaging infection—knowledge that can guide the breeding of resistant crops and the design of more sustainable, targeted control of parasitic weeds. Yellow witchweed ( Alectra vogelii Benth., Orobanchaceae) is an obligate hemiparasitic weed and a major pest of grain legumes across sub‐Saharan Africa, where it causes severe crop losses and threatens smallholder food security, yet its developmental biology and mechanisms of host compatibility remain poorly understood. By combining phenotypic, anatomical and transcriptomic analyses, we show that host compatibility in Alectra is expressed primarily through post‐attachment developmental progression rather than attachment success alone. Matched‐stage comparisons reveal accelerated development on compatible hosts and profound reorganisation in the host–parasite interface region, characterised by host tissue proliferation, vascular integration and coordinated transcriptional programmes spanning both host and parasite, whereas incompatible interactions are dominated by defence and reinforcement responses that constrain parasite growth. Notably, compatible interactions are associated with early activation of photosynthesis‐related programmes, indicating a transition towards metabolic autonomy that is supported by enhanced nutrient acquisition and internal recycling. Predictive modelling further identifies pathway‐level transcriptional states associated with successful development and reinforces the view that compatibility reflects systems‐level integration rather than parasite gene expression alone. These findings position the Alectra haustorium as a dynamic, host‐participatory composite organ central to host compatibility and highlight post‐attachment integration, metabolic reprogramming and autophagy‐related processes as key determinants of developmental success.

title: [Effects of climate change and weather on physical activity].
abstract: From a public health perspective, the health-promoting potential of physical activity is already not being fully utilized. Rising temperatures and other climate changes could further exacerbate existing physical inactivity. This narrative review therefore examines the relevance of climate and weather to physical activity and how climate change could affect physical activity patterns in the future.Numerous retrospective studies demonstrate, in particular, the importance of air temperature. While rising outdoor temperatures promote physical activity up to a certain point, activity levels decline again at high temperatures. Studies also show that physical activity during acute heat waves can be significantly reduced. The typical inverted U‑shaped relationship between air temperature and physical activity peaks at approximately 26 °C to 29 °C. However, it is influenced by other climatic elements as well as individual, temporal, and spatial factors, which complicates forecasts of future physical activity patterns. While physical activity can be modeled well retrospectively, projections therefore yield varying and sometimes contradictory results.It remains unclear at this point over what time periods and in what settings ongoing climate change will lead, overall, to an increase or a decrease in physical activity-for example, in Germany. Regardless, prevention strategies such as heat action plans and model heat protection plans should aim to counteract a further exacerbation of existing physical inactivity, particularly among vulnerable groups during the summer and heat waves.

AI-driven early warning of psychological crisis in college students using network theory and few-shot learning through survey-parameterized simulation
abstract: Psychological crises among college students are often detected too late because current practice relies on periodic screening that is passive and infrequent. This paper proposes an AI-driven early-warning framework that organizes multi-source campus behavioral traces into a three-layer student–behavior–space–time heterogeneous dynamic graph. A heterogeneous graph neural network with hierarchical and temporal attention detects behavioral-pattern drift preceding a crisis, while graph contrastive pre-training and few-shot fine-tuning yield a student-specific dynamic behavioral representation from scarce crisis-positive labels; the risk score is decomposed into behavioral-dimension attributions for counselors. Evaluation uses a survey-parameterized simulation: eight thousand synthetic student records generated from distributions calibrated to the desensitized behavioral records of 316 real students, with a field-survey-parameterized crisis-generating mechanism applied to sixty designated cases. The method achieves an AUPRC of 0.249, recall of 0.607, and average lead time of 2.79 weeks, ahead of all baselines; ablation attributes most gain to contrastive pre-training and heterogeneous representation. Against stronger competitors the advantage narrows, and against four additional crisis-generating mechanisms evaluated with the model frozen, it persists when the signature carries relational and directionally persistent structure but disappears otherwise. An information-flow audit shows discriminative ability persisting to roughly two weeks ahead and flooring beyond three, indicating detection of ongoing deterioration rather than forecasting of future decline. At recall 0.700 the alert load reaches 8.2 per counselor per week; the framework is accordingly a methodological contribution, not a validated system for real crises.

Don’t Blame the Code! AI Paternalism Reconsidered
abstract: AI-driven diagnostic and therapeutic systems are being rapidly integrated into clinical practice. A growing literature contends that this integration threatens patient autonomy by exposing patients to a novel form of AI paternalism. I argue that this framing is misguided on both theoretical and practical grounds. Theoretically, AI systems cannot be paternalists: their outputs lack the normative and agential standing that paternalism requires – a limitation I articulate as the is–ought gap for AI-generated output. Any paternalistic force in AI-integrated care must therefore reside in human agents, not in the systems themselves. Hence, we should not blame the code for any paternalism that patients may be subjected to in AI-integrated healthcare, but rather the human agents who purpose and develop these systems. In addition to these theoretical and conceptual concerns, there are practical worries. Casting AI integration as a case of paternalism risks framing the use of AI as prima facie objectionable and channels the debate toward a narrow, binary remedy that leans heavily on algorithmic transparency as a prerequisite for informed consent and shared decision-making. These discussions, I argue, are better served by revising our underlying conception of autonomy itself. I therefore conclude this article by arguing that replacing traditional, individualist conceptions of autonomy with a relational account better captures the distributed, socially embedded character of decision-making in AI-integrated care. This also redirects normative attention from the prevention of paternalism toward the conditions under which patient autonomy can be actively enabled and promoted.

Lekking without color differences: a case of monochromatism in a tropical flycatcher
abstract: Lekking birds are often associated with conspicuous plumage and pronounced sexual dichromatism, yet some species exhibit little or no visible differentiation between sexes. We investigated whether the olive-striped flycatcher (Mionectes galbinus), a Neotropical lekking tyrannid, exhibits sexual differences in plumage coloration. A total of 48 adult museum specimens of the subspecies Mionectes galbinus heredaceus (18 females and 30 males) from the Vertebrate Collection_Birds (CVA-UV) of the Department of Biology, Universidad del Valle (Cali, Colombia), were analyzed. Reflectance spectra were measured for four body regions, and plumage coloration was evaluated using colorimetric variables and avian visual models. Reflectance spectra showed similar patterns between sexes, with no significant differences in coloration. MANOVA detected no significant sex differences, and modeled chromatic distances remained below 2 JND. These results support functional monochromatism in the studied population of Mionectes galbinus heredaceus and add to growing evidence that lekking species may exhibit limited or absent plumage dichromatism.

title: Drivers of CO₂ emissions in Africa: corruption perceptions, foreign aid, economic growth, and globalization
AI-driven multi-agent digital twin conceptual framework for real-time domestic water quality monitoring, purification and smart billing
abstract: Access to safe drinking water remains a critical global challenge, with over 2.2 billion people lacking reliable access despite water’s abundance, as only 3% of Earth’s water is freshwater. Current systems suffer from unreliable analog metering, tampering risks, and the absence of real-time platforms for monitoring quality, consumption, purification and billing—creating a literature gap in scalable, integrated, and intelligent water management solutions. To address this situation, a pilot-scale, machine learning–enabled multi-agent digital twin-inspired framework is developed for domestic water systems, integrating IoT sensors to continuously monitor key parameters (pH, turbidity, temperature, flow, and TDS); purification status; and employing predictive models for anomaly detection and forecasting. Among several tested algorithms (ARIMA, autoregression, and additive regression), additive regression demonstrated comparatively better performance under the constraints of the pilot dataset, relatively low error rates were achieved under evaluation conditions for temperature, pH, flow, pressure, TDS and color. The system links to a web-based platform providing real-time visualization, automated billing, and user alerts, while incorporating an integrated purification module capable of reducing heavy metals and microbial load with above 96.96% accuracy. These actions result in a compact end-to-end prototype framework that demonstrates the feasibility of safe real-time water use under controlled conditions while improving accountability, reducing billing errors, and promoting conservation through predictive alerts. The novelty lies in the seamless integration of IoT sensing, ML-driven analytics, purification, and digital billing into a pilot-scale integrated digital twin framework. This system offers future prospects for deployment in smart city infrastructures, enhanced resilience through cybersecurity integration, and alignment with SDG 6 (Clean Water and Sanitation), indicating its potential as a future step toward scalable water management solutions. However, the system is validated under limited pilot-scale deployment conditions, and further large-scale validation is required.

title: Dimensionality reduction of atmospheric concentration fields using a 3D convolutional autoencoder with spatial attention mechanism
abstract: High-dimensional atmospheric chemistry simulations produce volumetric concentration fields that are costly to store and repeatedly process in inverse-modelling and data-assimilation workflows. This study evaluates reduced representations for CO concentration fields from WRF-Chem over Novosibirsk and CAMS over Europe. We propose a three-dimensional convolutional autoencoder with a lightweight spatial attention module (SAM3D) and compare it with linear, spectral, tensor-based, interpolation, manifold-learning, and neural-network baselines. The evaluation includes latent dimensions from 8 to 64, temporally separated validation protocols, storage-cost estimates, and computational-efficiency measurements. On the larger CAMS dataset, SAM3D achieves the lowest MSE and relative \documentclass[12pt]{minimal} \usepackage{amsmath} \usepackage{wasysym} \usepackage{amsfonts} \usepackage{amssymb} \usepackage{amsbsy} \usepackage{mathrsfs} \usepackage{upgreek} \setlength{\oddsidemargin}{-69pt} \begin{document}$$L_2$$\end{document} error among methods compared at equal latent-vector dimensions and improves over the plain 3D autoencoder. On the smaller WRF-Chem dataset, rankings depend more strongly on the split protocol, with fixed transforms and tensor decompositions remaining competitive. SAM3D adds less than 1% FLOPs and only a small increase in model size while retaining a differentiable encoder–decoder mapping. These results support SAM3D as a practical reduced-state representation for three-dimensional atmospheric concentration fields.

title: Content associations with answer selection and engagement in supply chain community question answering
abstract: Community question-answering (cQA) platforms are important ecosystems for knowledge sharing, yet research on what makes an answer “best” or a question engaging has often focused on either individual lexical features or broad topics. This exploratory study examines both levels in Yahoo! Chiebukuro, asking which nouns and semantic noun clusters are associated with best-answer selection and question engagement. We analyze a large corpus of questions and answer-tier posts collected under the keyword “logistics,” using an offline machine-translation pipeline with manually validated noun-level fidelity. Best-answer selection is modeled with conditional logistic regression within question threads, controlling for answer length, order, and question-answer noun overlap. Engagement is modeled in two stages: whether a question receives any response and, conditional on receiving one, how many responses it attracts. Operational logistics nouns such as “distribution,” “warehouse,” and “center” are associated with best-answer selection, whereas broader civic and infrastructure nouns such as “car,” “tax,” and “shinkansen” are associated with higher engagement. At the cluster level, most semantic noun clusters are associated with best-answer selection, while the clusters associated with response likelihood and response volume are largely distinct. These findings reveal differentiated content-outcome profiles across answer and question levels and provide a domain-wide descriptive map of engagement and answer selection in logistics-related cQA discourse.

title: Digital twin forestry as an informatics framework integrating remote sensing ecosystem modelling and data assimilation
abstract: Forests are essential to the Earth system, regulating carbon, water, and biodiversity cycles while underpinning ecosystem resilience. Yet they face mounting pressures from climate and land-use change, requiring integrative informatics approaches that link high-resolution observations with advanced ecosystem models. This systematic review defines Digital Twin Forestry (DTF) as an emerging paradigm that continuously couples multisensor Earth Observation data with ecosystem models through data assimilation, enabling dynamic, uncertainty-aware forecasting and adaptive decision support. Following PRISMA 2020 guidelines, we synthesized 57 peer-reviewed studies published between 2016 and 2025 that combined EO datasets with ecosystem modeling and assimilation frameworks. Demonstrated advances include CubeSat constellations, spaceborne LiDAR, UAV hyperspectral systems, and hybrid machine-learning surrogates. Data assimilation methods such as Ensemble Kalman Filters and Particle Filters serve as computational bridges between multi-temporal observations and dynamic model states. Results reveal uneven biome representation, with tropical and boreal forests underrepresented compared to temperate zones, underscoring equity concerns in biodiversity-rich regions. While most forestry digital twins remain at prototype or early operational stages, continuous coupling of sensing platforms to models demonstrates the potential for near-real-time forecasting that extends beyond static inventories. Future priorities include physics-informed machine learning, FAIR-compliant cloud-native workflows, and expanded monitoring in underrepresented ecosystems. Embedding biodiversity and resilience monitoring into near-real-time, uncertainty-aware workflows will be critical, enabling DTF to evolve into operational systems that provide adaptive, policy-relevant decision support for climate-resilient forest management. This review offers an integrative roadmap for advancing DTF, contributing to global sustainability and supporting the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals, including Climate Action (SDG 13) and Life on Land (SDG 15).

title: The Carbon Footprint of Clinical Artificial Intelligence in Anaesthesiology: An Order-of-Magnitude Comparison with Current Clinical Practice.
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is rapidly reshaping anaesthesiology and critical care, enhancing physiological monitoring, perioperative risk prediction, and clinical decision-making. As its adoption accelerates, attention has increasingly turned to the environmental consequences of digital healthcare, raising important questions regarding the energy consumption and carbon footprint associated with clinical AI. This study examines the environmental implications of AI in anaesthesiology and critical care by placing computational emissions within the broader context of healthcare sustainability. Current evidence indicates that, although AI systems generate measurable greenhouse gas emissions, their operational carbon footprint remains several orders of magnitude lower than that of established sources of emissions, including volatile anaesthetic agents, intensive care, and surgical care. Quantitative comparisons, complemented by an illustrative environmental break-even analysis, suggest that even modest improvements in healthcare efficiency may be sufficient to offset the operational emissions of current clinical AI applications. These findings indicate that the sustainability of clinical AI should not be judged solely by its computational footprint, but by its overall environmental value. The relevant question is not simply how much AI emits, but whether its implementation reduces resource utilisation, avoids unnecessary healthcare activities, and generates environmental savings that outweigh its own operational costs. Achieving this objective will require computationally efficient model design, low-carbon digital infrastructures, lifecycle assessment, and the routine integration of environmental metrics into AI evaluation. Rather than representing a major new source of healthcare emissions, clinical AI should be viewed as an opportunity to advance both digital innovation and environmental stewardship. By integrating sustainability alongside clinical effectiveness, anaesthesiologists are uniquely positioned to guide the responsible development and implementation of AI technologies that benefit both patients and the healthcare systems in which they are delivered.

title: Mammography and Ultrasonography for Symptomatic Male Breast Lesions: A PRISMA-DTA Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
abstract: RATIONALE AND OBJECTIVES Male breast disease is uncommon, but symptomatic men require reliable differentiation between benign conditions and lesions warranting biopsy or oncologic management. This PRISMA-DTA (Preferred Reporting Items for a Systematic Review and Meta-analysis of Diagnostic Test Accuracy Studies) systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated the diagnostic accuracy, clinical utility, and evidentiary limitations of mammography and ultrasonography for malignant versus benign male breast lesions. MATERIALS AND METHODS PubMed, Embase, Web of Science Core Collection, and Scopus were searched from inception to May 30, 2026. The protocol was registered in PROSPERO before journal submission (CRD420261429183). Eligible reports evaluated mammography or ultrasonography in male breast disease and provided extractable 2 × 2 diagnostic data. Methodological quality was assessed using Quality Assessment of Diagnostic Accuracy Studies-2. Diagnostic accuracy was synthesized separately for each modality using bivariate random-effects modeling and summary receiver operating characteristic analysis. RESULTS Thirteen eligible reports were included. Seven mammography datasets and five ultrasonography datasets were available for quantitative synthesis. Mammography showed a pooled sensitivity of 0.840 (95% confidence interval [CI], 0.705-0.921) and a specificity of 0.951 (95% CI, 0.884-0.980), whereas ultrasonography showed a pooled sensitivity of 0.881 (95% CI, 0.775-0.941) and a specificity of 0.958 (95% CI, 0.869-0.987). Although pooled specificity estimates were high, their magnitude may have been influenced by heterogeneous diagnostic thresholds, differential verification, variable follow-up, and sparse malignant case counts. Nine of 13 reports were judged to have an overall high risk of bias, and consistent paired head-to-head data were lacking. CONCLUSION Current evidence supports mammography and ultrasonography as complementary tools in risk-stratified assessment of symptomatic male breast lesions. Pooled estimates should be interpreted cautiously because the evidence base is small and methodologically limited. Current data do not establish direct modality superiority, do not justify biopsy avoidance when clinical-imaging discordance persists, and do not determine the incremental value of routine combined imaging.

Cross-cohort transfer of clinical Alzheimer's EEG signatures to cognitively healthy APOE-ε4 and PICALM rs3851179 risk carriers using differentiable logic gate networks.
abstract: Neural alterations associated with Alzheimer's disease (AD) may emerge years before clinical diagnosis, and genetic risk factors such as APOE-ε4 and PICALM rs3851179 may identify individuals vulnerable to these shifts. We tested whether electroencephalography (EEG) signatures learned from clinically diagnosed AD patients transfer to cognitively healthy middle-aged adults carrying these variants. Differentiable logic gate networks (Diff-Logic) and neural baselines were trained on log-relative power spectral density features from a clinical cohort of AD patients and cognitively normal (CN) controls. These models were then applied without retraining to an independent genetic-risk cohort of neutral-risk non-carriers (N), APOE-ε4-only carriers (A+P-), and dual APOE-ε4/PICALM G-allele carriers (A+P+), yielding a continuous AD-like EEG signature score per participant. Diff-Logic matched neural baselines in clinical classification (balanced accuracy 0.809±0.028; AUROC 0.845±0.023) while enabling edge inference with a 7.4× model-size reduction and 0.22 ms model-only latency on a 7 W single-core CPU. In the genetic-risk cohort, scores were highest in A+P+ participants (0.393±0.167) relative to N (0.296±0.154) and A+P- (0.285±0.143; subject-level mean ± SD). This elevation was nominally significant before correction (A+P+ vs. A+P-, punc=0.036) but did not survive Holm correction (pHolm=0.109), and the cohort carried no AD pathology or conversion ground truth; the association was therefore exploratory. Integrated gradients attribution of the trained model showed genetic-risk relevance in delta, theta, and alpha, partially overlapping clinical AD topography. These findings support the feasibility of zero-shot EEG transfer in genetically at-risk individuals and highlight the need for replication in larger cohorts. Code is publicly available at https://github.com/Shyamal-Dharia/ad-difflogic-transfer.

A large-scale climate-aware satellite image dataset for domain adaptive land-cover semantic segmentation
abstract: A few well-annotated datasets for land-cover semantic segmentation have recently been introduced to advance the field of earth observation technologies. However, these datasets overlook the significant diversity among geographic areas with different climates, which can greatly impact and diversify land cover. Consequently, this leads to a domain gap in remote sensing images and severe performance degradation of the segmentation models. To enhance land-cover semantic segmentation with improved generalization ability, we conducted the first investigation into the impact of climate on this task. In this paper, we present a unique large-scale Climate-Aware Satellite Images Dataset (CASID) specifically designed for domain adaptive land-cover semantic segmentation. It consists of 980 satellite images with a size of 5000 x 5000 pixels, collected from 30 different regions around Asia, covering over 24,500 square kilometers. These images are gathered from four distinct climate zones, namely temperate monsoon, subtropical monsoon, tropical monsoon, and tropical rainforest. It includes four sub-datasets/domains, each representing one of the aforementioned climate zones. This characteristic makes CASID the first climate-aware land-cover semantic segmentation dataset with multiple domains. Additionally, we provide a comprehensive analysis of the samples from the four climate zones, emphasizing differences in global image features, image texture, category distribution, spectral value, and object shape. These analyses offer valuable insights for subsequent research in this field. Moreover, we conduct extensive experiments to evaluate the latest semantic segmentation and unsupervised domain adaptation methods on the CASID dataset. These results serve as a robust baseline for future research endeavors. Our dataset will be made publicly available at https://github.com/Linwei-Chen/CASID.
