title: Pharmacophore Modelling-Based Screening of Natural Allosteric EGFR Inhibitors Using Molecular Docking, DFT, and Molecular Dynamics Simulations
journal: Journal of Molecular Graphics and Modelling
abstract: The development of allosteric inhibitors is a promising strategy for targeting epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) mutations in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), especially in cases where orthosteric inhibitors face resistance. However, despite their selective inhibition of EGFR mutations, fourth-generation allosteric inhibitors show limited antiproliferative efficacy without cetuximab. The present study aims to identify potent natural product-derived allosteric inhibitors for NSCLC using a comprehensive approach, including pharmacophore modelling, Lipinski's Rule of Five (Ro5), ADMET profiling, density functional theory, and molecular docking. Experimentally validated EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs) were used to build a pharmacophore model. The validated pharmacophore model was used to screen the Natural Product Activity and Species Source database. Drug-likeness was assessed using Ro5 and ADMET to predict pharmacokinetic and toxicity profiles for further drug development. Molecular docking studies revealed that the identified natural compounds exhibited more favorable docking scores (-8.74 to -7.87 kcal/mol) than the co-crystallized ligand (-7.32 kcal/mol), indicating significant interactions with the receptor residues. Geometry optimization, electrostatic potential, and frontier molecular orbital analyses were performed to assess potential reactive sites and molecular stability. Molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, subsequent post-MD analyses, and binding free energy calculations provided additional support for these findings. The free-energy landscape revealed stable, favorable binding conformations, suggesting that they may act as allosteric inhibitors. These results highlight the potential of natural compounds to combat resistance to EGFR-TKIs in NSCLC. In particular, compounds 1 and 2 emerged as promising candidates targeting mutant EGFR and warrant further experimental validation as potential leads for NSCLC treatment.

title: Prolonged Transient Persistence of Polygenic Polymorphism under Stabilizing Selection Alone.
abstract: In evolutionary theories of quantitative traits, a mutation-selection balance is essential to preserve polymorphism, where stabilizing selection is widely considered to eliminate genetic variation at underlying loci. To isolate the role of selection, we re-examine the effect of stabilizing selection on genetic polymorphism in a mathematically rigorous manner. Following the classical stabilizing-selection model, we explicitly decompose the population mean μ across all n contributing loci, transforming the model within a n-dimensional dynamical system. The fully polymorphic stationarity equations have a unique algebraic candidate, which is a biologically feasible interior equilibrium if and only if all its components lie in (0,1). Linearization at the equilibrium point reveals a saddle-point structure: under equal allelic effects, exactly one eigenvalue is negative, and n-1 eigenvalues are positive. Under equal allelic effects, the linear stable and unstable eigenspaces are Es=span{1} and Eu=ker(1T), respectively; the corresponding local nonlinear invariant manifolds are tangent to these spaces at p*. The stable mode restores the population mean toward the equilibrium value μ*, which need not equal the optimum θ, whereas the unstable modes are mean-neutral to first order. The relative rate ratio |λs|/λu=2n-1 shows that collective relaxation is faster than locus differentiation, while the absolute local residence time is controlled by λu and the initial unstable displacement. A nonzero unstable component causes local departure from the fully polymorphic saddle, but the local analysis does not classify the global limiting state. In the full nonlinear system, the non-trivial equilibrium is not asymptotically stable. Simulations show that escape from the polymorphic neighborhood is substantially delayed, producing long finite-time persistence of polymorphism. Consequently, the saddle geometry can generate potentially long deterministic finite-time persistence of polygenic polymorphism, but it does not provide asymptotically stable or finite-population maintenance in the absence of mutation.

title: Pre-driven and post-gated memristive Hopfield network: Dynamics, FPGA realization and image encryption.
abstract: Many existing memristive synaptic models merge presynaptic and postsynaptic activities into a single aggregated stimulus, making their distinct functional roles difficult to interpret. To address this issue, this paper proposes a memristive synapse with a pre-driven and post-gated state-update mechanism, in which presynaptic activity drives synaptic-state evolution while postsynaptic activity nonlinearly modulates the direction and strength of the update. The proposed synapse is embedded into a compact two-neuron memristive Hopfield neural network to investigate how this functional decomposition influences network dynamics. Equilibrium and stability analysis, bifurcation diagrams, Lyapunov exponents, and multistability analysis reveal variable-wing chaotic attractors, parameter-dependent transitions, and coexisting dynamical states. FPGA implementation verifies the hardware realizability of the proposed system, while a color-image encryption scheme demonstrates the application potential of the generated chaotic sequences. These results show that the proposed framework provides a functionally interpretable modeling route for incorporating differentiated pre/post synaptic regulation into memristive Hopfield dynamics.
journal: Neural networks : the official journal of the International Neural Network Society

title: Synthetic host defence peptides modulate phagocytic activity and release of inflammatory mediators by BV-2 microglial cells.
abstract: Microglia are the predominant resident innate immune cells of the brain that maintain homeostasis and mitigate damage caused by injury and pathogens. Synthetic variants of host defence peptides, also termed antimicrobial peptides, are designed based on their endogenous counterparts and have been demonstrated to exhibit enhanced immunomodulatory activities, including an ability to selectively modulate the release of cytokines by monocytic cells. These peptides exert therapeutic benefits in a murine brain injury model, but it is unknown whether they can modulate microglial immune responses. We tested the effects of three host defence peptides, namely innate defence regulators (IDR)-1002, IDR-1018 and D-3006, on selected functions of BV-2 murine microglial cells, as well as differentiated HL-60 monocytic cells, which were used as a human model of nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide phosphate (NADPH) oxidase-dependent reactive oxygen species (ROS) production. It was demonstrated here that IDR-1002, IDR-1018 and D-3006 reduced the production of nitric oxide, tumor necrosis factor-α (TNF), ROS, and cytotoxic factors, depending on whether the cells were stimulated with lipopolysaccharide (LPS), interferon (IFN)-γ, or their combination. All three IDRs also reduced LPS-induced phagocytic activity of BV-2 microglia, while IDR-1018 and D-3006 increased this function in unstimulated cells, though our findings are limited to cell lines and require validation in primary or human microglia. By altering selected inflammatory, cytotoxic, and phagocytic readouts of microglial cells in a context-dependent manner, synthetic host defence peptides such as IDRs warrant further investigation as candidate modulators of neuroinflammation, including in animal models of relevant neurological disorders.

title: Plant embryogenesis from zygotic genome activation to seed maturation: Comparative mechanisms and engineering opportunities.
abstract: Plant embryogenesis converts a zygote into a patterned, maturation-competent embryo. Since the major syntheses published in 2019 and 2021, allele-resolved transcriptomics, single-cell and spatial profiling, and three-dimensional imaging have revealed substantial variation in zygotic genome activation and cleavage geometry across angiosperms, challenging models derived solely from Arabidopsis. Here, we organize recent advances along a comparative zygote-to-seed trajectory and ask how conserved regulatory modules are redeployed across lineages, how early patterning is coupled to seed maturation, and which developmental transitions can be engineered in crops. We first compare the maternal-to-zygotic transition and associated chromatin-state changes, explicitly distinguishing observations from hypotheses about their evolutionary drivers. We then examine how PIN-FORMED (PIN)-dependent auxin transport, local auxin biosynthesis, membrane and peptide signaling, and WUSCHEL-RELATED HOMEOBOX (WOX)-family transcription factors establish embryonic axes and meristems. Next, we connect these early programs to source-sink relations, nutrient partitioning, proteostasis, and hormone-redox control during seed maturation, while separating maturation from dormancy release and germination. Finally, we assess how spatial multi-omics, live imaging, CRISPR activation, and synthetic apomixis can interrogate or engineer these transitions. This framework identifies conserved modules, lineage-specific solutions, and major evidence gaps that must be resolved before embryogenesis can be predictably manipulated for crop improvement.
journal: Plant science : an international journal of experimental plant biology

title: Passive microwave sea ice concentration biases in the Southern Hemisphere revealed by ICESat-2 linear ice fraction
A revised model for atmospheric adjacency effect correction in optical satellite earth observation images
Programming brain endothelial identity: Transcription factor and genome engineering approaches to improve iPSC-derived BBB models.
abstract: Human induced pluripotent stem cell-derived brain endothelial-like cells (iBECs) serve as important human relevant in vitro blood-brain barrier (BBB) models for evaluating central nervous system (CNS)-targeted therapies. However, conventional differentiation protocols often generate heterogeneous populations constrained by incomplete endothelial maturation. Overcoming these limitations requires precise control over developmental gene regulatory networks throughout differentiation. This review examines transcription factor-based forward reprogramming strategies designed to induce brain endothelial cell fate and prime BBB identity. Integrating these approaches with novel genome engineering tools enables the rational design of next generation BBB models with improved physiological fidelity and predictive power for CNS therapeutic discovery and validation.

title: Female iPSC X chromosome inactivation erosion and its transcriptomic effects during CRISPR gene editing and neural differentiation.
abstract: Human induced pluripotent stem cells (hiPSCs), together with CRISPR editing, are commonly used for studying neurodevelopmental disorders. Female iPSCs gradually lose the expression of the noncoding X chromosome inactive-specific transcript (XIST), leading to random X chromosome inactivation (XCI) erosion that affects both X-linked and autosomal gene expression. However, the effects of CRISPR editing and neural differentiation on XCI erosion and how this may confound a real-world analysis of differentially expressed genes (DEGs) are poorly understood. Here, we analyzed hundreds of RNA sequencing (RNA-seq) samples of CRISPR-edited iPSC lines for 66 genes and the matched single-neuron RNA-seq data. We found variable XCI in CRISPR-edited female iPSCs, which was largely preserved in iPSC-derived neurons and predominantly influenced X-linked genes. Mechanistically, XIST mediates allele-specific epigenetic regulation of both X-linked and autosomal genes, with the former showing stronger allele-specific expression (ASE) bias that affects neurodevelopmental genes. These results have significant implications in hiPSC-based modeling of neurodevelopmental disorders.

title: Artificial intelligence is not enough to enhance organizational performance
A Contemporary Analysis of Positive Surgical Margin Length and Oncologic Outcomes After Radical Prostatectomy: Results from an Institutional Registry with Long-Term Follow Up.
abstract: OBJECTIVE To evaluate the impact of positive surgical margins (PSM) after radical prostatectomy (RP) and oncologic outcomes in a large institutional registry with long-term follow up and explore various methods of margin characterization. Prior studies remain limited by heterogeneous margin characterization, small cohorts, and limited follow-up. METHODS We queried our prospectively maintained institutional registry for patients who underwent RP from 1987-2023. PSM were analyzed as binary (negative/positive) and focality (negative/unifocal/multifocal). Cox proportional hazards regression models evaluated associations with oncologic outcomes. Cutpoint analysis identified an optimal threshold that differentiated outcomes by linear PSM length. RESULTS Among 24,855 patients with median follow-up of 10.9 years, 6454(26%) had PSM. On multivariable analysis, PSM were associated with increased risk of biochemical recurrence (BCR, HR 1.74 [1.57-1.93], p<.0001), but not metastasis-free (MFS), cancer-specific (CSS), or overall survival (OS). Unifocal (HR 1.66 [1.48-1.86]) and multifocal (HR 2.01 [1.7-2.37]) PSM were similarly associated with increased risk of BCR (p<.0001), but not MFS, CSS, or OS. Cutpoint analysis identified a threshold of 1mm. PSM length ≥1mm was associated with increased risk of BCR (HR 1.72[1.53-1.92, p<.0001), while <1mm was not. CONCLUSIONS In this large cohort with long-term follow-up, PSMs were only associated with BCR but not with MFS, CSS, or OS. These results may inform postoperative surveillance protocols and adjuvant therapy risk stratification. Additionally, on exploratory analyses in a small subgroup of men with limited follow-up duration, PSMs shorter than 1mm did not appear to be associated with BCR, a hypothesis-generating finding which warrants further investigation in the modern era of digitized pathology.

title: Shrimp-derived peptides restore spermatogenesis by activating the GDNF/GFRα1/c-RET pathway in a rat model of NAFLD.
abstract: OBJECTIVE The present study was carried out to investigate the protective effects of peptides derived from Pacific white shrimp (Litopenaeus vannamei) by-products on spermatogenesis and spermatogonial stem cell (SSC) self-renewal in a rat model of non-alcoholic fatty liver (NAFLD). DESIGN Experimental study. SETTING Urmia University, Urmia, Iran. ANIMALS Twenty-four adult male Wistar rats (8 weeks old, average weight 230.2 ± 23 g). EXPOSURE Rats were divided into four groups (n=6): control (standard chow), high-fat diet (HFD), HFD + 20 mg peptide/kg body weight (BW), and HFD + 300 mg peptide/kg BW. Peptides were enzymatically hydrolyzed at 50°C, yielding 70-75% low molecular weight peptides (<500 Da), and administered via oral gavage for 10 weeks. MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES The expressions of Glial cell line-derived neurotrophic factor (GDNF), GDNF family receptor alpha-1 (GFRα1), c-RET and BCL6b were evaluated by qPCR and immunohistochemistry. Spermatogenesis and tubular differentiation indices, tubular differentiation index (TDI), spermiogenesis index (SPI), histological alterations, oxidative stress biomarkers (malondialdehyde [MDA], reduced glutathione [GSH], oxidized glutathione [GSSG], and insulin resistance (HOMA-IR), were assessed. RESULTS HFD markedly reduced SSC self-renewal markers, impaired spermatogenesis, increased oxidative stress and HOMA-IR, compared with the control group (p < 0.05). Peptide supplementation, especially at 300 mg/kg, upregulated the expression of GDNF, GFRα1, c-RET and BCL6B, improved spermatogenic indices, partially restored redox balance, reduced HOMA-IR, and ameliorated histological damage in the testes. CONCLUSIONS In conclusion, these findings provide new evidence that shrimp-derived peptide supplementation was associated with reduced oxidative-stress markers, enhanced GDNF/GFRα1/c-RET-related measures, and improved spermatogenic indices and support SSC self-renewal in NAFLD-induced male reproductive dysfunction.

title: A xenolith perspective on the continental lithospheric mantle under NW Ireland at ∼43 Ma
abstract: The extent to which interaction occurred between the proto-Iceland mantle plume and the continental lithospheric mantle (CLM) during establishment of the Palaeogene British and Irish Igneous Province (BIPIP) has wide-ranging and important implications, not least for understanding the nature and differentiation of the parental melts, models of contamination of primary magmas as well as base and precious metal mineralization. This study focuses on a rare Palaeogene-aged xenolithic dyke from Inver, NW Ireland. Geothermobarometric calculations indicate that spinel lherzolites from the Inver dyke represent relatively fertile, cold, deep CLM. The Al-in-olivine thermometer yields 865–974°C for two xenoliths studied in detail and equilibration pressures (using the Ca-in-olivine-clinopyroxene barometer) of 12–15 kbar. Oxygen fugacity calculations indicate relatively reducing conditions (Δlog f O2[QFM]) of −3.2 to −2.3, a characteristic not inconsistent with deeply sourced CLM materials. Thermobarometry on the dyke host rock suggests that its parental melt equilibrated with the mantle at 1326°C and 18.6 kbar, constraining the depth to the lithosphere-asthenosphere boundary at ∼43 Ma to ∼59 km. Taken together, these observations attest to the localized survival of relatively unmodified CLM following the main pulse of BIPIP magmatism at 61–58 Ma. The new constraints are permissive of magmatic mineral deposit formation or enhancement by exchange between locally metasomatized CLM and rising asthenospheric melts, but such processes may be localized, i.e. beneath individual igneous centres of activity.

title: Spatiotemporal Approach to Assess the Impact of Urbanization Policies on Urban Expansion and Sprawl Using Remote Sensing in Tiaret, Algeria
abstract: This study examines the spatial implications of urbanization policies on urban expansion and sprawl. While the shortcomings of urban containment policies have garnered considerable scholarly attention, policies promoting urbanization remain underexplored, with limited empirical research assessing their spatial impacts. To address this gap, we integrate key urbanization policies into a spatiotemporal analysis of 50 years, enabling a nuanced evaluation of policy interventions on urban growth and sprawl through the analysis of their rates, directions, and spatial patterns. This is accomplished using remote sensing techniques and GIS, complemented by standard deviational ellipse, multibuffer ring, landscape metrics, and other spatial indices, to quantify and analyze urban dynamics. The study focuses on Tiaret, a medium-sized Algerian city characterized by a dynamic urban governance trajectory, contributing to research on underexplored urban contexts. The findings demonstrate a significant correlation between urbanization policies and the rate, direction, and patterns of urban expansion and sprawl. Over four decades of policy-driven urbanization, the city experienced an overall average annual urban expansion rate of 28.2%, with urban sprawl dominating 99% of newly developed areas, which were marked by low density and high fragmentation. This study provides an evidence-based framework that quantifies how urbanization policies shape the extent, direction, and spatial patterns of urban growth, enabling planners to anticipate unintended consequences and design more sustainable, policy-sensitive urban strategies.
journal: Journal of Urban Planning and Development

title: The Reflection Penalty: when managers accept leadership coaching from a human but not an AI agent
Development of Calcium Phosphate Composite Cement Enabling Alkaline Microenvironment pH Regulation for Osteomyelitis Control and Bone Regeneration
abstract: Osteomyelitis, a chronic bone infection, poses significant challenges in clinical management due to the risks of severe bone necrosis and the increasing prevalence of antibiotic-resistant bacteria. Conventional therapeutic strategies, including surgical debridement and systemic antibiotic therapy, often fall short of achieving optimal outcomes due to antibiotic resistance and failure to achieve high-quality bone regeneration post-surgery. To address these clinical challenges, this study developed an alkaline calcium phosphate cement enabling sequential osteomyelitis control and bone regeneration. This cement was formed through a stepwise reaction between calcium hydroxide (Ca(OH)2) and sodium polyphosphate ((NaPO3)n) in an aqueous environment, enabling provisional defect filling as well as immediate generation of a hyperalkaline environment upon implantation to effectively inhibit both Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacteria. The pH value of bone cement extract gradually decreased from a hyperalkaline state (>11.5) to a mildly alkaline microenvironment (7.8-8.5) over time with the progression of the reaction between Ca(OH)2 and (NaPO3)n in situ, subsequently fostering a favorable microenvironment for bone regeneration. Meanwhile, a stable and effective rat osteomyelitis model was established to verify the sequential antibacterial and osteogenic performance of the material in vivo. In vitro cellular experiments demonstrated that bone cement enhances the proliferation and osteogenic differentiation of rat bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells (rBMSCs). Moreover, an in vivo osteomyelitis rat model also revealed the absence of infectious reactions or tissue necrosis, as well as bone formation around the cement post-implantation, confirming the feasibility of this material in treating osteomyelitis. Collectively, these results indicated that the as-developed cement can serve as an active bone repair material adapted to dynamic microenvironment regulation needs, offering a promising approach for the treatment of osteomyelitis and the promotion of bone regeneration in a sequential manner.

title: Digital transformation-driven supply chain resilience and sustainable supply chain performance: an empirical investigation of the fresh agricultural product industry
abstract: The fresh agricultural product supply chain, as a foundational industry critical for safeguarding people’s livelihoods, has increasingly encountered frequent external uncertainties in recent years. These disruptions severely undermine operational stability and precipitate multifaceted adverse economic, social and environmental consequences. Consequently, fostering supply chain resilience (SCR) has emerged as a critical imperative for sustainable industry development, with digital transformation (DT) identified as a pivotal enabler for enhancing such resilience. Based on dynamic capabilities theory, this study constructs a theoretical framework integrating DT, dynamic capabilities, SCR and sustainable supply chain performance (SSCP). Data were collected through a structured questionnaire administered to 343 supply chain managers and senior executives in China’s fresh agricultural product industry. The theoretical model was empirically validated using partial least squares structural equation modeling. Research findings reveal that DT effectively enhances dynamic capabilities in three critical dimensions: resource integration capability, organizational learning capability and resource reconfiguration capability, which subsequently strengthens SCR. Moreover, this DT-driven SCR positively affects SSCP to a certain extent. This study reveals the critical role of DT in enhancing SCR. By enabling rapid resource coordination, knowledge internalization and strategic resource reconfiguration, DT empowers firms to effectively respond to supply chain disruption risks and continuously strengthen resilience over the long term. Moreover, embedding the development of SCR into corporate strategy is a valuable managerial lever, which positively contributes to sustainable performance and long-term competitiveness in volatile markets. This study contributes to the literature on SCR and DT from the perspective of dynamic capabilities and offers theoretical insights for building resilience in the fresh agricultural product industry.

title: Consumers’ motivation to donate second-hand clothing: concurrent mixed-methods belief elicitation and norms validation using the Theory of Planned Behavior
abstract: The goal of this research is twofold. First, this research aims to identify the salient beliefs that motivate consumers to donate second-hand clothing (SHC). Second, this research establishes an extended theory of planned behavior (TPB) model of SHC donation and examines whether past donation experience differentiates the model relationships across donors and non-donors. This research applies a concurrent mixed-methods approach, comprising a qualitative open-ended survey with 39 consumers and a quantitative closed-ended survey with 401 consumers analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM). The qualitative study identifies a set of salient behavioral beliefs, injunctive normative beliefs, descriptive normative beliefs, and control beliefs toward SHC donation. The quantitative study shows that attitudes, moral norms, and perceived behavioral control significantly predict intentions to donate SHC, whereas injunctive and descriptive norms do not. The multigroup analysis shows that the influence of attitudes on intentions toward SHC donation is stronger for donors than for non-donors. This research contributes to an integrated understanding of SHC donation through a concurrent mixed-methods design that elicits context-specific beliefs and examines an extended TPB model that contrasts donors with non-donors, thereby offering more in-depth insight into why consumers choose to donate or choose not to donate SHC.
journal: Journal of Fashion Marketing and Management: An International Journal

title: Advance care planning as life planning: financial consultations as a cross-sector node in integrated care
abstract: Advance care planning (ACP) is conceptually defined as a proactive, value-based and anticipatory process. However, in practice, it remains structurally reactive, initiated in response to clinical deterioration or institutional prompts within fragmented care pathways. This conceptual paper examines financial consultation during comparatively healthy stages of life, as an upstream, cross-sector context to foster psychological readiness for ACP and strengthen integrated care. This paper adopts a conceptual synthesis approach, which differs from a systematic review because its aim is theory-building rather than exhaustive evidence aggregation. Literature was identified through structured Google Scholar searches and cross-referencing of key publications, with a focus on peer-reviewed publications from 2000 onwards supplemented by seminal earlier works. The terms included ACP, integrated care, psychological readiness, financial planning, narrative medicine and cross-sector collaboration. Sources were selected purposively to represent key theoretical frameworks and empirical findings relevant to the proposed argument. I prioritized international consensus statements, systematic reviews and conceptual contributions that illuminate the conditions under which ACP engagement occurs across institutional settings. Financial consultations routinely address uncertainty – including illness risk, long-term care costs and life-course planning – through non-acute, future-oriented conversations in which clients articulate values, goals and trade-offs. These characteristics mirror key psychological and narrative conditions associated with ACP engagement. Financial consultations may be useful upstream, cross-sector nodes to cultivate preparatory reflection and lower barriers to initiating ACP. This could aid the actual clinical decision-making and documentation which remain health and social care services' responsibility. This paper reframes ACP as part of broader life planning within integrated care systems, and proposes financial consultations as complementary entry points into cross-sector ACP pathways. By highlighting role differentiation and coordination issues between healthcare professionals, financial advisors, insurers and local care networks, it identifies ethical, professional and policy safeguards needed to support collaboration. In addition, it proposes a model to improve individuals' psychological readiness for engaging in ACP.

title: Governing incompleteness: coordinative adequacy and the limits of computational observation
abstract: This paper asks when representational incompleteness becomes an organizational coordination problem and develops coordinative adequacy as a second-order, regime-level criterion for evaluating computational observation regimes. A problem-driven conceptual synthesis uses second-order cybernetics as an epistemology of observation to integrate organization, coordination and digital-systems research. Doomsday supplies a historical limit model; Euclid's wall isolates the representational condition; a retrospective Horizon application probes diagnostic reach; evidence and revision conditions delimit the claims. Incompleteness becomes a coordination problem not through omission alone, but when task-relevant loss makes different states decision-equivalent and authorized use makes that loss consequential for affected parties. Coordinative adequacy evaluates that relation without treating more computation as inherently better. Consequential authority specifies the representation–decision coupling; reflexive effects denote attributable changes propagated through it; computational restraint governs justified limits to computation and conditions of revision. Comparative operationalization and empirical testing require task-grounded evidence and outcomes differentiated across affected parties. The evaluative questions support deployment review, audit, procurement, incident review and redesign. Evaluation must consider authorized purposes, consequences for affected parties, effective contestation and justified computational limits. The paper develops coordinative adequacy as a second-order, regime-level criterion for when incomplete representation becomes a coordination problem. It identifies consequential authority as the coupling that makes task-relevant loss operative and treats justified non-computation and revision as constitutive of adequacy.

title: The illusion of algorithmic belonging: why generative AI cannot substitute for relational reciprocity in mental health social inclusion
abstract: This study aims to critically discuss the fast-moving rollout of generative artificial intelligence (AI) and conversational agents as purported remedies to loneliness and social isolation, analysing the fact that the creation of companionship by algorithms substitutes a one-way connection and fundamentally jeopardises real social inclusion. An interdisciplinary perspective that draws from relational sociology, the social model of disability, critical digital studies and various literatures on psychiatric rehabilitation to critique the inter-personal ethics, psychological dangers and political economy of digital mental health companions. It also comprises a comparative analysis of the existing market leaders in conversational AI. Proximate affective containment is provided by generative AI, but lacks of relational reciprocity, moral agency and shared vulnerability. The replacement of civic infrastructures in community settings by automated, conversational agents can set up a divided mental health system: human-centred relational mental health care for the privileged and synthetic, automated containment for the marginalised service user. Moreover, AI companionship takes out user vulnerability as property information, turns it into a commodity, the lived experience of solitude. As a perspective, this paper does not contain empirical data of its own; it constructs the argument by conceptual synthesis instead of a systematic review, and the examples of markets discussed (e.g. Woebot, Wysa, Replika) are illustrative, but not comprehensive or evaluative of current versions of products and so may have changed significantly since the time of writing. Longitudinal studies that compare the outcomes of service users using algorithmic companionship with peer-support and Clubhouse models will confirm the synthetic inclusion construct developed here, and could be used for future research. Offers evaluative tools to the mental health commissioners, clinicians and third sector organisations to avoid the “community replacement” trap of digital engagement, keeping AI a cognitive prosthetic and not a substitute for interpersonal interactions. Disciplines policymakers from adopting techno-solutionism as an excuse for austerity-driven disinvestment of physical community centres, peer respites and inclusive civic spaces and calls for the protection of the human social commons. This paper outlines the concept of a “synthetic inclusion” that reveals that the illusion of connection created by conversational AI is a commodity, and that social isolation is structurally reinforced. It contributes to the critique of mental health in the digital age by examining unconstrained large language models from a perspective of surveillance capitalism and intersectionality.

title: Transformational vs. authentic leadership in task performance: the mediating roles of trust and psychological safety
abstract: This study investigates the differential effects of transformational and authentic leadership on task performance within a high-stakes organizational context. It specifically examines the mediating roles of trust in leadership and psychological safety in these relationships. A mixed-methods explanatory sequential design was employed, grounded in Social Exchange Theory and the Job Demands-Resources model. Quantitative data were collected from 292 military personnel in the Ghana Armed Forces using validated questionnaires and analyzed via Structural Equation Modeling (SEM). Qualitative insights from 18 semi-structured interviews provided contextual depth to the findings. The findings reveal a critical distinction within this specific context: while both leadership styles positively influence task performance, they operate through fundamentally different mechanisms. Authentic leadership appears to enhance task performance both directly and indirectly, through the partial mediation of trust and psychological safety. In contrast, transformational leadership’s influence on performance is fully mediated by psychological safety, with trust playing no mediating role. These findings suggest that, in hierarchical, high-stress military environments, authentic leadership appears to be more effective in building the relational resources (trust) necessary for sustained performance. However, given the cross-sectional design and single-country, single-organizational context, these findings require replication and should be interpreted with appropriate caution. This study challenges the universal applicability of transformational leadership theory and extends the Job Demands-Resources model by demonstrating that leadership behaviors function as differentiated job resources with style-specific pathways to performance. These findings provide robust evidence for HRM practitioners and policymakers to prioritize the development of authentic, transparent and ethical leadership to foster a high-performing and psychologically healthy workforce.

title: Context Matters! Social, Spatial, and Semantic Coordination with an Embodied Agent in Immersive Analytics
abstract: Embodied AI agents in Augmented Reality (AR) could enable more natural collaboration in immersive analytics by engaging users through spatial, conversational, and visual interaction. However, designing such agents requires careful attention to context. We propose a preliminary conceptual framework for context-aware design of embodied agents structured around three dimensions of spatial, social, and semantic. This framework is further categorised into embeddedness (how agents are situated in the contexts) and awareness (how agents perceive and respond to the contexts). To explore this, we present Cobot, an embodied AI agent designed as a design probe. Cobot supports context-sensitive interaction through features such as gaze cues, spatial sound, and task-aware behaviour. We reflect on its design and identify implications for future contextaware embodied agents.

title: PSO-MAC-Based Optimization of Vibration Sensor Placement for Heavy Vehicle Electromechanical Transmission
abstract: In prognostics and health management (PHM) research for heavy vehicle electromechanical transmission (EMT), vibration signal dataset construction faces challenges of poor acquisition quality and low signal-to-noise ratio, leading to difficulties in fault feature extraction and unsatisfactory diagnosis performance. This study develops an operating-condition-informed sensor-placement framework integrating calibrated finite-element (FE) modeling, multibody dynamic loading, modal superposition analysis, particle swarm optimization (PSO), and the modal assurance criterion (MAC). The transmission-housing models are updated using impact hammer modal tests, and modal consistency is evaluated by comparing experimental and numerical mode shapes. Dynamic bearing loads under rated conditions are then obtained from a multibody model and applied together with the actual mounting constraints. Candidate locations are screened from the resulting mode shapes, and a discrete PSO procedure optimizes the off-diagonal elements of the MAC matrix to determine a 12-sensor layout. Rig tests under six operating conditions show that the windowed Pearson correlation coefficient (WPCC) of the gear-related pair ranges from 0.583 to 0.784, while the mean gear-bearing coefficient remains between −0.030 and 0.007. The correlation-based partitions yield mean silhouette coefficients of 0.326–0.514. The gear group remains in the same cluster under all six conditions, whereas the internal relationships among the bearing-related channels vary with the conditions. The results demonstrate that the selected placement retains common structural-response information while providing stable differentiation between the gear- and bearing-related measurement regions over the six conditions.

title: Comparison of Clinical Indicators for Differentiating Unipolar and Bipolar Depression.
abstract: BACKGROUND The global prevalence of major depressive disorder and bipolar depression (BD) has increased, with BD often underdiagnosed and mismanaged. This study aims to identify key biomarkers from demographic and laboratory indicators to differentiate unipolar depression (UD) from BD, aiding early diagnosis and personalized treatment. METHODS This study was conducted at the Second Affiliated Hospital of Xinxiang Medical University between January 2022 and December 2024. A total of 174 inpatients were included, with 87 diagnosed with UD and 87 with BD. Demographic and laboratory data were collected. Univariate and multivariate logistic regression analyses were conducted to identify the risk factors. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis was used to evaluate discriminatory ability. RESULTS BD exhibited a higher male proportion (p = 0.004) and significantly elevated total bilirubin (TBIL), creatinine, and creatine kinase (CK) levels, along with lower thyroxine (T4) levels, compared to UD (p < 0.05). Multivariate analysis identified platelets, TBIL, T4, and CK as independent risk factors (p < 0.05). ROC analysis revealed TBIL (Area Under the Curve [AUC] = 0.609) and CK (AUC = 0.621) as key discriminators, with a combined model achieving an AUC of 0.724, sensitivity of 75.9%, and specificity of 59.8%. CONCLUSIONS Key metabolic and muscular biomarkers, including TBIL, CK, PLT, and T4, were identified as potential differentiators between UD and BD. These findings demonstrated diagnostic potential and underscored the need for further validation in larger studies.

title: Mismatches between genetic and assessment units in commercial fish species: A systematic review in the North-East Atlantic.
abstract: While sustainable fisheries depend upon spatial and temporal identification at below the species level (i.e., stock units), the choice and identification of appropriate units remain challenging. Advances in DNA sequencing and improved computational power have generated extensive genetic and genomic data on the spatio-temporal dynamics and resolution of marine fish populations. Here, we clarify terminology employed to designate fishery units and highlight the benefits of alignment between assessment units and biological processes. Our systematic review synthesises four decades of population genetic and genomic data in major North-East Atlantic commercial fishes, appraising mismatches between genetic and assessment units. We confirm the progressive increase of genetic data, also indicating an increased detection of genetic population structure. Patterns of small-scale temporal and spatial differentiation yield demonstrable tools for elucidating the integrity and dynamics of assessment units, including in mixed-stock fisheries. Atlantic cod (Gadus morhua) and herring (Clupea harengus) remain extensively researched (46% of the reviewed studies). We found that genetics is informing realignment of stock boundaries, with increased incidence of alignment between genetic and assessment units, though mismatches persist for many stocks. Moreover, several species and fisheries lack genetic data. With reduced costs of molecular analysis and implementation of real-time applications, we anticipate increased re-evaluation of stock boundaries and monitoring of complex population structure, providing baseline genetic tools for management of mixed-stock fisheries and inclusion of genomic data in stock assessment models. Generating reference genetic databases of populations will also facilitate studies on distributional range shifts in marine fishes, supported by increasingly precise predictive forecasting in a changing world.

title: Virus-Induced Genome Editing in the Parasitic Plant Phtheirospermum japonicum.
abstract: Phtheirospermum japonicum is a genetic model for parasitic Orobanchaceae, a family that includes agriculturally important weeds such as Striga , Orobanche , and Phelipanche . Functional genetic studies in these species are limited by the lack of stable transgenesis protocols, restricting heritable CRISPR/Cas9 genome editing. This challenge is common to many non‐standard model plants and crops. Here, we combined Agrobacterium rhizogenes ‐mediated transformation with virus‐assisted delivery of the ultracompact TnpB nuclease to achieve stable, transgene‐free, heritable genome editing in P. japonicum , independent of tissue regeneration or floral dip transformation. Homozygous knockouts were obtained within one to two generations. Modifications to this system increased editing efficiency and expanded the target space for editing. Our approach enables targeted functional genetic studies in parasitic plants and offers potential for broad application in non‐classical model species and crops.

title: A New Application of 64CuCl2 PET/CT: Imaging of Cats With Mammary Carcinoma.
abstract: Feline mammary carcinoma (FMC) is an aggressive and highly metastatic cancer that shares molecular and clinical characteristics with human triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC), making it a relevant comparative model for a disease lacking targeted therapies. This study investigated the feasibility and clinical utility of 64CuCl2 PET/CT imaging in cats with naturally occurring mammary carcinoma. Eight cats (seven tumour-bearing, one healthy control) were administered an intravenous dose of 64CuCl2 and underwent whole-body PET/CT imaging. Semi-quantitative analysis was performed using standardized uptake values (SUVs), and tumour-to-muscle ratios were calculated to assess lesion conspicuity. Serum ceruloplasmin concentrations were measured as a marker of systemic copper metabolism. All primary masses were 64Cu-avid and conspicuous, with consistently elevated tumour-to-muscle ratios across tumour-bearing cats, allowing clear differentiation between neoplastic and normal tissue. Imaging provided additional staging information by identifying locally invasive and metastatic disease that was not fully evident on physical examination. Physiologic tracer distribution was characterized by high uptake in the liver and gallbladder and low uptake in skeletal muscle, which served as a reliable reference tissue. Serum ceruloplasmin concentrations varied widely and did not correlate with tumour uptake. These findings suggest that 64CuCl2 PET/CT is a feasible functional imaging modality for FMC, potentially aiding in tumour detection. This was an exploratory study, and not all imaging results could be confirmed by cytology or histopathology. Nonetheless, our findings suggest that 64CuCl2 PET/CT should be investigated further as a method for probing copper utilization in FMC.

title: Gate-tunable chiral spin mode in WSe 2 /WS 2 moiré superlattices
abstract: The interplay between many-body and spin-orbit coupling (SOC) effects can lead to previously unobserved phenomena in solids. Chiral spin modes (CSMs) are collective spin excitations that arise from such interplay and connect states with opposite chirality. Here, we report a gate-tunable CSM that occurs between conduction SOC-split minibands in near-0°-twisted WSe 2 /WS 2 bilayers. This mode manifests as a sharp resonance with giant Raman efficiency in the pseudovector-symmetry channel of the Raman spectra. By varying the filling, the CSM transitions from a chiral spin exciton to an excitonic polaron. The spin-flip nature is directly confirmed by the Zeeman effect, and the filling dependence indicates a charge-transfer insulator at unity filling. Our results demonstrate that transition metal–dichalcogenide moiré superlattices are a fertile platform for exploring exotic low-lying collective excitations.

title: Frequency encoding regulates cell type composition in the small intestine
abstract: Intestinal homeostasis requires tight regulation of stem cell maintenance and differentiation to absorptive and secretory cell types, two major intestinal lineages. Key signaling pathways have been identified, but how they balance cell type composition remains unclear. We uncovered oscillatory expression of the Notch-target protein Hes1 (hairy and enhancer of split 1) that controls cell fate specification in a frequency-dependent manner. An endogenous fluorescent Hes1 reporter revealed distinct, cell type–specific oscillation frequencies forming a gradient along the crypt-villus axis, which was modulated by cell cycle phase as well as Wnt (wingless-related integration site)–signaling and Notch-signaling activity. We developed a microfluidic system to modulate Notch-signaling oscillations in organoids and found the oscillation frequency to regulate the balance of cell type composition. This study provides evidence that information for cell fate specification is encoded in the frequency of an oscillatory signal.

title: A pair of chitosan receptors confer broad-spectrum fungal resistance
abstract: Chitosan, a major fungal cell wall component, activates plant immunity, yet the underlying perception mechanism remains unknown. In this study, we identified OsFID1, an apoplast-localized DUF26 domain protein, as a chitosan-binding receptor essential for chitosan-triggered immunity. OsFID1 forms a receptor complex with OsFID2, a plasma membrane–localized DUF26 receptor-like kinase, to mediate chitosan sensing and immune activation, requiring OsFID2 phosphorylation for function. The OsFID1-OsFID2 complex confers broad-spectrum resistance to fungal pathogens. OsFID1 homologs are conserved in land plants, which show chitosan-binding activity in both monocots and dicots. Ectopic expression of OsFID1 in wheat and maize enhanced fungal resistance without growth penalty. These findings uncover a conserved receptor complex for direct chitosan sensing, advancing our understanding of plant-fungus interactions and providing a potential strategy for engineering durable fungal resistance crops.

title: Structural basis for size-selective perception of chitin in plants
abstract: Plants detect microbes through pattern recognition receptors that perceive conserved microbial surface motifs known as microbe-associated molecular patterns (MAMPs). Lysin motif (LysM) receptors recognize and mediate downstream responses to chitinous MAMPs. In this study, we elucidated the mechanism for the specific recognition of long-chain chitin oligomers and identified a hallmark bridge domain characteristic of the CHITIN PERCEPTION (CHIP) receptor class. Structural analysis of receptor-ligand complexes, biochemistry, and in planta functional studies of inhibitory nanobodies revealed the mechanism of size-selective, high-affinity chitin perception in Lotus japonicus and Medicago truncatula . Additionally, we identified the CHITIN ELICITOR RECEPTOR KINASE (CERK) class as low-affinity, yet essential, co-receptors and propose a mechanistic model for a ligand-induced core signaling heterocomplex. Our findings establish the structural and mechanistic basis of differential chitin perception and receptor complex assembly in chitin-elicited plant immune signaling.

title: Regulation of target gene expression by chromatin-associated protein-coding transcripts in plants
abstract: Protein-coding transcripts are regarded as intermediates that mediate DNA-to-protein information flow, leaving their noncoding regulatory potential largely underappreciated. Genome-wide profiling of RNA–chromatin interactions in Arabidopsis has uncovered widespread associations between protein-coding transcripts and distinct genomic loci, implying that they possess regulatory functions. Here, we found that BT2 and GSL8 transcripts modulate target gene transcription independently of their protein products through distinct mechanisms. The BT2 transcript represses transcription of its targets CEP2 and MRF4 by forming RNA–DNA triplexes, thereby restricting root growth and promoting flowering, whereas GSL8 acts through a triplex-independent pathway. Our findings unveil intrinsic regulatory activities of protein-coding transcripts, challenging the canonical definition of mRNA function and blurring the functional distinction between coding and noncoding RNAs in the context of genome evolution.

title: Dendritic computation for abstract rule-based flexible decision-making
abstract: Intelligent behavior involves flexible integration of sensory input and abstract rule knowledge. Dendritic computation has been shown to contribute to top-down modulation of sensory processing; however, whether and how it is involved in flexible cognitive processing remains to be elucidated. Combining a rule-based flexible decision-making task with in vivo two-photon imaging and optogenetics in mice, we found that within single layer 5 extratelencephalic neurons in the auditory cortex, apical dendrites preferentially encoded the inferred abstract rule and somata preferentially represented sensory stimuli, whereas choice signals were present in both compartments. Optogenetic dendritic inhibition impaired rule-dependent somatic choice coding, supporting a task-relevant integration across the dendritic and somatic compartments. These results indicate that dendritic computation in cortical neurons mediates flexible behavior.

title: Empirical constraints on ice cliff calving
abstract: When calving cliffs at the margins of Earth’s ice sheets exceed a critical height, runaway retreat may be initiated in a process called the marine ice cliff instability. However, sufficiently tall ice cliffs have rarely been observed. To address this gap, we measured the characteristics of 15,330 ice cliffs across Earth’s ice sheet margins using laser altimetry. We show that cliff height is highly correlated with mélange thickness, water depth, and crevassing. We found that tall cliffs calve more rapidly than parameterizations assume, but dynamic thinning and retreat into regions with low ice thickness gradients prevent runaway retreat. These observations suggest that model projections may underestimate subannual rates of cliff calving, but that the potential for instability will depend sensitively on additional quantities, not cliff height alone.

title: Airflows redefine the cost of aerial transport in the wild
abstract: Fuel economy matters to both animals and machines, as the cost of transport can determine where, when, and how far locomotion is possible. However, established estimates of these values for animal flight come from laboratories and treat the atmosphere as constant, even though free-flying animals routinely extract energy from atmospheric flows. Using high-resolution movement data, we estimate the cost of transport for 50 bird and bat species flying in the wild. Our results revise the classic ranking of locomotion costs, suggesting that flying can be cheaper than swimming though almost as costly as running, depending on interactions between physical environment, morphology, and behavior. Linking transport costs to atmospheric conditions provides a mechanistic basis for predicting how changing windscapes will reshape the energetics, movements, and distributions of flying animals.

title: Magic state cultivation on a superconducting quantum processor
abstract: Fault-tolerant quantum computing requires a universal gate set, but the necessary non-Clifford gates represent a significant resource cost for most quantum error correction architectures. Magic state cultivation offers an efficient alternative to resource-intensive distillation protocols; however, testing the proposal’s assumptions represents a challenging departure from quantum memory experiments. We present an experimental study of magic state cultivation on a superconducting quantum processor. We implement cultivation, including code-switching into a surface code, and develop a fault-tolerant measurement protocol to bound the magic state fidelity. Cultivation reduces the error by a factor of 40, with a state fidelity of at least 0.9999(1) (retaining 8% of attempts). Our results experimentally establish magic state cultivation as a viable solution to one of quantum computing’s most important challenges.

title: Engineering ordered two-dimensional defect phases to strengthen structural alloys
abstract: Defects in crystals are usually considered to be consequences of deformation, but they can also be engineered as strengthening features. Planar defects can strengthen structural alloys but usually form only during deformation or service, limiting control over their density, stability, and chemistry. We show that predeformation followed by aging can convert such defects into a designed architecture of ordered defect phases. In a single-crystal cobalt-nickel–based superalloy and a polycrystalline cobalt-chromium-tungsten alloy, this treatment creates dense networks of coherent, atomically thin, ordered defect–confined phases. These increase room-temperature strength by more than 200 megapascals and reduce the superalloy’s minimum creep rate by more than threefold. Electron microscopy and simulations show that local chemical ordering amplifies strengthening and that the ordered defect phases remain shearable while impeding slip transmission.

title: Atomic functional site scaffolding in biopolymers with RFdiffusion3
abstract: The catalytic and other sophisticated functions of biomolecules arise from the placement of many atoms in three-dimensional space. Here, we describe a generative artificial intelligence method for biopolymers, RFdiffusion3 (RFD3), which employs free atom diffusion to satisfy complex sets of atomic constraints more rapidly and accurately than previous methods across several challenges from enzyme design to RNA structure design. We demonstrate experimentally the power of the RFD3 pipeline for enzyme design by designing de novo phosphotriesterases with a complex active site architecture incorporating a carbamylated lysine coordinating two metal ions and zinc proteases specific for the transthyretin protein involved in amyloid diseases; in both cases we obtain active catalysts in zero shot 96 construct design campaigns.

title: Electrically driven chiral emission from plasmonic tunnel junctions
abstract: Chirality plays a crucial role in a broad range of processes, including light-matter interactions in physics, chemistry, and biology, while quantum tunneling provides a promising mechanism for light generation at the nanoscale. By integrating tunnel junctions with chiral plasmonic nanohelicoids, we achieved electrically induced nanoscale generation of chiral light at the single-particle level. The tunneling-driven resonant excitation of chiral dipolar modes of the nanohelicoids results in emission of a vortex light beam possessing both spin angular momentum with handedness selectivity of more than 0.8 and orbital angular momentum equal in magnitude and opposite in sign. Our electrically driven approach offers a means for engineering photon spin generation at the nanoscale, highlighting its potential for next-generation optical components in display applications, as well as quantum information processing and photochemistry.

title: Deterministic generation and distribution of genuine multipartite entanglement in macroscopic acoustic resonators
abstract: Generating complex multimode entanglement is a central goal of quantum information science. However, scalable creation of genuine multipartite entanglement is challenging as it requires excellent control and efficient state verification. We report the generation and transfer of genuine multimode entanglement across two multimode acoustic resonators. We prepare genuine multipartite entangled states involving two, four, and six modes across the resonators with respective fidelities of 0.912 ± 0.003, 0.790 ± 0.003, and 0.570 ± 0.001. We further demonstrate the transfer of two- and four-mode genuine entangled states between the resonators with fidelities of 0.785 ± 0.006 and 0.601 ± 0.006. This hardware-efficient and scalable architecture enables deterministic control and generation of complex multimode mechanical states. Our results push the boundary of quantum control in macroscopic mechanical systems, establishing a pathway toward large-scale mechanical quantum networks.

title: Modular van der Waals MOSFETs through layer-by-layer chalcogen substitutions
abstract: In two-dimensional transition-metal dichalcogenides (TMDCs), the local electrostatic field of the chalcogen p -orbitals dictates the crystal field splitting of the transition metal d -orbitals, stabilizing diverse electronic states from semiconducting and semimetallic to exotic topological phases. On-demand substitution of the lattice chalcogens is therefore an efficient route to tuning TMDC electronic phases. Here, we custom-molded van der Waals (vdW) heterostructures by layer-by-layer vapor-phase chalcogen substitution starting from p -type WSe 2 multilayers into which we locally inscribed insulating WO x , n -type WS 2 , and semimetallic WTe 2 . This spatially precise conversion seamlessly integrated distinct electronic phases, both vertically and laterally, into modular vdW semiconductor heterostructures that are otherwise inaccessible. As a demonstration, we integrated WO x /WSe 2 local gate stacks to build ultrascaled metal oxide–semiconductor field effect transistors (MOSFETs), achieving an unprecedented subthreshold swing at subnanometer equivalent oxide thickness.

title: To reverse nature loss, change what drives it
abstract: This week, at the 17th Meeting of the Conference of the Parties to the Convention on Biological Diversity (COP17), delegates from 195 countries and the European Union are gathering in Yerevan, Armenia, for a global review of progress under the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework, an international set of goals and targets adopted in 2022 to tackle the biodiversity crisis. The urgent question before them is clear: What must change now to halt and reverse nature’s decline and put it on a path to recovery by 2030? COP-17 comes as international cooperation is under increasing strain. Extreme weather is intensifying, ecosystem deterioration is creating new security risks, and geopolitical tensions are rising. Yet nature’s decline does not pause for geopolitical instability—it deepens it. That makes effective multilateralism, with North and South as equal partners, more important, not less.
