В статье осуществляется теоретическое обоснование и разработка практических подходов к формированию мелиоративных ландшафтов как объектов агрокреаномики — нового научного направления, синтезирующего инженерные решения с креативными и культурными практиками для создания многофункциональной среды. Исследование базируется на комплексном системном подходе, сравнительном анализе международных и российских практик, а также на методах алгоритмизации. В статье раскрыта сущность понятия «агрокреаномика» и ее приложение к мелиорации. Проведен сравнительный анализ традиционного и креативного подходов к проектированию мелиоративных ландшафтов, предложен коэффициент экологической стабильности как критерий их оценки. Рассмотрены успешные кейсы применения биоинженерных решений и цифровых технологий, а также выявлены основные барьеры внедрения. Основным результатом работы стала разработка авторской пятиэтапной схемы проектирования агромелиоративных ландшафтов нового типа. Предложенная модель включает этапы от междисциплинарного аудита и создания цифрового двойника до капитализации территории через брендинг и маркетинг впечатлений. In the context of systemic transformation of the economy and transition to a priority of knowledge and environmental responsibility, the agricultural sector requires rethinking of the role of land reclamation. The traditional technocratic approach focused solely on maximizing yield is exhausting its potential. This article provides theoretical justification for and development of practical approaches to the formation of reclamation landscapes as objects of agrocreanomics, a new scientific field that synthesizes engineering solutions with creative and cultural practices to create multifunctional environment. The research is based on a comprehensive systematic approach and comparative analysis of international and Russian practices as well as algorithmization methods. The article reveals the essence of the concept of “agrocreanomics” and its application to land reclamation. A comparative analysis of traditional and innovative approaches to the design of reclamation landscapes is conducted, and the coefficient of ecological stability is proposed as a criterion for their assessment. Successful cases of bioengineering solutions and digital technologies are considered, and the main barriers to implementation are identified. The key outcome of the research was the development of an author's five-step design scheme for a novel type of agro-reclamation landscapes. The proposed model comprises stages ranging from interdisciplinary auditing and creation of a digital twin to the capitalization of the area through branding and impression marketing.

title: Цифровая трансформация подотраслей ОТДЕЛЬНЫХ СЕКТОРОВ ЭКОНОМИКИ: феномен неравномерности и пути еЕ минимизАЦИИ
abstract: В статье проводится анализ фундаментальной проблемы структурного развития — феномена неравномерности цифровой трансформации подотраслей в ключевых секторах национальной экономики. В качестве репрезентативного эмпирического кейса рассмотрен аграрный сектор России, в частности его основные подотрасли: растениеводство и животноводство. Статья выявляет и систематизирует ключевые институциональные и экономические барьеры, детерминирующие эту асимметрию: высокие трансакционные издержки внедрения, провалы рынка в части цифровой инфраструктуры, дефицит компетенций, недостаточность экономических стимулов и внешние шоки. С опорой на методы системного анализа, сравнения и экспертных оценок авторы демонстрируют, как специфика активов, производственных циклов и каналов сбыта предопределяет различные траектории и скорость технологической адаптации, что ведет к дивергенции темпов роста и формированию структурных диспропорций. Основным научным результатом работы является разработка универсального алгоритма (абстрактной модели) управления процессом цифровизации, направленного на минимизацию межотраслевой асимметрии. Модель включает этапы от диагностики готовности и выбора инструментов до кадрового, финансового обеспечения и мониторинга. Теоретическая значимость исследования заключается в переходе от отраслевого анализа к разработке концептуальной модели управления структурными переходами в сложных экономических системах в условиях распространения цифровых технологий. The article analyzes the fundamental problem of structural development — the phenomenon of uneven digital transformation of sub-sectors in key sectors of the national economy. Russian agricultural sector, in particular, its main sub-sectors: crop production and livestock, is considered as a representative empirical case. The article identifies and systematizes key institutional and economic barriers to this asymmetry: high transaction costs of implementation, market failures related to digital infrastructure, lack of competencies, insufficient economic incentives, and external shocks. Using system analysis methods, comparison, and expert assessments, the authors demonstrate how specific assets, production cycles, and sales channels determine different trajectories and speeds of technological adaptation, resulting in divergent growth rates and structural imbalances. The main scientific result of the work is the development of a universal algorithm (abstract model) for managing the digitalization process, aimed at minimizing intersectoral asymmetry. The model includes steps from readiness diagnostics and tool selection to staffing, financial support, and monitoring. The theoretical significance of the research lies in the transition from industry analysis to the development of a conceptual model for managing structural transitions in complex economic systems in the context of the spread of digital technologies.

title: Climate Change and Extreme Weather Effects on Nebraska Corn Production: Differential Responses in Irrigated and Non-irrigated Systems
abstract: This study investigated the effects of climate change-driven extreme weather in July, especially drought, on corn yields in Nebraska. The yields of irrigated and non-irrigated (rainfed) corn were compared using data over 20 years, from 1998 to 2018, to see the effect of irrigation on reducing crop losses during the drought period. Simple linear regression models were applied to examine relationships between crop yield and precipitation in July and the Palmer Drought Severity Index (PDSI). As a result, rainfed corn showed clear sensitivity to July weather conditions, with yields dropping sharply in dry years and varying between years. However, irrigated corn remained stable and wasn't largely affected by either drought or rainfall levels. Overall, the study suggested that sustainable irrigation could reduce yield sensitivity to July moisture stress, resulting in higher mean yields and resistance to weather change. The findings suggest that irrigation is an effective way to protect corn production against warmer summer weather, while over-depleting groundwater sources like the Ogallala Aquifer would negatively affect future sustainability. Therefore, adaptive water management will be important for maintaining reliable corn output under a changing climate.
journal: Advances in Economics, Management and Political Sciences

title: Adaptability of Lightweight AI Models for Embedded Deployment: A Case Study of an Agricultural Monitoring Robot
abstract: Many artificial intelligence programs require powerful computing hardware, whereas agricultural robots, drones, and smart cameras rely on small embedded devices with limited computing power, battery capacity, and heat dissipation. Lightweight models reduce parameters and computational costs while maintaining acceptable accuracy, enabling AI deployment on resource-constraint network devices. This paper reviews key lightweighting methods, including compact network architectures, model pruning, model quantization, and knowledge distillation. It compares common platforms such as Jetson, Raspberry Pi, and microcontrollers. Using an agricultural monitoring robot as an example, this study proposes a system combining a camera, a lightweight YOLO model, Jetson, and a microcontroller for real-time crop monitoring. Experiments are designed to evaluate accuracy, speed, power consumption, temperature, and battery life. Rather than pursuing maximum model complexity, this paper focuses on explaining how to select a model that is truly suitable for the actual device. For agricultural robots, effective deployment requires sufficient accuracy, real-time performance, and low energy consumption.

title: Smart Snail-Production Skills Required by Agricultural Science Education Students for Self-Reliance and Economic Development in Niger Delta University, Bayelsa State
abstract: The study examined the smart snail-production skills required by Agricultural Science Education students for self-reliance and economic development in Niger Delta University, Bayelsa State. Specifically, it focused on three objectives, research questions and hypotheses. An analytic descriptive survey research design was adopted. The population comprised 63 Agricultural Science Education students and the entire population of 63 was used as the sample of the study, consisting of 28 students in 300 level and 35 students in 400 level, using the census sampling technique. Data were collected using the Smart Snail Production Skills for Self-Reliance and Economic Development Questionnaire, which contained 18 items and yielded an overall Cronbach’s alpha reliability coefficient of 0.82. Out of the 63 questionnaires administered, 59 were retrieved and used for analysis, representing approximately 94%. Mean and standard deviation were used to answer the research questions, while independent-samples t-test was used to test the hypotheses. The findings revealed that smart housing, automated feeding and digital breeding skills were required to high extents, with grand means of 3.23, 3.26 and 3.20 respectively. The hypotheses showed no significant differences between the responses of 300 and 400 level students, as the p-values of .530, .545 and .523 exceeded 0.05. The study concluded that these smart production skills were essential for students’ self-reliance and economic development. It recommended that the university provide practical facilities and integrate smart housing, automated feeding and digital breeding technologies into Agricultural Science Education training.
journal: INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF AGRICULTURE AND EARTH SCIENCE

title: Effect of Digital Financial Inclusion on Access to Agricultural Finance Among Smallholder Farmers in Selected States in North Central Nigeria
abstract: This study examined the effect of digital financial inclusion on access to agricultural finance among smallholder farmers in Benue, Kogi and Nasarawa States and the Federal Capital Territory, Nigeria. Kwara, Niger and Plateau States were excluded to maintain a manageable geographical scope. A cross-sectional survey design was adopted, and 440 questionnaires were administered, of which 387 valid responses were analysed. Data were collected using a structured questionnaire and analysed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modelling in SmartPLS 4. The findings showed that FinTech-based credit access had a strong positive and significant effect on access to agricultural finance (β = 0.924, p < 0.001). Agent-banking accessibility (β = 0.293, p < 0.001) and digital payment usage (β = 0.098, p < 0.001) also had positive and significant effects. Digital financial literacy had a negative but significant effect (β = −0.279, p < 0.001), while mobile banking usage had a negative and insignificant effect (β = −0.067, p = 0.069). The study concluded that digital financial inclusion improves agricultural-finance access when it provides affordable, timely and suitable credit rather than connectivity and routine transactions alone. It recommended expanding farmer-oriented FinTech credit, strengthening rural agent-banking networks, using digital payment histories for credit assessment and aligning digital loan conditions with agricultural production cycles.
journal: INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF ECONOMICS AND FINANCIAL MANAGEMENT
pdfUrl: https://iiardjournals.org/get/IJEFM/VOL. 11 NO. 9 2026/EFFECT OF DIGITAL FINANCIAL INCLUSION 167-176.pdf

title: A Mathematical Model to Predict Pediatric Macrocephaly
abstract: Objective: Macrocephaly is defined as a head circumference (HC) above +2 standard deviations (SD) for age and sex, and a value above +3 SD is generally regarded as clinically relevant. Both thresholds are published only as discrete, month-by-month reference tables. This study aimed to reduce the World Health Organization (WHO) upper reference limits of HC to continuous, closed-form functions of age, and to assess how closely such functions reproduce the tabulated values. Methods: The WHO HC-for-age values corresponding to +2 SD and +3 SD for girls and boys (1–60 months) were used. Six regression models were applied separately to each sex and each threshold. The model with the highest coefficient of determination (R²) was selected as the best fit. Results: Logarithmic regression gave the highest R² in all four datasets (R² = 0.996 throughout). For +2 SD, the models were HC = 38.685 + 3.509 × ln (t) for girls and HC = 39.574 + 3.533 × ln (t) for boys. For +3 SD, they were HC = 39.906 + 3.562 × ln (t) for girls and HC = 40.653 + 3.628 × ln (t) for boys, where t is age in months (all p < 0.001). Deviation from the reference was largest in the first three months (up to 0.57 cm) and did not exceed 0.35 cm beyond the first year. Conclusion: The upper limits of HC follow a logarithmic function of age. Expressing them in closed form allows the thresholds to be embedded in radiological reporting software, evaluated at any age without interpolation, and differentiated to obtain the slope of the threshold curve. A lookup table permits none of these directly. Because the largest deviation from the reference, up to 0.57 cm, occurs within the first three months, a borderline value measured on cross-sectional imaging at that age should be confirmed against the table.

title: E-Commerce Information System for Sales of Agricultural Products in North Aikmel Village
abstract: North Aikmel Village faces significant challenges in agricultural marketing due to middleman dependency and price uncertainty. This study addresses these issues by designing a web-based e-commerce system optimized for rural connectivity. Unlike standard e-commerce platforms, this system incorporates technical trade-offs such as optimized database queries and minimalist frontend assets to ensure a load time of <2.5 seconds under 3G network conditions (2 Mbps). The development followed a User-Centered Design (UCD) approach within the Waterfall model. Beyond functional black-box testing, the system was evaluated using the System Usability Scale (SUS) with 20 local farmers, yielding an average score of 82.5 (Excellent), indicating high acceptance. Results demonstrate that technical optimization for rural contexts significantly improves accessibility and digital inclusion for farmers.
journal: Bulletin of Network Engineer and Informatics

title: Effects of Dish Name, Visible Amount, Persona, and Explicit Instruction on Energy Estimates From Food Photographs by 26 Vision-Language Models: Comparative Evaluation Study
abstract: Background: Vision-language models (VLMs) are being considered for estimating energy intake from meal photographs. Prompt descriptions such as a Japanese-dietitian persona shift the estimates, suggesting their use for calibration; what the estimates rest on was unknown. Objective: We examined whether prompt descriptions can serve as calibration, at which training stage responses to a nationality persona and to an amount instruction arise, and whether estimates follow the visible amount or one associated with the identified dish. Methods: Eleven commercial and 15 open-weight models were evaluated on NutriImage (887 Japanese single-dish photographs) and SNAPMe (1,134 US meal photographs) under eight prompt conditions (no description, five personas, and smaller- or larger-portion instructions). With one model, images were cropped or replaced by the dish name. Before- and after-meal photographs of 804 meals (ACETADA) were estimated. Pre-trained and post-trained weights of Gemma 3 and InternVL3.5 8B were compared by likelihood scoring. Prompts were compared with numerical calibration. Results: Where the dish was named as in the full image, a 25% crop changed neither the median absolute percentage error (MedAPE; 33.8% vs 34.4%) nor the persona shift (-20 vs -20 kcal); dish names alone gave similar accuracy (MedAPE 31.7%); nearly empty trays still received 39%-75% of the before-meal estimate, often described as already eaten. Between models, the persona shift was related to baseline bias (r = -0.77) and less to instruction following (r = -0.36); the instruction shift showed the reverse (r = -0.14 and -0.95). In Gemma 3, the Japan-US contrast was 2-4 times larger before post-training, and the instruction response 2-4 times larger after it (InternVL3.5 8B: 3 and 1.4 times). Across images, the Japan-US contrast was uniform on US meals and, for Japanese dishes in the commercial models, Gemma 3, and Qwen3-VL 32B, larger where overestimated. In these models, the persona lowered MedAPE for Japanese dishes as much as, or slightly more than, subtracting the mean bias, and no more than dividing by a ratio; on US meals it did not; in open-weight families that responded little, only numerical calibration lowered error. The smaller-portion instruction raised MedAPE in models with little bias (eg, 30.0% to 50.2%). Conclusions: In the model examined most closely, the estimates behaved as if anchored on an amount associated with the identified dish and only partly corrected by the visible amount. Prompt descriptions moved them by amounts depending on model and cuisine, not on the correction needed; a persona is therefore not proposed as a general means of calibration. In a facility, the findings suggest showing the identified dish for correction, calibrating by a ratio measured on reference meals with the deployed model, keeping amount statements out of the prompt, and not deriving intake from before-after-meal differences.

title: Machine Learning-based Prediction of Pacing-Induced Cardiomyopathy in Patients with Atrioventricular Block Underlying Heart Failure with Mildly Reduced or Preserved Ejection Fraction
abstract: Background: Pacing-induced cardiomyopathy (PICM) is a major complication of chronic right ventricular pacing and develops in up to 25% of patients. Reliable prediction of PICM may facilitate individualized pacing strategy selection; however, currently available approaches demonstrate limited discriminative performance. This study aimed to develop and validate machine learning (ML) models for predicting PICM in patients with atrioventricular block (AVB) underlying heart failure with mildly reduced or preserved ejection fraction. Methods: In this multicenter prospective study derived from the RISK-PICM registry (January 2002 to January 2026), 125 patients with AVB who underwent pacemaker implantation were analyzed. PICM was defined as a ?10% reduction in left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) resulting in an LVEF <50%. Four ML algorithms, including logistic regression, support vector machine, random forest, and XGBoost, were trained using stratified 4-fold cross-validation with hyperparameter optimization and model discrimination was evaluated. Results: PICM developed in 41 patients (32.8%) during a median follow-up of 4.8 years. Male sex, pre-implant minimum QTc interval, and post-implant maximum QRS duration were significantly associated with PICM in univariable Cox regression. XGBoost achieved the highest discriminative performance (AUROC 0.831; sensitivity 0.805; specificity 0.845). Feature importance analysis identified baseline LVEF and post-implant maximum QRS duration as the most influential features. Model-derived risk stratification significantly differentiated high-risk and low-risk groups on Kaplan-Meier analysis (P < 0.001). Conclusions: ML-based models, particularly XGBoost, demonstrated clinically meaningful performance for PICM and may support individualized pacing strategy selection in patients with AVB and underlying heart failure with mildly reduced or preserved ejection fraction.

title: Serial measurements of Growth Differentiation Factor-15 in patients with Non-ST-Elevation Acute Coronary Syndrome and recurrent ischemic events
Multistage AI Crop Inspection and Segmentation Framework (MACISF)
abstract: Crop quality assessment is one of the most critical components of modern agriculture, which directly influences yield optimization, post-harvest management, and food security. Conventional evaluation of field crops relies on manual inspection, which is time-consuming, subjective, and unscalable. This paper proposes the Multistage AI Crop Inspection and Segmentation Framework (MACISF), an automated multistage deep learning pipeline for fruit quality evaluation from visual features. The pipeline is comprised of three stages: (i) an EfficientNetV2-L backbone, fine-tuned with a three-stage progressive strategy, for crop type classification; (ii) seven species-specific EfficientNetV2-S classifiers for healthy-versus-defective detection; and (iii) a YOLOv8m module for defect localization. Trained and evaluated on a composite dataset spanning seven fruit species, MACISF achieves 99.23% crop type accuracy (macro F1-score 99.23%, macro AUC-ROC 0.993), 99.39% mean health state accuracy with 99.51% mean defective-class recall, and a projected grading mAP@0.5 of 92.3%. On crop type classification, the Stage 1 classifier is second only to InceptionV3 (by 0.15 percentage points) among seven models trained on the same data, and outperforms ResNet-50, Xception, EfficientNetB3, DenseNet-121, and MobileNetV2. Unlike these single-task baseline models, MACISF additionally delivers health-state assessment, defect severity grading, and a per-unit economic and nutritional evaluation. Results are reported on held-out test data from a controlled dataset, and field validation is left for future work.

title: An experimentally tractable Arabidopsis–Swede Midge model to explore host reprogramming by gall-inducing insects
abstract: Insect-induced galls are striking examples of host developmental reprogramming, yet their causal mechanisms remain poorly understood because few insect gall systems combine experimental tractability with precise control of insect and host developmental state. Here, we establish Arabidopsis thaliana and the gall-inducing Swede Midge (Contarinia nasturtii) as an experimental system for insect gall research. We show that the Swede Midge, a major pest of Brassica crops, completes its full life cycle on Arabidopsis, and induces characteristic inflorescence galls. To define and quantify galling while accounting for changes in developmental stage in both partners, we developed three complementary approaches. On the insect side, a larval phenotyping pipeline monitors how many larvae are present and how far they have developed, and a larval droplet assay delivers defined numbers of stage-selected larvae directly to host inflorescences, fixing the insect input and establishing a precise time zero for the interaction. We found that early-stage larvae can induce galls, whereas late-stage larvae (L3) cannot, defining the developmental window for gall induction. On the host side, we established a phyllotactic dissection and staging framework that enables galled and non-galled floral tissues to be compared at defined developmental positions. We found that galling enlarged floral buds, floral primordia and the inflorescence meristem while delaying floral developmental progression, with accompanying changes in cell size, shape and tissue organisation. Together, these tools combine Arabidopsis genetics with controlled insect manipulation, opening the way to mechanistic dissection of how insects reprogram plant pathways.

title: Work-Life Balance, Burnout, and Organizational Commitment Among Higher Education Faculty: A Systematic Review Toward a Conceptual Structural Equation Model
abstract: Work-life balance become a growing concern in higher education, where faculty face increasing worloads, blurred work-home boundaries, and their consequences for well-being, commitment, and retention. This study systematically reviewed literature published between 2022 and 2025 examining the relationship among work-life balance, burnout, organizational commitment, job satisfaction, and faculty well-being, drawing on both international and Philippine higher education contexts. Anchored on the Job Demands-Resources (Jd-R) model and Social Exchange Theory (SET), the review synthesized findings across demographic factors (age, gender, marital status, rank, employment type, and tenure), dimensions of faculty well-being (physical, mental, emotional, and social), work-life balance factors linked to burnout ( workload distribution, job resources, scheduling, and role/boundary management), and the dimensions of organizational commitment (effective, continuance, and normative). The review indicates that heavier workload, weaker institutional support, and poorly managed role boundaries are consistently associated with higher burnout and lower well-being while adequate job resources, supportive scheduling, and effective commitment are associated with stronger job satisfaction and retention intentions. Demographic factors such as age, tenure, and employment type moderate these relationships in ways that carry direct implications for differentiated institutional policy. Building on this synthesis, the study proposes a conceptual structural equation model linking work-life balance factors, burnout, organizational commitment, job satisfaction, and faculty well-being, intended to guide future empirical validation and to inform higher education institutions seeking a more sustainable approach to academic workforce management.
journal: The International Review of Multidisciplinary Research

title: ENHANCING POST-HARVEST TOMATO VALUE THROUGH PASTEURIZATION: AN ACTION RESEARCH INTERVENTION FOR SMALLHOLDER FARMERS IN KEBBI STATE, NIGERIA
abstract: Tomato (Solanum lycopersicum L.) is a major cash crop in northern Nigeria, yet post-harvest losses exceed 50% due to perishability, seasonal gluts, and limited preservation infrastructure. Pasteurization offers a low-cost, scalable preservation alternative but remains underutilized among smallholders. A participatory action research design was implemented in Dongo Community, Zuru Local Government Area, Kebbi State. Thirty tomato farmers were purposively selected based on production activity and willingness to participate. Data were collected through structured questionnaires, focus group discussions, and hands-on training demonstrations. Profitability was evaluated using gross margin analysis. Respondents were predominantly male (72%), aged 26–45 years (73%), and formally educated (90%). Traditional sun-drying (80%) dominated current preservation practices, with zero prior awareness of pasteurization. Post-intervention, 93% of participants independently replicated the process. Gross margin analysis yielded ₦16,650 from a ₦23,350 investment, corresponding to a return of ₦0.71 per ₦1 invested. Key adoption constraints included inadequate training (43%), limited access to affordable equipment (31%), and insufficient technical knowledge (26%). Pasteurization-based tomato processing is technically feasible, economically viable, and socially acceptable among smallholder farmers. Sustainable scale-up requires integrated extension support, equipment subsidies, and cooperative processing models.
journal: KEBBI JOURNAL OF AGRICULTURE AND NATURAL SCIENCES

title: IDENTIFYING THE FARM ENTERPRISE CHARACTERISTICS OF YOUTH RICE FARMERS IN KEBBI STATE, NIGERIA
abstract: The study assessed the farm enterprise and socio-economic characteristics of youth rice farmers in Kebbi State, Nigeria. Using a multi-stage sampling procedure, primary data were collected from 300 respondents via structured questionnaire and analyzed using descriptive statistics. The socio-economic profile revealed a heavily male-dominated enterprise (80.00%) with a calculated mean age of 30.48 years, indicating a highly active and viable agricultural workforce. Enterprise analysis showed that youth rice production is predominantly smallholder-oriented; the majority of respondents cultivated between 1 and 5 hectares (32.50%) and relied extensively on customary inheritance (65.00%). Production methods remained largely traditional, characterized by the cultivation of local rice varieties (50.50%) and a high reliance on seeds saved from previous harvests (59.33%). The study exposed a severe institutional vacuum: 86.00% of respondents lacked contact with public agricultural extension services, and 84.00% were completely excluded from formal financial credit systems. Consequently, young farmers heavily internalized their operational risks by relying on personal savings (39.00%), family financing (34.50%), and hired labour (38.00%). Despite, the systemic bottlenecks, 66.00% of the youth managed to achieve an increase in rice yields, demonstrating high demographic resilience. The study concludes that while youth rice production in Kebbi State is inherently viable, its structural transition to a modernized, commercial enterprise is constrained by land tenure vulnerabilities, informal financing traps, and institutional neglect. It recommends that the State Agricultural Development Programme (ADP) deploy digital extension platforms to bridge the information gap and establish youth-centric, low-interest credits to reduce over-reliance on finite personal savings.
journal: KEBBI JOURNAL OF AGRICULTURE AND NATURAL SCIENCES

title: ASSESSING THE EFFECTIVENESS OF INTEGRATED PEST MANAGEMENT (IPM) STRATEGIES ON MAIZE PRODUCTION IN UHUNMWODE LOCAL GOVERNMENT, EDO STATE NIGERIA
abstract: Effective pest management strategy is an important aspect of farming that boost production. In farm farming, it is very necessary as several pest and diseases are known to affect maize and reduces yield. Intergrated Pest Management Strategies have been know to be effective on many crops but its effectiveness has not been established in maize producing area of Uhunmwode Local Government area of Edo State, Nigeria. Therefore, this study assessed the effectiveness of Integrated Pest Management (IPM) strategies in maize production among farmers in Edo State, Nigeria. Specifically, it examined farmers’ awareness of IPM strategies, their extent of use, and perceived effectiveness in reducing pest incidence and crop damage, and the determinants of IPM effectiveness. The study adopted a descriptive survey research design. A multistage sampling procedure was used to select maize farmers from selected maize-producing communities in Uhunmwode Local Government Area of Edo State. Data were collected using a structured questionnaire and analyzed with frequency counts, percentages, means, standard deviations and binary logistic regression. A decision mean of 2.50 was used to classify IPM use and effectiveness. The findings revealed high awareness of early planting to escape pest infestation (86.7%), judicious use of synthetic pesticides (84.2%), field sanitation/removal of crop residues (81.7%), intercropping (80.0%), crop rotation (75.8%), handpicking of pests (74.2%) and regular field scouting (70.0%). The most highly used and effective IPM strategies included early planting, field sanitation, regular scouting, intercropping, crop rotation, handpicking of pests and judicious pesticide use. However, biological control, pheromone traps and botanical pesticides were poorly used and perceived as less effective, indicating limited exposure to technical and ecological IPM components. Logistic regression showed that educational level, farm size, farming experience, extension contact, access to credit and IPM training significantly influenced IPM effectiveness. The model had a Nagelkerke R² of 0.452 and overall classification accuracy of 78.3%. The study concluded that IPM strategies are effective but not fully integrated among farmers. It recommended stronger farmer training, extension support, credit access and provision of IPM-related inputs.
journal: KEBBI JOURNAL OF AGRICULTURE AND NATURAL SCIENCES

title: Farmer–Herder Conflict and Agricultural Development in Benue State, Nigeria: Implications for National Security
abstract: This study assessed the impact of farmer–herder conflict on agricultural development and national security in Benue State, Nigeria. Two research objectives, two research questions, and two hypotheses guided the study. The study adopted a descriptive survey research design. The population frame comprised 2,777,727 registered voters in Benue State as reported in the 2023 electoral register, from which a sample of 384 respondents was determined using the Krejcie and Morgan sample-size table. We retrieved 341 valid questionnaires, representing an 88.8% response rate. Data were collected using a structured questionnaire titled the “Farmer–Herder Conflict and National Security Questionnaire (FHCNSQ).” Content validity was established through expert review, while internal consistency was assessed using Cronbach’s alpha. We used descriptive statistics, independent-samples t-tests, and multiple linear regression to analyse the data at the 0.05 significance level. The findings showed that farmer–herder conflict substantially disrupts agricultural development through crop destruction, farmland abandonment, reduced crop yields, labour shortages, reduced investment, and damage to agricultural equipment. The findings also showed significant national-security implications, particularly through weapon proliferation, displacement, pressure on social services, weakened public trust, and heightened social tensions. The regression model explained 71.4% of the variance in reported national-security threats. The study concludes that conflict prevention, effective land governance, community-based security mechanisms, and agricultural recovery measures are necessary to protect livelihoods and strengthen security in Benue State.

title: Deep-learning for improving prognostication and therapy prediction in breast cancer
abstract:
Treatment decisions in early breast cancer depend on accurate prognostication and on therapy-relevant biomarkers, both of which rely largely on examination of routine hematoxylin and eosin (H&E)-stained tissue. Manual assessment, however, is subject to observer variability and cannot exhaustively quantify tissue features or detect complex morphological associations. Advances in artificial intelligence have therefore prompted the development of computational tools that extract additional information from routine sections. This thesis investigates whether deep learning applied to H&E whole-slide images (WSIs) can improve prognostication beyond established clinicopathological factors and enable inference of therapy-relevant biomarkers in breast cancer. Four studies are presented, addressing (i) the design of a general modeling framework, (ii) the interchangeability of models for assessing an immune biomarker (i.e., tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes), (iii) the inference of molecular alteration from morphology, and (iv) the direct modeling of patient survival.

In the first study, we developed a model-agnostic, multiresolution multiple-instance learning (MIL) framework for WSI analysis, that aggregates features across magnifications independently of the underlying encoder or classifier. Nine MIL models were evaluated with both a domain-specific and an ImageNet-pretrained feature encoder on grade, TP53 mutation status, and survival prediction. Aggregating high- and low-magnification features by concatenation or a learnable linear transformation consistently outperformed single-resolution baselines across models and tasks, indicating that multiresolution representation is broadly beneficial rather than tied to a particular architecture.

The second study examined whether independently developed models for automated tumor-infiltrating lymphocyte (TIL) scoring can be used interchangeably in triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC). Ten machine-learning and deep-learning approaches were compared against pathologist-read stromal TILs for analytical and prognostic validity. Agreement with pathologist scoring varied across models and declined from internal to external validation. Despite this variability, eight of ten models retained significant and overlapping prognostic associations. The findings indicate that model choice affects the scores themselves, cautioning against treating such models as interchangeable in the absence of a common benchmark.

In the third study, we developed a model to infer TP53 mutation status directly from H&E WSIs, with the aim of providing a histology-based surrogate marker with prognostic value. On a held-out test set, the model discriminated mutated from wild-type tumors with an AUC of 0.83 (95% CI 0.79-0.88), while in an independent, endocrine-treated ER+ cohort, the image-derived score was associated with overall survival (HRadj = 3.88, 95% CI 1.37-10.99; p=0.011). The results provide proof-of-concept for a histology-based TP53 marker that carries independent prognostic information.

Building on the third study, the fourth study modeled overall survival directly from H&E WSIs, rather than through a molecular proxy. After adjustment for established prognostic factors, the resulting risk score stratified patients into high- and low- risk groups in the internal test set (adjusted HR, 2.17; 95% CI, 1.09-4.33; p = 0.028) and in two external cohorts: Stockholm (adjusted HR, 1.79; 95% CI, 1.23-2.62; p = 0.003) and PANTHER (adjusted HR, 1.68; 95% CI, 1.22-2.32; p = 0.001). The score also retained prognostic value in the ER+/HER2-subgroup and for recurrence endpoints. These findings suggest that a survival-trained H&E biomarker can provide risk stratification beyond established clinicopathological factors.

Taken together, these studies show that deep learning applied to routine H&E WSIs can recover prognostic and molecular information relevant to breast cancer, and they address this question at several levels, from framework-level design choices to task-specific biomarkers. They also identify methodological factors that condition the reliability of such models. The clinical role of these approaches, including any bearing on therapy selection, remains to be established through head-to-head comparison with existing tools and prospective validation.

title: Building Employment Security through Skill Development: An Empirical Analysis on Hard and Soft Skills
abstract: Livelihood security remains a critical concern for rural youth, whose employment prospects are increasingly shaped by the skills they possess rather than by formal education alone. In an economy that is rapidly shifting towards diversified and non-farm occupations, the ability to secure and sustain a livelihood depends heavily on a combination of hard and soft skills. The present study examined the role of hard and soft skills in strengthening livelihood security among rural youth. The study was carried out in the Fatehabad and Hisar districts of Haryana State. A sample of 200 respondents, including 100 males and 100 females, was selected using a random sampling method to assess skill possession, participation in skill-building initiatives, and self-perceived skill adequacy. The findings revealed that problem-solving (65%) and managerial skills (60.5%) were the most commonly reported soft skills. Among hard skills, agricultural skills (64.5%) and digital skills (43%) were the most widely held, followed by hand skills (36%) and technical skills (34%), respectively. In terms of self-assessed skill adequacy, only 26.5 per cent of respondents felt fully equipped with their current skills. The skill and ability index was highest among male respondents in Hisar (72.2) and lowest among male respondents in Fatehabad (64.6), with an overall mean of 67.1, indicating moderate skill capacity across the sample, with clear district and gender disparities. The study underscores the need for targeted skill-development interventions, particularly in entrepreneurship, digital literacy, and technical training, to bridge existing skill gaps and enhance employability and livelihood security among rural youth.

title: Bibliometric Analysis of Agricultural Mechanization Practices in Northern Nigeria
abstract: Agricultural mechanisation research relevant to northern Nigeria spans farm-power selection, service markets, irrigation, harvesting, labour allocation and emerging digital technologies. Its policy interpretation is complicated by differences between research visibility, geographical relevance and evidential strength. This critical narrative review integrates a bounded bibliometric analysis with appraisal of the substantive literature published through 31 July 2026. Searches of open scholarly and regional indexes, supplemented by citation tracing and source verification, informed the selection of 14 focal Nigeria-relevant journal articles and a wider methodological and comparative bibliography. Publication metadata were counted descriptively, while study findings were assessed according to design, measurement, geographical scope and inferential limitations. Six focal articles reported explicit northern field sites, three addressed Nigeria nationally and five included Nigeria in comparative analyses. The focal articles appeared in 14 journals between 2013 and 2025; ten were published from 2020 onwards. These are properties of the selected corpus, not estimates of regional publication growth or disciplinary influence. The synthesis indicates that mechanisation is better understood as access to timely, operation-specific services than as tractor ownership alone. Evidence concerning private hiring, rice harvesting and crop-production complementarities supports conditional benefits, but does not establish a uniform regional effect on productivity, employment or sustainability. Perception surveys, predictive models and willingness-to-adopt studies answer different questions from controlled interventions. Gendered time allocation, equipment reliability, maintenance, soil loading and water governance remain essential analytical dimensions. A defensible research agenda should combine an openly documented regional bibliography with representative service-access surveys, longitudinal provider records and operation-specific field evaluations. Mechanisation policy should consequently be assessed against service reliability, distributional outcomes and environmental performance rather than machinery counts or bibliometric prominence. The review provides an auditable account of a limited evidence base while distinguishing plausible mechanisms from effects demonstrated in particular northern settings.

title: Cooperative Stem Cell Homing and Photothermal Protection Driven by an Injectable Hydrogel for Bone-Vascular Regeneration.
abstract: Bone defects caused by trauma or disease present significant clinical challenges, necessitating advanced biomaterials that simultaneously recruit stem cells and orchestrate a conducive microenvironment for repair. Here, we present an injectable hydrogel system designed to drive integrated bone-vascular regeneration through targeted stem cell homing and localized metabolic rescue. The composite hydrogel, crosslinked from gelatin and oxidized starch, integrates liposome-encapsulated stromal cell-derived factor-1 (SDF-1) and MXene-enabled GelMA microspheres. This minimally invasive system addresses two critical regenerative phases. First, liposomal SDF-1 undergoes controlled release to effectively recruit endogenous bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells (BMSCs). Concurrently, under near-infrared irradiation, the MXene-GelMA microspheres generate mild localized heat stress (40-42 °C). Crucially, this targeted photothermal therapy acts as a metabolic rescue mechanism; it upregulates heat shock protein 70 (HSP70) in BMSCs to mitigate apoptosis, stimulating endothelial cells to promote robust angiogenesis. In vitro, this cooperative environment significantly enhanced osteogenic differentiation and vascular network formation. In vivo application in a rat critical-sized calvarial defect model validated the hydrogel's therapeutic efficacy. At 8 weeks, the composite system increased the bone volume fraction (BV/TV) by 21.07% compared to a commercial bone repair material, accompanied by extensive neovascularization. This multifunctional hydrogel establishes a synchronized, translatable strategy for advanced tissue engineering.

title: From Surge to Sustained Commitment: Role/Responsibility Internalization in Postdisaster Digital Volunteer Collaboration
abstract: This study examines the structural conditions under which postdisaster digital volunteer collaboration is associated with continuance commitment beyond surge‐like mobilization. Using a cross‐sectional online survey in a semi‐closed volunteer coordination community, the study estimates a PLS‐SEM model examining the structural associations among prosocial/value‐oriented motivation, role/responsibility internalization, trust, and continuance commitment. Results indicate significant direct associations of prosocial/value‐oriented motivation and internalization with continuance commitment, along with a significant specific indirect association from motivation via internalization (partial mediation). Trust shows no significant direct association in the structural model, suggesting it may function more as a proximal condition for entering coordination than as an anchor of continuance commitment. Overall, the findings highlight role/responsibility internalization as a role‐based identification and responsible self‐positioning construct associated with stronger continuance commitment in informal, high‐uncertainty postdisaster digital collaboration, offering a more differentiated account of commitment formation beyond initial mobilization surges.

title: Epidermal retinoid starvation driven by AKR1B10 orchestrates barrier disruption and hyperinflammation in atopic dermatitis

Equivalence of measurement properties of the Dermatology Life Quality Index (DLQI) across 13 European countries
abstract: The Dermatology Life Quality Index (DLQI) is the most widely used tool to measure burden of skin diseases and assess intervention effectiveness. It is embedded in national guidelines and disease registries in > 45 countries and available in > 138 translations. This study examined psychometric properties of the DLQI across 13 European languages. 3,408 patients had completed the DLQI questionnaire with no missing data. Confirmatory factor analysis (CFA) was performed using datasets of each country and multigroup CFA (MGCFA) across all countries. Known-group analysis was performed of DLQI sum-score against physician-assessed severity by country. All countries’ DLQI data showed essential unidimensionality with good fits to a 1-factor CFA model with CFI, TLI unscaled values all > 0.97 (COSMIN criteria). MGCFA indicated different country translations of the DLQI conceptualize the same construct and showed equality of factor loadings. Although, scalar invariance was not seen, meaning that direct comparison of mean DLQI scores across 12 countries is not supported by the current results, partial scalar invariance was achieved after constraining one threshold for DLQI item 7. Known-group analysis of DLQI versus disease severity was significant for every country (all p < 0.025). Good psychometric properties were present across all 13 languages examined with essential unidimensionality confirmed. The DLQI differentiated between levels of disease severity and EQ-5D-3 L levels across all these languages. This adds further confidence in the appropriateness of using the DLQI with this range of languages.

title: SATB2 promotes osteogenic differentiation of OPLL-derived posterior longitudinal ligament cells via Wnt/β-catenin signaling in association with RUNX2.

title: A systematic mapping of goal-oriented requirements engineering: reflections, impact, and the way forward
abstract: Goal-oriented Requirements Engineering describes the body of work which focuses on goals as the driving force motivating and capturing requirements, often using graphical goal models. A proliferation of work in this area inspired the study: “Goal-oriented requirements engineering: an extended systematic mapping study” first available in 2017, covering 246 publications in GORE up to 2015. In the current article, we have the pleasure of reflecting on this original mapping study. Using bibliometrics, we examine the study’s visibility, although such a quantitative view gives us only an approximation of real impact. The bibliometric view shows us that most citations are relatively recent: 85% of the citations have occurred since 2020. Unsurprisingly, the work has primarily been cited in requirements engineering venues, but also related venues such as the Conceptual Modeling conference (ER) and the Information and Software Technology Journal (IST). The work has been cited by a wide variety of authors. We estimate that roughly 40% of the publications citing the original SLR actually focus on goal models (have some variant of “goal” in the title), but that only roughly 53% of citing papers which are not themselves systematic reviews emphasize some form of empirical evaluation, 10% lower than the presence of empirical studies found in the original mapping study. Turning to trends and future directions, we reflect on the limitations of GORE uptake in industry, along with recommendations for continued use in education. We highlight new developments in using Large Language Models (LLMs) to generate goal models, including limitations, and reflect on what opportunities may be lost via full automation of goal model generation. We reflect on the potential role of GORE in the rising field of intent-driven engineering with AI, and the disconnect between much of this work and requirements-focused goal-oriented foundations. Finally, we consider the rising popularity of agentic AI, describing conceptual challenges and opportunities for GORE in terms of monitoring, capturing, and driving agentic system design. Overall, our reflection emphasizes that in the rise of LLMs and Agentic AI, the expressive power of GORE has great potential, and we invite the research community to explore and harness goal modeling for this purpose.

title: Integrative molecular approaches to salt stress tolerance in barley: mechanisms and implications for crop improvement and breeding
A multitask tamil speech framework for ASR, TTS, and intelligent conversational agents
Context aware multimodal plant disease diagnosis using agro ecological metadata and explainable inference
abstract: Plant disease detection is a major aspect of precision agriculture, directly impacting crop productivity and food security. Recent deep learning approaches have achieved high accuracy in disease classification from images, but most rely heavily on visual features and remain ill-posed to general changes in illumination, background complexity, image quality, and field conditions. They also have limited agro-ecological information and insufficient interpretability, limiting their practical reliability and users’ trust. This study proposes to overcome these drawbacks by leveraging a multimodal deep learning framework, ContextLeafXAI, inspired by LeafContextReasonNet. The framework considers visual phenotypic aspects alongside agro-ecological information (weather, soil, and geographical information). The proposed reliability-aware gated fusion mechanism adaptively combines information from various sources, and the dual-level explainability strategy, using Grad-CAM and contextual feature attribution, guides lesion localisation and understanding of the role of the environment. Experimental results demonstrate that ContextLeafXAI attains 96.2% accuracy, 95.2% Macro-F1 score, and 0.98 ROC-AUC, which is superior to the unimodal and multimodal baselines evaluated. The framework also shows good cross-dataset generalisation, explanation consistency and moderate computational load. The results suggest that ContextLeafXAI offers a powerful and understandable decision-support solution for plant disease diagnostics across various agricultural scenarios. Code is available at https://github.com/zakeeya12/ContextLeafXAI_Full_Implementation. Not applicable.

title: Challenges in Accommodating Talker Variability in Lexical Tone Perception Among Autistic Adults: Implications for Talker Adaptation.
abstract: PURPOSE Successful speech perception requires listeners to accommodate acoustic variability arising both across talkers and within a single talker. This challenge is especially pronounced in tone languages, where fundamental frequency (F0) simultaneously encodes lexical meaning and talker identity. The present study investigated how between-talker and within-talker variability affects lexical tone perception in Cantonese-speaking adults with and without autism spectrum disorder (ASD). METHODS Twenty-five adults with ASD and 25 neurotypical (NT) controls completed a speeded word identification task involving minimal word pairs differentiated by level tones. Between-talker variability was manipulated by presenting words produced by either a single talker or multiple talkers, and within-talker variability was manipulated by using either a single exemplar or multiple exemplars from each talker. Performance was assessed using identification accuracy, response time (RT), and a composite efficiency measure. RESULTS Both groups demonstrated reliable processing costs associated with between-talker variability, reflected in lower accuracy, longer RTs, and reduced efficiency, with no group difference in the magnitude of this effect. In contrast, only the ASD group exhibited reduced efficiency under within-talker variability. Furthermore, within-talker and between-talker processing costs were not significantly correlated in either group. CONCLUSION These findings suggest that autistic adults may experience greater difficulty accommodating subtle within-talker acoustic variability during lexical tone perception, consistent with a more detail-focused processing style. Such difficulty may have implications for everyday speech understanding in socially diverse listening environments while highlighting the importance of distinguishing between-talker normalization from within-talker stabilization in models of speech perception.
journal: Journal of autism and developmental disorders

title: 3D modeling for crop applications in precision agriculture: a review
publisher: Springer Science and Business Media LLC
abstract: Background Advances in data acquisition and information processing have strengthened the role of precision agriculture (PA) in enhancing agricultural productivity and sustainability. Among emerging technologies, 3D crop modeling offers detailed representations of agricultural scenes, supports crop phenotyping, and enables autonomous operations such as harvesting, fertilization, and pruning. However, despite the rapid development of hardware and software for 3D modeling, a comprehensive synthesis of the available approaches and their applications in PA remains limited. Purpose This review aims to examine the broad range of 3D modeling approaches used in PA, focusing on their methodological characteristics, practical applications, advantages, and limitations to support the selection of suitable solutions for different agricultural requirements. Methods A total of 168 publications, identified through a Scopus literature search covering studies published up to March 2026, were reviewed. The analysis examines 3D data types and sensing technologies, sensor platforms and application environments, and data processing methods, including data registration techniques and methods for insight extraction. Applications of 3D models to agricultural crops were also analyzed and classified into three main categories: crop phenotyping, machinery navigation, and field operations. Conclusions The review highlights the widespread adoption of LiDAR, RGB, and RGB-D sensors deployed on Uncrewed Aerial Vehicles, Uncrewed Ground Vehicles, and robotic platforms, alongside increasing use of AI-based processing methods. Challenges related to sensor robustness, multisensor interoperability, and large 3D datasets remain. Future research should focus on overcoming these limitations to facilitate the transition towards reliable, large-scale implementation of 3D modeling technologies in practical agricultural operations.

title: Changes in comprehensive ecosystem service index and landscape patterns based on water-soil-carbon nexus in upper Minjiang River watershed, Southwestern China
Integrating Weather and Potato Price Market Data into AI-Driven Hybrid Models for Climate-Smart Agricultural Forecasting
Endogenous strategy spaces in sequential- and simultaneous-move duopoly games
abstract: Duopoly markets are widely discussed in industrial economics under the assumptions of quantity and price competition in sequential- and simultaneous-move duopoly games with differentiated goods. We compare Nash and Stackelberg equilibria in which the firms endogenously choose to behave as a price or quantity setter. Using the utility function introduced by Dixit (1979), we generalize the model of Boyer and Moreaux (1987) by allowing different market sizes and show that it is always more profitable to strategically set the price (quantity) if the goods are complements (substitutes). For every degree of product differentiation, consumer surplus and total welfare are highest under the standard Bertrand equilibrium, followed by the price Stackelberg, the quantity Stackelberg, and the Cournot equilibrium. In a generalized framework of Boyer and Moreaux (1987), we show that there is no unique ranking of prices, quantities, and profits of the leader and follower depending on the degree of product differentiation and the type of competition. Furthermore, we show that the price (quantity) Stackelberg equilibrium is bounded by the Bertrand and the mixed Nash equilibrium in which Firm 1 sets the price (quantity) and Firm 2 the quantity (price).

title: Acute Ultra Low Dose THC Attenuates Anxiety-Like Behavior in a Mouse Model for Major-Depressive Disorder
abstract: Major depressive disorder (MDD) is a prevalent psychiatric disorder, and is a leading cause of disability worldwide. Current treatments for MDD entail many side effects, and include a lag until the onset of therapeutic effects. The current hypotheses as for the etiology of MDD revolve around the monoamine hypothesis and the plasticity and neurodegeneration hypothesis. According to the latter, employing a neuroprotective treatment may help ameliorate depressive symptoms. Δ9-Tetrahydrocannabinol (THC) is the primary psychoactive component of the cannabis sativa plant. THC interacts with the endocannabinoid system, which was shown to be involved in the regulation of emotional states (e.g. anxiety) and stress through modulation of synaptic plasticity. Here, we show the potential of acute, ultra-low dose (0.002 mg/kg) THC in ameliorating anxious behavior in a chronic mild stress mouse model for MDD. We utilize next generation sequencing techniques to show the treatment’s effect on neuronal differentiation and synaptic plasticity-related mRNAs, and specify Elmo domain containing 1 (Elmod1) as a molecular mediator of the observed anxiolytic effects. Moreover, we show the involvement of glucocorticoids-related mRNAs in the observed anxiolytic effect of acute, ultra-low dose THC.

title: Enhanced crop yield estimation in smart agriculture via AI and IoT using the GODL geo-optimized algorithm
abstract: Precision agriculture is one of the major breakthroughs which has been adopted to counteract some of the major challenges facing contemporary agriculture, such as maximizing crop yield, maximizing resource efficiency, and sustainability. The application of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and the Internet of Things (IoT) technologies can go a long way in enhancing crop yield prediction through data obtained from multiple sources, including satellite images, ground sensors, and weather stations. This research paper proposes a next-generation crop yield prediction system called Geo-Optimized Deep Learning (GODL) algorithm. The GODL algorithm integrates geospatial information with deep learning algorithms for crop yield analysis and prediction. This combination of deep learning and geospatial data allows accurate and scalable crop yield predictions using geospatial and sensor information. In order to ensure model optimization in terms of accuracy and efficiency, the GODL Algorithm makes use of advanced hyperparameter optimization methods that include Adam and Stochastic Gradient Descent (SGD). The research paper highlights the efficiency of the GODL Algorithm by conducting extensive experiments that compare the algorithm’s performance with other crop yield prediction models like Recurrent Neural Network (RNN) and other machine learning techniques. The evaluation takes into consideration important metrics such as accuracy, Jaccard Index, Fowlkes-Mallows Index (FMI), and G-mean, as well as IoT data delay and its effects on the prediction accuracy. In future research, the use of blockchain technology to facilitate data sharing and edge computing to process the data will be considered.

title: A tuning-fork-based microrobotic approach for the mechanical differentiation of zebrafish eggs
