title: Increased Pupil Constriction Latency in Immunoglobulin G4-related Ophthalmic Disease.
abstract: PURPOSE To examine the pupillary light reflex (PLR) in Immunoglobulin G4-related ophthalmic disease (IgG4-ROD) compared with healthy controls using virtual reality-based infrared pupillometry. DESIGN Cross-sectional matched case-control study. PARTICIPANTS Twenty-five eyes from 25 biopsy-proven IgG4-ROD patients without a history of optic neuropathy and 50 eyes from 50 age-, sex-, and smoking-matched healthy subjects were included. METHODS Participants underwent PLR assessment using a virtual reality head-mounted display with integrated infrared pupillometry. Pupillary responses to three progressively increasing white-light stimuli were recorded at 120 Hz. Twenty-seven PLR parameters were extracted across response latency, constriction, and redilation phases. Group differences were analyzed using paired t-tests, multinomial logistic regression, and backward stepwise variable selection. Machine learning classifiers were evaluated using accuracy and area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC). Main Outcome Measures Pupil constriction latency, constriction amplitude, velocity, redilation parameters, and machine learning classification performance metrics. RESULTS Pupil constriction latency at the third (highest intensity) stimulus (LAT3rd) was significantly prolonged in IgG4-ROD eyes compared with controls (P < 0.05), while other PLR parameters were comparable between groups. LAT3rd remained a significant differentiating feature on multinomial logistic regression and backward stepwise selection. Machine learning models using all features showed good performance, with Random Forest achieving an accuracy/AUC of 0.875/0.900. When using bootstrapped LAT3rd-only data, K-nearest neighbors, decision tree, and random forest models also demonstrated good classification performance. CONCLUSION IgG4-ROD eyes exhibit prolonged pupil constriction latency, suggesting subclinical involvement of the pupillary light reflex pathway. Virtual reality-based infrared pupillometry may serve as a useful non-invasive tool for detecting neural or autonomic dysfunction in IgG4-ROD.

title: Increasing Detection of Early-Onset Rectal Neuroendocrine Neoplasms in the Era of Earlier Colorectal Cancer Screening.
abstract: BackgroundThis study aimed to evaluate contemporary national trends in the presentation, management, and outcomes of early-onset rectal neuroendocrine neoplasms (EORNETs).MethodsA retrospective cohort analysis of patients <50 years who underwent surgery for rectal neuroendocrine neoplasms was performed using the National Cancer Database (NCDB) (2004-2023). Patients undergoing surgery were categorized as local tumor excision or radical resection. Five-year overall survival (OS) was estimated using Kaplan-Meier analysis, and multivariable Cox proportional hazards analysis was used to identify factors associated with OS. A sensitivity analysis was also performed in the well-differentiated neuroendocrine tumor subgroup.Results7285 patients were included; 6638 (91.1%) underwent local excision and 647 (8.9%) radical resection. The annual number of surgically treated cases increased from 234 in 2004 to 778 in 2023. 83.0% of tumors with known grade were low grade, and 90.6% of tumors with known clinical stage were stage I. Radical resection was associated with larger tumors, higher grade, more advanced stage, lymphovascular invasion, and liver metastases (all P < .001). Five-year OS was higher after local excision than radical resection (97.5% vs 85.7%, P < .001). In the full multivariable model, radical resection was associated with worse OS (HR 3.43, 95% CI 1.60-7.36; P = .002); however, this association was no longer statistically significant in the well-differentiated tumor subgroup (HR 2.52, 95% CI 0.97-6.54; P = .057).ConclusionsThe number of surgically treated EORNET cases substantially increased over time. Local excision was the predominant treatment. These findings are compatible with increased detection of indolent lesions through greater endoscopic evaluation.

title: Constraints and opportunities in cluster-based farming in Ethiopia
abstract: In many developing countries, smallholders play a central role in the agricultural sector, and holding significant potential for agricultural growth and rural development. In Ethiopia, agriculture contributes about 37.57% to Et GDP and supports the livelihoods of most of the population. However, recent agricultural growth has not efficiently addressed persistent challenges of food insecurity, malnutrition, and rural poverty among smallholder farmers. To improve productivity and promote commercialization, the Agricultural Transformation Agency introduced cluster-based farming approach aimed at transforming subsistence farming into market-oriented production system. Despite its potential benefits, the adoption and expansion of cluster farming remain limited due to several constraints. Therefore, this study reviews the opportunities and constraints of cluster-based farming in Ethiopia from social, economic, ecological/environmental, institutional, and political perspectives. This study employed a systematic literature review methodology. Relevant studies were identified through digital libraries, web sources, Ethiopian public university repositories, ATA government website and other academic databases. A keyword-based search strategy was used to identify relevant publications mainly covering the period from 2015 to 2026. Based on relevance to study objective, a total of 23 empirical studies were selected and analyzed. The findings indicate that cluster-based farming in Ethiopia provides several opportunities across multiple dimensions. Social opportunities include enhanced farmer-to-farmer interaction, knowledge sharing, and collaboration. Economic opportunities involve improved productivity, economies of scale, better market access, and increased bargaining power. Ecological opportunities include improved natural resource management and the potential adoption of climate-smart agricultural practices. Institutional opportunities arise from stronger partnerships and coordination among farmers, government agencies, and development organizations, while political support through national agricultural development strategies further promotes cluster initiatives. However, several constraints also affect the implementation of cluster-based farming. These include farmers’ resistance to collective approaches, limited economies of scale among smallholders, unfavorable agro-ecological conditions, weak institutional coordination, and political instability. Cluster-based farming has the potential to transform smallholder agriculture in Ethiopia by improving productivity, commercialization, and rural livelihoods. However, its success depends on addressing key social, economic, ecological, institutional, and political constraints. Prioritize should be given to improving rural infrastructure to better connect cluster farms with markets. Expand agricultural research, strengthening farmer training, and securing financial support for cooperatives are also essential. In addition, promoting pro-poor agricultural strategies, extending extension services and ensuring continuous government monitoring and evaluation are necessary to enhance the effectiveness and sustainability of cluster- based farming in Ethiopia.

title: Star-ov: satellite-oriented trusted authorization and responsibility with stratified model encryption and ownership verifications
abstract: With the increasing adoption of deep neural networks (DNNs) in remote sensing interpretation and on-orbit intelligent processing, protecting the intellectual property of deployed models faces new challenges, including limited onboard computational resources, constrained satellite–ground communication bandwidth, differentiated multi-user services, and difficulty in ownership attribution after model leakage. Existing model protection approaches mainly rely on either active encryption or passive watermarking mechanisms, which are insufficient to simultaneously satisfy the requirements of access control, service continuity, and post-leakage accountability in satellite-based scenarios. In this paper, we propose STAR-OV, a stratified and controllable model protection framework tailored for satellite deployment. By introducing a two-stage reversible parameter perturbation mechanism, STAR-OV enables progressive degradation of model performance from the original high-accuracy state to an intermediate-accuracy state and finally to a fully unusable state. The perturbations introduced at different stages are organized into distributable hierarchical keys, thereby supporting differentiated service access for users with varying authorization levels. Furthermore, after the model is fully restored to its original accuracy, a latent watermark is embedded. The watermark remains inactive during normal inference without the activation key, while producing stable and verifiable responses on a trigger set once the corresponding key is applied, enabling reliable ownership verification in the event of model leakage. Experimental results on multiple benchmark datasets demonstrate that the proposed method significantly reduces the usability of unauthorized models by modifying an extremely small fraction of parameters, while maintaining strong robustness against fine-tuning, pruning, and weight noise attacks. Owing to its low computational overhead and flexible deployment capability, STAR-OV provides a practical solution for resource-constrained satellite-based onboard intelligent inference scenarios.

title: Omicron SARS-CoV-2 shows NRP1-linked susceptibility in adipose-derived MSCs and alters primitive cord blood CD34⁺ HSPCs
abstract: SARS-CoV-2 infection is linked to hematologic abnormalities, but whether early hematopoietic compartments and their stromal niche are directly engaged remains unclear. We used in vitro exposure models to compare variant-associated responses of adult mesenchymal stromal cells (MSCs) and umbilical cord blood (UCB) CD34 ⁺ hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells (HSPCs). Adipose–derived (AD) and bone marrow–derived (BM) MSCs exposed to wild-type, Delta, or Omicron showed source- and variant-dependent nucleocapsid protein (NP) positivity, highest with Omicron in AD-MSCs; infectious virus in supernatants was undetectable. AD-MSCs expressed higher neuropilin-1 (NRP1) than BM-MSCs, and NRP1 knockdown reduced Omicron-associated NP signal, implicating an NRP1-linked entry process. SARS-CoV-2 exposure induced indoleamine-2,3-dioxygenase 1 (IDO1), most prominently in AD-MSCs. In UCB CD34 ⁺ HSPCs, Omicron increased NP positivity enriched in long-term HSCs, reduced primitive fraction frequencies, increased colony formation, and promoted early erythroid progenitor accumulation; heat-inactivated virus did not. NanoString profiling revealed host-response activation and altered cell-cycle/differentiation programs. These data indicate Omicron can engage stromal and early hematopoietic compartments and remodel stress-responsive hematopoiesis.

title: False Advertising, Market Competition, and Consumer Protection
abstract: We examine a model in which firms produce goods that are both vertically and horizontally differentiated. While firms know the quality of their product, either high or low, it is unobservable to consumers. Firms signal quality to consumers, and we investigate how market rivalry and public enforcement influence their incentives to misrepresent quality, as well as the implications for consumer welfare. Our analysis reveals that stronger enforcement, by curbing false advertising, can drive a low-quality signaling firm out of the market. This strengthens the market power of a high-quality signaling firm, leading to higher prices and ultimately harming consumers.

title: A Privacy-Preserving Federated Learning Framework for Paddy Leaf Disease Detection Using an Enhanced Pretrained Novel EfficientNet-Lite4 Model
abstract: The correct and prompt detection of leaf diseases in paddy crops remains essential for protecting agricultural output and yield stability and reducing major losses that occur during severe disease outbreaks. The widespread use of conventional centralized machine learning techniques becomes impractical for real-world agricultural applications, as their effectiveness diminishes under three main conditions: data privacy limitations, delayed transmission of information, along with reduced performance accuracy from non-independent and identically distributed (non-IID) data properties across different agro-climatic regions. This research develops a decentralized diagnostic system which combines Federated Learning with an Enhanced Pretrained Novel EfficientNet-Lite4 model designed for paddy leaf disease classification. The Paddy Doctor dataset served as training material for the system which contained 16,225 RGB images that classified 12 disease types alongside healthy categories. The proposed model reached 98.7% classification accuracy and 98.5% precision and 98.6% F1-score while maintaining a final loss of 0.21 after 100 communication rounds. The system underwent field testing which demonstrated its ability to generate accurate diagnostic results in real time in various working conditions. The study demonstrates how privacy preserving AI-based paddy disease management works in practice and recommends local agricultural institutions to build decentralized learning systems. The suggested system will give farmers direct access to field level decision support and facilitate the creation of sustainable digital pest management systems required to ensure food supply.

title: Early Detection of Apple Scab in Orchards and Mildew in Vineyards Using A Novel Deep Learning Model and Multispectral Imagery
abstract: Agricultural diseases are a significant problem for growers as they cause substantial damage to fruits and leaves, leading to yield losses. Therefore, developing systems for early detection of plant diseases is a crucial issue. In this study, a new deep learning-based hybrid model is presented for the detection and segmentation of plant diseases, specifically apple scab disease in apple orchards and mildew disease in vineyards. Multispectral imagery data collected in agricultural areas of Tekirdag province in Turkey via drones between May 2023 and December 2024 were used in developing the early disease detection system. The datasets contain 3625 images of apple orchards and 5625 images of vineyards. DJI Phantom 4 Multispectral drone, equipped with five spectral bands (Blue, Green, Red, Red Edge, and Near Infrared), was utilized to capture both spectral richness and temporal progression. This study introduces a novel deep learning architecture developed specifically for time series-based disease detection and segmentation using multispectral drone imagery. Changes in plants over time provide important information about the occurrence of plant diseases. For this reason, time series were used in this study to extract features from the changes in plants over time. The proposed model architecture was specifically designed to leverage time series information, enabling robust tracking of crop health changes over time. The model trained with the dataset collected for apple diseases achieved an average Intersection Over Unit (IoU) value of 82.05%, while the model trained with the dataset collected for vineyard diseases reached an IoU value of 79.67%. The findings highlight the effectiveness of integrating drone-acquired multispectral time-series data with advanced deep learning models for scalable, accurate, and timely plant disease detection in precision agriculture.

title: Beyond accuracy in crop classification: calibration, selective prediction, and robustness
abstract: Introduction: Near-perfect crop-label accuracy can conceal uncertainty, perturbation sensitivity, and weak explanations. This study evaluates these reliability dimensions without treating benchmark classification as an agronomic recommendation. Materials and methods: Ten classifiers were evaluated using five matched stratified fitting, validation, and test partitions on a 2200-record crop-label benchmark and an independent 3810-record rice-grain benchmark. A Calibrated Selective Forest combined Random Forest, validation-fitted temperature scaling, and confidence-based abstention. Analyses included feature and component ablations, probability calibration, Gaussian input perturbations, computational cost, and explanation fidelity. Results: Mean crop-label accuracy was 99.59% for Random Forest, 99.23% for Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), and 98.32% for Feature Tokenizer Transformer (FT-Transformer). Random Forest (RF) calibration reduced mean expected calibration error from 0.0449 to 0.0038. At a 0.95 threshold, calibrated selection retained 98.59% of predictions with 0.091% mean selective error. Under perturbations of 0.20 training standard deviations, its accuracy fell to 86.96% and selective error rose to 4.29%. On rice grains, RF accuracy was 91.71%, and calibration did not improve every probability metric. Local explanation rankings were often stable despite a median neighborhood-weighted R 2 of 0.293 under the specified Local Interpretable Model-agnostic Explanations (LIME) configuration. Conclusions: Accuracy, calibration, selective reliability, and explanation fidelity are distinct properties. The composite pipeline provides an auditable benchmark procedure, not a new learning algorithm or a validated farm recommendation system. Geographic and temporal agronomic validation remain necessary.

title: Agile AI Agentic Neural Based Framework for Complex Workflow Forming, with Multiple Implementations Upon Upstream and Downstream Scenarios
abstract: The oil&gas sector increasingly depends on agile, reliable, and explainable workflow automation to support production and operations activities such as wellbore fault diagnostic, maintenance, and pipeline scheduling. However, existing genAI-based agents technologies are limited by complex workflow forming, lack of cross-scenario generalization, and insufficient continuous refinery mechanisms, which restrict their ability to support long procedure workflows or adapt to evolving operating conditions. This study proposes an Agile Agentic Neural (AAN) framework that autonomously forms, executes, and refines complex workflows. The approach is designed to address upstream wellbore workovers and downstream pipeline scheduling, enabling event sensing, task planning, tools coordination, and continuous improvement through dual human-machine feedforward mechanism. The objective is to establish an operationally robust and scalable approach that accelerates production decision-making while maintaining interpretability and safety across integrated asset operations. The AAN framework adopts a neural network inspired architecture with 3 layers. The input layer performs scene recognition, semantic understanding, and task decomposition from multimodal field data (e.g., SCADA, production logs), using distributed self supervised distributed agents to ensure quality-grounded fusion. The computational layer organizes sub-agents within dynamically selected topologies—mesh, tree, code or workflow structures based on operational context. A supervisor agent uses in-context refinement and historical success logs to optimize decisions such as diagnostics, workflow planning, and response actions examining. The output layer assembles executable workflows and employs a dual feedforward loop that integrates engineer feedback and machine-observed metrics, enabling digital-twin-like self-refinement without retraining. Validation includes 60 shale wellbore maintenance cases (pump leaks, rod failures, scaling, wax deposition) and pipeline scheduling scenarios within previous couples of years, involving equipment faults, weather anomalies, and supply-demand disturbances. Ablation studies compare four feedback mechanisms to assess robustness. Across wellbore maintenance tasks, the AAN framework achieved human and agent evaluation scores of 0.76-0.98, with standard deviations <0.1 in event sensing, task planning, agent coordination, and tool use. Pipeline scheduling cases showed comparable performance, with 0.74-0.93 accuracy and strong stability under multiphase flow and hydrat risk conditions. Cross-scenario generalization maintained 0.85-0.94 accuracy, though toolusage precision declined in highly heterogeneous cases. Ablation testing confirmed the superiority of the global dual-feedback design, achieving 0.78-0.98 accuracy with the lowest variance (0.02-0.19), highlighting its value for real-time production control and risk mitigation.
journal: SPE Asia Pacific Oil & Gas Conference and Exhibition

title: An Ontology Construction Framework for Asset Lifecycle Management: Agentic Travelling Approach with Field Application in Shale Oil Wellbore Maintenance
abstract: The rapid deployment of AI-native applications in complex wellbore operations requires unified, high-quality data integration to sustain continuous model evolution and reliable asset lifecycle management. However, heterogeneity in standards, semantics, and system architectures across legacy operational datasets limits their immediate applicability for dynamic and agile AI workflows. In alignment with the digital transformation priorities on information management, knowledge integration, and emerging technology implementations, this study develops a Human- and Entity-Centric Agentic Travelling Approach (HATA) for constructing dynamic-static ontology that support adaptive, cross-scenario data integration. This supports the energy transformation by enabling adaptive data integration for complex decision scenarios, validated through 3 typical types of downhole failure cases. HATA introduces a self-organising ontology construction framework composed of three specialised AI agents configured to address data quality challenges in knowledge modelling, and semantic enabled data integration. The planner interprets engineer-determined themes and decomposes them into ontology construction tasks; the traveller explores latent representational spaces to generate ontology candidates optimised for scenario relevance; and the supervisor assesses structural and semantic consistency, providing iterative feedback to guide refinement. The approach was evaluated using operational datasets (2021-2024) from 45 shale-oil wellbores in western China, focusing on wax deposition, scaling, and pump leakage, with corresponding financial management. More than 40 multi-modal parameters including deviation surveys, dynamometer cards, electrical parameters, inspection logs, operational and maintenance (O&M) alarms, and workover records were mapped through the HATA semantic and compared with expert curated benchmarks using a similarity threshold of 0.8 to quantify semantic alignment and structural completeness. Across all evaluated scenarios, the agentic ontology builder demonstrated substantial improvements in interpretability, operational efficiency, and data assembly performance. User intent comprehension achieved expect accuracy, with a single misinterpretation observed. Task planning precision approached optimal levels, while ontology construction cycles were completed within 40 seconds to 2 minutes, requiring minimal supervisory adjustments. Generated datasets reached an average semantic similarity exceeding 0.82 compared with field engineer benchmarks. Importantly, the resulting dynamic ontologies reduced decision-making time for failure diagnosis from approximately 1.5 hours to ≤10 minutes per case. These outcomes demonstrate the potential of HATA to benefit asset lifecycle management and strengthen AI-enabled operational workflows envisioned for wellbore intelligent transformation. This work introduces an innovative agentic travelling methodology for ontology construction, representing a novel innovation of genAI agentic system for ontology and knowledge modelling within shale oil wellbore downhole operations. Unlike static ontology, HATA also supports continuous evolution through digital-twin-driven updates, enabling the generation of adaptive "data blueprints" for predictive analytics. By bridging fragmented legacy datasets with emergent AI workflows, the methodology advances data science priorities in new technology deployment, valuation, and knowledge management, offering a scalable pathway for future energy transformation capabilities.
journal: SPE Asia Pacific Oil & Gas Conference and Exhibition

title: Reaction-Kinetics Control on Geo-Hydrogen Generation in Fractured Ultramafic Rocks
abstract: Natural hydrogen is increasingly considered a potentially low-carbon subsurface energy resource, particularly where H2 can be generated through serpentinization of iron-bearing ultramafic rocks. Engineered or stimulated natural hydrogen concepts rely on the same water–rock reactions, but the rate at which hydrogen is generated at reservoir scale remains uncertain because reported kinetic parameters for olivine alteration vary widely between laboratory studies. This extended pilot paper isolates the influence of reaction kinetics on reservoir-scale hydrogen generation using a dual-porosity reactive transport model implemented in CMG-GEM. The model represents a fractured olivine-rich reservoir at approximately 5000 m depth, 300 °C, and 500 bar, with all petrophysical properties held constant while the Arrhenius frequency factor and activation energy are varied systematically. The results show that kinetic parameters strongly control both the timing and magnitude of H2 generation. Increasing the frequency factor from 5×10-8 to 5×10-6 1/(s·molality) shifts substantial H2 generation from late time to early time and raises the final cumulative yield. Similarly, reducing activation energy from 25 to 2.5 kJ/mol accelerates reaction onset by more than an order of magnitude and increases the plateau yield by approximately one quarter. A new kinetic-response summary is introduced to compare breakthrough timing, t₅₀, t90, and plateau yield across the tested cases. The findings demonstrate that production forecasts for stimulated hydrogen systems cannot rely on generic kinetic inputs alone; site-specific calibration against representative core or pilot data is essential before field-scale performance can be assessed reliably.
journal: SPE Asia Pacific Oil & Gas Conference and Exhibition

title: A Scoping Review of Foundation Models in Dementia Research
abstract: Foundation models (FMs) are increasingly applied to dementia for multiple purposes, but their main scopes and limitations remain unclear. We examined how FMs are used for dementia detection, diagnosis, prognosis and risk prediction. Eligible studies applied a pre-trained, fine-tuned or commercial LLM FM to these tasks in people with or at risk of dementia, in English, January 2022 to August 2026. Searches of PubMed, Europe PMC, arXiv and Google Scholar yielded 474 unique records, screened to 50 analysed papers, charted by taxonomy, scope, dataset, performance and validation. Of these, 8 used pre-trained FMs, 26 fine-tuned FMs and 16 commercial LLMs (detection and diagnosis predominated). Performance was not comparable across classes (tasks, datasets and metrics differed). Demographic reporting was poor: race and ethnicity in 4/50 studies, age in 24/50, studies concentrated in the USA. The literature remains at proof of concept, requiring larger, diverse datasets and rigorous validation.

title: LLM-HB: Language-Aware LLM-Guided Hotword Biasing for Code-Switching ASR
abstract: Code-switching (CS) speech, characterized by language alternation within a single utterance, is prevalent in multilingual communities and poses challenges to automatic speech recognition (ASR) due to rapid language transitions. We propose LLM-HB, a language-aware large language model-guided hotword biasing framework for code-switching ASR (CS-ASR). The framework incorporates a mixture-of-experts (MoE) adaptor and an auxiliary language prediction head to better capture and differentiate multilingual representations, while hotwords are injected through LLM-based prompting. Experiments on the ASRU2019 code-switching challenge test set demonstrate that LLM-HB achieves a 20.30% relative reduction in mixed error rate (MER) over the baseline, reaching 5.85% MER under a 15-distractor hotword setting. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first work to integrate LLM-guided biasing into code-switching ASR. We further release the extracted ASRU2019 hotword list to support future research.

title: Comparison of wastewater treatment processes through a water-energy-carbon lens: insights from South Korean sewerage statistics and process-based modelling
abstract: This study evaluated water-energy-carbon performance of municipal wastewater treatment plants in South Korea by integrating the Korean Sewerage Statistics Yearbook (2018–2024) with process simulations. Greenhouse gas emissions were evaluated following the 2019 refinement of Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change guidelines. The public data analysis showed that electricity-related emissions accounted for 44.9% of total greenhouse gas emissions, while direct emissions of nitrous oxide and methane from bioreactors accounted for 42.6%. Environmental performance of six processes was assessed using an integrated water–energy–carbon coupling index combining effluent quality, energy consumption, and carbon footprint. As a result, each process had weakness on following factors: energy consumption for anaerobic-oxic (AO), effluent quality for modified Ludzack-Ettinger, and greenhouse gas emission for AO, anaerobic-anoxic-oxic, and four-stage biological nutrient removal. Multi-linear models for estimating direct emissions with operational factors based on simulation results were built. Dissolved oxygen and sludge retention time had a negative relationship with direct emissions. Simulation results further indicated that higher effluent ammonia concentrations were associated with increased direct emissions. Simulation would be a powerful tool for finding weakness of process and guiding management on the integrated perspective.

title: NB+: Diabetes Prediction using Novel NeuroBoost Algorithm NeuroBoost: A Novel Hybrid Deep Learning and Boosting Framework for Accurate Diabetes Prediction
journal: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology
publisher: Dr. Yashwant Research Labs Pvt. Ltd.
abstract: Diabetes is among the major chronic diseases that have adversely impacted millions of individuals all around the world. Early prediction of diabetes is crucial as it will help the clinicians to provide timely medications and prevent health-related problems from happening. Past researches done on the topic of diabetes prediction utilized conventional machine learning techniques such as Logistic Regression, Random Forest, Support Vector Machines, and Artificial Neural Network (ANN). Though conventional machine learning models have proven to be effective in producing accurate results, they are still constrained with their inability to offer high levels of accuracy while predicting results and inability to establish the linkages between different health factors. In order to solve these problems, this research suggests the usage of NeuroBoost which is characterized by the uniqueness of the model since it is a combination of learning capability of neural network and boosting prediction capability. The main goal of the innovative model is to identify hidden patterns from data related to diabetes. The efficiency of the suggested approach was evaluated via testing on two widely used databases such as PIMA Indian Diabetes Dataset and real-world Primary dataset obtained from the Hospital. As a result of the experiments, the performance of the NeuroBoost model was identified as 98.00% accuracy with PIMA and 91% with primary dataset. Such results demonstrate the superiority of the suggested model in comparison with some other methods concerning the prediction of diabetes. Thus, the NeuroBoost innovative model can help healthcare practitioners identify patients who have high risks of developing diabetes and take necessary measures.

title: Childhood-Oncology Intelligence for Predicting Cancer Emergence, Optimizing Precision Therapies, and Simulating Lifelong Outcomes in Pediatric Malignancies Using Autonomous Foundation Models
journal: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology
publisher: Dr. Yashwant Research Labs Pvt. Ltd.
abstract: Background. Pediatric malignancies remain a leading cause of disease-related mortality in children, yet prediction of cancer emergence, optimal therapy selection, and long-term survivorship is constrained by fragmented multimodal data and limited transfer of adult oncology models to childhood disease biology. We developed an autonomous foundation model (PedOnco-FM) that jointly learns from clinical, genomic, imaging, histopathology, and laboratory data to support the full pediatric oncology care continuum. Methods. A retrospective cohort of 350 children (0–18 years) was assembled across four tertiary centers, spanning acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL), acute myeloid leukemia (AML), neuroblastoma, Wilms tumor, medulloblastoma, osteosarcoma, and Ewing sarcoma. PedOnco-FM employs self-supervised pretraining followed by task-specific fine-tuning for risk stratification, treatment-response prediction, progression forecasting, and survivorship simulation. Performance was benchmarked against Random Forest, XGBoost, and a deep neural network using nested cross-validation with an external held-out test set. Results. PedOnco-FM achieved an accuracy of 0.931, F1-score of 0.921, and an area under the receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve (AUC) of 0.961 for outcome prediction, exceeding XGBoost (AUC 0.908) and the deep neural network (AUC 0.926). Predicted risk strata separated five-year survival cleanly (low risk 0.93, intermediate 0.74, high 0.51). MYCN amplification, TP53 mutation, and minimal residual disease (MRD) were the dominant predictors. Survivorship simulation reproduced observed late-event hazards with a concordance index of 0.84. Conclusions. An autonomous foundation model integrating multimodal pediatric data delivers accurate, interpretable, and clinically actionable predictions across the disease lifecycle, supporting earlier risk-adapted intervention and individualized survivorship planning. Prospective multi-center validation is the necessary next step toward clinical deployment.

title: Precision Oncofertility: Integrating Genomics, Reproductive Biomarkers, Treatment Toxicity Profiles, and Foundation Models for Fertility Preservation in Men and Women with Cancer
journal: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology
publisher: Dr. Yashwant Research Labs Pvt. Ltd.
abstract: Background: Cancer survivors of reproductive age face substantial risks of treatment-induced gonadotoxicity, yet clinical decision-making for fertility preservation remains largely empirical and population-based. A precision oncofertility framework that integrates genomic, biomarker, and toxicity data is urgently needed. Objective: To develop and validate a multimodal foundation model that integrates genomic variants, sex-specific reproductive biomarkers, treatment toxicity profiles, and clinical variables to predict fertility impairment risk and support individualized fertility-preservation decisions in cancer patients. Methods: A retrospective observational cohort of 400 patients (age 18–45 years) diagnosed with breast cancer, lymphoma, leukemia, testicular cancer, ovarian cancer, cervical cancer, or colorectal cancer was assembled. All patients received fertility-preservation counselling prior to treatment. Data included reproductive biomarkers (anti-Müllerian hormone (AMH), antral follicle count (AFC), follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH), estradiol; sperm concentration, motility, testosterone, inhibin-B), genomic features (BRCA1, BRCA2, CHEK2, TP53, FMR1), treatment toxicity variables (alkylating agent and platinum exposure, radiation dose, stem cell transplantation), and standard clinical covariates. A transformer-based foundation model with four specialised encoders and cross-modal attention was developed. Performance was benchmarked against Random Forest, XGBoost, and a Deep Neural Network using accuracy, precision, recall, F1 score, and area under the receiver-operating-characteristic curve (AUC). Results: The foundation model achieved the highest performance across all metrics: accuracy 0.883, precision 0.876, recall 0.862, F1 0.869, and AUC 0.934. AMH (importance score 0.187), AFC (0.171), and alkylating agent exposure (0.152) were the strongest predictors. Fertility risk stratification identified 37.0% (n=148) low-risk, 35.5% (n=142) moderate-risk, and 27.5% (n=110) high-risk patients. BRCA1/2 mutations and radiation dose independently amplified impairment risk. Conclusion: A precision oncofertility framework incorporating multimodal data and transformer-based architecture substantially outperforms conventional machine-learning approaches. AI-guided risk stratification can enable individualized, evidence-based fertility-preservation counselling and intervention, with direct implications for clinical oncofertility practice.

title: Integration of information technology in agricultural extension to enhance innovation and farmers' income in agribusiness
abstract: Information technology has increasingly transformed agricultural extension by expanding farmers’ access to timely knowledge, innovation, and market information. This study aims to examine the integration of information technology in agricultural extension and its contribution to agricultural innovation and farmers’ income in agribusiness. This study employs a library research approach using relevant primary and secondary literature obtained from books, peer-reviewed journals, scientific articles, research reports, and other academic sources. Data were collected through literature review and analyzed using content analysis to identify patterns, relationships, and significant findings related to information technology, agricultural extension, innovation adoption, and farmers’ income. The findings indicate that digital technologies can improve information accessibility, strengthen technology acceptance, facilitate innovation adoption, and support better production and marketing decisions. The study concludes that information technology can strengthen agricultural extension and contribute to improved farmers’ economic outcomes when supported by digital literacy, adequate infrastructure, relevant information, and institutional support.

title: FROM AIOPS TO AGENTOPS: SERVICE-LEVEL OBJECTIVES AND ERROR-BUDGET-GOVERNED AUTONOMY FOR PRODUCTION AI AGENTS
abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents now run production workflows, including IT and network operations, yet they are usually monitored with signals designed for deterministic services: availability, latency, and error rate. An agent can satisfy all three while completing the wrong task. This paper extends AIOps-style service management to agentic systems. It contributes a layered set of service-level indicators (SLIs) covering platform health, step-level tool use, verified task outcomes, and guardrail integrity; a taxonomy of seven agent failure classes mapped to the signals that expose them; and an error-budget policy that governs an agent's autonomy as well as its release cadence. A Monte Carlo simulation of a production operations agent evaluates the approach across 2,100 injected incidents. Conventional platform monitoring detected only platform failures, firing in at most 1.7% of runs for the other six classes. Burn-rate alerting on verified task outcomes detected every class in 89.7% to 100% of runs within 24 hours, with no false alarms, but took a median of 3.5 to 10.6 hours under standard thresholds. A change-aware rule, active for six hours after a deployment or model change, cut median detection of change-induced regressions to 44 to 63 minutes at a cost of about one additional page per month. The results support layered, outcome-based service-level objectives as the operational basis for production agents.
journal: World Journal of Advanced Engineering Technology and Sciences

title: The concept of adaptive management of the process of launching innovative medicines to the pharmaceutical markets of BRICS countries (review)
abstract: The article substantiates the need for the BRICS countries to transition from static to adaptive models of regulatory governance for the process of launching innovative medicines, primarily advanced therapy medicinal products (ATMPs), to the market. Based on a system-oriented analysis of scientific publications and official regulatory documents, trends in the development of biotechnological medicines and the transformation of regulatory systems are identified. It is demonstrated that China, India, Brazil, South Africa, Russia, and the EAEU states are implementing various configurations of adaptive regulation, including accelerated and prioritized procedures, conditional approvals, reliance approaches, Early Access Programs (EAPs), digitalization of dossiers (CTDs), and the integration of realworld evidence. A concept of adaptive management is proposed, including interrelated notions as follows: adaptive drug lifecycle management, adaptive regulation, adaptive pathways and adaptive design of clinical trials. This model is shown to allow for reducing delays in providing access to vital innovative medicines along with strengthening the scientific and methodological basis for regulatory decisions. Priority areas for the formation of a common adaptive regulatory space for BRICS countries are identified, including the development of joint scientific consulting centers, the harmonization of procedures, the expansion of mutual recognition practices, and the integration of digital technologies.

title: A Hybrid Multi-Objective Optimization Framework for Crop Planting Planning under Digital Economy
abstract: With the deep integration of artificial intelligence and the digital economy in agriculture, traditional crop planting planning still suffers from slow convergence, limited optimization accuracy, and weak adaptability to ecological and market uncertainties. To address these challenges, this study proposes a multi-objective crop planting optimization model that integrates the Multi-Objective Grey Wolf Optimizer (MOGWO), the non-dominated sorting genetic algorithm II, and proximal policy optimization, enabling dynamic decision-making driven by multi-source data. Experimental results on two authoritative datasets showed that the model achieved Pareto frontier coverage above 90% and stable convergence within 500 iterations. Multi-scenario simulations indicated that peak annual net profit exceeded 1.8 million yuan, and annual carbon reduction potential generally exceeded 150 tons of CO2, while computation time was maintained at approximately 4.8s per 100 iterations. Overall, the proposed model demonstrates strong robustness, ecological effectiveness, and computational efficiency, supporting intelligent agricultural decision-making under the digital economy framework.
journal: Journal of Engineering, Project, and Production Management

title: OPERATIONAL MANAGEMENT OF A LARGE AGRICULTURAL ENTERPRISE IN ECUADOR: AN INTEGRATED APPROACH TO PRODUCTION, LOGISTICS AND SUSTAINABILITY
abstract: The transformation of the agricultural sector, driven by technological development, climate change, resource constraints, market volatility and geopolitical risks, is reshaping the role of operational management within agricultural enterprises. The aim of this study is to analyse the operational management system of a large agricultural enterprise in Ecuador, using Reybanpac as a case study, with a focus on the integration of production, digital technologies, quality management, logistics, resource efficiency, sustainable development and operational resilience. The methodology combines a systems approach, the case study method, comparative analysis and the evaluation of quantitative indicators of production and export activities. A high level of vertical integration and coordination of processes, from banana cultivation to international distribution, has been identified. The role of GPS technologies, drones, biological plant protection, water recirculation systems, certification and traceability has been substantiated. It has been demonstrated that the combination of technological innovations, logistical integration, resource efficiency and sustainability form an operational model capable of ensuring the enterprise’s competitiveness and resilience.

title: АДАПТАЦІЯ АГРОПРОМИСЛОВОГО СЕКТОРУ УКРАЇНИ ДО СУЧАСНИХ ЕКОНОМІЧНИХ ВИКЛИКІВ: ФІНАНСОВО-ЕКОНОМІЧНИЙ АСПЕКТ
abstract: The current development of Ukraine’s agro-industrial complex is taking place against a backdrop of significantly increasing pressures in the economic, social, geopolitical, and environmental spheres, which have negatively impacted the operational efficiency of economic entities, as well as their financial stability and competitiveness. Military operations, macroeconomic instability, inflationary pressures, disruptions in supply chains, labor shortages, exchange rate fluctuations, changes in global agricultural market conditions, climate risks, and the acceleration of European integration processes are shaping the new conditions under which the agro-industrial sector is forced to operate, and existing models for managing and financing the sector require adaptation. This article examines the current economic challenges that shape the trends in the functioning and development of the agro-industrial sector amid global economic instability, military conflicts, the transformation of international markets, climate change, and the intensification of European integration processes. It systematizes the key internal and external factors influencing the production, financial, and investment activities of agro-industrial enterprises. The study analyzes the impact of macroeconomic instability, inflationary pressures, logistical constraints, disruptions in production and distribution chains, labor shortages, changes in tax and credit policies, as well as risks associated with martial law, on the operational efficiency of the agro-industrial sector. The paper justifies the need to adapt the management system of agro-industrial enterprises to contemporary economic challenges by enhancing financial stability, diversifying funding sources, implementing digital technologies and innovative management approaches, developing export potential, and utilizing government support mechanisms. It has been demonstrated that increasing the agro-industrial sector’s adaptability to contemporary economic challenges is a necessary prerequisite for ensuring its competitiveness, the country’s food security, and Ukraine’s sustainable socioeconomic development.

title: Enhancing PISA-aligned argumentation skills of prospective biology teachers through generative artificial intelligence
abstract: Despite scientific argumentation being a fundamental competency of the PISA assessment framework, prospective biology teachers often demonstrate insufficient development in evidence-based reasoning and rebuttal construction skills. Considering the limitations of large-scale implementation of individualized approaches in higher education, this study evaluates the effectiveness of Generative Artificial Intelligence (ChatGPT-4) configured as a “Socratic tutor” in developing argumentation skills among future educators. An 8-week quasi-experimental study involving 124 students from a pedagogical university employed traditional peer discussion methods in the control group ( n = 62), while the experimental group ( n = 62) utilized an AI agent that induced cognitive dissonance regarding socio-scientific issues. Analysis of Covariance (ANCOVA) of data obtained through Toulmin's Argument Pattern (TAP) and PISA rubrics confirmed that the experimental group achieved statistically significantly higher overall argumentation quality compared to the control group (F (1,121) = 14.23, p < .001, η 2 = .105). Particularly, participants who received AI-assisted instruction showed marked improvement in forming rebuttals and evaluating counterevidence, which are considered among the most cognitively demanding components within the PISA scientific literacy framework (OECD). These findings suggest that a Generative AI-mediated Socratic instructional package can be an effective and scalable approach for developing epistemic cognition, and they propose a pedagogical model for integrating structured AI-based tutoring into teacher preparation systems aligned with international assessment standards. These findings should be interpreted as evidence for the effectiveness of the structured, AI-mediated Socratic instructional package as a whole, rather than as evidence of AI's inherent superiority over other methods; the relative contribution of the AI medium versus the structured pedagogical protocol it delivers was not directly tested in this design.

title: Geminiviruses and their satellites: genomic diversity, evolutionary insights, and emerging models
abstract: Geminiviruses infect a wide range of economically important crops, including tomato, cassava, cotton, common bean, and maize, and are characterized by twinned icosahedral particles containing circular single-stranded DNA (ssDNA) genomes. Their genomes have undergone extensive diversification through mutation, recombination and association with satellite molecules. Depending on the genus, geminiviruses are transmitted by hemipteran vectors, including whiteflies, leafhoppers, aphids, and treehoppers, and replicate in plant cell nuclei using host replication machinery, which complicates disease management. Recent taxonomic updates by the International Committee on Taxonomy of Viruses (ICTV) in MSL41 recognize 549 species distributed across 15 genera, with Begomovirus accounting for most of the documented species diversity and Mastrevirus representing the second-largest genus. Analysis of documented records across eight geographic regions revealed the highest documented geminivirus species richness in the Indian subcontinent. Current evidence indicates that geminivirus diversification is shaped by multiple interacting evolutionary mechanisms, with recombination and modular genetic exchange contributing substantially to the formation of mosaic genomes, while host compatibility and vector ecology impose important ecological and functional constraints on their persistence and diversification. The discovery of previously unrecognized geminivirus lineages, endogenous geminivirus-related sequences, and additional genomic diversity through high-throughput sequencing indicates that the currently recognized diversity of geminiviruses remains incomplete. The evolutionary origin of geminiviruses remains partly unresolved because replication-associated and capsid-associated components show distinct evolutionary histories. Based on comparative genomic, phylogenetic, and recombination evidence, we propose a modular evolutionary model in which replication-associated and capsid-associated components followed distinct evolutionary trajectories, followed by genome-level assembly and diversification associated with the emergence of bipartite genome organization. Overall, the emerging view is that geminiviruses represent genetically and ecologically dynamic lineages shaped by interacting evolutionary processes rather than a single evolutionary trajectory. Broader sampling of hosts and vectors, comparative genomics and functional validation will be essential for resolving their origin and evolutionary relationships.

title: A study on the identification of wheat powdery mildew using chlorophyll fluorescence imaging
abstract: Wheat powdery mildew poses a serious threat to global wheat production, and its accurate identification is key to smart agriculture. This study combines chlorophyll fluorescence imaging with deep learning algorithms to investigate the temporal dynamics of key fluorescence parameters (such as maximum photochemical efficiency, QYmax) during the progression of powderymildew. A QYmax-based chlorophyll fluorescence image dataset for wheat powdery mildew was constructed. Building on this, the LCRNet model was proposed, which effectively processes fluorescence image data through a collaborative mechanism integrating the Large Selective Adaptive Fusion (LSAF) and Coordinated Attention (CA) modules. On an independent test set, the model achieved an accuracy of 94% and an F1 score of 94.1%, outperforming comparison models. This study proposes a method for classifying the severity of powdery mildew in wheat that reduces the computational cost of fluorescence data processing, providing important methodological support and technical insights for advancing the intelligent, precise, and green transformation of crop disease prevention and control systems.

title: Multi-source temporal fusion and multi-station learning for early warning of diamondback moth infestation in Brassica crops
abstract: Meteorological variability influences diamondback moth (DBM; Plutella xylostella ) infestation and the resulting damage to Brassica crops. Accurate multi-horizon forecasting requires models that preserve short-lived meteorological exposures while integrating thermal timing, spatial dependence, and recent infestation dynamics within a transparent framework. The Temporal–Geospatial Pest Network (TG-PestNet) forecasts the weekly percentage of inspected plants classified as DBM-infested 1 to 4 weeks ahead at four Guangdong stations, from origin-time information only. It preserves hourly exposure, encodes lookback weeks on a thermal-time axis, couples stations through a wind-informed graph, and protects infestation history in a gated anchor. Evaluation used 344 synchronized weeks, 66 later test origins, 13 history-only comparators, retraining ablations, matched-width controls, and input-matched generic encoders. TG-PestNet achieved the lowest observed root-mean-square error, mean absolute error, and mean absolute percentage error in all 12 station–metric combinations, with mean reductions of 5.9%–13.0%. Year-ahead forecasts outperformed persistence in all four test years. Removing the history anchor increased error by 14.3% and remained significant after multiplicity correction, demonstrating its central contribution to forecast accuracy. Meteorological information provided complementary predictive value: its occlusion increased the error by 9.3%, and retraining without it increased the macro RMSE by 3.6%. TG-PestNet also substantially outperformed the two input-matched generic encoders, whose errors were approximately one quarter higher. These results establish TG-PestNet as an accurate, reproducible and auditable framework for multi-station pest forecasting, with component-level analyses that identify the dominant contribution of recent infestation history and characterize the predictive roles of high-resolution meteorology and structured spatial information.

title: PlantDefender: a unified deep learning approach for maize disease and pest detection
abstract: Maize crops face severe threats from various diseases and pests, significantly affecting crop quality and yield. Prompt and accurate diagnosis is essential to minimize agricultural losses. Existing models have demonstrated limitations in handling complex backgrounds, inter- and intra-class variations, and inefficient feature extraction, which complicate the recognition of maize diseases and pests. This study proposes a unified deep learning model, termed PlantDefender, for the simultaneous recognition of maize diseases and pests. PlantDefender employs an improved Faster R-CNN architecture with a refined InceptionResNet-V2 as its backbone. The conventional InceptionResNet-V2 is modified by replacing the ReLU activation function with Swish to enhance feature extraction. The extracted features are subsequently processed through the Region Proposal Network (RPN), ROI Align, regression, and classification modules for accurate detection and recognition. The model is evaluated using the IP102 dataset for maize pest recognition and the CD&S dataset for maize leaf disease recognition. PlantDefender achieves an accuracy of 78.67% on the IP102 dataset and 98.44% on the CD&S dataset. The results demonstrate effective localization and classification performance across both maize pest and disease recognition tasks. The experimental results indicate that the proposed PlantDefender framework can effectively address the challenges associated with the recognition of maize diseases and pests. By integrating the refined InceptionResNet-V2 backbone with Faster R-CNN, the proposed unified model provides a promising approach for automated and accurate maize crop protection.

title: From solar heat to digital drying: integrating computational fluid dynamics, process optimisation, and digital twins for sustainable tuber-chip drying
abstract: Root and tuber crops such as cassava, yam, and sweet potato are central to tropical food systems but remain highly vulnerable to postharvest deterioration because of their high moisture content. Solar drying offers a renewable route to stabilisation, yet practical performance is constrained by fluctuating weather, non-uniform airflow, spatial temperature and humidity gradients, product loading, and strong coupling between external convection and internal moisture transport. This structured narrative mini-review, informed by SANRA and PRISMA reporting principles, synthesises evidence on active solar drying, computational fluid dynamics (CFD), experimental validation, response-surface and multi-objective optimisation, artificial intelligence (AI), sensor systems, and digital twins for tuber-chip processing. Six databases were searched, sources were screened against explicit eligibility criteria, and each of the 45 cited sources was classified by its relationship to tuber-chip drying so that tuber-specific evidence is separated from evidence transferred from other foods and dryer types. Only 12 of the 45 sources were tuber-specific; they concentrate on yam drying kinetics, cassava dryer performance, and one integrated machine-learning and 4E study of sweet-potato solar drying. CFD validation, robust optimisation, surrogate modelling, and digital-twin architectures are, in the evidence assembled, largely transferred from other products or from unloaded or non-tuber systems. Reported effective moisture diffusivities for yam span roughly 6.4 × 10 −9 to 1.6 × 10 −7 m 2 s -1 (up to 4.2 × 10 −8 m 2 s -1 for water yam); an indirect solar dryer for sweet potato achieved 15% overall thermal efficiency, 4.5 kWh per kilogram of moisture removed, and a 29-month payback; and a CFD–ANN–genetic-algorithm framework reproduced no-load airflow and temperature fields to within 7.3% error. Because these values arise from different dryers, products, and metric definitions, they are compared critically rather than ranked. The evidence suggests that CFD is most valuable when it resolves spatial transport phenomena that cannot be inferred from inlet and outlet measurements, and that AI is most defensible when it accelerates validated physics rather than replacing it. A prioritised research agenda is proposed, beginning with tuber-specific property data and loaded-dryer CFD validated against product moisture, and progressing conditionally to robust optimisation, validated surrogates, digital shadows, and multidimensional sustainability assessment for cassava, yam, and sweet-potato chips.
journal: Frontiers in Food Science and Technology

title: Smart water management in agriculture: convergence of sensors, imaging, AI, precision irrigation, and robotics systems
abstract: Agricultural irrigation systems can bear the heavy losses of water through runoff, evaporation, and deep percolation. Crop water requirements vary with crop species, growth stage, soil properties, evapotranspiration, weather, and plant water status; therefore, irrigation scheduling based on a single parameter is insufficient. Conventional water management systems often rely on uniform application, fixed scheduling, and limited real-time information, which overlooks spatial and temporal variation in soil, crop, and weather conditions and can result in water loss, over-irrigation, and under-irrigation. This review highlights studies on the integration of AI-driven sensing and imaging technologies, IoT-based precision irrigation, variable-rate technologies, digital twins, and agricultural robotics for crop water management. These approaches integrate field, crop, weather, and spatial information to support water-demand assessment, crop-stress monitoring, irrigation scheduling, site-specific application, and automated water management. The reviewed studies report water savings, improved water-use efficiency, crop performance, and more site-specific irrigation and input application across different crops and irrigation systems. The review also highlights the limitations of these systems, including sensing reliability, model transferability, connectivity, interoperability, cybersecurity, investment costs, and environmental effects. Overall, the integration of these technologies provides potential for timely and field-specific irrigation decisions and supports efficient and climate-resilient water management in agriculture.

title: Joint determination of factors influencing adoption of climate smart agricultural practices in modern rice production in Southwest Bangladesh: a multivariate probit approach
abstract: Climate change and environmental degradation are increasingly threatening rice production in the coastal regions of the developing world, where the goals of raising productivity and building resilience became a joint priority. Climate smart agriculture offers a portfolio of practices that serve both goals, yet knowledge on how farmers in saline rice systems combine these practices, and why adoption remains often partial, is still limited. This study jointly examines the factors associated with the adoption of five common climate smart practices (i.e., crop diversification, agroforestry, integrated soil fertility management, small scale irrigation, and integrated pest management) among modern rice farmers in southwest Bangladesh, using a multivariate probit model. The analysis draws on 493 farm households randomly selected from complete household lists in three purposively selected villages, one in each of three districts spanning the region’s salinity gradient. Results show that adoption decisions are interdependent, and most households maintain a portfolio of three or four practices. Soil improving practices complement one another, whereas small scale irrigation substitutes for diversification and soil and pest management. Education, farm size, livestock ownership, and climatic exposure are associated with specific individual practices, while access to credit, extension services, and market information are associated with adoption across the portfolio. The findings highlight the important roles of institutional access and climate-related factors in the adoption of climate smart agricultural practices, particularly advisory services, credit access, and support for investment-intensive practices.

title: From downstream demand to upstream innovation: how a digital platform coordinates agri-food value chain upgrading—the case of Taotian Digital Agriculture
abstract: Digital platforms are becoming increasingly involved in upstream agricultural production, yet existing research offers limited explanation of why consumer-facing platforms move beyond transaction intermediation or how they coordinate innovation across fragmented agri-food value chains. This study addresses this question through an in-depth case study of Taotian Group’s ready-to-eat kiwifruit project in China, drawing on interviews, field observations, internal corporate documents, government materials, and public sources. The case evidence indicates that upstream involvement followed the platform’s recognition that unstable fruit quality, inadequate postharvest technologies, and weak market rewards for quality improvement were constraining downstream value creation. Taotian Digital Agriculture responded by translating consumer demand into a clearly defined product target and coordinating the technological and organizational adjustments required across production, processing, storage, logistics, and sales. Demand forecasting, product grading, and differentiated market channels further reduced uncertainty over innovation returns and reinforced upstream investment. The study identifies a demand-to-innovation mechanism through which downstream market capabilities are converted into upstream innovation and coordination capabilities. The case further indicates that the durability and inclusiveness of platform-led upgrading may depend on stable economic returns, accessible local services, manageable compliance costs, risk-sharing arrangements, and platform governance. The study therefore clarifies how a consumer-facing platform can link demand interpretation, upstream innovation coordination, and market-value realization, while identifying economic and social conditions that warrant further empirical examination.

title: PRISM: Probabilistic Trajectory Prediction of Non-Cooperative Aerial Objects for Risk-Aware Path Planning in Urban Air Mobility Operations
abstract: Urban air mobility path planning must account for objects that do not provide cooperative surveillance information, but their motion and avoidance responses vary by class, making a single extrapolated trajectory insufficient to inform every path decision. We propose PRISM to bring alternative futures and their uncertainty into path planning. Using current sensor tracks, PRISM predicts three 15 s trajectory branches with probabilities and time-varying positional uncertainty. Forecast positions are used to screen candidate paths for potential collisions, while a time-indexed risk field derived from the predictive distribution ranks the paths that remain. This allows different possible futures to inform path selection without being collapsed into one trajectory. While work to extend the method to three-dimensional motion continues, the present study evaluates this approach in a two-dimensional horizontal-plane simulation containing aircraft, birds, and drifting objects with different motion and avoidance rules, including classes absent from training. Prediction tests, repeated futures from saved simulator states, and paired closed-loop episodes assess forecast quality and planning outcomes against a constant-velocity forecast. In in-distribution (ID) tests, PRISM’s mixture-mean average displacement error was 72.54 m versus 122.53 m for constant velocity, about 41% lower without future-based branch selection; the closest of three branches gave a 62% reduction. With raw predictive scales, exploratory paired comparisons supported fewer screened severe union encounters (minimum separation below 45 m) and greater lower-tail separation in three of five settings. The nominal out-of-distribution (OOD) severe-encounter contrast was uncertain without screening, while both ID contrasts retained support. Nominal-OOD sampling was extended after initial outcomes were examined. Total encounter counts within 152.4 m showed no clear difference from constant velocity. In the recalibration control, improved predictive coverage did not yield a consistent planning gain. PRISM brings possible motion across object classes into a common planning interface without requiring the target’s class or intent in advance. Its contribution is to make those alternatives and their uncertainty usable for path selection without changing the planner’s structure, and to assess their value through closed-loop separation as well as trajectory accuracy.

title: Sunflower Sector Performance in Romania, Hungary, and Bulgaria During 2005–2024: A Comparative Assessment of Production, Climate, Markets, and Trade
abstract: Assessing the performance of a sunflower sector requires more than simply tracking production volumes. How the sector performs over time also depends on yield stability, climate exposure, market adjustment, and the way trade is structured. This study provides an integrated overview of the sunflower sectors in Romania, Hungary, and Bulgaria over 2005–2024, focusing on their long-term performance and adjustment patterns. The analysis draws on harmonised data on crop production, growing-season climate, producer prices, and international trade. To capture these different dimensions, we combine area–yield decomposition, detrended instability measures, crop-area-weighted climate exposure, two-way fixed-effects models, and descriptive trade indicators within a non-compensatory analytical framework. Romania recorded the highest mean production (2.21 million t) and the greatest detrended yield instability (18.1%), whereas Hungary achieved the highest mean yield (2.61 t ha−1) and the lowest yield instability (8.2%). Across 57 annual country transitions, yield changes made a larger mean absolute contribution to production variation (313,628 t) than changes in area (116,954 t). In pooled two-way fixed-effects models, higher temperature anomalies were linked to lower yields, while a more favourable climatic water balance was linked to higher yields. A 1% rise in production was associated with a 0.31% fall in the real producer-price index, whereas lagged production coefficients were not statistically different from zero. Bulgaria had the highest mean net raw-seed export intensity (0.48), while Hungary recorded the highest processed-export share (0.60). These results identify areas for country-specific assessment of climate risk management, market adjustment, logistics, and processing economics rather than demonstrating the effectiveness of particular policy interventions. The framework reveals distinct national patterns without treating them as a resilience ranking or as direct evidence of domestic value added.

title: Machine Learning-Based Estimation of Crop Water Stress Index in Eggplant Under Different Irrigation Regimes
abstract: This study investigated water stress in eggplant (Solanum melongena L.) grown under field conditions in Bafra, Türkiye, from 2015 to 2017. Five irrigation treatments were evaluated with three replicates: full irrigation (I1), 75% (I2), 50% (I3), 25% (I4), and rainfed conditions (I5). The crop water stress index (CWSI) was calculated for each treatment. Five artificial intelligence algorithms—adaptive neuro-fuzzy inference system (ANFIS), fuzzy logic (FL), gene expression programming (GEP), support vector regression (SVR), and random forest (RF)—were used to estimate the calculated CWSI. Models were trained with combinations of canopy-to-air temperature difference (Tc − Ta), vapor pressure deficit (VPD), and solar radiation (Rs), producing 35 models across seven input combinations. Self-organizing maps (SOMs) were used separately to explore the topological relationships among the inputs and CWSI. Among the evaluated models, ANFIS4, based on Tc − Ta and VPD, produced estimates closest to the calculated CWSI values. Because the reference CWSI itself was derived from Tc − Ta and VPD, this result should be interpreted as accurate reproduction of the empirical CWSI relationship under the experimental conditions. The approach may provide a basis for sensor-assisted irrigation decision support, although independent validation is required before operational application.

title: WRF Cold-Pool Sensitivities Relevant to Winter Ozone Modelling in the Uinta Basin
abstract: Cold-pool structure controls the confinement of wintertime ozone and its precursors in Utah’s Uinta Basin. Previous studies have documented difficulty capturing stable cold pools in meteorological models, complicating air quality simulations when pollutants disperse too readily. Herein, we evaluate the meteorology behind one such high-ozone event on 2 February 2013 with Weather Research and Forecasting (WRF) simulations; the chemistry is not simulated. We test the sensitivity to Global Forecast System (GFS) or North American Mesoscale (NAM) forcing, domain feedback, boundary-layer and surface-layer schemes, slope-aware radiation, and terrain datasets (fine versus coarse). Across five hourly samples, GFS-driven runs were warmer at the evaluated surface sites, had an approximately 3.6 K smaller 50–500 m potential-temperature endpoint difference, and had a 0.8–1.0 m s−1 larger layer-mean wind-vector magnitude than feedback-matched NAM runs. The GFS also retained a lower mean heat deficit, indicating a weaker modelled cold pool. The heat deficit increased in all four runs from 1400 to 1800 UTC; hence the difference in driving model suggests a state difference without demonstrated faster cold-pool erosion. Toggling feedback and parametrisation settings yielded smaller responses; terrain fineness produced spatial responses that station comparisons could miss. The results guide diagnostics for subsequent air-chemistry modelling, while leaving initial versus lateral forcing, cold-pool depth, and basin export for future studies.

title: Installation Personas: A Persona-Centered Framework for AI-Driven Interactive Art Installations
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is enabling interactive art installations to become increasingly adaptive and socially interactive, yet limited conceptual guidance exists for analyzing installations themselves as persona-like entities. In this study, the Installation Persona Framework is proposed, extending persona-centered analysis from users and individual AI agents to AI-driven interactive installations. The framework conceptualizes Persona Identity through two complementary dimensions—Persona Type and Persona Role—and examines their expression through Persona Behavior and Interaction and association with Artistic Function and Intended Audience Experience. Using a structured screening process, 41 AI-driven interactive installations were selected from 329 artworks presented at the IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (CVPR) AI Art Gallery from 2024 to 2026. Qualitative analysis identified seven recurring Persona Archetypes and eight higher-order Persona Role Families. An independent classification assessment carried out by four external coders showed statistically significant but fair intercoder agreement for Persona Archetype (Fleiss’ κ = 0.266) and Persona Role Family (κ = 0.203), indicating measurable but limited classification reproducibility and ambiguity in category boundaries. Because audience evaluation was not conducted, audience experience was limited to artist-intended or researcher-inferred interpretations based on available documentation. Overall, the framework provides a structured vocabulary for analyzing AI-driven interactive installations as integrated persona-like entities.

title: Foundation Models and Vision-Language Models in Medical Imaging: A Review
abstract: Foundation models (FMs) and vision-language models (VLMs) have emerged as a transformative paradigm in artificial intelligence, reshaping the landscape of medical image analysis and clinical decision support. Building upon large-scale pretraining on heterogeneous datasets, these models exhibit unprecedented generalization and zero-shot transfer capabilities, effectively overcoming the perennial bottleneck of annotated data scarcity that has historically constrained deep learning applications in healthcare. This review paper presents the state of the art in FMs and VLMs applied to medical imaging, encompassing a broad spectrum of modalities including radiography, computed tomography (CT), magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), pathology whole-slide images, ophthalmology, dermatology, and echocardiography. A structured taxonomy of architectures, training strategies, and adaptation mechanisms is provided, covering contrastive learning (CLIP-based), generative, and hybrid paradigms. Also, seminal works are critically analyzed, such as MedCLIP, BioViL, BiomedCLIP, MedSAM, SAM-Med2D, LLaVA-Med, Med-PaLM 2, CONCH, and BiomedGPT, examining their methodological contributions, benchmark performance, and inherent limitations. Additionally, research gaps are discussed, including insufficient 3D volumetric understanding, limited multimodal reasoning in rare disease contexts, translational barriers for clinical deployment, and critical ethical concerns such as algorithmic bias and privacy. Further, emerging trends are presented encompassing instruction-tuned multimodal large language models (LLMs), agent-based systems, federated learning, and FMs for time-series physiological data. Finally, research directions are highlighted for clinically validated, equitable, and deployable AI systems in medical imaging.
