title: Feature-level fusion of Sentinel-1 SAR and Sentinel-2 optical imagery for crop-type mapping in humid tropical mountainous terrain
abstract: Accurate crop-type mapping in humid tropical mountains is challenged by persistent cloud cover, rugged topography, and fragmented smallholder parcels. This study evaluates a feature-level fusion workflow that integrates Sentinel-2 optical indices and Sentinel-1 SAR backscatter for crop-type mapping in Candipuro District, Lumajang, East Java, Indonesia. Sentinel-2 surface reflectance and Sentinel-1 IW data acquired in June–July 2023 were harmonised in Google Earth Engine to a common 10 m pixel grid, so that all comparison maps were evaluated on the same spatial support. The optical component comprised NDVI, NDBI, and NDWI, whereas the radar component used the VH/VV polarisation ratio. A DEM was used only to characterise the mountainous setting and to assist terrain interpretation, and was not included as a predictor in the classifier. The stacked feature image was classified using a Random Forest model trained with 101 field-survey ground control points representing eight land-cover/crop-related classes. Accuracy was assessed using 393 stratified random validation points. The fused-image classification achieved an overall accuracy of 93% and a kappa coefficient of 0.90. The fusion workflow yielded richer thematic differentiation than the optical-only comparison scenarios, particularly for water bodies, sugarcane, and shrubland. However, class-level results reveal substantial uncertainty for corn fields and moderate confusion in built-up and water classes. Therefore, the present workflow should be interpreted as a site-specific, single-date proof of concept rather than a fully transferable operational solution. The results indicate that Sentinel-1/Sentinel-2 feature fusion is promising for crop-type mapping in cloud-prone mountainous landscapes, while future work should incorporate multi-temporal phenology, richer vegetation indices, SAR texture features, uncertainty mapping, and broader field sampling.

title: A Deep Learning-Based Framework for Tomato Leaf Disease Classification Using Image Preprocessing and Convolutional Neural Networks
abstract: Tomato leaf diseases can reduce crop productivity and quality, motivating automated image-based classification systems. This paper presents an experimentally evaluated convolutional neural network (CNN) framework for ten-class tomato leaf disease classification. The final reported model is a custom CNN consisting of three convolutional layers, three max-pooling layers, ReLU activations, and a fully connected classification head with ten outputs. Convex-hull preprocessing and Otsu thresholding are applied before CNN classification. The dataset contains 18,345 images covering nine disease classes and one healthy class, with 300 images reported as the held-out test set. The experimental record reports a class-wise average test accuracy of 94.5%. Class-wise precision, recall, and F1-score are additionally reported from the supplied experimental figures. The submitted training/validation learning curve spans approximately 1000 epochs, which resolves an inconsistency in the earlier manuscript that stated five epochs. The comparison with VGG16, InceptionV3, and MobileNet is retained as a descriptive author-run baseline comparison; because the available record does not preserve complete split and hyperparameter information for every baseline, the values are not treated as a rigorously controlled benchmark. The study demonstrates performance on the evaluated public dataset, but it does not establish generalization to independently collected field images
journal: Interdisciplinary Journal of AI, Machine Learning & Data Science

title: A Review of Machine Learning and Deep Learning Techniques for Automated Tomato Leaf Disease Detection
abstract: Tomato is an economically important crop, and disease infection can reduce plant health, productivity, and fruit quality. Image-based machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL) methods have therefore been investigated for automated recognition of tomato leaf diseases. This narrative review examines the progression from handcrafted feature-based ML methods to convolutional neural networks (CNNs), transfer learning, lightweight architectures, attention mechanisms, and recent model-compression and multi-task approaches. The review considers the data characteristics, preprocessing strategies, learning paradigms, evaluation conditions, computational requirements, and evidence of generalization reported by representative studies. The literature shows that conventional ML can perform well on small, carefully prepared datasets but depends on the quality of handcrafted representations. CNN-based methods learn task-specific visual representations and generally provide stronger performance on multi-class tomato leaf image datasets. However, very high reported accuracies are frequently obtained on controlled or curated datasets, particularly PlantVillage-derived data, and therefore should not be interpreted as direct evidence of field performance. Studies using field images or explicitly measuring model size, FLOPs, inference speed, or mobile/edge execution provide stronger evidence concerning practical deployment. The principal research gaps are limited field diversity, illumination and background variation, class imbalance, weak cross-dataset validation, inconsistent evaluation protocols, and insufficient reporting of deployment metrics. Future research should therefore evaluate not only classification accuracy but also robustness, independent validation, computational cost, and reproducible deployment conditions.
journal: Interdisciplinary Journal of AI, Machine Learning & Data Science

title: FUZZY MODELING OF SOIL SALINITY BASED ON SPECTRAL INDICATORS DERIVED FROM DIGITAL IMAGERY
abstract: This study addresses the assessment of soil salinity levels in irrigated agricultural lands using digital remote sensing data. The main objective of the research is to develop a mathematical model for the quantitative assessment of soil salinity by processing spectral information contained in digital imagery and remote-sensing indicators associated with salinity on the basis of fuzzy set theory. The proposed approach considers the use of membership functions to account for the natural and transitional nature of salinity boundaries, the fuzzy evaluation of different spectral indicators, and their aggregation into a single integral salinity indicator. Based on the model, an algorithm for spatial identification and digital mapping of salinity levels is envisaged. The research results are aimed at establishing a scientific and methodological basis for rapid and spatially differentiated assessment of the salinity status of irrigated agricultural lands, supplementing existing field studies with remote sensing data, and automating salinity monitoring.
journal: Natural Sciences in the Modern World, Vol. 5, No. 18 (2026)

title: IMPROVING GRAPEVINE CULTIVAR SELECTION AND CULTIVATION TECHNOLOGIES IN OLTIARIQ, UZBEKISTAN: AGROBIOLOGICAL EVALUATION, CLIMATE ADAPTATION, AND MARKET-ORIENTED PRODUCTION
abstract: Grapevine cultivation is an important component of agricultural production in the Fergana Valley of Uzbekistan, where local viticultural knowledge and favorable growing conditions provide opportunities for producing high-quality table grapes and other grape products. However, the long-term competitiveness of grape production increasingly depends on selecting cultivars that are well adapted to local agroecological conditions, improving vineyard management practices, optimizing water and nutrient use, and meeting changing market requirements. This article examines scientific approaches to improving grapevine cultivar selection and cultivation technologies in Oltiariq district, Fergana region. Particular attention is given to the relationship between cultivar characteristics, soil and climatic conditions, irrigation management, pruning and canopy management, disease susceptibility, fruit quality, and economic performance. An integrated cultivar evaluation framework is proposed, combining phenological observations, yield measurements, berry quality analysis, water-use indicators, disease monitoring, and market assessment. The article also proposes a comparative field-trial model for identifying grape cultivars with the greatest agronomic and commercial potential under local conditions. The study is conceptual and based on scientific literature and international guidelines for grapevine cultivar characterization. It does not present new experimental measurements from Oltiariq. The proposed framework can serve as a foundation for future field research, demonstration vineyards, and evidence-based recommendations for grape producers.
journal: Natural Sciences in the Modern World, Vol. 5, No. 18 (2026)

title: Zonation Hallmarks in Human PSC-Derived Hepatic Organoids Integrated into an Immune-Compatible Organ-on-Chip for Liver Injury Modeling.
abstract: Liver metabolic zonation enables hepatocytes to carry out diverse, spatially organized functions essential for liver homeostasis and metabolism. However, in vitro recapitulation of zone-specific diversity, particularly in human pluripotent stem cell (PSC)-derived hepatocyte-like cells (HLCs), remains challenging, as these cells typically exhibit an immature phenotype. Here, we report a scalable differentiation protocol for generating 3D organoids from PSCs with defined zone 1 (z1-HLCs) or zone 3 (z3-HLCs) identities. When benchmarked against primary human hepatocytes (PHHs), these HLCs exhibit zone-specific enhanced postnatal metabolic functions. z1-HLCs reveal high albumin and urea production, whereas z3-HLCs show elevated glutamine secretion and cytochrome P450 (CYP) enzyme activity, including CYP3A4, CYP1A2, and CYP2C9. Hallmarks of functional zonation were further confirmed via proteomics, transcriptomics, metabolic assays, and oxygen consumption. z3-HLCs show increased sensitivity to acetaminophen-induced cytotoxicity and distinct immune interactions with primary monocytes. Collectively, the zonated liver organoids provide a promising platform for studying zone-specific liver metabolism, drug metabolism, toxicology, and liver disease, including liver injury.

title: Photo-Controlled Treatment for Psoriasis-Like Skin Lesions by UVB-Photoactivated Hydrogen Sulfide Donors and Pterostilbene.
abstract: Smart and efficient drug delivery is always desirable, especially for chronic diseases, such as psoriasis. We developed an ultraviolet B (UVB) light-triggered scaffold, 1,4,2-dioxazol-5-thione (DOT), for the controlled release of hydrogen sulfide (H2S), a pivotal endogenous gaseous signaling molecule with promise for anti-inflammatory and antioxidant therapies. In the DOT scaffold, the kinetics for H2S release are efficiently tuned by fine-adjusting the electronic properties. Upon photoirradiation, DOT releases carbonyl sulfide (COS), which is rapidly converted to H2S by carbonic anhydrase (CA). Furthermore, the DOT platform is conjugated to the active pharmaceutical ingredient pterostilbene (PTE) to afford a hybrid prodrug, PTE-DOT. Under UVB irradiation at 308 nm, a standard wavelength for psoriasis phototherapy, PTE-DOT simultaneously released H2S and PTE, thereby exerting combined anti-inflammatory and antioxidant effects in vivo. In the psoriasis mouse model, PTE-DOT effectively reduced epidermal thickening and hyperkeratosis, suppressed the production of key psoriatic inflammatory cytokines, and inhibited the differentiation of Th17 cells in the spleen. Thus, the photo-controlled prodrug strategy provides a platform for designing smart drug delivery systems to ameliorate psoriasis-like skin inflammation.

title: LLMs as Representation Generators for Gradient-Free Scientific Optimization: A Case Study in Battery Fast Charging.
abstract: Scientific optimization problems are often characterized by slow, expensive, and non-differentiable evaluations, which severely limit efficient exploration of rich design spaces. In these settings, performance depends not only on the optimizer itself, but also on whether the chosen search space can represent good solutions and whether important design requirements are effectively incorporated into the search. Here, we introduce a gradient-free optimization framework based on large language models (LLMs) that enables the generation and refinement of executable control policies directly from natural language. We propose two complementary paradigms: Prompt-to-Optimizer (P2O), which combines LLM-based structural generation with gradient-free parameter optimization, and Prompt-to-Protocol (P2P), which directly synthesizes fully specified control policies. We apply this framework to battery fast-charging protocol design, a representative slow-feedback optimization problem. Across multiple case studies, our methods outperform conventional approaches restricted to predefined functional forms. In a realistic fast-charging scenario, both approaches improve battery state of health by approximately 4.2% over a representative baseline, with P2P achieving this under matched evaluation budgets. More broadly, our results suggest that LLMs can serve as representation generators that expand the hypothesis space of scientific optimization, enabling efficient search in domains where evaluations are costly, and gradients are unavailable.

title: Heel movement and foot biomechanics in aluminium nail-on and indirect glue-on fabric cuff shoes in horses.
abstract: BACKGROUND Heel movement is critical to shock absorption and vascular perfusion of the equine digit. Conventional horseshoeing techniques are suspected to restrict natural hoof deformation, affecting hoof biomechanics. Several studies have explored the effects of shoeing on hoof function, though many have been limited to artificial conditions, cadavers, or homogenous populations. OBJECTIVE We aimed to compare the effects of two aluminium shoeing techniques, nail-on versus indirect glue-on fabric cuff shoes, on heel movement in horses. Our objective was to determine which technique allowed greater heel movement on hard and soft footing. STUDY DESIGN A controlled in vivo experimental study using a repeated-measures design. METHODS Fifteen healthy horses underwent three trials: (1) indirect glue-on fabric cuff shoes, (2) barefoot, and (3) aluminium nail-on shoes. A displacement sensor was affixed to the heels of one forelimb. Measurements were taken on hard and soft footing. Data were analysed using mixed-model ANOVA to determine differences in heel movement. RESULTS Heel movement was significantly greater when barefoot (p < 0.0001). Mean heel displacement for the walk on hard ground was highest in barefoot horses (3.03 ± 0.67 mm), followed by glue-on shoes (2.23 ± 0.58 mm), and aluminium nail-on shoes (1.96 ± 0.48 mm). At the trot, mean heel movement was greatest in barefoot horses (3.29 ± 0.62 mm), followed by glue-on shoes (2.56 ± 0.55 mm), and aluminium nail-on shoes (2.12 ± 0.47 mm). MAIN LIMITATIONS The two main limitations were: (1) The lack of an absolute zero baseline measurement, preventing differentiating between heel expansion and contraction. (2) Low heel conformation in some horses prevented recordings on soft footing, reducing the statistical power. CONCLUSIONS This study reinforces previous findings that shoeing restricts heel movement. Indirect glue-on shoes allow for more heel movement than nail-on shoes at the trot; both techniques limit heel movement compared to barefoot.

title: Circulating Tumor Cell Synaptophysin and Androgen Receptor Expression Reflect Prostate Cancer Phenotypes in Metastatic Disease.
abstract: BACKGROUND Chronic exposure to androgen receptor (AR)-targeted therapies can drive lineage plasticity, leading to treatment resistance and neuroendocrine prostate cancer (NEPC), characterized by loss of AR expression and acquisition of neuroendocrine (NE) markers including synaptophysin (SYP). We evaluated concordance between circulating tumor cell (CTC) AR and SYP expression patterns and evidence of NE differentiation defined by clinical, pathologic, and genomic features. METHODS CTCs from patients with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (mCRPC) were analyzed using the RareCyte platform with quantitative immunofluorescence imaging for SYP and AR. In patients with ≥ 5 CTCs, associations of CTC phenotype with PSA at collection and overall survival (OS) were assessed using the Wilcoxon rank-sum test, Fisher's exact test, and Kaplan-Meier analysis. Patients were retrospectively classified as AR-positive adenocarcinoma or NE-differentiated based on clinical, pathologic, and genomic data. RESULTS The AR/SYP CTC assay was analytically validated using cell-line spike-in models, achieving > 90% accuracy for both biomarkers. Of 52 patients with mCRPC, 27 had ≥ 5 evaluable CTCs and were included in the primary CTC phenotype analyses. The NE-differentiated cohort had a higher fraction of SYP-positive CTCs (median 28.6% vs 0.0%, p = 0.0084), whereas the AR-positive adenocarcinoma cohort had a higher fraction of AR-positive CTCs (median 96.7% vs 0.0%, p = 0.0004). Classification based on high AR or SYP expression (≥ 80% of CTCs positive) significantly distinguished cohorts and was associated with tissue histology (p = 0.0048). PSA at CTC collection was lower in the NE-differentiated cohort (median 3.83 vs 486.89 ng/mL; 95% CI: -1016 to -190.9). OS did not significantly differ between groups. CONCLUSION SYP and AR CTC expression showed strong concordance with tissue histology and clinical features of NE differentiation and AR-positive adenocarcinoma. These findings support the feasibility of CTC immunophenotyping to characterize lineage-associated phenotypes including SYP-expressing NE differentiation in mCRPC. Prospective validation in larger cohorts with matched tissue biopsies is needed to define the clinical utility of this approach.

title: Automatic insect identification, counting, and monitoring techniques: a review.
abstract: BACKGROUND Insect pests threaten agricultural productivity, while conventional surveillance is labour-intensive and excessive pesticide use creates environmental and health risks. This review evaluated automated insect detection, counting, classification and monitoring technologies, focusing on machine-learning integration, field transferability, and operational readiness. RESULTS A PRISMA 2020-guided formal search covering publications from 2010 to 2024 identified 313 records relevant to the technological and methodological scope of the review. After title/abstract screening and full-text eligibility assessment, 116 publications were retained. The evidence encompassed camera- and vision-based systems; acoustic, infrared, and optoelectronic sensors; electrostatic and physical approaches; non-lethal photonic monitoring; radar and biosensing technologies; Internet of Things-enabled platforms; and machine- and deep-learning methods. Camera- and vision-based systems were among the most extensively documented and field-oriented approaches, particularly when integrated with remote image acquisition, communication networks, and automated classification. Acoustic systems provided complementary options for continuous or low-power monitoring, whereas radar, biosensing, and other emerging approaches broadened applications toward biodiversity assessment, large-area surveillance, and early detection. Reported performance was not directly comparable across publications because metrics, acquisition conditions, and validation levels differed substantially, ranging from laboratory or dataset benchmarks to semi-field trials, field validations, and operational deployments. CONCLUSION No single technology is optimal for all monitoring objectives. Operational adoption requires standardized task-specific reporting, independent and sustained field validation, representative datasets, improved transferability across crops and environments, and system-level assessment of robustness, energy autonomy, connectivity, maintenance, and cost. Sensor fusion, edge artificial intelligence, and domain-adaptive or uncertainty-aware models are promising when they provide measurable decision-support benefits. © 2026 The Author(s). Pest Management Science published by John Wiley & Sons Ltd on behalf of Society of Chemical Industry.

title: Mogroside V Promotes Brown Adipose Thermogenesis via FTO-m6A-LETMD1-UCP1 Pathway to Combat Obesity.
abstract: Obesity is a chronic, recurrent, and progressive disease caused by energy imbalance. N6-methyladenosine (m6A) modification regulates fat thermogenesis, potentially counteracting obesity. Mogroside V (MV) is a triterpene glycoside extracted from Siraitia grosvenorii and has shown beneficial effects in models of obesity. However, its underlying mechanism remains unknown. The objective of this study is to investigate the effects of MV on adipose thermogenesis and explore the mechanism of m6A modifications in mediating these effects. Mitochondrial respiration analysis, histological and molecular biological methods were used to investigate the thermogenesis in differentiated C3H10T1/2 brown adipocytes and adipose tissue in high-fat diet (HFD)-fed mouse models, respectively. Stable cell models with overexpression or knockdown of fat mass and obesity-associated protein (FTO) were generated to investigate the effects of FTO on m6A modification and thermogenesis in brown adipocytes. Methylated RNA immunoprecipitation-quantitative-PCR (MeRIP-qPCR) and RIP-qPCR analysis were used to reveal the potential downstream molecular targets of FTO. MV improved HFD-induced obesity and metabolic dysfunction in mice. MV also increased uncoupling protein 1 (UCP1) expression in brown adipose tissue and enhanced mitochondrial respiration and expression of peroxisome proliferator activated receptor γ coactivator 1α (PGC1α) and UCP1 in differentiated C3H10T1/2 cells. Further analysis of the relevant molecular mechanisms showed that MV suppressed FTO expression, thereby increasing m6A modification of LETM1 domain-containing protein 1 (Letmd1) mRNA. The m6A-modified Letmd1 transcript was recognized by the m6A reader YTH domain-containing protein 2 (YTHDC2), thereby increasing the stability of Letmd1 mRNA. The increased Letmd1 mRNA levels were correlated with increased LETMD1 protein abundance, which subsequently enhanced the expression of PGC1α and UCP1, ultimately promoting brown adipocyte thermogenesis. MV promoted brown adipocyte thermogenesis through the FTO-m6A-LETMD1-UCP1 axis, suggesting a potential therapeutic strategy for obesity.

title: Positioning agroforestry within the scientific literature on Vanilla planifolia: a global bibliometric and thematic assessment
An empirical performance comparison of deep learning models for apple leaf disease recognition
abstract: Currently, Biotic and abiotic factors, in agriculture, are estimated to be responsible for around 22% of the total losses in crop production. It is therefore very important, but at the same time very difficult for farmers to identify these constraints at the earliest possible stage. The most recent developments in computer vision have made it possible to identify as well as classify plant lesions at a primary level. Various deep learning techniques have made it possible to detect biotic stress in apple plant leaves with a very high degree of accuracy. Hence, automated segmentation of images of diseased leaves has become a leading research theme all over the world. In this paper, a dataset from FGVC7, which is an open, source dataset and contains four different classes of leaf diseases of the apple crop is used to measure the performance of the proposed model. A three, step image preprocessing procedure is conducted, which involves image enhancement, removal of background noise, and object identification through a variety of approaches. Using UNet, PSPNet, and UNet++, disease areas are identified. UNet + + delivering the most precise object segmentation. The segmented patch data are then fed into a fusion, based classification model as input. Patch segmentation makes it possible to separate the various disease areas, thus increasing the classification accuracy. The proposed framework combines several CNN architectures, namely, VGG16, InceptionV3, AlexNet, and GoogleNet, in order to take advantage of their complementary strengths, then a Vision Transformer (ViT) is used to identify distinct local features via early feature fusion. After this, the efficiency of the proposed model is check in comparison with the pre-trained CNN models individually. Comparing with all other models the proposed model has shown the accuracy of highest order i.e. 98.85%, clearly out performing individual CNN models.

title: Systematic review of machine learning models for plant and leaf disease detection and classification
abstract: Plant leaf diseases significantly affect crop yield and quality, posing ongoing challenges across the agriculture sectors, including cereals, vegetables, fruits, and floriculture. In response, a wide range of machine learning (ML) techniques have been explored for effective disease detection and classification. This systematic review provides a comprehensive analysis of 102 peer-reviewed studies published between 2001 and 2024, exclusively focused on ML-based approaches for identifying plant leaf diseases. Based on the PRISMA methodology, studies were selected from four major databases and organized under eight research questions (RQs), covering the end-to-end ML pipeline. The review investigates key components such as dataset collection methods, model architectures, evaluation strategies, and comparative model performance. It further analyzes the distribution of studies by plant type, disease category, and publication source. Special emphasis is placed on dataset characteristics, model generalization across domains, and challenges in real-world implementation. The review also highlights performance metrics, cross-validation strategies, and the need for scalable, explainable, and lightweight models. Gaps in the literature—such as limited availability of high-quality datasets, lack of standard benchmarking, and poor model transferability—are identified to guide future research. This focused review offers a structured, comparative overview of ML-driven leaf disease classification efforts and serves as a roadmap for researchers and practitioners aiming to enhance agricultural productivity through intelligent, data-driven plant health diagnostics.

title: PI-TransUNet: A Physics-Informed TransUNet Model for Steel Plate Defect Detection in Electromagnetic Tomography
abstract: Steel plate defect inspection based on electromagnetic tomography (EMT) has attracted increasing attention because of its ability to perform non-invasive imaging without direct contact with the inspected object. Nevertheless, accurate image reconstruction remains difficult owing to the highly ill-conditioned inverse mapping and the diffuse nature of electromagnetic fields, which often result in distorted defect boundaries and unstable reconstructions. Although deep neural networks have demonstrated considerable potential in EMT imaging, their predictions may deviate from underlying physical principles when trained solely from data. To improve both reconstruction accuracy and physical reliability, a physics-guided image reconstruction framework named PI-TransUNet is developed. The framework integrates a TransUNet-based inverse solver with a pretrained differentiable forward surrogate model, forming a closed-loop learning architecture. Spatial positional information is incorporated into the measurement sequence to strengthen topological awareness, while a physics-consistency objective is introduced to regularize the reconstruction process. Furthermore, a progressive weighting strategy is employed to stabilize optimization and facilitate the incorporation of physical constraints. Numerical simulations and laboratory experiments conducted on a nine-coil planar EMT platform demonstrate that the proposed approach achieves superior defect localization, enhanced boundary preservation, and improved robustness against measurement noise. Quantitative results indicate consistently high structural similarity and low reconstruction error, highlighting the effectiveness of PI-TransUNet for EMT-based steel plate defect imaging.

title: Semantic-geography integrated spatiotemporal safety mapping for urban low-altitude airspace environments.
abstract: Unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) safety is becoming increasingly critical as UAV operations are integrated into urban service and transportation systems, creating an urgent need for risk representations that can support refined low-altitude airspace management. Existing urban safety maps are still mainly expressed as two-dimensional or height stratified representations, which cannot capture the continuous variation of risk with altitude and therefore remain inadequate for continuous low-altitude flight scenarios. This paper develops a continuous three-dimensional spatiotemporal safety mapping framework for urban low-altitude environments. The framework integrates semantic information, digital surface model (DSM) and digital terrain model (DTM) derived morphology, pedestrian related exposure, and meteorological conditions within a unified geo-referenced support. A vertical continuous interpolation function is introduced to transform discrete risk representations into a continuous three-dimensional spatiotemporal risk field, thereby enabling continuous risk analysis across space, altitude, and time. Experiments in a real urban scene show that risk values vary significantly across different regions, time periods, and scene conditions, and that the resulting field reveals clear vertical differentiation and temporal redistribution patterns that conventional planar safety maps cannot represent consistently. These findings show that the proposed reusable continuous three-dimensional and time varying risk model offers a practical basis for refined low-altitude airspace management and has the potential to support future high density UAV operations.

title: Balancing adversariality and naturalness in autonomous vehicle testing scenario generation via multi-objective reinforcement learning.
abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL)-based adversarial scenario generation through dynamic agent-environment interactions has emerged as a promising approach for accelerating autonomous vehicle (AV) testing. However, existing RL approaches struggle to balance adversariality and naturalness because naturalistic driving behaviors avoid risk whereas adversarial behaviors intentionally induce it. The reward-driven nature of RL can further lead to objective polarization under linearly weighted rewards, resulting in scenarios biased toward a limited range of adversariality-naturalness trade-offs. This study proposes a preference-conditioned safety-critical scenario generation framework based on multi-policy multi-objective reinforcement learning (MORL), which models adversariality and naturalness as separate components of a vectorized reward and jointly optimizes them across the preference space. The adversariality reward incorporates risk-liability screening to filter two predefined invalid-risk patterns, while the naturalness penalty leverages a computationally efficient shadow-mode evaluation to provide real-time behavioral-deviation feedback relative to a reference driving policy. Envelope Q-learning is adopted to learn multiple preference-conditioned policies and is enhanced by a Kullback-Leibler divergence-based policy differentiation mechanism that mitigates policy mode collapse and encourages diverse behavioral evolution. Experiments in highway car-following and lane-changing environments show improvements in the evaluated scenario-quality and diversity metrics over the RL baselines. Compared with multi-round linearly weighted RL, the proposed method achieves 2.70 times the Pareto-front hypervolume, increases the valid safety-critical scenario success rate from 4.4% to 14.6%, and achieves 2.83 times the feature-space coverage volume. The results support the framework's ability to generate diverse safety-critical scenarios across testing preferences within the studied highway operational design domain.

title: Contrasting climatic controls on bimodal growth of Pinus elliottii plantations between northern and southern subtropical zones
A process-oriented framework for daily dynamic monitoring of summer maize drought: From meteorological stress to agricultural impact
Sustainable biomanufacturing of paclitaxel: From pathway elucidation to green production systems.
abstract: Paclitaxel remains irreplaceable in cancer therapy, yet its supply is critically constrained by the ecological unsustainability of plant extraction and the prohibitive costs of chemical synthesis. The recent and near-complete elucidation of its complex biosynthetic pathway in Taxus species has created a pivotal opportunity to transition toward sustainable microbial bioproduction. This review synthesizes the latest breakthroughs in the field, beginning with the comprehensive mapping of the paclitaxel biosynthetic network. This includes the recent discovery of key cytochrome P450 and 2-oxoglutarate/Fe(II)-dependent dioxygenase enzymes that resolve long standing questions regarding taxane core oxidation and oxetane ring formation. We critically evaluate the progress and inherent challenges in reconstructing this intricate pathway within heterologous chassis, including Escherichia coli, Saccharomyces cerevisiae and plant-based systems, highlighting bottlenecks related to P450 catalytic efficiency, metabolic burden and product cytotoxicity. Furthermore, this review explores emerging frontiers in synthetic biology, such as AI-driven enzyme engineering, the development of novel chassis like oleaginous yeast, the design of synthetic consortia and photosynthetic microalgae as promising platforms. By integrating fundamental pathway discovery with industrial application, this review provides insights for establishing a scalable, economically viable and environmentally sustainable supply of this essential agent.

title: Reliability-aware superpoint graph learning for large-scale point cloud semantic segmentation: Evaluation on indoor, mobile, and airborne benchmarks
journal: ISPRS Journal of Photogrammetry and Remote Sensing

title: A dual-bioeffect nanoengineered piezoelectric-photothermal hydrogel induces endochondral ossification and promotes critical-sized bone regeneration.
abstract: INTRODUCTION Critical-sized bone defects remain a major clinical challenge in orthopedics. Current strategies including inert implants and autologous bone grafts suffer from complications like loosening, infection, and donor site morbidity. Piezoelectric and photothermal stimuli synergistically regulate bone regeneration, and black phosphorus nanosheets (BPNSs) possess both effects and biodegradability, but are prone to oxidation and aggregation. OBJECTIVES This study aims to develop an injectable biomimetic hydrogel with dual piezoelectric-photothermal bioeffects for minimally invasive and efficient repair of irregular critical-sized bone defects. METHODS BPNS@rhCOL1MA composite system was constructed by embedding BPNSs into recombinant human methacrylated type I collagen hydrogel. Physicochemical characterization, in vitro cell assays, transcriptomic analysis, and in vivo validation in a rabbit rib defect model were performed. RESULTS The material exhibited stable network, injectability, and controllable dual-responsive properties. It significantly enhanced osteogenic differentiation of BMSCs in vitro. Transcriptomics revealed activation of electrical/thermal signal transduction and angiogenesis pathways. In vivo, it markedly improved new bone formation, bone mineral density, and mechanical properties. CONCLUSION This work first integrates the dual bioeffects of BPNSs with injectable human-derived collagen hydrogel, providing a novel strategy for minimally invasive repair of irregular bone defects.

title: Residual polyethylene film loading alters soil quality and maize productivity, with distinct bacterial communities in plastisphere soil.
abstract: Residual polyethylene (PE) film can alter soil resources and crop production, but its effects across loading levels and at the soil-film interface remain poorly resolved. In a maize field experiment established in 2011 in northwestern China, we assessed soil properties, bacterial communities, nitrogen cycling indicators, and crop performance across five PE loadings (0-600 kg ha-1). Soil firmly adhering to residual film was pooled across the four film treatments to characterize plastisphere soil. Soil quality and maize performance responded nonmonotonically to loading. Grain yield was 20% higher at 150 kg ha-1 and 22% lower at 600 kg ha-1 than in the control. At the highest loading, lower nutrient levels and root biomass coincided with greater soil water content after harvest and lower bacterial network connectivity. Pooled plastisphere communities showed greater diversity and contrasting assembly patterns. Their higher connectivity did not consistently correspond to greater simulated robustness. Plastisphere soil had higher nitrification potential than bulk soil, despite lower summed nitrification gene abundance than at 300 and 450 kg ha-1. Structural equation modeling linked yield positively to total nitrogen and available phosphorus. These findings identify loading and microbial differentiation at soil-film interfaces as complementary dimensions of residual-film impacts.

title: KIF1A c.773C > T impairs neural progenitor differentiation and axonal transport in association with dysregulated Wnt/β-catenin-BDNF signaling.
abstract: Pathogenic KIF1A variants are established cause neurodevelopmental and neurodegenerative disorders. However, the mechanisms by which they perturb early human neural development remains undefined. Here, we identified a heterozygous KIF1A c.773C > T (p.T258M) mutation in a Chinese family with hereditary spastic paraplegia and modeled its pathogenicity using patient-derived iPSCs and CRISPR-Cas9-corrected isogenic controls. We found that KIF1A-mutant neural stem cells (NSCs) exhibited hyperproliferation, impaired cell-cycle exit, and defective neuronal differentiation, accompanied by defective neurite outgrowth, neuronal complexity, and calcium activity. Mechanistically, the KIF1A c.773C > T mutation compromised the binding affinity of KIF1A for β-tubulin and thereby impaired microtubule-associated localization of BDNF and synaptophysin. Integrated transcriptomic and biochemical analyses further revealed dysregulation of the Wnt/β-catenin signaling pathway. Notably, pharmacological activation of Wnt signaling restored BDNF expression, whereas exogenous BDNF rescued the proliferative and differentiative defects, indicating a potential functional relationship between BDNF and Wnt/β-catenin signaling. Collectively, these findings suggested that dysregulated Wnt/β-catenin-BDNF signaling may serve as a contributory mechanism linking KIF1A motor dysfunction to aberrant neural stem cell fate.

title: Bile acid and bacterial β-ADP-heptose induce gastric epithelial remodeling through the NF-κB-LIF axis.
abstract: Bile reflux and bacterial dysbiosis are recognized risk factors for gastric carcinogenesis; however, whether bile acids and bacterial-derived metabolites enhance gastric epithelial plasticity and drive inflammatory and metaplastic remodeling remains poorly understood. Here, using human gastric organoids and complementary mouse models, we investigated how chenodeoxycholic acid (CDCA) and the bacterial metabolite β-ADP-heptose influence gastric epithelial fate during early gastric carcinogenesis. Transcriptomic analysis revealed that combined exposure to CDCA and β-ADP-heptose induced extensive epithelial remodeling, characterized by activation of inflammatory and stem-cell pluripotency-associated pathways. Mechanistically, combined CDCA and β-ADP-heptose treatment activated NF-B signaling, resulting in robust induction of leukemia inhibitory factor (LIF). Elevated LIF expression was accompanied by loss of gastric lineage identity, including reduced expression of TFF2, GKN1, and GKN2, and acquisition of intestinal metaplasia-associated features marked by increased REG4 and CDX1 expression. Pharmacological inhibition of NF-κB or genetic depletion of LIF substantially attenuated these pathological changes, restoring gastric lineage markers and suppressing intestinal-like differentiation. Collectively, our findings show that exposure to CDCA and β-ADP-heptose activates NF-κB-LIF signaling and promotes gastric epithelial lineage remodeling characterized by loss of gastric lineage-associated features and acquisition of intestinal-like features.

title: A supergene and genomic mosaicism are associated with phenotypic evolution in Galápagos tree finches
abstract: Adaptive radiations provide powerful models to study the origins of phenotypic novelty and species diversity. Darwin’s finches constitute a classic example of adaptive radiation, in which beak morphology is a key trait related to fitness. Here, we focus on Camarhynchus tree finches by analyzing whole genomes in combination with morphological data to revisit long-standing questions regarding their origins raised before genetic evidence became available. Camarhynchus diversified over the last 100,000 years, yielding some striking morphological differences despite shallow genetic divergence. We identify several highly differentiated loci, including G03, a supergene affecting beak and body size. We reveal a striking example of genomic mosaicism, in which autosomal differentiation between two sympatric species is restricted primarily to a single locus -(G03)- that approaches fixation, shifting them from one phenotypic optimum to another. Contextualized in a broader phylogenetic framework, we also reveal an unexpected diversity of G03 haplotypes and show that the small and large G03 alleles diverged early in the radiation, suggesting a key genetic innovation enabling ecological expansion among species of Darwin’s finches. Our results further establish Camarhynchus as a model example of speciation with gene flow, underscoring the broader role of hybridization in generating biodiversity. Adaptive radiations produce striking phenotypic diversity over remarkably short evolutionary timescales. This study uses genomic analyses of Darwin’s tree finches to reveal a cryptic lineage, in which autosomal differentiation with another sympatric species is restricted primarily to a single locus (G03) that approaches fixation, shifting them from one phenotypic optimum to another.
