title: Rhizosphere Microbiomes Respond to Plant-Parasitic Nematode Cues and Contribute to Host Defence.
abstract: Plant-parasitic nematodes (PPNs) cause major crop losses, while current nematicides face increasing regulatory restrictions and often show inconsistent efficacy. We tested whether nematode-associated cues activate rhizosphere microbiomes and cuticle-associated fungi to produce suppressive metabolites that impair nematodes and stimulate host defence. Maize rhizosphere microbiomes from different soils and fungal isolates recovered from nematode cuticles were exposed to Meloidogyne hapla, after which cell-free filtrates were assessed for juvenile mortality, root invasion, gall formation, egg production and reactive oxygen species (ROS) accumulation in tomato. Nematode-conditioned microbiome filtrates increased M. hapla juvenile mortality relative to nonconditioned controls across soils, although the magnitude of this effect varied with soil origin. Several fungal isolates also showed suppressive activity against Pratylenchus penetrans in maize and M. hapla in tomato, with distinct outcomes across biological assays. Among them, Akanthomyces sp. F20/JKI73389 was selected for mechanistic follow-up: stimulation by M. hapla, or by nematode-derived molecules, induced F20 to release a filtrate that reduced nematode root invasion and triggered a strong ROS response in host tissue. UHPLC-MS analysis further revealed a distinct nematode-induced metabolite profile in F20, including six candidate features that were absent from non-stimulated controls and were provisionally associated with enhanced nematode mortality. These results support a model in which nematode-derived cues alter the metabolite output of indigenous rhizosphere microbes and associated fungi in ways linked to nematode suppression and host defence, highlighting their potential as environmentally compatible tools for PPN management.

title: A controlled experimental study on overfitting mitigation using data augmentation and random seed stabilization
abstract: We ran a set of controlled experiments to see whether basic data augmentation helps CNNs avoid overfitting. Using SimpleDLA on CIFAR-10, we first trained a baseline model with no augmentation and saw clear signs of overfitting— training accuracy kept climbing while test accuracy plateaued early. Adding simple augmentations (random crops and horizontal flips) pushed test accuracy from 74.36% to 79.79%. To check if results were just luck, we repeated training with three different random seeds (42, 123, 999). Test scores varied between 72.32% and 76.45%, showing that seed choice does matter. Our takeaway: even basic augmentation helps generalization, and reporting multi-seed runs should be standard practice.
journal: International Conference on Advanced Image Processing Technology

title: ECA_FNet: a ConvNeXt-based model for soil type identification
abstract: Soil classification and mapping are essential for agricultural resource management and sustainable production. Although deep learning—particularly convolutional neural networks (CNNs)—has advanced digital soil mapping, models frequently suffer from poor generalization across diverse environments due to background complexity and fine-grained variations in soil texture and porosity. To address these limitations, we propose ECA_FNet, a novel, highly efficient soil identification framework based on ConvNeXt. Specifically, we integrate a Faster Block into the backbone to capture discriminative soil features while drastically reducing computational overhead. Simultaneously, we employ an Efficient Channel Attention (ECA) mechanism to adaptive enhance feature extraction. Compared to the baseline ConvNeXt, our network is substantially more lightweight yet more precise. Extensively evaluated on an upland soil dataset from Bishan, Chongqing, ECA_FNet achieves over 90% across accuracy, precision, F1-score, and recall, specifically reaching a peak accuracy of 93.31% and consistently outperforming state-of-the-art methods.
journal: International Conference on Computer Vision, Robotics and Automation Engineering

title: End-to-end differentiable ResNet-XGBoost joint training framework for DOA estimation
abstract: In recent years, Deep Learning (DL) has demonstrated remarkable performance in the field of Direction of Arrival (DOA) estimation, revealing its superior advantages over traditional algorithms. Among relevant research, the hybrid framework combining Neural Network (NN) and Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) has gradually become an emerging research hotspot in various fields. However, the non-differentiable characteristic of conventional XGBoost restricts the NN-XGBoost hybrid framework to two-stage independent training, which fails to achieve global optimization. To address the above issues, this paper proposes an end-to-end differentiable ResNet-XGBoost joint training framework. Firstly, Residual Network (ResNet) is adopted to extract spatial features from the covariance matrix of array received signals. Subsequently, an integrated regression layer composed of multiple differentiable soft decision trees is connected to replace the traditional non-differentiable XGBoost, ensuring the overall differentiability of the model and realizing end-to-end joint training. Simulation results verify that under the experimental conditions set in this paper, the proposed algorithm outperforms the Multiple Signal Classification (MUSIC) algorithm, standalone ResNet, standalone XGBoost and the traditional two-stage independent ResNet+XGBoost training framework in terms of Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) and Mean Absolute Error (MAE).
journal: International Conference on Computer Vision, Robotics, and Automation Engineering (CRAE 2026)

title: A geometry-consistent local RPC regeneration method for GF-7 stereo imagery based on virtual control points
abstract: In three-dimensional reconstruction from high-resolution satellite stereo imagery, the RPC geometric model provides the basis for establishing the mapping between image space and object space. However, after local region-of-interest (ROI) cropping, scale normalization of the right-view image, and resampling, the full-scene image coordinate system described by the original RPB files becomes inconsistent with the processed local image coordinate system, which reduces the accuracy of epipolar image generation and limits the reliability of subsequent stereo matching. To address this problem, this paper proposes a geometry-consistent local RPC regeneration method based on virtual control points. The proposed method crops the left- and right-view images under the constraint of the same object-space center point, estimates the local axial ground sampling distance (GSD), and performs anisotropic scale normalization on the right-view image; virtual control points are then constructed using the original RPC model and image-space transformations, and local RPB files consistent with the final image coordinate system are generated through refitting. Experiments are conducted using GF-7 forward- and backward-view stereo imagery, and the effectiveness of the proposed method is verified through multi-scale ROI projection accuracy evaluation and epipolar consistency analysis. The results show that the local RPC projection errors at different cropping scales are all within one pixel, and the disparities of corresponding points after epipolar rectification are mainly distributed in the horizontal direction, providing a consistent geometric basis for subsequent stereo matching and DSM reconstruction.
journal: Conference on Advanced Algorithms and Signal Image Processing

title: Improving medical product recognition using a hybrid YOLO-ResNet framework
abstract: Object detection models are important for vision systems, especially in real-world situations where both finding and correctly identifying objects is needed. This research proposes a simple two-stage deep learning framework to improve performance. The system is designed to detect whether medicine is present or not (“medicine” vs. “non-medicine”). It first uses a single-class YOLO model to locate the object, and then applies a ResNet-based classifier to accurately classify the cropped region. A confidence-based filtering step is also added to reduce false detections. Experimental results show that this two-stage approach performs much better than using YOLO alone. The YOLO model achieves an accuracy of 67.84%, while combining it with ResNet increases the accuracy to 91.23%. These results show that the proposed method improves accuracy and reliability, making it useful for medicine detection and quality control.
journal: Conference on Advanced Algorithms and Signal Image Processing

title: A joint signal-and-image processing method for pulse-coded laser recognition and spot localization
abstract: Pulsed lasers that encode information in their pulse-timing sequence appear in many optical sensing and ranging systems, and analyzing such a source involves two complementary tasks: recognizing its pulse-coding scheme from the timing sequence, and localizing its spot in the image plane. The tasks are difficult in opposite ways: the coded pulses are narrow and have a low duty cycle, so an imager with a fixed exposure easily misses them, while the spot is small and buried in cluttered backgrounds. This paper proposes a joint signal-and-image processing method with a cue-then-image structure. On the signal side, a multi-channel recognizer scores repetition-frequency, arithmetic, variable-interval and pseudorandom coding hypotheses on the pulse time-of-arrival (TOA) sequence; confidence fusion with mode locking yields a stable decision, and a code-specific predictor forecasts the next pulse arrival to gate the imaging exposure. On the image side, frame differencing and local difference-of-Gaussian (DoG) enhancement, followed by adaptive thresholding, morphology and connected-component filtering, yield a clean spot mask, from which a gray-weighted centroid and a fitted ellipse give the spot location and an incident-direction estimate. On ten measured TOA sequences the method recognizes every coding scheme correctly, with sub-microsecond next-pulse prediction error for the regular codes; on cluttered outdoor imagery it returns a single compact spot where fixed-threshold and global-saliency baselines over-segment.
journal: Conference on Advanced Algorithms and Signal Image Processing

title: TLR3-TRIF signaling in villus-like enterocytes drives type III interferon responses to enteroviruses.
abstract: Enteroviruses initiate infection at the intestinal epithelium but can spread systemically to cause severe disease. Although both MDA5 and TLR3 have been implicated in enterovirus sensing, the mechanisms by which the intestinal epithelium detects these viruses remain poorly defined. To address this, we infected human intestinal organoids (enteroids) with the group B enterovirus echovirus 11 (E11) and compared responses in models differentiated to mimic either crypt-like or villus-like epithelium. Villus-like enteroids produced significantly more type III interferons following E11 infection and exhibited heightened responsiveness to type III interferon signaling. Single-cell RNA sequencing of infected enteroids revealed that E11 broadly infected epithelial cell types, but type III interferon expression was largely restricted to mature enterocytes. Notably, enterocyte differentiation was also associated with upregulation of TLR3 and other innate immune genes. Using CRISPR-Cas9 knockout enteroids, we found that TLR3-TRIF signaling was essential for intestinal type III IFN responses to E11 infection, whereas loss of MAVS, the adaptor for MDA5, had no effect. Together, these data support a model in which mature enterocytes serve as key sensors of enterovirus infection via TLR3-TRIF signaling, triggering a localized type III IFN response that may help restrict viral spread. IMPORTANCE Enteroviruses are commonly circulating viruses that can cause a broad spectrum of disease, particularly in pediatric populations. Innate immune sensing in the intestinal epithelium likely plays a critical role in determining the outcome of enterovirus infections. Deficiencies in TLR3 signaling, type III IFN responses, or crypt-villus architecture may contribute to severe disease presentations. Our findings highlight the importance of TLR3-mediated sensing in mature enterocytes, which may also have broader implications for other intestinal viruses, as well as for inflammatory conditions like inflammatory bowel disease. A deeper understanding of how TLR3 sensing and type III IFN production are regulated in the intestine could inform new therapeutic strategies aimed at modulating mucosal sensitivity to viral nucleic acids and enhancing antiviral defense. title: UltraDiff: Differentiable Ray Tracing in Ultrasound for Shape Optimization
abstract: Physically-based differentiable rendering enables gradient-based optimization of scene parameters by matching rendered images to measurements, but has so far mainly focused on light transport. We extend this paradigm to medical ultrasound, where image formation resembles transient rendering: echoes are binned by time-of-flight rather than projected onto an image plane. We present UltraDiff, a modular framework for differentiable ultrasound ray tracing. UltraDiff formulates ultrasound image formation as a path-space integral, gated by travel time between the transducer and tissue interfaces, and derives a Monte Carlo estimator of both the forward model and its gradients with respect to scene parameters. We demonstrate this on an inverse geometry estimation: starting from a sphere, an SDF is optimized until simulated echoes match measured ones, recovering vertebral surfaces from simulated B-mode sweeps and from a real robotic acquisition of a spine phantom. Unlike state-of-the-art ultrasound shape reconstruction methods, which rely on pre-segmented images, our approach operates unsupervised on B-mode images through analysis-by-synthesis, while achieving competitive geometric accuracy. Implemented on top of Mitsuba 3, UltraDiff brings differentiable path tracing to a new sensing modality and provides a foundation for inverse problems in acoustic imaging.

title: Programming Is a Real-Time Strategy (RTS) Game Now
abstract: Software development is moving away from writing code line by line. Instead of using AI only for simple autocomplete, developers now manage multiple coding agents across different parts of a codebase at once. While these tools make individual tasks faster, recent data shows that teams are generating far more code without shipping significantly more working software. Managing several parallel agents also creates heavy context switching. Agents often produce changes that pass their own isolated tests, but break system contracts during integration. This article uses a real-time strategy model to address these challenges. To keep systems stable, developers must supply clear architecture context upfront, enforce strict test gates before merging, and focus on code review instead of prompting. Finally, engineering organizations must update how they work. This requires tracking finished software instead of code volume, building better dashboards to monitor active agents, and continuing to train junior engineers so they can oversee agent output.

title: GeoNatureAgent (GNA): A Framework and Benchmark for Pre-Production Evaluation of Tool-Using Agents on Geospatial and Environmental Tasks
abstract: Before tool-using LLM agents are deployed in environmental and geospatial workflows, teams need evidence that an agent reliably selects the right operations against real APIs. We introduce GeoNatureAgent (GNA), a framework for pre-production evaluation of tool-using agents: a fixed sixteen-tool geospatial interface published as a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server, so the agent under test is the only variable, scored against an identical tool layer, task suite, and deterministic scorer. Its flagship instance is a 103-task benchmark (a 93-task main suite across 18 categories plus a ten-task comparison expansion) evaluated against an open, self-hostable geospatial API serving three environmental indicators across Spain and Portugal. We evaluate nine LLMs under three temperature-1.0 seeds, reporting capability and per-case cost as orthogonal axes. (1) Claude Sonnet 4 achieves the highest capability (61.7% +/- 0.7% on all 103 tasks; 60.8% on the main suite), followed closely by DeepSeek V3.2 (57.9%), while no other model exceeds 53%; (2) the cost-accuracy Pareto frontier is mostly open-weight, with DeepSeek V3.2 offering 93% of Claude's capability at 11.3x lower list-price cost; (3) under strict all-checks scoring the best model sits 24-36 points below the 85-97% reported on general-purpose GIS benchmarks, whereas per-check partial credit for the top four models (86-90%) is comparable, so much of that gap reflects scoring strictness rather than task difficulty alone. The MCP server, evaluation harness, benchmark, and API are publicly available; swapping the tool executors and task suite instantiates an equivalent benchmark for any geospatial domain.

title: Basal Stem Cell Signaling Pathways Regulating Collective Epithelial Cell Migration and Airway Repair.
abstract: The airway epithelium serves as a critical barrier against pathogens, allergens, and other environmental insults. Disruption of this barrier contributes to respiratory diseases such as chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, making rapid epithelial repair essential for maintaining lung function. Basal cells (BCs), the primary regenerative cell population of the proximal airway epithelium, drive repair through coordinated collective cell migration rather than isolated cellular behaviors. This process is closely linked to dynamic transitions between jammed and unjammed tissue states that regulate migratory capacity and tissue remodeling. Emerging evidence identifies extracellular matrix (ECM) remodeling, Wnt, and transforming growth factor-β (TGF-β) signaling as key regulators of these multicellular responses. ECM remodeling establishes the mechanical substrate for migration, while non-canonical Wnt signaling promotes cytoskeletal reorganization, cell polarity, and coordinated BC movement. TGF-β signaling acts as a context-dependent regulator of BC migration, differentiation, epithelial jamming, and cytoskeletal remodeling through canonical and non-canonical pathways. ECM-integrin signaling links the extracellular environment to cytoskeletal dynamics and collective migration, while inflammatory and mechanical cues modify these responses. Integrin αvβ5/αvβ6-mediated interactions with the ECM connect mechanical forces to focal adhesion signaling and activation of latent TGF-β, linking tissue mechanics to epithelial repair. Together, integration of inflammatory, biochemical, and biomechanical signals that coordinate collective migration and epithelial restoration. This mini-review highlights recent advances supporting a model where coordinated ECM remodeling, Wnt signaling, and TGF-β signaling regulate BC migration and restore epithelial barrier integrity following injury, and examines how disruption of these processes contributes to abnormal repair in chronic lung disease.
journal: American journal of physiology. Lung cellular and molecular physiology

title: Surgical Efficiency, Learning Dynamics, and Positional Accuracy of Freehand Immediate Implant Placement Under Standardized Digital Planning: An In Vitro Study.
abstract: PURPOSE To characterize surgical efficiency and within-operator learning dynamics during freehand immediate post-extraction implant placement performed under standardized, prosthetically driven digital planning, and to describe the positional accuracy achieved across operators of differing experience in a 3D-printed phantom model. MATERIALS AND METHODS In a prospective in vitro study, 80 tissue-level implants (TLC/TLX; Institut Straumann AG) were placed by three operators stratified by cumulative experience (0; 100 implants) at ten anterior maxillary sites on standardized 3D-printed extraction-socket phantoms. All sites were planned in coDiagnostix and prepared with an identical drill sequence; implant type was disclosed only after osteotomy completion. Site and implant allocation were randomized using permuted blocks, and a blinded examiner performed all digital superimposition. The primary outcome was angular deviation; secondary outcomes were 3D offset at the implant base and apex and total procedure time. Between-operator comparisons used the Kruskal-Wallis test and Bonferroni-corrected Mann-Whitney U tests; within-operator learning was evaluated by regression of outcomes against sequential case order. RESULTS Seventy-six implants were evaluable. Positional accuracy did not differ between operators for any metric after correction (angular deviation: Novice 7.14°, Intermediate 9.36°, Expert 7.11°; Kruskal-Wallis P = 0.086; 3D offset at base P = 0.154; at apex P = 0.710), and all values fell within published freehand benchmark ranges. Total procedure time differed across operators (Expert 3.71 ± 1.49, Intermediate 4.96 ± 1.50, Novice 6.40 ± 2.83 minutes; P 0.30). Overall, TLC and TLX did not differ in positional accuracy (all P ≥ 0.340). CONCLUSIONS Under standardized prosthetically driven planning, positional accuracy did not differ significantly across operators and fell within established freehand benchmark ranges, whereas procedure time and within-operator efficiency gains were the principal differentiators. Because each experience level comprised a single operator, comparisons are operator-level and do not support experience-based generalization.
journal: The International journal of oral & maxillofacial implants

title: The Oxidized Phospholipid PGPC Impairs Angiogenesis by Inhibiting Endothelial Autophagosomal-Lysosomal Fusion Through NPC1-Induced Syntaxin 17 Acetylation and Ubiquitination.
abstract: BACKGROUND Angiogenesis is essential for the recovery of ischemic hearts with coronary artery disease (CAD). PGPC (1-palmitoyl-2-glutamyl-sn-glycero-3-phosphocholine) is a major phospholipid oxidation product in atherosclerotic lesions. Autophagy participates in angiogenesis. However, whether PGPC affects angiogenesis in ischemic hearts by regulating autophagy remains unclear. METHODS Plasma PGPC concentrations were quantified and the effects of PGPC on angiogenesis were evaluated in cultured endothelial cells and in vivo using a subcutaneous Matrigel plug assay, as well as in hindlimb ischemia and myocardial infarction models in C57BL/6J mice. Autophagic flux and the expression and modification of proteins associated with autophagy and angiogenesis were also assessed. RESULTS Plasma PGPC levels were increased in patients with CAD, and they were positively correlated with the severity of CAD and negatively correlated with coronary collateral artery formation. PGPC inhibited endothelial cell migration and tube formation. PGPC suppressed neovascularization in Matrigel plugs and reduced blood flow recovery in hindlimb ischemia. In a mouse model of myocardial infarction, PGPC attenuated angiogenesis in the ischemic myocardium. These proangiogenic effects induced by VEGFA (vascular endothelial growth factor A) in ischemic hearts were significantly inhibited by PGPC. Mechanistically, PGPC inhibited the expression of STX17 (syntaxin 17), a crucial molecule that controls autophagosomal-lysosomal fusion by promoting the acetylation and subsequent ubiquitination and degradation of STX17. PGPC upregulated the expression of NPC1 (NPC intracellular cholesterol transporter 1) through CD36 (cluster of differentiation 36). NPC1 not only promoted the acetylation and subsequent ubiquitination and degradation of STX17 through the recruitment of ACAT1 (acetyl-CoA acetyltransferase 1), but also competed with STX17 to bind VAMP8 (vesicle-associated membrane protein 8), leading to inhibition of the expression of eNOS (endothelial nitric oxide synthase), ERK1/2 (extracellular signal-regulated kinase 1/2), and nitric oxide production. Oxidized phospholipid-neutralizing antibody E06, STX17 overexpression, or silencing of NPC1 reversed the inhibitory effect of PGPC on angiogenesis by restoring autophagic flux. CONCLUSIONS PGPC promotes the acetylation and subsequent ubiquitin-mediated degradation of STX17 by increasing NPC1, leading to a reduction in the level of STX17 associated with VAMP8, which inhibits autophagosomal-lysosomal fusion and angiogenesis. Targeting PGPC, NPC1, or STX17 may represent novel therapeutic approaches to promote angiogenesis in patients with CAD.

title: Inhibition of ROCK2 via KD025/Belumosudil Alleviates Hypertensive End-Organ Damage.
abstract: BACKGROUND Despite achieving target blood pressure, hypertensive individuals have an elevated risk of cardiovascular disease, likely due to unresolved inflammation. Thus, adjunctive immune-modulating therapies are needed to protect patients with hypertension from end-organ damage. We previously showed that T helper 17 cells, which produce the proinflammatory cytokine IL (interleukin)-17A, contribute to hypertensive tissue injury. ROCK2 (Rho-associated coiled-coil-containing protein kinase 2) is a molecular switch governing T helper cell differentiation by promoting T helper 17 polarization and inhibiting T regulatory cell polarization. The present study tests whether T-cell-specific deletion of Rock2 or the Food and Drug Administration-approved ROCK2-specific inhibitor KD025/belumosudil protects against hypertension-associated end-organ damage. METHODS T-cell-specific Rock2 knockout mice (Rock2fl/flCD4Cre+) and Rock2fl/fl littermate controls were subjected to a 21-day deoxycorticosterone acetate-salt model of hypertension. In parallel, KD025/belumosudil treatment (50 mg/kg per day) starting after day 10 in wild-type mice was used to test the therapeutic potential of targeting ROCK2. Blood pressure, cardiac fibrosis, renal injury, and infiltration of immune cells were assessed. RESULTS T-cell-specific Rock2 deletion in mice attenuated the hypertensive response in the deoxycorticosterone acetate-salt model and protected from cardiac and aortic fibrosis. KD025/belumosudil treatment did not reduce blood pressure but did decrease proinflammatory T helper 17 polarization in vivo and increased the cardiac regulatory T cells/T helper 17 ratio. Despite no blood pressure change, KD025 reduced cardiac and aortic fibrosis, improved echocardiographic and invasive hemodynamic indices, and attenuated albuminuria and renal T-cell infiltration. CONCLUSIONS ROCK2 inhibition may serve as an adjunct immune-modulating therapy to mitigate the end-organ damage that occurs in the heart, vasculature, and kidney in hypertension.

title: Nucleocytoplasmic shuttling of USP15 promotes pathological autophagy that disrupts neural stem cell homeostasis and neurodevelopment.
abstract: During organogenesis, stem cells undergo cellular and metabolic remodelling, facilitated by autophagy-mediated turnover of organelles. Autophagy impairment has been linked to human diseases, including neurodevelopmental disorders associated with disrupted neural stem/precursor cell (NPC) homeostasis, but the underlying mechanisms and pathogenic processes governing these connections remain poorly understood. Here, we report three de novo variants of uncertain significance (p.Gly223Asp, p.Gly889Glu, p.Met978Val) in the deubiquitinase USP15 in human probands with diverse clinical features, including a spectrum of brain malformations and metabolic phenotypes. Proband variants differentially altered USP15 activity and nucleocytoplasmic localization. USP15 showed dynamic localization in NPCs of embryonic mouse cerebral cortex. Using a knock-in mouse model carrying the p.Met978Val variant, we showed that aberrant cytoplasmic accumulation of USP15, but not its loss-of-function, impaired NPC self-renewal and differentiation, leading to reduced neuronal output and enlarged lateral ventricles. Mechanistically, USP15 deubiquitinated autophagy regulator ATG16L1, impeded its normal turnover, and impaired autophagy. Concurrently, lipid droplet mobilization and mitochondrial dynamics were attenuated. Reestablishing the ubiquitination-deubiquitination balance restored autophagy activity and normal neurogenesis. Our findings suggest that nucleocytoplasmic shuttling of USP15 creates a switch-like autophagy signal controlling NPC homeostasis, and its disruption may contribute to the pathogenesis of complex neurodevelopmental conditions.

title: Pharmacologic HIF-2α inhibition preserves T cell effector function in clear cell renal cell carcinoma.
abstract: Hypoxia-inducible factor 2α (HIF-2α) is a central oncogenic driver in clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC) and a therapeutic target of the small-molecule inhibitor belzutifan. Genetic studies in murine models have suggested that hypoxia signaling may support T cell effector programs, raising concern that HIF-2α inhibition could impair antitumor immunity. However, whether pharmacologic HIF-2α inhibition alters human T cell biology remains unknown. Here, we investigated the cell-intrinsic effects of EPAS1 (encoding HIF-2α) perturbation in primary human T cells. CRISPR/Cas9-mediated deletion of HIF-2α demonstrated no notable transcriptional effects. Similarly, pharmacologic treatment with belzutifan produced minimal transcriptional changes and did not impair proliferation, cytokine production, polyfunctionality, or cytotoxic activity in T cells derived from healthy donor peripheral blood, peripheral blood from patients with ccRCC, or tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes under hypoxic conditions. High- dimensional immunophenotyping revealed preserved T cell differentiation and activation states following pharmacologic HIF-2α inhibition in vitro and in peripheral blood from patients receiving HIF-2α inhibitor therapy. Together, these findings demonstrate that pharmacologic HIF-2α inhibition preserves key effector programs, providing a mechanistic basis for the immunologic safety of HIF-2α-targeted therapy in ccRCC.

title: VIDD or CIADD? The ventilator remains a bona fide culprit
abstract: Rosà and colleagues recently proposed that mechanical ventilation (MV) may not be the primary driver of diaphragm dysfunction in critically ill patients, advocating the term “critical illness-associated diaphragm dysfunction” (CIADD) over “ventilator-induced diaphragm dysfunction” (VIDD). While we support distinguishing VIDD from CIADD, we contend that the review’s central conclusion underestimates the causal role of MV itself. This commentary addresses three questions in turn. First, does MV injure the diaphragm under controlled conditions? Here the evidence is strong: brain-dead donor studies—dismissed by the authors as a “unique patient category”—are a uniquely informative, though not pure, human model of controlled MV exposure, and their dismissal creates an unfalsifiable position. Second, how much does MV contribute to diaphragm dysfunction in critically ill patients? This is considerably less certain: the molecular abnormalities observed in critically ill patients (ubiquitin-proteasome activation, RyR1 calcium leak, mitochondrial oxidative stress) coincide with pathways that MV reliably induces in controlled animal experiments, providing biological plausibility—though not proof—that MV contributes to the molecular phenotype of critical illness. Third, do MV and critical illness interact? We propose that CIADD should serve as an umbrella term encompassing VIDD as a distinct mechanistic subtype—rather than replacing it—analogous to how “pneumonia” subsumes VAP, HAP, and CAP, and we propose three differentiated model types for future research: pure VIDD models, pure CIADD models, and combined models with factorial design. VIDD and CIADD are mechanistically distinct but interacting entities. Future research should employ models that minimize confounding from critical illness to isolate ventilation-specific injury pathways. Importantly, establishing that VIDD exists is not equivalent to establishing that preventing VIDD is beneficial; clinical trials are needed to demonstrate the feasibility and benefit of diaphragm-protective strategies. Diminishing MV’s role risks undermining the mechanistic foundation of diaphragm-protective ventilation strategies.

title: Multi-locus genome-wide association analysis of grain yield, plant height, panicle length, and flowering time in the Senegalese pearl millet [Pennisetum glaucum (L.) R. Br.] germplasm
abstract: Pearl millet [Pennisetum glaucum (L.) R. Br.] is a staple cereal underpinning food and nutritional security across the semi-arid Sahel, yet locally calibrated genomic resources for its improvement in West Africa remain scarce. Improving its key agronomic traits is therefore a breeding priority, despite the crop’s inherent hardiness. This study characterized the genetic architecture of four agronomically decisive traits: grain yield, plant height, panicle length, and flowering time, in a Senegalese panel combining internationally derived PMiGAP inbred lines with locally adapted breeding material. Genotypes were evaluated across multiple Senegalese locations between July and October 2024 and genotyped on the DArTseq platform, yielding 14,718 high-quality SNPs. Analysis of variance revealed highly significant genotypic effects, with broad-sense heritability ranging from 0.75 to 0.91. Plant height, panicle length, and grain yield were positively correlated, whereas flowering time was negatively correlated with yield, consistent with an early-flowering drought-escape strategy. The association panel showed weak population structure (k = 2), and linkage disequilibrium decayed rapidly, falling below r2 = 0.1 at approximately 8 kb. Genome-wide associations were tested in a subset of 137 stable genotypes using a multi-locus mixed-model approach with correction for population structure and kinship. Eleven marker–trait associations were detected across six of the seven pearl millet chromosomes (LOD 6.83–10.78), explaining 5.92% to 48.67% of phenotypic variance, with plant height the most extensively resolved trait. Candidate-gene annotation linked several markers to genes plausibly involved in cell expansion, inflorescence development, and hormone-mediated growth, including an expansin, an AP2/ERF transcription factor, and an auxin-conjugating glucosyltransferase. Flowering time associated with a single chromosome-2 locus implicated in auxin homeostasis, on the same chromosome as PHYTOCHROME C (PHYC), a principal flowering-time determinant in the crop. Together, these associations provide candidate targets for marker-assisted and genomic selection and offer a foundation for genomics-assisted pearl millet improvement in Senegal and the broader West African Sahel.

title: Synergistic spatial-sequential modeling for enhanced Rosa roxburghii disease detection
abstract: The rapid advancement of smart agricultural technologies has enabled deep learning–based approaches to markedly enhance the efficiency of crop disease detection and quality monitoring. To overcome the challenges of low detection efficiency and high false-positive rates in large-scale cultivation of the characteristic economic crop Rosa roxburghii, this study introduces a synergistic spatial–sequential modeling framework. This synergy is achieved via a gated fusion mechanism that bidirectionally enhances CNN-extracted local spatial features and Mamba-derived global sequential features through adaptive re-weighting, forming a mutual refinement loop instead of a simple cascade. Built upon YOLOv8, the model integrates the Mamba module from state space models (SSMs) to develop a hybrid feature extraction framework, jointly optimizing detection accuracy and inference efficiency. A selective feature enhancement strategy further strengthens the network’s ability to characterize subtle lesions on the surface of Rosa roxburghii by adaptively amplifying informative responses through channel-wise recalibration and spatial refinement. The backbone network also incorporates the selective scan for 2D data (SS2D) module to capture long-range dependencies beyond conventional convolution. Experimental validation conducted on our self-constructed dataset, which consists of field-captured images of Rosa roxburghii plants manually collected and annotated by the research team, demonstrates that the proposed model delivers notable performance gains, achieving mAP@50 improvements of 6%, 2.87%, 8.38%, 7.08%, 16.27%, and 6.55% over YOLOv5-N, YOLOv8-N, YOLOv10-N, YOLOv11-N, YOLOv12-N, and MambaYOLO-T, respectively. Concerning mean average precision (mAP)@ 50–95, the model attains corresponding gains of 6.85%, 0.27%, 6.99%, 5.19%, 13.66%, and 2.57%, all while maintaining comparable FLOPs (G) and parameter counts. These results highlight the model’s excellent performance, confirming its effectiveness for agricultural visual inspection and suggesting a promising approach for intelligent disease monitoring in mountainous specialty crop production.

title: Multivariate Assessment of Soil Quality under Natural and Conventional Farming Systems in Andhra Pradesh, India
abstract: Background: Soil quality is a key indicator of sustainable agricultural productivity and ecosystem health. This study evaluated the effects of natural farming (NF) and conventional farming (CF) on soil physicochemical properties and soil quality across three model mandals of Andhra Pradesh, India. Methods: Thirty composite soil samples (15 NF and 15 CF) were collected during the 2024-2025 cropping season and analysed for pH, electrical conductivity, bulk density, porosity, soil organic carbon and available nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium. Soil quality index (SQI), fertility index (FI) and nutrient index (NI) were determined using principal component analysis (PCA)-based weighting and standardized scoring methods. Result: Natural Farming soils exhibited comparatively higher soil organic carbon, lower bulk density and greater porosity than conventional farming soils. Principal component analysis explained 59.3% of the total variance, indicating that soil structural and nutrient attributes were the major contributors to soil quality. Although nutrient availability was comparable between farming systems, Natural farming recorded higher SQI values, indicating improved overall soil quality. These findings demonstrate that natural farming can enhance soil quality while maintaining soil fertility under the agroecological conditions of coastal Andhra Pradesh.

title: The Changing Role of AI Agents in Science Must be Recognized
abstract: Current editorial guidelines from organizations such as the International Committee of Medical Journal Editors (ICMJE) treat generative artificial intelligence (AI) primarily as an administrative assistant or text manipulator, relegating its contributions to footnotes or acknowledgments. This policy framework misinterprets the operational reality of modern biomedical research, where advanced language models function as active intellectual partners capable of logical stress-testing, data synthesis, and hypothesis generation. Conflating operational cognitive contribution with legal and ethical accountability creates unnecessary opacity in scholarly publishing. To resolve this tension, this paper examines four structural credit frameworks—ranging from the institutional status quo to dual-track independent lists and expanded contributor taxonomies. We propose that medical publishing must evolve beyond obsolete binary definitions, establishing transparent attribution models that separate human regulatory liability from the recognition of machine-assisted scientific co-creation.

title: Multimodal Deep Learning for Drug–Drug Interaction Prediction using Structural Biological and Semantic Information
abstract: Drug–drug interactions are a major source of adverse drug events and represent a significant challenge for medication safety and clinical decision-making. Although experimental methods provide reliable evidence for DDI identification, they are often costly, time-consuming, and unable to keep pace with the rapidly increasing number of approved drugs and potential drug combinations. Recent advances in machine learning have enabled large-scale computational prediction of DDIs; however, effectively integrating heterogeneous drug information remains a key challenge. To address this limitation, we propose HySEAtt-DDI, a multimodal deep learning framework for DDI prediction that integrates chemical, biological, and semantic drug information. The proposed framework combines structural similarity derived from molecular fingerprints, biological similarity obtained from drug–protein interaction profiles, and semantic similarity extracted from drug descriptions using BioGPT. These complementary representations are fused into a unified feature space and compressed through an autoencoder to learn compact latent representations. A hybrid architecture consisting of convolutional neural networks (CNNs), Squeeze-and-Excitation blocks, and multi-head self-attention is then employed to capture local patterns, channel-wise feature importance, and long-range dependencies associated with drug interactions. In addition, we construct a curated DrugBank-derived dataset containing 2,148 approved small-molecule drugs, 2,056 protein targets, and 592,840 drug–drug interaction instances. Extensive experiments and ablation studies demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework and highlight the contribution of each modality 1 and architectural component. The results show that HySEAtt-DDI consistently outperforms conventional machine learning methods and competitive deep learning baselines, demonstrating the value of multimodal representation learning for DDI prediction. Overall, the proposed framework provides an effective and scal-able approach for identifying potential drug–drug interactions and supporting computational pharmacology research.

title: Scalable Nonparametric Demand Estimation in Differentiated Product Markets
abstract: Estimating demand for differentiated products is central to many economic questions. Existing approaches face a trade-off between flexibility and scalability. In particular, nonparametric approaches suffer from a curse of dimensionality, whereby the number of parameters grows rapidly with the number of products. In this paper, I develop a scalable nonparametric approach using market-level data for demand models that satisfy mild and economically motivated restrictions. A key restriction, permutation invariance, requires that a product's demand remain unchanged under any permutation of its competitors. Leveraging these restrictions, I employ a recent approximation result that overcomes the curse of dimensionality by expressing the model in terms of competitor-pooled rather than competitor-specific arguments, making the number of parameters independent of the number of products. I demonstrate the empirical performance of the approach through simulations and an application to the U.S. breakfast cereal market.

title: Smallholder Farms in Russia: Status and Sales Channels
abstract: Smallholder farms and their product distribution channels are important components of Russia’s food security. This article describes the current state of commercial family farms in Russia and their distribution channels, summarizing the experience of agricultural aggregators in the Volgograd Region.The research focused on smallholder farms, agricultural aggregators, and farm product distribution channels. The data were subjected to standard research and statistical processing methods.Small farms account for approximately 14.0% of the national gross agricultural output. In 2025, the output of smallholder farms and individual entrepreneurs reached 1,518.5 billion rubles, which was by 14.4% higher than in 2024. Farms concentrate mostly in the Southern, Volga, and North Caucasus Federal Districts. Agricultural aggregators were studied for their role in addressing marketing challenges and distributed by region. The comprehensive analysis of aggregators in the Volgograd Region showed that traditional markets, cooperatives, digital platforms, marketplaces, and agritourism remain effective distribution channels.These findings can be applied to develop efficient distribution systems for farm products amid the digitalization of the agricultural sector.

title: Deficit Loop: Closed-Loop Adaptive Calorie Targeting With Per-User AI Agents Over Consumer Messaging — Development and 7-Week Observational Field Report (Preprint)
abstract: BACKGROUND Consumer weight-management tools prescribe daily calorie targets open-loop: a population prediction equation estimates energy expenditure, an intended deficit is subtracted, and the number is rarely checked against what happens to the individual. Self-reported energy intake carries a large, stable, person-specific under-reporting bias, so a weight-loss stall presents two indistinguishable failure modes — a wrong target or an incomplete log — that demand opposite interventions. OBJECTIVE To describe the design of the deficit loop, a deterministic closed-loop calorie-target controller operating inside per-user large language model (LLM) coaching agents over consumer messaging (SMS and WhatsApp), and to report engineering constraints and field observations from its first 7 weeks of production operation. METHODS The controller maintains two energy-expenditure estimates in deliberately different units: an apparent expenditure back-solved from the user's own logged meals and weigh-ins, which inherits the user's reporting bias by construction, and an anthropometric prediction in physiological units, used exclusively for safety bounds. Their ratio routes each weekly run between re-deriving the target and repairing the measurement. An absolute deficit applied in the user's own logging units yields a provable fixed-point property: the steady-state true deficit equals the intended deficit for any stable multiplicative reporting bias. All arithmetic is computed outside the generative layer, and estimator internals are structurally excluded from user-facing messages. Observations are retrospective, de-identified aggregates from production snapshots (July and September 2026) of a commercial service; there was no control group. RESULTS Across users with at least one closed-loop control window (n=29), measured expenditure ran a median of approximately 284 kcal/day below the plan's textbook-formula prediction (24/29 below) and approximately 511 kcal/day below a consumer-calculator recommendation (22/24 below) — for the median user, roughly half of the formula-promised weekly progress. On 28-day forward weight-change prediction (57 windows, 19 users), the loop nearly eliminated the formula baseline's systematic bias (−0.02 vs −0.15 kg/week) and improved median absolute error (0.26 vs 0.36 kg/week). Over 7 weeks the controller landed 65 target movements (35 down, 30 up; median absolute change 100 kcal/day), and sub-floor detection reclassified roughly half of the recently active fleet (19/36) as not having a calorie-target problem. In a scan of 3,345 outbound coaching messages, 725 (21%) "room to eat" encouragements were sent while the user's standing target exceeded measured expenditure by at least 150 kcal/day, motivating the paper's central architectural argument: in an LLM-mediated coach, the dominant harm of an over-estimated target is behavioral. CONCLUSIONS Closing the loop on the prescription itself — while routing between "fix the target" and "fix the measurement" under self-report bias — is feasible at production scale inside LLM-mediated coaching, with all numbers kept outside the generative layer. This is an observational systems report from a self-selected commercial cohort, not a clinical-efficacy claim; controlled evaluation is future work.

title: An Alternative Method for Determining the Drag Force of Fixed-Wing Unmanned Aircraft Systems
abstract: It is noted that in agriculture, fixed-wing unmanned aircraft systems successfully perform the tasks of crop monitoring, pest and disease detection across large areas remote from the operator. Further improvements in unmanned aircraft speed, flight range, and payload capacity can be achieved by reducing aerodynamic drag. Research in this area is constrained by the lack of affordable experimental facilities with satisfactory operating characteristics. (Research purpose) To develop an alternative method for determining the aerodynamic drag of the objects under study. (Materials and methods) Existing experimental facilities used to evaluate the aerodynamic characteristics of models were analyzed. The design of a differential aerodynamic rotary machine was described. The operating principle of the experimental facility is based on comparing the drag forces acting on the test model and a reference body. (Results and discussion) The factors limiting the development of aerodynamically efficient aircraft shapes were identified, including the high cost of wind tunnels and the disturbances generated behind the test model and the reference body during their circular motion in a standard rotary machine. It was proposed to replace the aerodynamic balance of the rotary machine with a differential mechanism, thereby exposing the test model and the reference body to identical external disturbances. (Conclusions) The use of reference bodies and a differential mechanism would increase the cost of the differential aerodynamic rotary machine by 31 percent compared with a standard rotary machine. At the same time, the accuracy of the experimental results would increase by 33 percent, approaching that achieved in wind-tunnel testing.

title: Application of Navigation Systems in Breeding-Plot Sowing Technologies for Grain Crops
abstract: The use of navigation systems in agriculture enables crop seeds to be sown with the required accuracy and electronic field maps to be generated during sowing. (Research purpose) To conduct an analytical review of the use of navigation systems in cereal breeding-plot sowing technologies and to identify promising approaches to their application in newly developed robotic machines. (Materials and methods) Publications by domestic and foreign researchers in scientific journals, conference proceedings, as well as information available from open Internet sources, were analyzed using a qualitative approach. (Results and discussion) An analytical review of technologies and technical means using navigation systems in selective sowing of grain crops was conducted. The use of electronic mapping of breeding plots during cereal sowing was examined. The Federal Scientific Agroengineering Center VIM developed automated methods for marking breeding plots based on mathematical and digital models for positioning cereal-sowing equipment within the plots. The use of navigation systems to control robotic seed-delivery devices in plot seeders was also considered. (Conclusions) The use of navigation systems in cereal breeding-plot sowing technologies makes it possible to create electronic field maps, mark fields and breeding plots, track the movement of sowing units across the field, coordinate the operation of various robotic seed-delivery devices with that of the metering units, and provide a basis for implementing and improving automatic steering functions. These capabilities are particularly important for the development of new robotic plot seeders.

title: Разработка методических подходов к классификации моделей контрактных отношений в российском агропромышленном комплексе в условиях цифровой трансформации
abstract: В статье обосновывается актуальность разработки методических подходов к классификации моделей контрактных отношений в агропромышленном комплексе России с учетом процессов цифровой трансформации. В современных условиях развития агропромышленного комплекса России контрактные отношения выступают важнейшим механизмом координации взаимодействия между сельскохозяйственными товаропроизводителями, перерабатывающими предприятиями, торговыми организациями, финансовыми институтами и государством. Рост неопределенности внешней среды, необходимость обеспечения продовольственной безопасности и повышение требований к эффективности агробизнеса обусловливают потребность в совершенствовании методологических подходов к классификации моделей контрактных отношений. Предложена многоуровневая система классификации контрактных отношений в АПК России, учитывающая институциональные, организационно-экономические, управленческие и технологические характеристики взаимодействия участников агропродовольственных цепочек. Результаты исследования могут быть использованы государственными органами управления АПК при формировании политики цифровой трансформации отрасли, а также агрохолдингами для проектирования контрактных систем с поставщиками сырья. The article justifies the relevance of developing methodological approaches to classifying models of contractual relations in Russia’s agro‑industrial complex, taking into account the processes of digital transformation. In the current conditions of the development of Russia’s agro‑industrial complex, contractual relations serve as the most important mechanism for coordinating interaction between agricultural producers, processing enterprises, trading organizations, financial institutions, and the state. The growing uncertainty of the external environment, the need to ensure food security, and the increasing demands on the efficiency of agribusiness necessitate the improvement of methodological approaches to classifying models of contractual relations. A multi-level system for classifying contractual relations in the agro‑industrial complex of Russia has been proposed, taking into account the institutional, organizational‑economic, managerial, and technological characteristics of the interaction between participants in agri‑food chains.. The research results can be used by state bodies responsible for managing the agro‑industrial complex when formulating policies for the digital transformation of the sector, as well as by agro‑holdings for designing contractual systems with raw material suppliers.

STRATEGIC PRIORITIES FOR IMPROVING HUMAN RESOURCE MANAGEMENT EFFICIENCY IN AGRICULTURAL ENTERPRISES BASED ON DIGITALIZATION, ADAPTABILITY AND SUSTAINABLE DEVELOPMENT
abstract: The strategic priorities for enhancing human resource management efficiency in agricultural enterprises through digitalization, adaptability, and sustainable development are substantiates in the article. It is emphasized that HRM digital transformation should not be reduced to automation of isolated operations but should be understood as a transition toward integrated management of competencies, labor performance, personnel risks, and professional development based on interconnected HR, production, technical, and external data. A paradigm of HR function transformation is proposed, evolving from traditional administration through electronic HRM to strategic Digital HRM. A comprehensive model of a digital HR platform is developed, integrating HRIS, API, a unified HR directory, modules for recruitment, mobile fieldwork accounting, training, performance evaluation, safety and well being, People Analytics, and feedback mechanisms. A portfolio of six digitalization programs is formed, together with a methodological approach for selecting the priority program using a priority index. Empirical testing conducted on three agricultural enterprises confirmed the potential to increase the integral HR efficiency index. Calculated NPV and PI values verified the economic feasibility of the programs. A motivational framework for digital change was designed, accounting for enterprise readiness, proportion of active wave employees, average temporary bonus size, level of digital adoption, and actual realization of program potential. The scientific novelty lies in establishing a consistent interrelation between digital HR architecture, selective program choice, KPI/KRI transformation, integral IHRM, economic effect, and personnel motivation support, thereby ensuring adaptability and sustainable development of HR systems in the agricultural sector. This approach highlights the strategic role of digital HRM in balancing productivity, resilience, and employee well being, while aligning organizational practices with long term sustainability goals and reinforcing the competitiveness of agricultural enterprises in dynamic environments.

title: Generative AI risk prediction capability and cross border agricultural trade resilience: a PLS-SEM empirical study of coastal Chinese enterprises
abstract: Maritime transport carries the predominant share of cross-border agricultural trade, and geopolitical conflicts, climate anomalies, port congestion, and proliferating trade barriers have intensified uncertainty for the coastal enterprises that depend on seaborne logistics. Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) offers new pathways for building resilient supply chains through multi-source data fusion and risk prediction capabilities. However, empirical evidence examining how GenAI risk prediction capability (GenAI-RPC) relates to cross-border agricultural trade resilience (CATR) remains scarce. Grounded in the resource-based view (RBV) and dynamic capability theory, this study develops a direct-effects model linking three GenAI-RPC dimensions---multi-source cross-border risk identification and scoring, prediction accuracy and anti-hallucination stability, and AI risk model calibration and decision empowerment---to CATR. Using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM), we analyzed survey data from 300 agricultural enterprises engaged in cross-border trade across four coastal Chinese provinces (Shandong, Guangdong, Fujian, and Zhejiang). The measurement model demonstrated satisfactory reliability and validity: Cronbach's α ranged from 0.817 to 0.855, composite reliability from 0.880 to 0.902, and average variance extracted (AVE) from 0.623 to 0.697. All heterotrait-monotrait (HTMT) ratios were below 0.85, supporting discriminant validity. The structural model showed that all three GenAI-RPC dimensions were positively associated with CATR: multi-source risk identification ( β = 0.291, p < 0.001), prediction accuracy ( β = 0.251, p < 0.001), and model calibration ( β = 0.287, p < 0.001). The model explained 46.1% of the variance in CATR ( R 2 = 0.461; Stone--Geisser Q 2 = 0.112), with SRMR = 0.069 indicating acceptable fit. Among the control variables, enterprise digital transformation maturity showed a strong positive association with CATR ( β = 0.577, p < 0.001), and all three GenAI-RPC dimensions remained statistically significant after controlling for it. These findings contribute to the theoretical integration of GenAI capabilities with maritime supply chain resilience research and offer practical guidance for coastal agricultural enterprises and policymakers seeking to strengthen the resilience of seaborne food trade.

title: A stage-weighted environmental risk and visual severity integration model for climate-smart management of cassava anthracnose in humid tropical systems
abstract: Colletotrichum anthracnose is a persistent constraint on cassava root yield and planting material quality in humid tropical systems, where calendar-based management often leads to poorly timed or excessive fungicide use. This study developed and pilot-tested the Cassava Anthracnose Risk Index (CARI), a stage-sensitive, persistence-adjusted early-warning framework integrating low-cost environmental sensing with structured visual severity scoring for climate-smart, input-reduced disease management. Microclimate sensors were deployed at CSIR-CRI Fumesua, Ghana, across a 13-month rainfed crop cycle (March 2025 – April 2026) using the susceptible landrace Debo . A stage-weighted Environmental Risk Subscore (ERS; 0–600 points, ERS%) was constructed from six environmental components, moderated by a persistence factor requiring sustained infection-favorable conditions, and stratified across three growth stages. A Visual Symptom Subscore (VSS; 0–40) was derived from standardised weekly severity assessments of 15 sentinel plants, integrated into a composite CARI (0–100) with stage-specific alert thresholds. Across 73 valid Stage 3 monitoring days, CARI classified all observations as Low Risk and issued no Amber or Red alerts, including on 37 of 73 days with sustained nocturnal high-humidity conditions that would have triggered a precautionary alert under a simple threshold approach. In the single confirmed disease episode observed, an approximately one-day interval separated the highest environmental risk signal from confirmed symptom onset; this is not presented as a validated lag value, a preceding 25-day sensor outage means antecedent conditions cannot be characterised. CARI did not issue an intervention recommendation during this episode (11–24 February 2026) because concurrent environmental risk remained below the Amber threshold. Published decision support systems for Colletotrichum anthracnose in other pathosystems report fungicide reductions of 30–70% relative to calendar-based approaches; these figures are cited only for benchmarking and were not measured here, as no comparative fungicide trial was conducted. These results provide proof of concept for the technical operability of CARI and identify the dataset and analyses required for formal predictive evaluation in a planned multi-season study; they should not be interpreted as evidence of CARI’s predictive accuracy or input-reduction performance.

title: Calcium application coordinates seedling heat tolerance and yield-quality formation in ginger under summer high-temperature conditions
abstract: Summer heat stress constrains ginger production. Although calcium (Ca) enhances stress tolerance in various crops, its effects on heat tolerance, yield, and quality in ginger remain unclear. A pot experiment was conducted using Zingiber officinale cv. ‘Laiwu Big Ginger’ to evaluate Ca effects on plant growth and quality under natural summer high-temperature conditions. Six Ca rates (0, 15.2, 30.5, 45.7, 60.9, and 76.2 mmol Ca 2+ plant -1 ) were established using calcium nitrate tetrahydrate [Ca(NO 3 ) 2 ·4H 2 O]. Seedling-stage physiological and biochemical parameters were analyzed with linear mixed-effects models; harvest-stage growth, biomass, and quality parameters were analyzed with ANOVA or non-parametric tests. PCA, correlation analysis, and membership function analysis were used for multivariate evaluation. At Day 16, the 60.9 mmol Ca 2+ plant -1 treatment significantly improved photosynthetic capacity (chlorophyll +23.3%, Pn +13.0%), antioxidant enzyme activities (SOD, POD, CAT), and proline content, while reducing oxidative damage (MDA, REC) and ROS (O 2 ·- , H 2 O 2 ). These adjustments promoted biomass and rhizome quality, with the highest rhizome fresh weight (727.7 vs. 447.3 g plant -1 ), dry matter (+3.6%), soluble sugars (+28.1%), soluble protein (+36.5%), free amino acids (+19.1%), and vitamin C (+17.5%). Multivariate analyses confirmed positive correlations among photosynthetic traits, antioxidant activity, biomass, and quality parameters, with the 60.9 mmolCa 2+ plant -1 treatment ranking highest in comprehensive evaluation by membership function analysis. Calcium application at this optimal rate, as determined under our experimental conditions, was associated with enhanced heat tolerance and subsequent growth and quality formation. These findings provide practical insights for sustaining ginger productivity under heat stress within the scope of our experimental conditions.

title: Towards the One Exposome: harnessing artificial intelligence and digital health technologies across One Health toxicology, new approach methodologies, and environmental public health
abstract: The One Exposome framework integrates exposomics, One Health toxicology, New Approach Methodologies (NAMs) and artificial intelligence to advance environmental health from reactive risk assessment towards predictive, preventive, and participatory science. The paper positions One Health as the ethical and conceptual rationale for recognizing the interdependence of human, animal, and environmental health, the Exposome as the framework for measuring cumulative and life-course exposures, and NAMs together with digital and AI-enabled tools as the means to generate, integrate, and interpret mechanistic and adverse outcome pathway (AOP)-based evidence across biological scales. In this review, environmental health challenges such as antimicrobial resistance, endocrine disruption, and other complex multi-stressor exposures cannot be adequately addressed through compartmentalized, single-substance, or purely retrospective approaches. The One Exposome paradigm instead proposes a systems-based model that links exposure data, mechanistic toxicology, and public health intelligence across humans, animals, and ecosystems. It draws on human-relevant NAMs, including microphysiological systems, together with AI and multi-omics approaches, to support cross-species interpretation, earlier hazard identification, and more preventive intervention strategies. Within this framework, sentinel surveillance, integrated monitoring, and interoperable data systems are central for detecting shared risks across environmental, veterinary, food, and human health domains. The approach is also presented as requiring governance reform so that agricultural practice, environmental management, and clinical stewardship are aligned within a common preventive and planetary health perspective. Overall, the paper frames the One Exposome as a transdisciplinary architecture for environmental public health that combines measurable environments, mechanistic understanding, and computational integration. By connecting cumulative exposures to biological responses and population-level consequences, it offers a foundation for more anticipatory, equitable, and scientifically integrated environmental health decision-making.

title: Bridging the performance–efficiency gap: a resource-efficient hybrid DL-ML framework for jackfruit disease detection
abstract: Complex environment variability and limited computational resources in agricultural settings create challenges in automated detection in tropical regions, where jackfruit diseases pose major threats to harvest productivity and food security. Conventional machine learning models often fail to generalize across diverse image conditions. For sustainable, field-deployable diagnostic systems, it is essential to close the performance–efficiency gap, as traditional deep learning methods require large amounts of training data and high-end hardware. We propose a hybrid deep learning machine learning (DL-ML) framework that has been tailored for accurate and resource-efficient jackfruit disease identification. This framework discusses deep visual representations that are extracted using a lightweight custom Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) combined with a previously trained EfficientNet-B0, capturing both localized and nested image features. Principal Component Analysis (PCA) is utilized for feature optimization to enhance discriminative power and eliminate redundancy, while SMOTE minimizes dataset imbalance by generating synthetic minority samples. These selected features are then classified by employing a variety of machine learning algorithms, including Random Forest (RF), Support Vector Machine (SVM), XGBoost, CatBoost, and k-Nearest Neighbors (KNN). A stacked ensemble model incorporates the strengths of these classifiers, enhancing generalization and robustness under diverse lighting and background conditions. Experiments across multiple dataset configurations show a noticeable improvement in accuracy from 76.80% on raw data to 99.39% on the PCA-augmented dataset, illustrating that this hybrid ensemble consistently outperforms all individual deep and machine learning baselines. Although the approach is currently tailored to jackfruit disease datasets, its applicability to other crops or stress conditions requires greater domain adaptation studies. However, the model's high accuracy highlights its scalability and utility in low-resource agricultural environments. Additionally, it establishes a cost-effective diagnostic paradigm where efficient ML classification and deep feature extraction collaborate, laying the foundation for next-generation smart farming and precision agriculture systems.

title: Exact Elliptic and Solitary Waves in a Fourth-Order Generalized Burgers–Huxley-Type Equation with Truncated M-Fractional Derivatives
abstract: Most studies of generalized Burgers–Huxley equations model spatial transport with a second-order diffusion term. Fourth-order spatial terms have received less attention, although they occur in long-range dispersal and regularized reaction–diffusion models and change the dominant balance of traveling-wave reductions. We consider a fourth-order generalized Burgers–Huxley-type equation with local truncated M-fractional derivatives and reaction polynomials of degrees two, three, or five. For the differentiable solutions considered here, the truncated M-operator is local, and its parameters enter through an exact nonlinear reparameterization of the independent variables rather than through a memory kernel. A derivative-enriched elliptic expansion reduces the resulting fourth-order differential equation to algebraic coefficient systems. The bounded auxiliary profiles are Jacobi sn, cn, and dn functions, with tanh and sech obtained when roots of the auxiliary quartic coalesce. Within this ansatz, the coefficient systems yield two convective quadratic, two stationary quadratic, three stationary cubic, and one stationary quintic class in centered and shifted forms; only the convective quadratic families admit nonzero speed. Reality conditions and equivalences under reflection, phase and sign changes, and singular limits identify distinct bounded profiles. These profiles may provide closed-form reference solutions for numerical studies and illustrate the effect of the local coordinate transformation.

title: A Mass-Conserving Spatiotemporal Graph ODE Model for Multi-Step Streamflow Forecasting in a Sparsely Gauged Semi-Arid Basin
abstract: Semi-arid loess basins in the middle Yellow River have rapid runoff responses, short hydrological memory, and sparse gauging networks, so pooled metrics across all stations can conceal forecast failures in low-flow tributaries and during dry periods. This study proposes DaSTGODE, a data-augmented spatiotemporal graph ordinary differential equation model with a structural water balance constraint. DaSTGODE integrates directed advection–diffusion propagation, soil-moisture-limited evapotranspiration, and a recursive water balance within a unified framework, thereby closing the water budget at every forecast step through the model structure. A reference scenario with perfect meteorological forcing, DaSTGODE_pre, is also established. It supplies the decoder with meteorological conditions over the forecast window as future meteorological forcing and quantifies the potential contributions of future precipitation, air temperature, and potential evapotranspiration by channel. Using daily records from 10 stations in the Wuding River basin from 2006 to 2020, DaSTGODE is compared with long short-term memory (LSTM) and graph long short-term memory (GraphLSTM) models for 1-, 3-, 6-, and 12-day forecast windows. DaSTGODE increases pooled Nash–Sutcliffe efficiency (NSE) from 0.532 and 0.473 for the best baseline to 0.599 and 0.567 for the 6- and 12-day windows, respectively. Relative to the best baseline, DaSTGODE increases the 1-day station-macro logarithmic NSE (logNSE) from 0.266 to 0.612 and reduces the mean number of stations with a negative NSE in the 6-day window from 4.6 to 2.0. Under the reference scenario in which future meteorological conditions are known, DaSTGODE_pre increases the 6-day outlet NSE from 0.141 for DaSTGODE to 0.331, and future precipitation alone provides 94% of the gain obtained from all three meteorological channels. HBV virtual nodes yield only small improvements in metrics at gauged stations, but provide daily streamflow forecasts at the outlets of 16 ungauged subbasins. Taken together, these results show that, under the semi-arid and sparsely gauged conditions examined here, the complete physical graph ODE kernel mainly improves cross-station reliability and relative low-flow dynamics, while the perfect meteorological forcing experiment quantifies the contribution of meteorological information over the forecast period to accuracy at medium and long forecast windows and identifies the channels responsible for that contribution.

title: Empowering Farmers Through Agripreneurship for Sustainable Food Security in West Sumatra
abstract: Sustainable food security has become an important issue in agricultural development. Although previous studies have examined food access, food production, agripreneurship, and information technology separately, limited research has integrated these factors within an agripreneurship-based food security framework. This study examines the roles of food access, food production, agripreneurship, and information technology in shaping sustainable food security among farming households in West Sumatra Province, Indonesia. A total of 400 farming households were selected using a multi-stage random sampling technique across six districts. Data were collected through structured surveys from May to July 2025 and analyzed using PLS-SEM. The results show that food access, agripreneurship, and information technology significantly improve sustainable food security. In contrast, food production has no significant direct effect, indicating that higher output alone does not ensure sustainability. This highlights a shift from production-oriented to system-oriented food security approaches. Further analysis confirms that agripreneurship and information technology mediate the relationships between food access, food production, and sustainable food security. Agripreneurship strengthens innovation and income diversification, while information technology improves access to information and decision-making efficiency. This study contributes a novel integrated model of agripreneurship-based sustainable food security in rural Indonesia. The findings emphasize that sustainable food security depends on the synergy of market access, entrepreneurial capacity, and digital transformation. Policy implications highlight the need to strengthen farmer entrepreneurship, expand digital infrastructure, and improve food distribution systems.

title: Exploratory Explainable Machine Learning for Crop-Yield Interpretation: A Comparative Analysis of XGBoost, LightGBM, and CatBoost
abstract: Interpretable crop-yield modelling is important for agricultural planning and transparent decision support; however, the predictive value and generalizability of machine-learning explanations depend strongly on evaluation protocol and dataset quality. This study evaluates an exploratory XAI workflow combining XGBoost, LightGBM, CatBoost, SHAP, engineered features, leakage-aware feature selection, repeated cross-validation, nested cross-validation, and a cross-dataset transfer experiment. Among the three models using the common full original-plus-engineered representation, CatBoost achieved the strongest numerical held-out performance, whereas XGBoost was retained as the TreeSHAP reference model. Nested model selection chose CatBoost in all five outer folds (mean RMSE 1.0060; mean R² 0.0846). Nested SHAP selection was slightly weaker (mean RMSE 1.0199; mean R² 0.0586), supporting compact interpretation rather than a universally superior subset. The cross-dataset experiment used 7,509 mapped Maize and Rice observations and only Crop, Temperature, and Rainfall. All external R² values were negative; because the internal yield unit was undocumented and the external target was reported in hg/ha, these results indicate weak, non-unit-harmonized transfer rather than definitive external validation. Overall, the workflow is appropriate for transparent exploratory interpretation, not deployment-ready yield forecasting.

title: AI, Agents, and the Marketing Operating System
Machine Learning for Crop Recommendation and Yield Forecasting: A Practical Framework for Sustainable Agriculture
abstract: Agriculture is increasingly influenced by changing weather, soil conditions, water availability, and input costs. Farmers often have to make crop-selection and production decisions with incomplete or delayed information. This paper presents a practical machine-learning framework that connects basic soil and weather observations with crop recommendation and yield forecasting. The proposed workflow includes data preparation, feature selection, supervised learning, model validation, and explainability. For crop recommendation, we discuss classification methods such as Random Forest, Extra Trees, Logistic Regression, Decision Tree, K-Nearest Neighbour, Gaussian Naive Bayes, and Support Vector Machine. In contrast, regression methods such as Decision Tree Regressor, Random Forest Regressor, KNN Regressor, Support Vector Regressor, and XGBoost Regressor are considered for yield estimation. The supplied reference study reported very high benchmark performance on its datasets, including 99.7% classification accuracy for Random Forest and an R² value of 99.99% for SVR. We treat these numbers as reported benchmark results rather than new experimental results. The main contribution of this rewritten paper is a clearer, application-oriented framework that explains how machine learning can support agricultural decisions while recognizing data quality, geographic transferability, interpretability, and real-world deployment limitations

title: AIMS: Anchor-Integrated Multi-View Synthesis for Scalable Novel View Rendering
abstract: Feed-forward novel view synthesis methods achieve strong generalization from posed multi-view inputs, but scaling them to large input view sets remains challenging. Transformer-based approaches that jointly process all input-view tokens incur rapidly increasing computation and memory as the number of views grows, while simple view subsampling discards potentially useful observations. We introduce Anchor-Integrated Multi-View Synthesis (AIMS), a scalable framework that decouples the number of available observations from the number of views processed by the global synthesis model. AIMS selects a fixed set of spatially distributed anchor views using farthest point sampling, groups nearby observations around each anchor, and uses a lightweight learnable integrator to fuse their information into enriched anchor representations. This allows additional observations to contribute to synthesis while keeping the downstream global view budget fixed. Evaluations on RealEstate10K and ScanNet demonstrate a favorable quality--efficiency trade-off against transformer-based and Gaussian-based baselines. AIMS achieves 29.41 dB and 17.73 dB PSNR on the two datasets, respectively, with rendering averaging 7.24 ms per view.

title: PLUTO: An Agentic AI Tool for Interactive Spacecraft Rendezvous Trajectory Design
