title: Functional genomics in the WRKY transcription factor family: from model systems to crop species and beyond
abstract: WRKY transcription factors regulate plant responses to abiotic and biotic stresses. We reviewed studies of eight well-characterized Arabidopsis WRKY genes and their orthologs in Chinese cabbage, maize, rice, and tomato to assess conservation of stress-response functions. Many WRKY genes showed roles in both stress categories, with some conserved abiotic associations, such as drought response. These findings support crop improvement potential, though cross-species comparisons remain challenging.

title: A lightweight attention-enhanced YOLO-C2fGTR network for multi-class ship detection in remote sensing imagery
Enhancing Daily Hydrological Modeling in a Subtropical Region with the Implementation of a Multimodel Approach
abstract: Hydrologic modeling can be a powerful tool for forecasting, water availability estimation, water resource management, and land use change assessment. Thus, a good choice of models is vital. The most general classification of models in terms of their application is distributed and lumped. Lumped models are generally considered to be more straightforward to apply and implement than distributed models. One strategy for capitalizing the ease of application of these models is to implement multimodel approaches. These approaches are based on the ensemble of several models to achieve better performance than the individual models. In this context, the objective of the present work is to evaluate whether a multimodel ensemble, built from several lumped models, can reach the performance of two distributed models applied in watersheds with highly streamflow variability. In this sense, the present paper utilizes a variety of approaches to address hydrologic modeling in basins of a subtropical region characterized by high flow variability. The implemented models span the spectrum from lumped to distributed, encompassing a broad array of conceptualizations, ultimately culminating in the implementation of a multimodel approach. The findings indicate that although lumped hydrological models do not consistently yield optimal results, the construction of a multimodel ensemble from these models exhibits performance comparable to distributed hydrological models.

title: Micro–Nano Aerated Irrigation Mitigates the Accumulation of N, P, and COD Concentrations: Effects of Straw Return and Aerated Irrigation on Water Quality Dynamics under the Soaking Period of Paddy Fields
abstract: Straw returning to the field enhances crop yield and cultivated land quality while presenting risks of water quality degradation, particularly during the soaking period. In this study, a barrel planting experiment was used, three treatments (CK: no straw returning, ST: straw returning, SO: straw returning + micro–nano aeration irrigation) were set up to study the dynamic changes of surface water, soil solution (0–10, 10–20, and 20–30 cm), and key water quality indices [total nitrogen (TN), ammonia nitrogen ( NH 4 + - N ), nitrate nitrogen ( NO 3 − - N ), total phosphorus (TP), chemical oxygen demand (COD), dissolved oxygen (DO), pH] in the rice soaking period. The results showed that (1) straw return significantly increased the contents of TN, COD, and TP in paddy field water. Micro–nano aerated irrigation effectively improved water quality after straw return, reducing the average concentrations of TN, TP, and COD by 5.14%–13.54%, 2.08%–37.14%, and 6.07%–43.44%, respectively. (2) During the whole soaking period, there was a significant positive correlation between TN, NH 4 + - N and NO 3 − - N ( p 0.01 ). However, DO showed a significant negative correlation with COD, TN, and TP only in the middle of immersion, indicating that the increase of pollutant concentration in this stage was accompanied by a continuous oxygen consumption process. (3) The structural equation model showed that DO was the key driving factor for regulating water quality. DO had a strong negative direct effect on COD ( λ = − 0.713 , p 0.001 ) and TN ( λ = − 0.051 , p 0.001 ) and indirectly inhibited COD accumulation by regulating the morphological transformation between NH 4 + - N and NO 3 − - N . This study uncovered the underlying mechanisms of straw incorporation and aerated irrigation on water quality during the soaking period, identified critical determinants driving water quality variations, and provided a more comprehensive and in-depth theoretical foundation for the precise and effective mitigation of water quality degradation caused by agricultural straw return.
journal: Journal of Irrigation and Drainage Engineering

title: Assessing Irrigation Potential in East Africa: A Critical Review of Multicriteria Analysis Using GIS and Land Suitability Assessment for Irrigation
abstract: This comprehensive review analyzes existing methodologies and applications for assessing irrigation potential in Ethiopia, a nation heavily reliant on rain-fed agriculture despite having significant water and land resources. Ethiopia faces challenges in fully utilizing its irrigation potential due to various problems related to planning, design, implementation, and maintenance of systems as well as inconsistencies in assessment methodologies. The review identifies a prevalent use of multicriteria analysis using a geographic information system (GIS), particularly the analytic hierarchy process, for land suitability assessment. Key factors consistently evaluated for irrigation suitability include soil, slope, land use/cover, and proximity to water sources. Methodologies often categorize land into suitability classes ranging from highly suitable to permanently unsuitable. The review highlights the importance of accurate data, such as high-resolution digital elevation models for slope analysis. By critically analyzing current practices, this review aims to identify their strengths and weaknesses and provide recommendations to improve the accuracy and relevance of future irrigation potential assessments in Ethiopia.
journal: Journal of Irrigation and Drainage Engineering

title: Long-Term Conjunctive Water Management for Agriculture with Groundwater Salinity
abstract: In California and other (semi-)arid regions, chronic groundwater overdraft and aquifer salinization limit irrigated agriculture, threaten crop yield, and reduce flexibility in groundwater management. Higher aquifer salinity reduces groundwater’s ability to irrigate in drier years, when fresher water is less available to dilute more saline groundwater. This paper employs a novel, nested hydro-economic optimization framework—a decadal stochastic quadratic optimization model within a 10-stage dynamic program—to analyze century-scale water and crop management for a salinizing aquifer with limited drainage and hydrologic variability, similar to conditions in California’s western San Joaquin Valley. Results shows that groundwater management with accumulating salinity differs fundamentally from freshwater aquifers, resulting in greatly reduced net extraction and earlier aquifer recharge to slow salinity accumulation and prolong the utility of groundwater. Key optimal strategies also include the strategic reduction of early perennial crop acreage to support salinity suppression. For an example basin, higher initial salinity of 1,500 mg / L (versus 500 mg / L ) can greatly reduce long-term regional economic value. The economic rationale for recharge with deteriorating groundwater salinity transitions from a drought storage mechanism to a high-cost but still useful input for preserving perennial agriculture, with feasibility constrained by discount rates and climate. This work provides a strategic and quantitative approach for managing the irreversible degradation of groundwater resources.
journal: Journal of Irrigation and Drainage Engineering

title: Hierarchical VMD parameter selection for short-term HVAC load forecasting: A compact TCN-LSTM implementation
abstract: Variational mode decomposition (VMD) separates heating, ventilation, and air-conditioning (HVAC) load into narrower-band signals, but the number of modes and the bandwidth-penalty parameter must be selected without using test-set outcomes. We evaluated a diagnostic-guided selection procedure using a multichannel temporal convolutional network (TCN) with long short-term memory (LSTM). The dataset comprised 2208 hourly observations from Wuhan Cigarette Factory in summer 2024. For each target, VMD used the preceding 168 h; the final 24 values from each mode served as TCN-LSTM input. Training-only diagnostics screened 64 parameter pairs using range-normalized reconstruction error, the coefficient of variation in mode-specific sample entropy, and the first-mode energy ratio. Sixteen pairs met the criteria. The eight lowest-scoring pairs formed a diagnostic shortlist, which was evaluated with seed 42 and then across seeds 42–44. The selected pair, K=7 and α=1500, yielded validation and test root-mean-square errors (RMSEs) of 2.113±0.079 and 2.253±0.161 kW across seeds 42–44 and 42–46, respectively. On the test segment, the reference 5,2000 and minimum-J admissible 8,1000 pairs yielded RMSEs of 2.243±0.094 and 2.285±0.161 kW, respectively. VMD-transformer with bidirectional LSTM (VMD-transformer-BiLSTM) and VMD-TCN-LSTM yielded 2.185±0.062 and 2.253±0.161 kW, respectively; Diebold–Mariano tests showed no consistent squared-loss difference across seeds. VMD-TCN-LSTM used 14 961 parameters, 73.8% fewer than VMD-transformer-BiLSTM. Excluding preprocessing and data handling, its single-sample network forward-pass time was 0.285±0.014 ms. Across 231 diagnostic-weight combinations, five pairs were selected, with seed-42 validation RMSE spanning 2.038–2.063 kW. Therefore, the procedure fixed VMD parameters without using test targets but did not establish an RMSE advantage over the reference pair.

title: Phytotoxicity of pyroxasulfone and pendimethalin, individually and in combination, in non-target vegetable crops.
abstract: Herbicides are increasingly used in modern agriculture, yet their unintended effects on adjacent non-target vegetable crops remain insufficiently investigated. This study evaluated the individual and combined phytotoxic effects of two pre-emergence herbicides, pyroxasulfone and pendimethalin, on nine non-target vegetable crops during early seedling development, integrating dose-response modeling (GR50), toxicity index (TI) assessment and onion root-tip cytological analysis. All treatments produced significant dose-dependent suppression of seedling growth, with dry weight emerging as the most sensitive indicator of herbicidal stress. Pendimethalin caused stronger growth inhibition (7.87 ± 1.41 to 60.76 ± 1.54%) than pyroxasulfone (3.27 ± 1.81 to 52.17 ± 0.68%), while combined exposure produced the greatest reductions across crops (11.02 ± 0.79 to 71.55 ± 1.22%). Highest Single Agent (HSA) analysis showed that fixed-ratio mixture produced greater growth inhibition than the individual herbicides, whereas Bliss independence indicated crop- and dose-dependent interaction outcomes. Onion was the most sensitive crop based on GR50, while metha and pea were comparatively more tolerant. Cytological analysis revealed reduced mitotic index and increased chromosomal abnormalities, particularly under combined treatment. These findings demonstrate that herbicide mixtures may produce greater phytotoxic responses than individual compounds, highlighting the importance of species-specific ecological risk assessment and herbicide stewardship.
journal: Journal of environmental science and health. Part. B, Pesticides, food contaminants, and agricultural wastes

title: Nonparametric Prioritization of Breath VOC Signatures for Differential Diagnosis of Asthma, Bronchiectasis, and COPD.
abstract: Accurate differentiation among asthma, bronchiectasis, and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) remains a major clinical challenge due to overlapping symptoms and limitations of conventional diagnostic approaches. This study proposes a nonparametric cumulative distribution function (CDF)-based framework combined with permutation testing to analyze volatile organic compounds (VOCs) in exhaled breath as non-invasive biomarkers for respiratory disease characterization. Breathomics data obtained via gas chromatography-mass spectrometry (GC-MS) from 121 patients were analyzed following log₂ transformation of VOC intensities. The analytical scope included not only shared VOCs but also pair-specific and disease-exclusive compounds. The discriminative ability of each VOC was assessed by comparing class-specific empirical cumulative distributions with null distributions generated through 2000 random permutations. CDF rankings were then generated for core, pair-specific, and disease-exclusive singleton VOCs. To evaluate classification utility, progressively reduced VOC subsets were assessed using Random Forest and Partial Least Squares Discriminant Analysis (PLS-DA) under repeated stratified cross-validation. Results showed that a reduced set of highly ranked VOCs preserved substantial classification performance, supporting the effectiveness of the proposed prioritization strategy. Candidate VOCs were then suggested based not only on their ranking scores, but also on biological interpretation and support from previously reported literature. Overall, the CDF- and permutation-based approach provides an interpretable, statistically robust, and model-independent framework for biomarker discovery in respiratory diseases.

title: A-251 Rapid AI-Based Detection of Acute Promyelocytic Leukemia from Digital Blood Smears
abstract: Acute promyelocytic leukemia (APL) is a distinct subtype of acute myeloid leukemia (AML) with PML::RARA fusion and a high risk of early mortality without treatment. Prompt recognition and treatment are critical for improving outcomes. Although most APLs demonstrate classic morphology, severe cytopenia makes APL identification on the peripheral blood smear (PBS) challenging. Additionally, the microgranular variant may mimic other myeloid neoplasms. CellaVision, an automated digital microscopy platform widely used for PBS review and differential counts, does not distinguish APL blasts from non-APL blasts, limiting early recognition. We developed and validated a deep learning model to automatically subclassify PB cells and identify APL blasts from CellaVision images to enable real-time detection of APL blasts in a clinical laboratory. A purposive sample of 36,938 curated single-cell images from 9,364 unique cases captured on CellaVision DM1200 and DI-60 systems were annotated by experts. Fourteen morphologic classes were defined: APL blasts, non-APL blasts, promyelocytes, myelocytes/metamyelocytes, mature myeloid cells, monocytes, lymphocytes, plasma cells, basophils, eosinophils, large platelets, nucleated red cells and artefact. The training and validation datasets comprised 32,840 and 4,098 images, with mature myeloid cells and lymphocytes comprising nearly 40%, APL blasts 6.1%, non-APL blasts 5.6% and promyelocytes 0.4% of images. A pretrained vision transformer backbone (DINOv3 ViT-B/16) was fine-tuned using a multi-view attention-based multiple-instance learning framework. Each cell image was processed through four complementary views, including full-field and multiscale center crops. An attention pooling head aggregated view-level embeddings for classification. Training used cross-entropy loss with label smoothing and layer-wise learning rate decay. Independent testing included 27 cases, including 8 non-APL AML, 6 APL, 3 myelodysplastic syndrome, 2 myeloma, 5 left-shift, and 3 normal cases, with one APL case scanned in triplicate for repeatability. Performance was evaluated using cell-level accuracy and Jensen–Shannon divergence (JSD) between predicted and reference distributions. False-positive rates were assessed on 1,000 randomly selected routine clinical cases. Across the 27-case independent test cohort, the mean accuracy at the cell-level was 89.0%. JSD values were low (<0.10) in all but one case, indicating close agreement between predicted and reference distributions. The model identified blasts in all non-APL AML cases. It detected APL blasts in all but one microgranular variant, in which atypical APL blasts were classified as non-APL blasts. Among 21 non-APL cases, two had misclassified as APL blasts: two plasma cells in myeloma and one blast in non-APL AML. Triplicate analysis of one APL case demonstrated consistent performance at cell-level (accuracy 0.79 ± 0.01 and JSD 0.082 ± 0.019). In the 1,000-case screening cohort (inference time 8 seconds/case), only two cells from two separate cases were falsely labeled as APL blasts (0.2% false-positive rate). We developed a deep learning system capable of accurately subclassifying PB cells and identifying APL blasts from routine digital microscopy images. The model demonstrated strong concordance with expert review and low false-positive rate. Integrating the model into hematology workflows enables rapid, automated morphologic triage of suspected APL, facilitating earlier diagnosis and treatment, and may improve efficiency and standardization in morphologic assessment.

title: A-370 MDx-in-a-Bead: scaling point-of-care diagnostics with a simplified, lyophilized LAMP framework
abstract: Effective infectious diseases management requires field-deployable, Point of Care (POC) tools for rapid pathogen detection near the patient or source. Current molecular methods are often hindered by "cold chain" requirements, complex reagent handling, and high cost. We addressed these practical challenges by developing a versatile “MDx-in-a-Bead” technology. The single lyophilized unit technology stabilizes all necessary Loop-mediated isothermal amplification (LAMP) reagents into one lyophilized bead (Lyobead) enabling fast, multiplex, ambient-stable molecular diagnostics enabling large-scale applications. We developed a stabilized LAMP master mix (Bst Polymerase, RT enzyme, dNTPs, and buffers) by incorporating specific lyoprotectants designed to maintain enzyme kinetics in a solid state through the freeze-drying cycle. This formulation is compatible with primers and probes or ion-based dyes for real-time colorimetric sensing of amplification byproducts. These Lyobeads dissolve rapidly upon sample addition, enabling both high-precision digital detection and immediate visual interpretation. To evaluate the Lyobeads universality, we performed sensitivity and specificity assays using both purified genetic material and direct-to-assay lysates (simplified digestion chemistry) to simulate field conditions across a diverse range of pathogens. Targets included human respiratory virus (SARS-CoV-2), foodborne pathogens (Salmonella), and agricultural threats such as Botrytis, Fusarium, and Hop Latent Viroid. The probe-based lyophilized reagents performed with functional equivalence to standard liquid LAMP reagents across all tested pathogens. In comparative trials for SARS-CoV-2, the beads achieved a time to respond (TTR) of 20 minutes, compared to freshly prepared liquid master mixes (TTR 19 minutes). For colorimetric beads, a distinct, binary color shift from pink to yellow was consistently observed in under 30 minutes across both human and agricultural targets, while non-template controls (NTCs) remained pink. The visual change remained robust even when using crude leaf extracts for plant pathogens and swab lysates, demonstrating high tolerance to complex sample matrices. The MDx-in-a-Bead technology offers a robust, cold chain-independent solution that integrates seamlessly into existing laboratory workflows or POC cartridges. By eliminating the logistical barriers of traditional diagnostics, the system enhances outbreak response in resource-limited settings. As a critical tool for programs such as Global One Health Surveillance, it facilitates immediate intervention to protect human health, agricultural productivity, and the safety of the global food supply.

title: Meso-scale spatial analysis of papilloma formation and clonal expansion in cancerized skin.
abstract: Somatic driver mutations pervade phenotypically normal epithelia, yet only a minority of clones progress to tumors. To understand how tissue context modulates clonal selection, we apply the classical two-stage DMBA/TPA model of carcinogenesis to mouse back skin. We collect coordinate-registered, meso-scale grids spanning multiple centimeters with 1-mm punches and profile genotype and transcriptome from the same positions (WES, n = 473; bulk RNA-seq, n = 690), complemented by matched single-cell RNA-seq. This paired, spatially resolved design enables direct coupling of clonal selection metrics to local transcriptional programs. All sequenced papillomas (n = 6) harbor Hras Q61L mutation events, but expected frequency versus observed papillomas indicate that Hras Q61L is necessary but insufficient to drive tumorigenesis within the observation period. To quantify how field-level signaling constrains driver potency, we compute pathway activities and introduce a Laplacian-based "ruggedness" score to capture meso-scale heterogeneity. We find that field-level signaling is rewired before visible tumorigenesis: TNF-associated epithelial necroptosis rises broadly across promoted skin, while TGFB activity becomes spatially "rugged"with papillomas at local TGFB signaling minima. Selection mapping reveals a context shift: in untreated skin, positive selection corresponds with cell cycle deregulation; in the cancerized field, it correlates with impaired differentiation. Moreover, the coupling between WNT signaling and selection evident in untreated tissue is abrogated for DMBA-initiated mutations. These data show that programs such as differentiation regulation, necroptosis, and TGFB topology reshape the selective landscape, constraining the effective potency of driver mutations and explaining why clones differ in their capacity to expand and progress to tumors.

title: From financial fragility to business discontinuation in crop agriculture: evidence from Spanish firm-level data
abstract: This study examines whether business discontinuation in crop agriculture is better explained by one-period accounting weakness or by cumulative financial fragility, focussing on profitability persistence, internal cash-flow generation and balance-sheet resilience. The analysis uses longitudinal accounting data for 438 Spanish crop-agriculture firms over 2014–2024, including 97 discontinuation events. Discrete-time hazard models, two-year lead logit models and three-year trajectory models distinguish contemporaneous weakness from accumulated deterioration. The discontinuation measure is validated against the legal status recorded in the Spanish Mercantile Register, and all core results are re-estimated under a register-validated event definition, within a single nested specification, and with out-of-sample evaluation. One-year negative profitability is not a robust predictor once broader financial conditions are considered. Weaker cash-flow generation predicts near-term discontinuation and higher tangible asset intensity is associated with lower discontinuation risk; both signals strengthen materially when the event is restricted to firms with a non-active register status. Repeated profitability weakness raises discontinuation probability in the final three-year window, although it does not dominate contemporaneous weakness as a strictly pre-event predictor. Discontinuation is proxied by the termination of the firm's accounting sequence; register-status validation shows that this proxy captures register closure and dissolution together with cessation of filing, rather than formal insolvency alone. Future research should incorporate legal failure events, credit conditions, policy exposure and production shocks. Accounting data can support screening indicators for lenders, advisors and policymakers. Out-of-sample discrimination is modest (cross-validated AUC of 0.67 under the register-validated event), so the indicators are proposed as screening devices rather than as operational early-warning classifiers. Monitoring cash-flow sufficiency and tangible asset intensity may help identify firms at risk before discontinuation becomes irreversible. Earlier detection of financial fragility can help preserve viable crop-production capacity and support targeted interventions in agricultural regions exposed to recurrent economic and climatic pressures. The study integrates agricultural exit, viability and financial-distress perspectives within a dynamic firm-level framework, showing that discontinuation in crop agriculture reflects accumulated financial fragility, namely weak internal financing capacity and a weaker tangible asset base, rather than isolated accounting weakness.

title: Beyond adoption: how algorithmic trust and data-driven culture translate agentic artificial intelligence readiness into strategic agility among Sri Lankan SMEs
abstract: This study aims to investigate how Agentic artificial intelligence (AI) readiness enhances Strategic Agility among small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) in Sri Lanka. Drawing on the Technology-Organisation-Environment framework, Resource-Based View, and Dynamic Capabilities theory, this study incorporated data-driven culture as a moderating variable. This quantitative study employed a questionnaire survey to collect data from 293 Sri Lankan SMEs. The variables were derived from previously validated instruments. Partial least squares structural equation modelling (PLS-SEM) with SmartPLS 4 was used to investigate the proposed relationships. The relative significance of the predictors was assessed using artificial neural network analysis (ANN) in SPSS 29. The results revealed that Technological Infrastructure Readiness, Algorithmic Self-Efficacy, Competitive Pressure, Leadership Strategic Orientation, Responsible AI Governance Maturity and AI Human Skills significantly influenced Algorithmic Trust. Algorithmic Trust significantly enhanced Strategic Agility, whereas a data-driven culture strengthened this relationship. The ANN results further confirmed the importance of Responsible AI Governance Maturity, Leadership Strategic Orientation and Algorithmic Trust. This study highlights the importance of Algorithmic Trust, Responsible Governance, AI-Related Human Skills and data-driven culture in translating Agentic AI Readiness into Strategic Agility. The findings offer useful implications for SME owners and policymakers seeking to implement autonomous AI systems in emerging economies. This study enhances the understanding of Agentic AI adoption in SMEs by moving beyond adoption intention and examining how AI Readiness produces strategic outcomes. It emphasises the role of Algorithmic Trust and data-driven culture in enabling SMEs to achieve Strategic Agility. By integrating Algorithmic Trust and data-driven culture, this study explains how SMEs can convert Agentic AI readiness into Strategic Agility, rather than merely adopting AI technologies.

title: The Coaching Effectiveness Pathways Model (CEPM): how workplace coaching creates organizational value
abstract: Workplace coaching is widely used as a learning and development intervention, yet much of the literature confirms effectiveness rather than explaining how coaching creates value within organizational systems. This paper introduces the Coaching Effectiveness Pathways Model (CEPM) to address this gap. The paper adopts a conceptual, theory-driven approach, integrating established workplace coaching research with organizational learning literature to identify how contextual conditions and psychological mechanisms shape coaching effectiveness. CEPM conceptualizes coaching effectiveness as a pathway-based process linking organizational enabling conditions, psychological mechanisms activated through coaching, and differentiated outcome trajectories. It distinguishes proximal outcomes, such as clarity and confidence, from distal outcomes, such as sustained behavior change and goal attainment, and explains why performance-related outcomes show the strongest effects. As a conceptual paper, CEPM is not empirically tested. Future research should examine the proposed pathways, mediating mechanisms, and contextual moderators using longitudinal and multilevel designs. CEPM gives HR and L&D professionals a framework for designing, embedding, and evaluating coaching within organizational learning systems, including evaluating proximal and distal outcomes separately. By clarifying how coaching sustains learning and behavior change, the framework supports healthier, more sustainable performance and humane, learning-oriented organizations. The paper shifts coaching scholarship from outcome confirmation to pathway-based explanation, clarifying what an integrative, coaching-specific framework adds beyond generic input–process–output and context–mechanism–outcome models.
journal: Development and Learning in Organizations: An International Journal

title: Different agents, different trust: private information disclosure in hybrid service encounters
abstract: As artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled service technologies become more common, consumers increasingly disclose private information to both human and technological service agents. This study aims to examine how service agent type shapes private information disclosure in hospitality and tourism encounters. Using an exploratory sequential mixed-methods design, Phase I explored disclosure experiences with human and technological service agents and informed the development of an agent-contingent conceptual framework. Phase II tested the relationships among multidimensional trust (competence, integrity and benevolence), perceived control (transparency, vulnerability and privacy empowerment) and willingness to disclose. Phase III experimentally examined the effects of service agent type and brand familiarity. Across the studies, service agent type influenced why consumers trusted an agent more than whether they were willing to disclose. Technological agents drew trust more strongly from competence, whereas human agents benefited more from benevolence. In turn, trust, rather than perceived control, was the primary predictor of willingness to disclose private information. Brand familiarity provided an additional organizational assurance cue, increasing both trust and willingness to disclosure across service agent types. Service firms should align disclosure practices with the trust cues associated with different service agents. AI-enabled interfaces can strengthen trust through clear data usage explanations and human support, while human agents can reinforce perceptions of competence through standardized privacy procedures. This study develops an agent-contingent framework of private information disclosure in hybrid service encounters, showing how disclosure reflects evaluations of the information requester, disclosure process and organization responsible for the data.
journal: International Journal of Contemporary Hospitality Management

title: Agentic AI in Healthcare 5.0: Reference Architecture, Applications, and Challenges
abstract: Healthcare systems are increasingly data-rich but remain fragmented, reactive, and difficult to coordinate across institutions, devices, and clinical workflows. Healthcare 5.0 addresses these limitations through human-centricity, resilience, and symbiotic human-artificial intelligence (AI) collaboration. This survey positions agentic AI, goal-oriented systems capable of contextual perception, persistent memory, multistep planning, tool use, and bounded action, as the orchestration layer of Healthcare 5.0. We make four contributions: 1) a reference architecture that maps perception, reasoning, planning, action, and memory across device, edge, and cloud tiers; 2) an autonomy-criticality taxonomy for four healthcare application domains; 3) a structured analysis of safety, security, privacy, ethics, and regulatory challenges; and 4) a phased roadmap for responsible clinical deployment. Our analysis shows that Healthcare 5.0 requires not only capable models, but also safety-governed, auditable, and ethically aligned agentic ecosystems.

title: Surface-Adaptive Robotic Ultrasound With Multisensor Fusion and Cascaded AI for 3-D Stenosis Assessment of Aneurysmal Arteriovenous Fistula
abstract: Stenosis assessment of aneurysmal arteriovenous fistulae (AVF) is difficult because the bulging skin and the underlying vessel rarely run in the same direction, so a probe that follows the surface drifts off the lumen, and single-stage segmenters tuned for smooth surfaces confuse the fistula with the adjacent artery. Unlike existing robotic AVF systems that scan the limb in a fixed pose and rely on remote sonographer interpretation, this work presents a surface-adaptive robotic ultrasound system (RUS) that performs assessment on-device using a cascaded AI framework. The system combined RGB-D sensing for surface-normal probe guidance, force/torque for contact regulation, and B-mode ultrasound for lumen imaging. A two-class YOLOv8s detector first disambiguated the fistula from the adjacent artery, resolving the failure mode of single-stage segmentation, after which U-Net++ segmented the lumen on the cropped region; a phantom-to-clinical two-stage transfer-learning scheme compensated for limited labeled clinical data. A point-to-point tilting scan adapted probe orientation to local skin normals, an intrascan vessel-tracking model kept the lumen centered, and a surface-and-lumen co-registered reconstruction yielded a 3-D record with stenotic-point localization. Under patient-level fivefold cross-validation, the detector reached a precision of 0.9967 and a recall of 0.9968, and the segmenter a Dice of 0.9239. On hand phantoms, degree-of-stenosis estimation achieved a per-measurement mean absolute error of 0.36% (95% CI, 0.21%–0.52%) versus 1.84% for an experienced sonographer, and stenotic points were localized to within 0.37 mm per axis, demonstrating the feasibility of AI-guided surveillance of aneurysmal AVFs on an off-the-shelf collaborative robot.

title: NIR-EKF: Normalized Innovation Ratio-Based EKF for Robust State Estimation
abstract: Sensors deployed in real-world conditions often produce measurements corrupted by outliers due to model uncertainties, changes in the surrounding environment, and/or data loss. As a result, managing these outliers becomes crucial for state estimation to avoid inaccurate estimations and a reduction in the reliability of results. To address this issue, we introduce a novel form of extended Kalman filter (EKF) based on the maximum a posteriori (MAP) principle for scenarios where outliers simultaneously occur in multiple dimensions. For detecting outliers during the filtering process, we introduce a novel variant of the normalized innovation ratio (NIR) test and embed it within the EKF framework. Our approach enhances the estimation accuracy and computational efficiency of state estimation process even when data from several sensors simultaneously contain outliers.

title: Artificial Intelligence Coding Agents in Software Engineering Education:: Why Development & Operations and Scale Matter
abstract: This article analyzes how artificial intelligence (AI) coding agents influence software engineering learning. Small programming tasks often allow AI to replace problem formulation and design reasoning, whereas large Development & Operations-oriented workflows expose the limitations of AI-generated output.

title: Balancing Centralized and Distributed Intelligence: The Role of Agentic AI-RAN in Smart City
abstract: Modern smart city increasingly relies on continuous perception, reliable communication, adaptive computation and coordinated intelligence across complex and fast-evolving urban environments. However, existing network architectures cannot provide unified or scalable support for these capabilities. Artificial intelligence–radio access network (AI-RAN) has recently been proposed as a potential solution by integrating communication, computation, storage, perception and AI (CCSPA) into a unified intelligent infrastructure, enabling the network itself to act as a pervasive source of perception, inference and decision support. In addition, recent advances in agentic AI, introducing goal-driven inference, long-term memory, multi-step decision-making and interactive multi-agent coordination, further extend the boundary of AI-RAN. This article redefines centralized approach vs. distributed approach in AI-RAN and proposes a collaborative agentic AI-RAN (CoAI) architecture, aiming to achieve dynamic balance between centralized and distributed intelligence and support deep fusion across CCSPA resources. The CoAI architecture enhances the ability to sustain complex smart city functions through multi-layer intelligence and cross-node collaboration. Furthermore, through analyses of representative scenarios such as low-altitude economy, digital twin city and embodied intelligence, we show that CoAI offers a unified and adaptive foundation for AI-native smart city systems.

title: Agentic AI for 6G ISAC
abstract: Agentic artificial intelligence (Agentic AI) represents a new framework for future sixth-generation (6G) integrated sensing and communications (ISAC) systems. Agentic AI can shift network management from passive, model-driven optimization to active, goal-driven autonomy. By reasoning, planning, and executing complex actions, Agentic AI aims to handle the high complexity of 6G networks. This article surveys this emerging topic, focusing on the basic principles of Agentic AI, reviewing its key applications in ISAC, and identifying its critical challenges. We also briefly discuss how large artificial intelligence models (LAMs) may support agentic reasoning and intent understanding in practical ISAC deployments. Furthermore, six promising research directions are outlined.

title: Agentic AI-RAN: Framework, Mechanism, and Applications
abstract: The rapid development of artificial intelligence (AI) has led to the emergence of agent technology driven by large language models (LLMs), which are regarded as valid solutions to numerous cross-field challenges owing to their tremendous intelligence and autonomy. When the agents are applied to the radio access network (RAN), a new paradigm, agentic AI-RAN, rises in response, which integrates communication, sensing, computation, and control through the advanced decision-making capabilities and self-sufficiency of agents. Due to different design purposes, agentic AI-RAN has two unique features compared to conventional AI-empowered RAN. First, an agent in agentic AI-RAN does not only process network data passively as a learning model but also perceives, reasons, plans, and acts upon the radio environment autonomously, which fundamentally reshapes the way RAN functions are orchestrated. Second, an agent in agentic AI-RAN must jointly handle multi-dimensional resources including communication, sensing, computation, and control rather than optimizing along a single dimension as done in standard AI-RAN systems, since the agentic capability emerges only from the co-deployment of these heterogeneous functionalities. Due to these unique features, in this paper, we present an overview on the fundamentals and key challenges in the design of agentic AI-RAN. We first introduce the concept of agentic AI-RAN and provide its basic framework. Then, we focus on agentic AI-RAN techniques in two areas: the co-deployment mechanism of agents over the RAN infrastructure and the agentic interaction with the radio environment. For each area, we identify the main problems and challenges. Then, we will provide a comprehensive treatment of these problems. Two use cases, one based on Py5chesim and another one based on Bubble RAN by NVIDIA, are demonstrated as well. Finally, we point out future research in the field of agentic AI-RAN. In a nutshell, this article provides a holistic set of guidelines on how to design agentic AI-RAN systems over real-world wireless communication networks, aiming to stimulate more innovative research on this emerging paradigm.

title: SageIQ: Scene-Graph-Guided Blind Image Quality Assessment
abstract: Conventional Blind Image Quality Assessment (BIQA) methods typically assess the entire image quality, which is suboptimal for tasks like autonomous driving that concern specific Task-Aligned Region (TAR). Moreover, we observe that advanced Multimodal Large Language Model (MLLM)-based BIQA models exhibit bias when evaluating small regions, leading to inaccurate perceptual judgments. To address these issues, we propose SageIQ (Scene-graph-guided Evaluation for Image Quality), a pipeline SageIQ-P for TAR localization, an approach consisting of an MLLM-based BIQA model SageIQ-M, and a dataset SageIQ-D. SageIQ-P is designed to automatically identify and evaluate TARs, with the advantages of being training-free and allowing plug-in integration of off-the-shelf BIQA models without retraining. It operates in three stages: scenegraphbased triplet construction, LLMdriven triplet analysis, and integration of weighted BIQA scores into a final assessment. Since SageIQ-P can produce small-sized TAR crops that may encounter small-region scoring bias in existing BIQA models, we propose SageIQ-M to alleviate this bias by injecting scale information through scale-aware images and size-prompted cues, achieving size awareness across both visual and textual modalities. In addition, we develop a fully automated approach to construct a region-level test set SageIQ-D, significantly reducing the human effort needed. Experimental results demonstrate that our methods achieve superior BIQA performance.
journal: IEEE Transactions on Emerging Topics in Computational Intelligence

title: A Multicriteria Game-Driven Constrained Multiobjective Evolutionary Algorithm
abstract: Solving constrained multiobjective optimization problems (CMOPs) involves simultaneously achieving convergence to the Pareto front, preserving solution diversity, and satisfying complex constraints. To address these challenges, this article proposes a multicriteria game-driven constrained multiobjective evolutionary algorithm (MGCMOEA), which leverages the complementary roles of a main population and an auxiliary population to jointly explore both feasible and infeasible regions. The algorithm introduces a refined feasibility classification mechanism that differentiates weakly feasible solutions from infeasible ones, thereby accelerating convergence while preserving potentially valuable solutions. To enhance cooperation between populations, MGCMOEA incorporates a multicriteria game-theoretic selection model that integrates dynamic game theory with the technique for order preference by similarity to ideal solution (TOPSIS). This model improves the guidance provided by the auxiliary population during evolution. Furthermore, to overcome inefficiencies associated with static population sizes, a dynamic resource allocation strategy is adopted, enabling adaptive distribution of computational resources throughout the evolutionary process. Experimental results on 47 benchmark functions and 12 real-world CMOPs demonstrate that MGCMOEA consistently outperforms 8 state-of-the-art algorithms in terms of convergence, diversity, and feasibility.

title: A Survey on End-to-End Autonomous Driving Training From the Perspectives of Data, Strategy, and Platform
abstract: Autonomous driving is a cornerstone technology for the future of intelligent transportation, where end-to-end learning has emerged as a transformative paradigm that directly maps multimodal sensory inputs to driving actions through unified differentiable models. While offering advantages, the effectiveness of end-to-end autonomous driving (E2E-AD) is ultimately determined by the quality of its training ecosystem. This paper provides a comprehensive review of training methods and ecosystem for E2E-AD. We introduce a Data-Strategy-Platform taxonomy that conceptualizes training as an interdependent system. The data layer defines what can be learned, the strategy layer governs how learning aligns with driving objectives, and the platform layer supports scalability and continuous evolution. Within this framework, we survey recent advances across data-centric pipelines, learning paradigms, and training infrastructures, and analyze their interplay in shaping model performance, robustness, and deployability. Finally, we reflect on current limitations and articulate a forward-looking vision that emphasizes a shift from data quantity to data value, from isolated optimization to foundation-driven generalization, and from static training to integrated training-testing loops, aiming toward robust, scalable, and trustworthy autonomous driving systems. We maintain a continuously updated repository tracking cutting-edge literature and works at \href{https://github.com/Jiaaqiliu/Awesome-Training-Ecosystem-for-E2E-AD}{Our Project Page}.
journal: IEEE Transactions on Intelligent Transportation Systems

title: TOE: Tackling Distribution Shifts in Time Series via Three-Perspective Online Ensemble
abstract: Persistent distribution shift poses a challenging problem in multivariate long-term time series forecasting (MTSF) tasks. Although existing methods have made considerable progress, they still encounter two key limitations. First, methods based on offline learning typically utilize a static set of parameters to model the entire time series. This static approach has limited capacity to adapt to the complex distribution shifts inherent in time-series data. Second, the learning processes of existing online methods are often confined to a single perspective, whereas distribution shifts may manifest across multiple dimensions simultaneously, such as time, frequency, and space. A single-perspective focus can make the model less sensitive to these multifaceted shifts and may lead to conflicts between dimensional adaptations. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a multi-perspective online ensemble framework, the Trio Online Ensemble framework (TOE). TOE consists of three branches—time, frequency, and space—and its core mechanism is summarized as follows: (1) During the training phase, TOE independently maintains a memory pool for each branch. As new data arrive, TOE assesses the current model’s suitability for these data via memory retrieval, which in turn informs the decision of whether to trigger branch retraining, thereby enabling dynamic adaptation to distribution shifts. (2) During the testing phase, TOE leverages the test sample from the previous time step to perform memory retrieval. This process indirectly matches the current test sample with suitable model parameters within each of the three branches. We implement a foundational version of TOE (TOE-Base) built upon a fully linear architecture and conduct comprehensive experimental evaluations on eight real-world and eight synthetic datasets. The experimental results show that TOE-Base achieves competitive or better performance than several advanced MTSF methods. Furthermore, applying the TOE framework to other existing methods also yields consistent performance improvements. .
journal: IEEE Transactions on Knowledge and Data Engineering

title: AoI-Aware Joint Sampling-Buffering-Routing Optimization for Autonomous UAV Swarms via a MARL Approach
abstract: Real-time monitoring in infrastructure-constrained environments presents critical challenges for time-sensitive applications. Conventional approaches relying on terrestrial sensors are impractical in remote regions, whereas UAV swarms operating as Flying Ad-hoc Networks (FANETs) offer autonomy but still depend on pre-deployed ground infrastructure. To overcome this limitation, we adopt a Leader–Follower UAV swarm architecture in which Follower UAVs serve dual roles as sensing platforms and communication relays, enabling a fully autonomous aerial monitoring system with enhanced adaptability. The effectiveness of real-time monitoring hinges on data freshness, rendering the optimization of information timeliness essential. To address this, we introduce the Adaptive Age-aware Sampling–Buffering–Routing (AASBR) framework to minimize Age of Information (AoI) through coordinated sampling, buffering, and routing. We model this problem as a Decentralized Partially Observable Markov Decision Process (Dec-POMDP) and propose a novel multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) approach named Curriculum-Orchestrated Multi-head Multi-Agent Proximal Policy Optimization (COMH-MAPPO) algorithm. COMH-MAPPO employs a multi-head policy architecture combined with curriculum learning to progressively address coupled decision-making challenges under partial observability. Simulation results demonstrate that COMH-MAPPO achieves over 48% and 15% improvement in average AoI compared with MARL and ablation benchmarks, respectively, while also outperforming benchmarks across key network metrics including transmission latency, packet delivery ratio, and throughput.

title: Safe and Scalable Collaboration in Multiagent LLM Systems: A Comprehensive Review
abstract: Large language model (LLM)-based multiagent systems are a rapidly evolving frontier of artificial intelligence that enables complex coordination, communication, and autonomous reasoning across distributed agents. This article presents a comprehensive review of multiagent LLM ecosystems, organized around four foundational pillars: coordination strategies, communication frameworks, safety challenges, and trust and alignment mechanisms. We synthesize a range of architectural approaches to agent interaction, including shared latent representations, strategic autonomy, task decomposition, and neuro-symbolic communication protocols. We then systematically examine the critical vulnerabilities distinctive to multiagent environments, namely prompt injection, perceptual adversarial attacks, reward misalignment, and operational overreach. To address these issues, we propose the trust stack: a multilayered trust framework spanning epistemic reliability, behavioral alignment, role awareness, social accountability, and institutional governance. Beyond synthesizing the literature, this review contributes a novel integrated perspective. It models the interdependencies among these four pillars, formalizes the trust stack as an operational framework with runtime-computable metrics, and derives design principles from a cross-system analysis of real multiagent deployment failures—contributions absent from prior surveys. We further investigate the prospects for superalignment through constitutional AI principles, multiagent value aggregation, and dynamic preference shaping. Collectively, this work establishes a theoretical and practical foundation for the secure, reliable, and dependable deployment of multiagent LLM systems and offers a roadmap for future research at the intersection of coordination, communication, and alignment.
journal: IEEE Transactions on Systems, Man, and Cybernetics: Systems

title: Robust Optimization of a Double-Primary Tubular Permanent Magnet Synchronous Linear Motor Considering Manufacturing Uncertainties
abstract: Manufacturing-induced uncertainties in structural parameters pose a critical challenge to the performance consistency and reliability of tubular permanent magnet synchronous linear motors (TPMSLMs), whereas most existing design approaches rely on deterministic assumptions. To address this issue, an efficient, robust optimization framework is proposed for a double-primary TPMSLM (DP-TPMSLM). A high-accuracy subdomain analytical model is established to capture slotting effects, end effects, and end tooth geometry, achieving a favorable balance between modeling fidelity and computational efficiency. An interval-based robust optimization method is formulated by integrating interval theory with backpropagation (BP) neural network differentiation, enabling efficient uncertainty propagation without repeated global searches. Compared with conventional interval-nesting approaches, the proposed method improves computational efficiency by 93% while maintaining comparable accuracy. Experimental validation on a prototype shows that the optimized design achieves a 75.9% reduction in detent force and a 6.49% increase in average thrust. These results demonstrate that the proposed method effectively enhances both performance and robustness under manufacturing uncertainties, providing a practical and efficient solution for robust motor design.

title: Vegetation Phenology Shifts Under Climate Change: Cross‐Season Mechanisms and Consequences for Ecosystem Productivity
abstract: Vegetation phenology—the timing of recurring life‐cycle events—has shifted markedly under climate change, with far‐reaching consequences for terrestrial ecosystems and the climate system. Yet phenological research has largely focused on discrete events, often overlooking the continuous and seasonally connected nature of vegetation development. Here, we synthesize recent evidence into a cross‐season framework in which spring (start of the growing season), peak (timing of maximum greenness/photosynthetic capacity), and autumn (end of the growing season) phenology are treated as dynamically linked phases. Within this framework, spring phenology is governed by chilling‐forcing dynamics, which are modulated by contemporary environmental cues, previous‐year autumn phenology, and resource status. Peak phenology is primarily driven by early‐season development and carbon uptake, both of which are influenced by spring phenology and temperature. Autumn phenology integrates late‐season environmental conditions with legacies of earlier development, mediated by carbon source‐sink balance and water and nutrient availability. Across these phases, the evidence points to reciprocal coupling between phenology, carbon uptake, and developmental processes: phenological shifts reshape the seasonal trajectory of productivity and growth, and the resulting carbon dynamics feedback to regulate subsequent developmental transitions. This seasonally integrated perspective provides a mechanistic basis for predicting how non‐linear, season‐specific climate change will reorganize the terrestrial carbon cycle, and calls for phenology models that explicitly represent cross‐season linkages.

title: Forest Densification and Pollution Rival Climate in Driving US Tree Demographic Change
abstract: Forests play critical roles in biodiversity, climate regulation, and human well‐being, yet their responses to simultaneous environmental changes remain poorly understood. Across the United States, forest demographic rates are influenced by climate change, atmospheric pollution trends, and systematic changes in forest density. In spite of long‐term interest in these facets of global change, their relative importance has not previously been quantified and compared. Here, we apply a framework that decomposes demographic trends into sensitivity (species' responsiveness to environmental variables) and exposure (magnitude of environmental change experienced). Using nationwide forest inventory data from 2002 to 2024, we analyzed how recruitment, growth, and mortality of 100 tree species responded to six environmental variables representing climate, pollution, and forest density. This analysis showed that, despite substantial research attention on climate impacts, changes in forest density and atmospheric pollutant deposition (particularly sulfur) showed stronger associations with all three demographic rates, driven by both higher exposure and greater sensitivity to these factors. We also found that, of the demographic processes, recruitment probability was the most sensitive to each of the six environmental drivers, emphasizing the importance of regeneration in shaping forest responses to global change. The results also document a general slowdown in forest dynamics over recent decades, with declining recruitment, growth, and mortality on average across the United States, albeit with substantial geographic and taxonomic variation. This comprehensive analysis provides a framework for understanding forest responses to complex environmental change, identifying the most influential drivers of demographic processes, and developing targeted conservation and management strategies in an era of rapid change.

title: Increasing Extreme Negative Vegetation Responses to Drought‐Related Compound Events
abstract: Vegetation growth is increasingly threatened by both extreme climate events and anthropogenic disturbances. Although considerable attention has been given to detecting large‐scale vegetation anomalies, comprehensive analyses of the spatiotemporal dynamics of negative extreme anomalies in vegetation growth (NEGs) and their underlying drivers remain limited. Here, we treat NEGs as event‐scale vegetation declines from onset to termination, enabling coherent tracking of vegetation decline events and their associated drivers. Applied to global leaf area index (LAI) data from 2001 to 2024, we find increasing tendencies in both NEG frequency (0.07% year −1 , p = 0.13) and affected area (394,471 km 2 year −1 , p = 0.04), reaching 39% of the global land surface by 2024. Interannual variations in NEG frequency and affected area show positive associations with annual mean CO 2 anomalies, which may suggest a potential influence on the stability of the terrestrial carbon sink. Coincidence analysis further indicates that drought‐related events dominate globally: single‐driver drought events, together with drought‐related compound events involving temperature extremes and wildfires, account for 58.5%–59.8% of all NEGs. By the end of the 21st century, up to 50.8% of the global land surface is projected to experience NEGs annually under the high‐emission scenario, approximately 1.6 times the simulated historical level. These findings highlight the urgent need for climate mitigation to reduce the intensification of compound climate extremes and underscore the importance of understanding how these events may destabilize ecosystems and amplify climate feedbacks in a warming world.

title: Integrating Soil Organic Carbon, Erosion and Land Productivity Dynamics as Composite Soil Health Indicators Under Semiarid Conditions: A Diagnostic Approach Within the Land Degradation Neutrality Framework
abstract: Soil health is foundational to sustainable land use, particularly in semiarid environments where surface‐driven degradation processes can rapidly undermine ecological stability. This study introduces an integrated diagnostic framework that evaluates Soil Organic Carbon (SOC) and soil erosion as critical surface process indicators influencing soil health, alongside Land Productivity Dynamics (LPD) as a functional response metric. The framework employs independent data sources for each indicator to avoid mathematical autocorrelation: SOC is derived from a national soil database, erosion is modelled using the Revised Universal Soil Loss Equation (RUSLE) approach with independently derived cover factors and LPD is calculated from multi‐temporal NDVI trends. Framed within the Land Degradation Neutrality (LDN) paradigm, the approach was applied to the Nallıhan district of Ankara, Turkey. By combining remote sensing, spatial modelling, and a multicriteria response hierarchy, the study identifies distinct degradation zones and intervention priorities. Results reveal that 18% of the area is degraded, with significant low SOC levels (mean SOC of 38.1 t/ha C (agriculture)) and high erosion risk (average soil loss of 7.96–11.25 t ha −1 y −1 between 2000 and 2018) concentrated in agricultural zones, where over 26% of the land showed early signs of productivity decline. Forest and pasture areas show relative resilience, attributed to sustainable management and afforestation. The interplay among SOC, erosion and LPD illustrates how surface processes shape long‐term soil functionality. This composite indicator approach enhances early warning diagnostics, offering a robust pathway for implementing Sustainable Land Management (SLM) strategies that foster soil regeneration, resilience and restoration under arid and semiarid pressures.

title: Synergistic polar states by selective atomic gradients
abstract: Materials that combine distinct properties within a single phase are of fundamental and technological interest. Here, we present a broadly applicable strategy to achieve strong bulk polarity that not only coexists with its originally incompatible properties, such as metallicity, but also synergistically enables exceptional functionalities. A combination of thin-film synthesis, atomic-scale imaging, and theoretical calculations reveals that A-site selective atomic gradients induce strong polar states in otherwise centrosymmetric perovskite oxides ABO 3 . These polar states unconventionally coexist with various preexisting properties, leading to bulk polar metallicity with tunable nonreciprocal transport; high-κ, low-loss dielectricity with an equivalent oxide thickness below 0.1 nanometer; and giant pyroelectricity. This work may enable the development of new multifunctional materials with unusual coexisting and synergistic properties.

title: Mitochondrial carrier SLC25A34 links clock, diet, and temperature control of adipocyte lipid cycling
abstract: Adipocyte lipid metabolism is coordinated by circadian rhythms, diet, and environmental temperature, but how these diverse signals are molecularly integrated remains unknown. We showed that these cues converge on the orphan mitochondrial transporter SLC25A34 to orchestrate lipid cycling. During the sleep phase, the adipocyte clock suppresses Slc25a34 expression through the REV-ERB transcriptional repressors. Entering the active phase, consuming lipid-rich diets, or exposure to cold abolishes REV-ERB repression, and lipolytic signals stimulate Slc25a34 transcription through the peroxisome proliferator–activated receptors. SLC25A34 is proposed to import oxaloacetate into mitochondria, dually supporting the tricarboxylic acid cycle and cytosolic acetyl–coenzyme A (acetyl-CoA) production. Elevated cytosolic acetyl-CoA then fuels the synthesis of lipids and promotes the transcription of genes enhancing mitochondrial oxidation. Thus, SLC25A34 confers circadian, dietary, and temperature control of adipocyte lipid metabolism.

title: Quadrupolar sea level fluctuations reveal episodes of rapid polar wander
abstract: True polar wander (TPW) is presently occurring at a rate of ~10 centimeters per year, exceeding the mean rate of differential plate motion. Whether this rate is transient and negligible on geological timescales or whether Earth has experienced rapid TPW lasting millions of years is unclear. Paleomagnetic evidence has been used to propose fast episodes of TPW, but limitations of the paleomagnetic record have precluded definitive results. Rapid TPW will induce global sea level fluctuations associated with relative changes in centrifugal potential, offering an independent test. We evaluated this prediction using continental flooding reconstructions and identified multiple robust quadrupolar patterns since 320 million years ago, confirming that protracted rapid TPW has occurred on Earth and that couplings among Earth’s rotational dynamics, mantle processes, and surface environments can be strongly episodic.

title: Loss of the tumor suppressor p53 generates a signaling gradient that drives epithelial clonal expansion
abstract: Although tumor protein p53 ( TP53 ) mutations are among the most common lesions in epithelial cancers, how p53 loss drives unrestrained clonal expansion remains unclear. Working with mouse epidermis, we found that p53 suppresses clonal expansion by limiting progenitor self-renewal. Integrating chromatin immunoprecipitation sequencing, transcriptional analyses, and genetic screens, we identified a p53-dependent network controlling progenitor renewal and differentiation, in which secreted frizzled-related protein 1 ( Sfrp1 ), low-density lipoprotein receptor–related protein 1 ( Lrp1 ), and ubiquitin-specific peptidase 22 ( Usp22 ) were direct targets of p53 and the most genetically upstream components. Their suppression after p53 loss generated a radial gradient of Wnt activity across mutant clones. Genetic manipulation showed that a Wnt activity gradient, rather than uniform elevation, was associated with sustained clonal expansion. These findings identify spatial organization as a determinant of clonal behavior and a mechanism by which TP53 inactivation drives tissue colonization.

title: Snowball refrigeration of Earth’s crust mimics glacial erosion
abstract: Glaciation cools the crust by setting its surface temperature to 0°C or well below. During the Cryogenian Snowball Earth glaciations, these conditions were in place long enough to cool the entire crustal column. Although crustal thermal history can be deciphered by thermochronology, these data are typically interpreted to record depth changes due to burial or erosion. Thermal models of the crust under Cryogenian boundary conditions predict that thermochronometers were substantially altered in the upper quarter to half of the crust. This Snowball Earth refrigeration, with little to no coeval erosion, may have imparted a cooling signal mimicking up to 3‒5 km of glacial erosion. Rock cooling previously attributed to massive Snowball erosion and linked to the Great Unconformity may instead reflect a great refrigeration of Earth’s crust, with implications for thermochronology across other climate events.

title: Hypertension fuels osteoarthritis through neuroendocrine signaling
abstract: Osteoarthritis (OA) is a degenerative joint disease, the progression of which is accelerated by systemic metabolic stress. Here, we identified a neuroendocrine pathway through which hypertension accelerates OA pathogenesis in joints predisposed by mechanical injury or aging. Nationwide cohort analyses and hypertensive mouse models demonstrated that elevated blood pressure exacerbates OA pathogenesis. OA-primed chondrocytes up-regulated arginine vasopressin (AVP) receptor 1A (AVPR1A), rendering them responsive to hypertension-associated circulating AVP. AVP-AVPR1A signaling enhanced catabolic signaling while suppressing anabolic regulators, thereby promoting cartilage catabolism. Genetic deletion or pharmacological inhibition of AVPR1A protected against hypertension-driven OA acceleration. Transcriptomic profiling and gene-silencing analyses identified NR4A3 as the principal downstream transcriptional mediator. Collectively, these findings establish the AVP-AVPR1A axis as a mechanistic link between systemic hypertensive stress and joint degeneration.

title: Incorporation of atmospheric components in planetary magma oceans through bubble–metal compounds
abstract: Atmophile elements (carbon, hydrogen, and nitrogen) were thought to accrete late during planetary formation, yet cosmochemical and astrophysical evidence suggests that they were already present while small bodies, such as Vesta, were forming. High-temperature magmatic events on small bodies, however, should have outgassed these ultravolatile elements because gravity would have been insufficient to retain them. In this study, experiments reveal that gas bubbles strongly attach to metal droplets in magma ocean–like mixtures, forming compounds that resist segregation. Early flotation of such compounds would have enhanced mantle siderophile endowment, eliminating the need for late accretion. On small bodies, low gravity would have enabled millimeter- to centimeter-sized compounds to sink, trapping atmophiles in their interiors. This mechanism links core formation to the early entrapment of atmophile elements and provides a framework for reconciling volatile delivery across planetary bodies and planetary accretion models.

title: Dynamic multimodal cation-carbon interaction for efficient adiponitrile electrosynthesis
abstract: Adiponitrile electrosynthesis from acrylonitrile hydrodimerization is critical for the nylon industry. However, the key step of single-electron acrylonitrile reduction demands toxic heavy-metal electrodes and leads to low energy efficiency. We developed a dynamic multimodal cation-electrode interaction strategy to enable efficient synthesis with environmentally friendly carbon electrodes. Optimal benzyltrihexylammonium cations create a water-depleted interface in aqueous electrolytes by squeezing the electric double layer through multimodal noncovalent interactions between the benzyl moieties of the cations and carbon electrodes. This strategy achieves selectivity comparable to the standard lead-based system but at substantially lower overpotentials, as demonstrated from the laboratory scale to a 159–square centimeter electrolyzer. This work underscores the importance of tailoring cation-centered microenvironments for sustainable, industrial organic electrosynthesis in more conductive aqueous systems.

title: Hierarchical crystalline organic-inorganic framework enabling high-modulus toughening in nacre
abstract: Enhancing toughness in nanocomposites often involves viscoelastic organic phases, but this typically reduces stiffness. We describe a high-modulus toughening mechanism in mature Cristaria plicata nacre arising from a crystalline organic-inorganic framework composed of aragonite nanorods alternately integrated with intratabular biomolecular crystallites. Due to the critical slip-length effect, these crystalline units approach the theoretical limits of modulus and strength. The nanoconfined biomolecular crystallites function as nanopins at interlamellar interphases, alleviating stress concentrations and enabling cross-scale synchronized deformation, thereby conferring high fracture toughness. Inspired by this mechanism, reconstituted nacre fabricated from regenerated aragonite flakes simultaneously achieved high stiffness and crack resistance. These insights offer a promising pathway toward reliable, high-performance structural materials.

title: Phage proteases activate CBASS antiphage immunity
abstract: Cyclic oligonucleotide–based antiphage signaling systems (CBASS) are bacterial immune pathways evolutionarily related to cGAS-STING (cyclic GMP-AMP synthase–stimulator of interferon genes) in humans. In CBASS, cGAS/DncV-like nucleotidyltransferase (CD-NTase) enzymes sense phage infection and synthesize nucleotide signals to initiate antiviral defense. Here, we reveal phage prohead protease activity as a widespread mechanism of CD-NTase activation. We reconstitute CBASS recognition of phage T4 in vitro and identify proteolytic cleavage of a CD-NTase activation loop as a trigger of immune signal synthesis. Phage prohead proteases directly activate CBASS in vivo, explaining how immunity is initiated late during infection. Structure-based phylogenetic analyses identify activation loops in clade A, D, and G CD-NTases and define residues controlling recognition of distinct phage families. Our results establish CBASS recognition of phage protease activity as a widespread antiviral defense mechanism.

title: Ultrahigh piezoelectricity by polaron-defect complexes
abstract: Materials capable of delivering giant and rapid piezoelectric responses at kilohertz frequencies are pivotal for advanced electromechanical technologies. However, their development has been constrained by a long-standing magnitude–speed trade-off: Ferroelectrics with intrinsic electric dipoles offer fast response but limited polarization, whereas ionic defect motion generates highly polarizable defect dipoles but responds slowly, limiting kilohertz-rate applications. We overcame this fundamental limitation by devising 8 mole % K-doped AgNbO 3 (Ag 0.92 K 0.08 NbO 3 ) thin films engineered to host dynamically reconfigurable polaron-defect complexes through electro-elastic interactions between small electron polarons and lattice defects. Field-driven multi–unit-cell polaron hopping reconfigures these complexes, producing giant defect polarization, and orders-of-magnitude faster kinetics of polaron hopping (versus ionic migration) enables their rapid response. This synergy leads to an unprecedented field-induced effective piezoelectric coefficient of ~7170 picometers per volt with ~6.2% strain at kilohertz frequencies in engineered silver niobate–based films.

title: Reframing menopause and menopause hormone therapy as opportunities for healthy aging
abstract: Menopause is an important biological transition with up to 72 symptoms that shapes aging trajectories across organs and encompasses ~40% of the female lifespan. Although menopause awareness is increasing, research on strategies for menopause symptom management and optimizing health in the postmenopausal period is lacking. This Review highlights that menopause characteristics, such as type, timing, and symptom burden, influence health outcomes and later-life disease risk. Similarly, menopause hormone therapy comes in >200 varieties that differ by dose, formulation of estrogens and progestogens, and timing, each with their own distinct risk-benefit profiles. These distinctions are often missed in the literature but have considerable repercussions for outcomes. Optimized menopause care necessitates a precision medicine approach that considers menopause symptoms, genetics, and previous hormone exposures.

title: Precise length and charge segmentation of billion-dalton supramolecular polymers
abstract: Supramolecular polymers with precise micrometer-scale segments of opposite charge are challenging to synthesize as discrete assemblies in water. These systems could be used to pattern charged surfaces, interact with the membranes of cells, or form hierarchical structures. We report a living polymerization of fibrillar peptide assemblies with a central positively charged segment flanked by negative ones that can have a collective molar mass on the order of billions of daltons. The self-capping supramolecular polymerization required an untwisted β sheet core persisting along the entire length of the assembly as well as dormant ends in the absence of a monomer source. The positive domains of the segmented structures were anchored to the membranes of neurons, leaving the connected negative segments in a highly dynamic state near the cells through charge repulsion. The segmented architecture generated extensive neurite growth and synaptic activity.

title: X and Y chromosomes as determinants of aging and disease
abstract: Sex differences have traditionally been attributed to gonadal hormones, but accumulating evidence shows that sex chromosomes exert distinct, cell-autonomous effects on health, aging, and disease. XX and XY complements alter gene dosage, epigenetic programming, immune signaling, metabolism, and cellular stress responses, which shape aging and disease trajectories in women and men. This Review integrates mechanistic advances in sex chromosome biology—including escape from X chromosome inactivation, X reactivation, parent-of-X-origin, X-skew, X- and Y-linked gene functions, and Y loss—with aging, neurologic disease, immunity, cancer, and cardiometabolic disease. We highlight insights from mouse models, human studies, and emerging technologies that disentangle hormone-driven effects from chromosome-mediated effects and discuss translational implications for diagnostics, biomarkers, therapeutics, and clinical trial design, emphasizing the integration of sex chromosome biology into precision medicine.

title: Stationary entanglement of a levitated oscillator with an optical field
abstract: Stationary entanglement between the motion of macroscopic objects and light is a long-standing goal of quantum optomechanics, with implications for both fundamental tests of quantum physics and emerging quantum technologies. We report the generation of quantum entanglement between the center-of-mass motion of a nanosphere levitated in an optical tweezer inside an optical cavity and the electromagnetic field. Using heterodyne detection, we reconstructed the full set of optomechanical correlations and observed a violation of separability bounds between the mechanical motion and a propagating optical mode, demonstrating the distribution of nonclassical correlations beyond the interaction region. The entanglement was generated at room temperature and remained robust over a broad range of parameters. Our results establish levitated optomechanical systems as a platform for continuous-variable quantum communication and for tests of macroscopic quantum physics.

title: Shaping maternal physiology: Immune control of reproductive adaptation
abstract: Pregnancy is one of the most extensive physiological transitions of adult life, requiring coordinated adaptation across virtually every maternal organ to support fetal growth while preserving maternal health. Although these changes have traditionally been viewed as endocrine driven, emerging evidence identifies the immune system as an active regulator of maternal physiology. The immune system is increasingly recognized as a broad regulator of host physiology, positioning it as a key driver of maternal adaptation. In this work, we discuss how pregnancy reprograms maternal immunity to orchestrate physiological reprograming of tissues. This framework shifts the view of maternal immunity from one centered on immune homeostasis and fetal tolerance to one in which immune cells actively instruct physiological short- and long-term adaptation across maternal organs to shape health beyond reproduction.

title: Sex-specific mechanisms of chronic pain
abstract: For decades, we have known that women, especially younger women, are disproportionately affected by pain disorders, including irritable bowel syndrome, endometriosis, menstrual migraines, fibromyalgia, osteoarthritis, and neuropathic pain, all of which degrade quality of life. The adoption of sex as a biological variable in 2016 has begun to transform the field, revealing distinct sex-specific pathways that initiate, amplify, and resolve pain. In this Review, we synthesize recent advances across visceral and somatic pain, highlighting the impact of sex hormones, immune-neural cross-talk, the gut microbiome, and endogenous analgesic circuits. Rather than clinging to the historical standard that simply described the female bias in pain symptoms, these studies begin to explain why females experience heightened pain, paving the path for mechanism-based precision therapeutics.

title: Keep AI-augmented science contestable
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is moving upstream in science. Systems such as AlphaFold have already transformed protein-structure prediction, while newer agentic systems can search literatures, generate hypotheses, write and execute code, interpret results, and automate much of the path from idea to paper. Recent debates have asked how such systems may change scientific progress, surprise, and human understanding. Yet they also change something more fundamental: who—or what—participates in deciding which questions are asked, which evidence is surfaced, and which alternatives survive. As machine intelligence becomes part of science’s epistemic infrastructure, steps must be taken to ensure that researchers who did not build, own, or operate the system can still contest how ideas and evidence became a claim.
